##### extractData(...) -> Dataset
- **Signature:** `public static Dataset extractData(final QueryResult queryResult) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Extracts data from a QueryResult into a Dataset for tabular operations.
- **Parameters:**
  - `queryResult` (`QueryResult`) — the QueryResult to extract data from. Must not be `null`; its items must be non-null maps, as the service returns them (a hand-built result holding a `null` item fails with `NullPointerException`).
- **Returns:** a Dataset containing the items from this single response page in tabular format; empty when the response carries no items, and also when none of its items has any attribute, because a Dataset without columns has no rows
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `queryResult` is `null`, or an attribute value has no supported DynamoDB type
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  QueryResult result = dynamoDBClient.query(queryRequest);
  Dataset dataset = DynamoDBExecutor.extractData(result);
  dataset.println();   // Print as table
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static Dataset extractData(final QueryResult queryResult, final int offset, final int count) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Extracts data from a QueryResult into a Dataset with pagination.
- **Parameters:**
  - `queryResult` (`QueryResult`) — the QueryResult to extract data from. Must not be `null`; its items must be non-null maps, as the service returns them (a hand-built result holding a `null` item fails with `NullPointerException`).
  - `offset` (`int`) — number of items to skip from the beginning
  - `count` (`int`) — maximum number of items to include
- **Returns:** a Dataset containing the specified range of results; empty also when none of the selected items has any attribute, because a Dataset without columns has no rows
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `queryResult` is `null`, if offset or count is negative, or a selected attribute value has no supported DynamoDB type
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  QueryResult result = dynamoDBClient.query(queryRequest);
  // Extract items 5-14 (skip first 5, take next 10)
  Dataset dataset = DynamoDBExecutor.extractData(result, 5, 10);
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static Dataset extractData(final ScanResult scanResult) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Extracts data from a ScanResult into a Dataset for tabular operations.
- **Contract:**
  - It does not follow `LastEvaluatedKey` or fetch subsequent pages — use `#scan(ScanRequest)` (which streams with automatic pagination) if you need every matching item.
- **Parameters:**
  - `scanResult` (`ScanResult`) — the ScanResult to extract data from. Must not be `null`; its items must be non-null maps, as the service returns them (a hand-built result holding a `null` item fails with `NullPointerException`).
- **Returns:** a Dataset containing the items from this single response page in tabular format; empty when the response carries no items, and also when none of its items has any attribute, because a Dataset without columns has no rows
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `scanResult` is `null`, or an attribute value has no supported DynamoDB type
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  ScanResult result = dynamoDBClient.scan(scanRequest);
  Dataset dataset = DynamoDBExecutor.extractData(result);
  dataset.toCsv(new File("data.csv"));
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static Dataset extractData(final ScanResult scanResult, final int offset, final int count) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Extracts data from a ScanResult into a Dataset with pagination.
- **Parameters:**
  - `scanResult` (`ScanResult`) — the ScanResult to extract data from. Must not be `null`; its items must be non-null maps, as the service returns them (a hand-built result holding a `null` item fails with `NullPointerException`).
  - `offset` (`int`) — number of items to skip from the beginning
  - `count` (`int`) — maximum number of items to include
- **Returns:** a Dataset containing the specified range of results; empty also when none of the selected items has any attribute, because a Dataset without columns has no rows
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `scanResult` is `null`, if offset or count is negative, or a selected attribute value has no supported DynamoDB type
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  ScanResult result = dynamoDBClient.scan(scanRequest);
  // Extract first 100 items only
  Dataset dataset = DynamoDBExecutor.extractData(result, 0, 100);
  ```

#### Public Instance Methods
##### dynamoDBClient(...) -> AmazonDynamoDBClient
- **Signature:** `public AmazonDynamoDBClient dynamoDBClient()`
- **Summary:** Returns the underlying Amazon DynamoDB client used by this executor.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the AmazonDynamoDBClient instance used by this executor, never null
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  AmazonDynamoDBClient client = executor.dynamoDBClient();

  // Direct table operations
  ListTablesResult tables = client.listTables();

  // Advanced configuration
  client.setTimeOffset(1000);
  ```
- **See also:** `AmazonDynamoDBClient`
##### dynamoDBMapper(...) -> DynamoDBMapper
- **Signature:** `public DynamoDBMapper dynamoDBMapper()`
- **Summary:** Returns the default DynamoDB mapper configured for this executor.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the DynamoDBMapper instance configured with this executor's settings, never null
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  DynamoDBMapper mapper = executor.dynamoDBMapper();

  // Direct mapper operations
  User user = mapper.load(User.class, "userId123");
  mapper.save(user);

  // Batch operations take annotated key objects and group results by table name
  User key = new User();
  key.setUserId("userId123");
  Map<String, List<Object>> usersByTable = mapper.batchLoad(List.of(key));
  ```

- **Examples:**

##### mapper(...) -> Mapper<T>
- **Signature:** `public <T> Mapper<T> mapper(final Class<T> targetEntityClass) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates a type-safe mapper for the specified entity class with automatic table name detection.
- **Contract:**
  - Entity classes must be annotated with @Table, @javax.persistence.Table, or @jakarta.persistence.Table to specify the DynamoDB table name.
  - Mapping fails if no ID or more than two IDs are declared.
  - The ID properties are those annotated with `@Id` or `@ReadOnlyId` (or a JPA `@Id`); when no property is annotated, a property named `id` of type `int`/`Integer`, `long`/`Long`, `String`, `java.sql.Timestamp` or `UUID` is the ID by convention.
- **Parameters:**
  - `targetEntityClass` (`Class<T>`) — the entity class to create mapper for. Must be annotated with @Table. Must not be null.
- **Returns:** a cached Mapper instance for the specified entity class, never null
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetEntityClass` is null, not a bean class or a `Map` type (an entity-annotated `Map` subclass included), is missing `@Table`, does not declare one or two ID properties, or two IDs map to the same DynamoDB attribute name
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  @Table("Users")
  public class User {
      @Id private String userId;
      private String name;
      // getters/setters
  }

  Mapper<User> userMapper = executor.mapper(User.class);
  User user = userMapper.getItem(asKey("userId", "123"));
  ```
- **Signature:** `public <T> Mapper<T> mapper(final Class<T> targetEntityClass, final String tableName, final NamingPolicy namingPolicy) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates a type-safe mapper for the specified entity class with explicit table name and naming policy.
- **Parameters:**
  - `targetEntityClass` (`Class<T>`) — the entity class to create mapper for. Must be a valid bean class with one or two ID properties (as described on `#mapper(Class)`). Must not be null.
  - `tableName` (`String`) — the DynamoDB table name to use for operations. Must not be null or empty.
  - `namingPolicy` (`NamingPolicy`) — the naming policy for converting property names to attribute names; if `null`, `NamingPolicy#CAMEL_CASE` is used.
- **Returns:** a new Mapper instance configured with the specified parameters, never null
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetEntityClass` is `null`, if `tableName` is null or empty, if `targetEntityClass` is not a bean class or is a `Map` type (an entity-annotated `Map` subclass included), or if it does not declare one or two ID properties, or if two IDs map to the same attribute name
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Mapper<Product> productMapper = executor.mapper(
      Product.class,
      "dev_products",
      NamingPolicy.SNAKE_CASE
  );
  productMapper.putItem(new Product("PROD-123", "Widget"));
  ```
##### async(...) -> AsyncDynamoDBExecutor
- **Signature:** `public AsyncDynamoDBExecutor async()`
- **Summary:** Returns an asynchronous version of this DynamoDB executor for non-blocking operations.
- **Contract:**
  - When the default is used, it is a shared thread pool of `max(64, CPU_CORES * 8)` threads (its larger maximum size never takes effect, because `AsyncExecutor` queues further tasks in an unbounded queue), shared by all executors of this class constructed without an explicit `AsyncExecutor`.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** an AsyncDynamoDBExecutor instance sharing this executor's configuration, never null
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  ContinuableFuture<User> future = executor.async().getItem(tableName, key, User.class);
  future.thenRunAsync(user -> {
      // Process user asynchronously
      System.out.println(user == null ? "(not found)" : user.getName());
  });
  ```

##### batchGetItem(...) -> varies by overload
- **Signature:** `public Map<String, List<Map<String, Object>>> batchGetItem(final Map<String, KeysAndAttributes> requestItems) throws AmazonClientException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Retrieves multiple items from one or more DynamoDB tables in a single batch operation.
- **Contract:**
  - If the request exceeds these limits, you'll need to make multiple batch calls.
  - Batch Operation Limits: Maximum 100 items per batch request Maximum 16 MB total response size Items can span multiple tables Unprocessed items: If DynamoDB cannot process every key (for example due to size limits or throughput throttling) the remaining keys are reported by `BatchGetItemResult.getUnprocessedKeys()`.
  - Call the underlying client directly (`dynamoDBClient().batchGetItem(request)`) when you need to detect and re-issue unprocessed keys with exponential back-off.
- **Parameters:**
  - `requestItems` (`Map<String, KeysAndAttributes>`) — a map of table names to KeysAndAttributes specifying which items to retrieve. Must not be null.
- **Returns:** a map of table names to lists of retrieved items, never null. Unprocessed keys are not included.
- **Throws:**
  - `com.amazonaws.AmazonClientException` — if the request is rejected by the underlying DynamoDB client (for example, when requestItems is null or invalid)
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if a returned attribute cannot be converted to the requested result type, or a result bean or container cannot be constructed or populated
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, KeysAndAttributes> requestItems = new HashMap<>();

  // Request multiple users
  List<Map<String, AttributeValue>> userKeys = Arrays.asList(
      asKey("userId", "user1"),
      asKey("userId", "user2")
  );
  requestItems.put("Users", new KeysAndAttributes().withKeys(userKeys));

  Map<String, List<Map<String, Object>>> results = executor.batchGetItem(requestItems);
  List<Map<String, Object>> users = results.get("Users");
  ```
- **See also:** `#batchGetItem(Map, String)`, `#batchGetItem(Map, Class)`

##### putItem(...) -> PutItemResult
- **Signature:** `public PutItemResult putItem(final String tableName, final Map<String, AttributeValue> item) throws AmazonClientException`
- **Summary:** Inserts or replaces an item in the specified DynamoDB table.
- **Contract:**
  - If an item with the same primary key already exists, it will be overwritten.
- **Parameters:**
  - `tableName` (`String`) — the name of the DynamoDB table. Must not be `null` or empty.
  - `item` (`Map<String, AttributeValue>`) — the item to put, as a map of attribute names to AttributeValues. Must not be `null`.
- **Returns:** a `PutItemResult` containing operation metadata (consumed capacity is not requested by this overload; use `#putItem(PutItemRequest)` with `ReturnConsumedCapacity` to obtain it)
- **Throws:**
  - `com.amazonaws.AmazonClientException` — if the request is rejected by the underlying DynamoDB client (for example, when tableName or item is null or invalid)
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, AttributeValue> item = asItem(
      "userId", "user123",
      "name", "John Doe",
      "email", "john@example.com",
      "createdAt", System.currentTimeMillis()
  );

  PutItemResult result = executor.putItem("Users", item);
  // result.getConsumedCapacity() is null: this overload does not request consumed capacity
  ```
- **See also:** `#putItem(String, Map, String)`, `#updateItem`
- **Signature:** `public PutItemResult putItem(final String tableName, final Map<String, AttributeValue> item, final String returnValues) throws AmazonClientException`
- **Summary:** Inserts or replaces an item in DynamoDB table with return value options.
- **Contract:**
  - This is useful for auditing or when you need to know what data was overwritten.
- **Parameters:**
  - `tableName` (`String`) — the name of the DynamoDB table. Must not be `null` or empty.
  - `item` (`Map<String, AttributeValue>`) — the item to put, as a map of attribute names to AttributeValues. Must not be `null`.
  - `returnValues` (`String`) — specifies what to return: "NONE" or "ALL_OLD"
- **Returns:** a `PutItemResult` containing operation metadata and optionally the replaced item
- **Throws:**
  - `com.amazonaws.AmazonClientException` — if the request is rejected by the underlying DynamoDB client (for example, when tableName or item is null or invalid)
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, AttributeValue> item = asItem(
      "userId", "user123",
      "name", "Jane Doe",
      "updatedAt", Instant.now().toEpochMilli()
  );

  PutItemResult result = executor.putItem("Users", item, "ALL_OLD");
  Map<String, AttributeValue> oldItem = result.getAttributes();
  if (oldItem != null) {
      System.out.println("Replaced item: " + oldItem);
  }
  ```
- **See also:** `com.amazonaws.services.dynamodbv2.model.ReturnValue`
- **Signature:** `public PutItemResult putItem(final PutItemRequest putItemRequest) throws IllegalArgumentException, AmazonClientException`
- **Summary:** Inserts or replaces an item using a fully configured PutItemRequest.
- **Contract:**
  - Use this method when you need advanced features like conditional puts or custom write concerns.
- **Parameters:**
  - `putItemRequest` (`PutItemRequest`) — the complete request with all parameters. Must not be `null`.
- **Returns:** a `PutItemResult` containing operation metadata and optional return values
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `putItemRequest` is null
  - `com.amazonaws.AmazonClientException` — if the SDK cannot send the putItem request or DynamoDB rejects it because of credentials, table/key data, conditions, or service limits
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  PutItemRequest request = new PutItemRequest()
      .withTableName("Users")
      .withItem(asItem("userId", "user123", "name", "John"))
      .withConditionExpression("attribute_not_exists(userId)") // Only if new
      .withReturnConsumedCapacity(ReturnConsumedCapacity.TOTAL);

  try {
      PutItemResult result = executor.putItem(request);
      System.out.println("Item created successfully");
  } catch (ConditionalCheckFailedException e) {
      System.out.println("Item already exists");
  }
  ```
##### batchWriteItem(...) -> BatchWriteItemResult
- **Signature:** `public BatchWriteItemResult batchWriteItem(final Map<String, List<WriteRequest>> requestItems) throws AmazonClientException`
- **Summary:** Performs batch write operations (puts and deletes) across multiple tables.
- **Parameters:**
  - `requestItems` (`Map<String, List<WriteRequest>>`) — map of table names to lists of write requests (puts/deletes). Must not be `null`.
- **Returns:** a `BatchWriteItemResult` containing any unprocessed items (consumed capacity is not requested by this overload)
- **Throws:**
  - `com.amazonaws.AmazonClientException` — if the request is rejected by the underlying DynamoDB client (for example, when requestItems is null, or when DynamoDB's batch limits are exceeded, which fails with a service `ValidationException`)
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<WriteRequest> userWrites = Arrays.asList(
      new WriteRequest(new PutRequest(asItem("userId", "user1", "name", "Alice"))),
      new WriteRequest(new PutRequest(asItem("userId", "user2", "name", "Bob"))),
      new WriteRequest(new DeleteRequest(asKey("userId", "user3")))
  );

  Map<String, List<WriteRequest>> requestItems = Map.of("Users", userWrites);

  BatchWriteItemResult result = executor.batchWriteItem(requestItems);
  if (!result.getUnprocessedItems().isEmpty()) {
      // Retry unprocessed items
      executor.batchWriteItem(result.getUnprocessedItems());
  }
  ```
- **See also:** `#batchWriteItem(BatchWriteItemRequest)`

  ```java
  BatchWriteItemRequest request = new BatchWriteItemRequest()
      .withRequestItems(requestItems)
      .withReturnConsumedCapacity(ReturnConsumedCapacity.TOTAL)
      .withReturnItemCollectionMetrics(ReturnItemCollectionMetrics.SIZE);

  BatchWriteItemResult result = executor.batchWriteItem(request);
  System.out.println("Total consumed capacity: " + result.getConsumedCapacity());
  ```
##### updateItem(...) -> UpdateItemResult
- **Signature:** `public UpdateItemResult updateItem(final String tableName, final Map<String, AttributeValue> key, final Map<String, AttributeValueUpdate> attributeUpdates) throws AmazonClientException`
- **Summary:** Updates specific attributes of an existing item in DynamoDB.
- **Parameters:**
  - `tableName` (`String`) — the name of the DynamoDB table. Must not be `null` or empty.
  - `key` (`Map<String, AttributeValue>`) — the primary key identifying the item to update. Must not be `null`.
  - `attributeUpdates` (`Map<String, AttributeValueUpdate>`) — map of attribute names to update actions; a `null` or empty map is sent as no update, which (as DynamoDB's UpdateItem does) succeeds and creates a key-only item when none exists
- **Returns:** an `UpdateItemResult` containing operation metadata
- **Throws:**
  - `com.amazonaws.AmazonClientException` — if the request is rejected by the underlying DynamoDB client (for example, when tableName or key is null or invalid, or an update is invalid)
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, AttributeValue> key = asKey("userId", "user123");

  Map<String, AttributeValueUpdate> updates = new HashMap<>();
  updates.put("lastLogin", toAttributeValueUpdate(Instant.now().toString()));
  updates.put("loginCount", new AttributeValueUpdate()
      .withAction(AttributeAction.ADD)
      .withValue(toAttributeValue(1)));
  updates.put("tempToken", new AttributeValueUpdate()
      .withAction(AttributeAction.DELETE));

  UpdateItemResult result = executor.updateItem("Users", key, updates);
  ```
- **See also:** `#updateItem(String, Map, Map, String)`
- **Signature:** `public UpdateItemResult updateItem(final String tableName, final Map<String, AttributeValue> key, final Map<String, AttributeValueUpdate> attributeUpdates, final String returnValues) throws AmazonClientException`
- **Summary:** Updates item attributes with options to return values.
- **Contract:**
  - This is useful for audit trails, optimistic locking patterns, or when you need to verify the update results.
- **Parameters:**
  - `tableName` (`String`) — the name of the DynamoDB table. Must not be `null` or empty.
  - `key` (`Map<String, AttributeValue>`) — the primary key identifying the item to update. Must not be `null`.
  - `attributeUpdates` (`Map<String, AttributeValueUpdate>`) — map of attribute names to update actions; a `null` or empty map is sent as no update, which (as DynamoDB's UpdateItem does) succeeds and creates a key-only item when none exists
  - `returnValues` (`String`) — specifies what to return (see method description)
- **Returns:** an `UpdateItemResult` containing operation metadata and optional values
- **Throws:**
  - `com.amazonaws.AmazonClientException` — if the request is rejected by the underlying DynamoDB client (for example, when tableName or key is null or invalid, or an update is invalid)
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, AttributeValue> key = asKey("userId", "user123");
  Map<String, AttributeValueUpdate> updates = asUpdateItem(
      "email", "newemail@example.com",
      "updatedAt", System.currentTimeMillis()
  );

  UpdateItemResult result = executor.updateItem("Users", key, updates, "ALL_NEW");
  ```
- **See also:** `com.amazonaws.services.dynamodbv2.model.ReturnValue`
- **Signature:** `public UpdateItemResult updateItem(final UpdateItemRequest updateItemRequest) throws IllegalArgumentException, AmazonClientException`
- **Summary:** Updates an item using a fully configured UpdateItemRequest.
- **Parameters:**
  - `updateItemRequest` (`UpdateItemRequest`) — the complete update request. Must not be `null`.
- **Returns:** an `UpdateItemResult` containing operation results
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `updateItemRequest` is null
  - `com.amazonaws.AmazonClientException` — if the SDK cannot send the updateItem request or DynamoDB rejects it because of credentials, table/key data, conditions, or service limits
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  UpdateItemRequest request = new UpdateItemRequest()
      .withTableName("Users")
      .withKey(asKey("userId", "user123"))
      .withUpdateExpression("SET #n = :name, #c = #c + :inc")
      .withExpressionAttributeNames(Map.of(
          "#n", "name",
          "#c", "counter"
      ))
      .withExpressionAttributeValues(Map.of(
          ":name", toAttributeValue("New Name"),
          ":inc", toAttributeValue(1),
          ":old", toAttributeValue("Old Name")
      ))
      .withConditionExpression("#n = :old")
      .withReturnValues("ALL_NEW");

  UpdateItemResult result = executor.updateItem(request);
  ```
##### deleteItem(...) -> DeleteItemResult
- **Signature:** `public DeleteItemResult deleteItem(final String tableName, final Map<String, AttributeValue> key) throws AmazonClientException`
- **Summary:** Deletes a single item from the specified DynamoDB table.
- **Contract:**
  - If the item doesn't exist, the operation completes successfully without error.
  - Consider implementing soft deletes (marking items as deleted) if you need recovery options.
- **Parameters:**
  - `tableName` (`String`) — the name of the DynamoDB table. Must not be `null` or empty.
  - `key` (`Map<String, AttributeValue>`) — the primary key of the item to delete. Must not be `null`.
- **Returns:** a `DeleteItemResult` containing operation metadata
- **Throws:**
  - `com.amazonaws.AmazonClientException` — if the request is rejected by the underlying DynamoDB client (for example, when tableName or key is null or invalid)
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, AttributeValue> key = asKey("userId", "user123");

  DeleteItemResult result = executor.deleteItem("Users", key);
  // result.getConsumedCapacity() is null: this overload does not request consumed capacity
  ```
- **See also:** `#deleteItem(String, Map, String)`
- **Signature:** `public DeleteItemResult deleteItem(final String tableName, final Map<String, AttributeValue> key, final String returnValues) throws AmazonClientException`
- **Summary:** Deletes an item with options to return the deleted item's attributes.
- **Parameters:**
  - `tableName` (`String`) — the name of the DynamoDB table. Must not be `null` or empty.
  - `key` (`Map<String, AttributeValue>`) — the primary key of the item to delete. Must not be `null`.
  - `returnValues` (`String`) — "NONE" or "ALL_OLD" to get deleted item attributes
- **Returns:** a `DeleteItemResult` containing metadata and optionally the deleted item
- **Throws:**
  - `com.amazonaws.AmazonClientException` — if the request is rejected by the underlying DynamoDB client (for example, when tableName or key is null or invalid)
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, AttributeValue> key = asKey("userId", "user123");

  DeleteItemResult result = executor.deleteItem("Users", key, "ALL_OLD");
  Map<String, AttributeValue> deletedItem = result.getAttributes();
  if (deletedItem != null) {
      System.out.println("Deleted user: " + deletedItem.get("name"));
      // Could save to audit log or archive table
  }
  ```
- **See also:** `com.amazonaws.services.dynamodbv2.model.ReturnValue`
- **Signature:** `public DeleteItemResult deleteItem(final DeleteItemRequest deleteItemRequest) throws IllegalArgumentException, AmazonClientException`
- **Summary:** Deletes an item using a fully configured DeleteItemRequest.
- **Contract:**
  - Use this for safe deletes with conditions or when you need detailed metrics.
- **Parameters:**
  - `deleteItemRequest` (`DeleteItemRequest`) — the complete delete request. Must not be `null`.
- **Returns:** a `DeleteItemResult` containing operation results
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `deleteItemRequest` is null
  - `com.amazonaws.AmazonClientException` — if the SDK cannot send the deleteItem request or DynamoDB rejects it because of credentials, table/key data, conditions, or service limits
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  DeleteItemRequest request = new DeleteItemRequest()
      .withTableName("Users")
      .withKey(asKey("userId", "user123"))
      .withConditionExpression("attribute_exists(userId) AND #s = :status")
      .withExpressionAttributeNames(Map.of("#s", "status"))
      .withExpressionAttributeValues(Map.of(":status", toAttributeValue("INACTIVE")))
      .withReturnValues("ALL_OLD");

  try {
      DeleteItemResult result = executor.deleteItem(request);
      System.out.println("Deleted inactive user: " + result.getAttributes());
  } catch (ConditionalCheckFailedException e) {
      System.out.println("User not found or still active");
  }
  ```
##### list(...) -> varies by overload
- **Signature:** `public List<Map<String, Object>> list(final QueryRequest queryRequest) throws IllegalArgumentException, AmazonClientException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Executes a DynamoDB query and returns results as a list of maps.
- **Parameters:**
  - `queryRequest` (`QueryRequest`) — the query parameters. Must not be `null`.
- **Returns:** the query items materialized according to the pagination behavior of `#list(QueryRequest, Class)`, never `null`
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if queryRequest is null
  - `com.amazonaws.AmazonClientException` — if the SDK cannot send the query request or DynamoDB rejects it because of credentials, table/key data, conditions, or service limits
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if a returned attribute cannot be converted to the requested result type, or a result bean or container cannot be constructed or populated
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  QueryRequest request = new QueryRequest()
      .withTableName("Sales")
      .withKeyConditionExpression("#region = :region")
      .withExpressionAttributeNames(Map.of("#region", "region"))
      .withExpressionAttributeValues(Map.of(
          ":region", toAttributeValue("US-WEST")
      ));

  List<Map<String, Object>> sales = executor.list(request);
  sales.forEach(System.out::println);   // Print each item as a map
  ```
- **Signature:** `public <T> List<T> list(final QueryRequest queryRequest, final Class<T> targetClass) throws IllegalArgumentException, AmazonClientException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Executes a DynamoDB query and returns results as a list of entities.
- **Contract:**
  - Automatic pagination: If the first response carries a non-empty `lastEvaluatedKey` and the caller did not set `exclusiveStartKey` on the request, this method transparently issues follow-up queries (cloning the request and advancing `exclusiveStartKey`) until every page has been read, and returns the concatenated results.
  - If the caller did set `exclusiveStartKey`, only the single page is returned — pagination is deferred to the caller.
- **Parameters:**
  - `queryRequest` (`QueryRequest`) — the query parameters. Must not be `null`.
  - `targetClass` (`Class<T>`) — the class to convert retrieved items to. Must not be `null`.
- **Returns:** a list of converted items aggregated across all pages (when pagination is auto-driven), never `null`; empty when the query matches nothing (or the client returns no response at all). A null response ends the result there: for the first page the list is empty, for a later page the list holds the rows of the pages before it and no further page is requested
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if queryRequest or targetClass is null, or a returned item cannot be converted to `targetClass`
  - `com.amazonaws.AmazonClientException` — if the SDK cannot send the query request or DynamoDB rejects it because of credentials, table/key data, conditions, or service limits
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if a returned attribute cannot be converted to the requested result type, or a result bean or container cannot be constructed or populated
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  QueryRequest request = new QueryRequest()
      .withTableName("Sales")
      .withKeyConditionExpression("#region = :region")
      .withExpressionAttributeNames(Map.of("#region", "region"))
      .withExpressionAttributeValues(Map.of(
          ":region", toAttributeValue("US-WEST")
      ));

  List<Sale> sales = executor.list(request, Sale.class);
  sales.forEach(System.out::println);   // Print each sale object
  ```
##### query(...) -> Dataset
- **Signature:** `public Dataset query(final QueryRequest queryRequest) throws IllegalArgumentException, AmazonClientException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Executes a DynamoDB query and returns results as a Dataset for tabular analysis.
- **Contract:**
  - Datasets are ideal for analytical operations, data manipulation, and when you need to work with query results in a spreadsheet-like format.
  - Dataset Benefits: Column-oriented operations Built-in aggregation functions Easy data export (CSV, JSON, etc.) SQL-like operations Usage Examples: Automatic pagination: When the caller has not set `exclusiveStartKey` on the request, all pages are fetched and concatenated into the returned Dataset.
  - If the caller did set `exclusiveStartKey`, only the single page returned by DynamoDB is materialized.
- **Parameters:**
  - `queryRequest` (`QueryRequest`) — the query parameters. Must not be `null`.
- **Returns:** a `Dataset` containing the query results materialized according to the pagination behavior above, never `null`; its columns are the attribute names of the returned items, so it is empty and has no columns when the query matches nothing, and also empty when no returned item has any attribute (for example a projection of attributes the items lack), because a Dataset without columns has no rows
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if queryRequest is null
  - `com.amazonaws.AmazonClientException` — if the SDK cannot send the query request or DynamoDB rejects it because of credentials, table/key data, conditions, or service limits
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if a returned attribute cannot be converted to the requested result type, or a result bean or container cannot be constructed or populated
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  QueryRequest request = new QueryRequest()
      .withTableName("Sales")
      .withKeyConditionExpression("#region = :region")
      .withExpressionAttributeNames(Map.of("#region", "region"))
      .withExpressionAttributeValues(Map.of(
          ":region", toAttributeValue("US-WEST")
      ));

  Dataset sales = executor.query(request);

  // Tabular operations (numbers are materialized as Strings). The columns are the attribute names of the
  // returned items: an item without "revenue" has a null cell, and no item with it means no such column.
  sales.println();   // Print as table
  double totalRevenue = !sales.containsColumn("revenue") ? 0.0
      : sales.<String>getColumn("revenue").stream()
          .filter(Objects::nonNull)
          .mapToDouble(Double::parseDouble)
          .sum();

  // Export to CSV
  sales.toCsv(new File("sales.csv"));
  ```
- **See also:** `#query(QueryRequest, Class)`
- **Signature:** `public Dataset query(final QueryRequest queryRequest, final Class<?> targetClass) throws IllegalArgumentException, AmazonClientException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Executes a DynamoDB query and returns results as a Dataset for the specified target class.
- **Contract:**
  - Note that, when the caller has not supplied an `exclusiveStartKey`, a `Limit` acts as a page size only and auto-pagination still fetches all matching rows.
- **Parameters:**
  - `queryRequest` (`QueryRequest`) — the query parameters. Must not be `null`.
  - `targetClass` (`Class<?>`) — the class to convert retrieved items to; if `null` or a `Map` type, each attribute becomes a column whose values are converted as by `#toMap(Map)` (for example, numbers are materialized as Strings). Otherwise it must be an entity class (a record or a builder-based bean included, see `#toEntity(Map, Class)`), whose properties become the columns: a Dataset cannot be built from object-array, collection, or single-value rows, so any other type is rejected before the query request is sent (use `#list(QueryRequest, Class)` for those)
- **Returns:** a `Dataset` containing query results in tabular format; all pages are materialized only when the request has no exclusive start key. When the query matches nothing the Dataset is empty and has no columns, for an entity class too. For a `null` or `Map` type it is empty also when no returned item has any attribute, because a Dataset without columns has no rows
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if queryRequest is null, if `targetClass` is not `null`, a `Map` type, or an entity class (checked before any request is sent, even if the query would match nothing), or if a returned item cannot be converted to `targetClass`
  - `com.amazonaws.AmazonClientException` — if the SDK cannot send the query request or DynamoDB rejects it because of credentials, table/key data, conditions, or service limits
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if a returned attribute cannot be converted to the requested result type, or a result bean or container cannot be constructed or populated
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  QueryRequest request = new QueryRequest()
      .withTableName("Sales")
      .withKeyConditionExpression("#region = :region")
      .withExpressionAttributeNames(Map.of("#region", "region"))
      .withExpressionAttributeValues(Map.of(
          ":region", toAttributeValue("US-WEST")
      ));

  Dataset sales = executor.query(request, Sale.class);
  sales.println();   // Print as table
  ```

- **Signature:** `public Stream<Map<String, Object>> stream(final QueryRequest queryRequest) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates a Stream of maps for DynamoDB query results with automatic pagination.
- **Parameters:**
  - `queryRequest` (`QueryRequest`) — the query parameters. Must not be `null`.
- **Returns:** a `Stream` of maps representing query results with automatic pagination; fetching or converting items can fail during stream traversal
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if queryRequest is null
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  QueryRequest request = new QueryRequest()
      .withTableName("Sales")
      .withKeyConditionExpression("#region = :region")
      .withExpressionAttributeNames(Map.of("#region", "region"))
      .withExpressionAttributeValues(Map.of(
          ":region", toAttributeValue("US-WEST")
      ));

  try (Stream<Map<String, Object>> stream = executor.stream(request)) {
      double totalRevenue = stream
          .filter(item -> "COMPLETED".equals(item.get("status")))
          .mapToDouble(item -> Double.parseDouble((String) item.get("revenue"))) // numbers are returned as Strings
          .sum();
      System.out.println("Total revenue: " + totalRevenue);
  }
  ```
- **See also:** `#stream(QueryRequest, Class)`
- **Signature:** `public <T> Stream<T> stream(final QueryRequest queryRequest, final Class<T> targetClass) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates a Stream of typed objects for DynamoDB query results with automatic pagination.
- **Contract:**
  - Unlike `#list(QueryRequest, Class)` and `#query(QueryRequest, Class)`, which return a single page when the request sets `exclusiveStartKey`, the stream only starts from that key and still continues to the last page; a `Limit` on the request is the page size, not a cap on the streamed rows (use `Stream.limit` for that).
- **Parameters:**
  - `queryRequest` (`QueryRequest`) — the query parameters. Must not be `null`.
  - `targetClass` (`Class<T>`) — the class to convert retrieved items to. Must not be `null`.
- **Returns:** a `Stream` of converted objects with automatic pagination; fetching or converting items can fail during stream traversal
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if queryRequest is null, or if targetClass is null
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  QueryRequest request = new QueryRequest()
      .withTableName("Users")
      .withKeyConditionExpression("#status = :status")
      .withExpressionAttributeNames(Map.of("#status", "status"))
      .withExpressionAttributeValues(Map.of(
          ":status", toAttributeValue("ACTIVE")
      ));

  try (Stream<User> userStream = executor.stream(request, User.class)) {
      List<String> adminEmails = userStream
          .filter(user -> "ADMIN".equals(user.getRole()))
          .map(User::getEmail)
          .collect(Collectors.toList());
  }
  ```

  - `scanRequest` (`ScanRequest`) — the complete scan request with all parameters. Must not be `null`.
  - `targetClass` (`Class<T>`) — the class to convert retrieved items to. Must not be `null`.
- **Returns:** a `Stream` of converted objects with automatic pagination; fetching or converting items can fail during stream traversal
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if scanRequest or targetClass is null
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  ScanRequest request = new ScanRequest()
      .withTableName("Products")
      .withFilterExpression("price BETWEEN :low AND :high")
      .withExpressionAttributeValues(Map.of(
          ":low", toAttributeValue(100),
          ":high", toAttributeValue(500)
      ))
      .withProjectionExpression("productId, #name, category, price")   // category is needed by groupingBy below
      .withExpressionAttributeNames(Map.of("#name", "name"))
      .withLimit(50);   // Page size

  try (Stream<Product> products = executor.scan(request, Product.class)) {
      Map<String, Double> avgPriceByCategory = products
          .collect(Collectors.groupingBy(
              Product::getCategory,
              Collectors.averagingDouble(Product::getPrice)
          ));
  }
  ```
- **See also:** `#scan(ScanRequest)`
##### close(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `public void close()`
- **Summary:** Closes the underlying DynamoDB client and releases its network resources.
- **Contract:**
  - Call this method when this executor — and the `AmazonDynamoDBClient` passed into its constructor — is no longer needed so that HTTP connections, idle thread pools, and socket resources held by the SDK can be released.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Explicit close
  DynamoDBExecutor executor = new DynamoDBExecutor(dynamoDBClient);
  try {
      executor.putItem("Users", DynamoDBExecutor.asItem("id", "1"));
  } finally {
      executor.close();   // shuts down the underlying AmazonDynamoDBClient
  }
  ```

### Class Mapper (com.landawn.abacus.da.aws.dynamodb.DynamoDBExecutor.Mapper)
Type-safe wrapper that binds a specific entity class, table name, and `NamingPolicy` together to provide a simplified, strongly typed API over the surrounding `DynamoDBExecutor`.

**Thread-safety:** thread-safe
**Nullability:** unspecified

- (none)

##### batchDeleteItem(...) -> BatchWriteItemResult
- **Signature:** `public BatchWriteItemResult batchDeleteItem(final Collection<? extends T> entities) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException, AmazonServiceException, AmazonClientException`
- **Summary:** Deletes multiple items from DynamoDB in a single batch operation for improved performance.
- **Contract:**
  - This is significantly more efficient than individual delete operations when you need to remove multiple items.
  - Batch Delete Limitations: Maximum 25 items per batch request Maximum 16 MB total request size Cannot use conditional expressions Unprocessed items: When DynamoDB cannot perform every requested delete (typically due to provisioned throughput throttling or item-size limits) the remaining `WriteRequest`s are returned via `BatchWriteItemResult.getUnprocessedItems()`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `entities` (`Collection<? extends T>`) — collection of entities containing the key values for deletion, must not be `null`
- **Returns:** the BatchWriteItemResult containing operation metadata and any unprocessed items
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `entities` or an element is null, or an entity ID is null, empty, or not a supported scalar key value (a non-finite number or a Boolean included)
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if an entity property accessor or value converter fails while constructing the request
  - `com.amazonaws.AmazonServiceException` — if the request exceeds the 25-item batch limit
  - `com.amazonaws.AmazonClientException` — if the SDK cannot send the batchWriteItem request or DynamoDB rejects it because of credentials, table/key data, conditions, or service limits
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  User user1 = new User();
  user1.setId("123");
  User user2 = new User();
  user2.setId("456");
  User user3 = new User();
  user3.setId("789");

  List<User> users = Arrays.asList(user1, user2, user3);
  BatchWriteItemResult result = mapper.batchDeleteItem(users);

  // Check for unprocessed items
  if (!result.getUnprocessedItems().isEmpty()) {
      System.out.println("Some items were not deleted and need retry");
  }
  ```

- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the request specifies a different table than configured, or if queryRequest is `null`
  - `com.amazonaws.AmazonClientException` — if the SDK cannot send the query request or DynamoDB rejects it because of credentials, table/key data, conditions, or service limits
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if a returned attribute cannot be converted to the requested result type, or a result bean or container cannot be constructed or populated
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  QueryRequest request = new QueryRequest()
      .withKeyConditionExpression("userId = :id")
      .withFilterExpression("age > :minAge")
      // one map for ALL bindings: a second withExpressionAttributeValues call would REPLACE the first
      .withExpressionAttributeValues(Map.of(
          ":id", new AttributeValue().withS("123"),
          ":minAge", new AttributeValue().withN("18")
      ));

  List<User> results = mapper.list(request);
  System.out.println("Found " + results.size() + " users");
  results.forEach(user -> System.out.println(user.getName()));
  ```
- **See also:** `#stream(QueryRequest)`
##### query(...) -> Dataset
- **Signature:** `public Dataset query(final QueryRequest queryRequest) throws IllegalArgumentException, AmazonClientException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Executes a query operation and returns the results as a Dataset for tabular analysis.
- **Contract:**
  - Datasets are ideal for analytical operations, aggregations, and when you need to work with query results in a structured, spreadsheet-like format.
  - If no table name is specified in the request, the mapper's configured table name is used.
- **Parameters:**
  - `queryRequest` (`QueryRequest`) — the QueryRequest containing query parameters, must not be `null`
- **Returns:** Dataset containing the query results with tabular structure, never `null`; its columns are the entity properties, except that a query matching nothing returns an empty Dataset without any columns
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the request specifies a different table than configured, or if queryRequest is `null`
  - `com.amazonaws.AmazonClientException` — if the SDK cannot send the query request or DynamoDB rejects it because of credentials, table/key data, conditions, or service limits
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if a returned attribute cannot be converted to the requested result type, or a result bean or container cannot be constructed or populated
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  QueryRequest request = new QueryRequest()
      .withKeyConditionExpression("userId = :id")
      .withExpressionAttributeValues(Map.of(
          ":id", new AttributeValue().withS("123")
      ));

  Dataset results = mapper.query(request);

  // Print tabular view
  results.println();

  // Perform aggregations over a numeric column (a result without items has no columns at all)
  double avgAge = results.isEmpty() ? 0.0
      : results.<Number>getColumn("age").stream()
          .filter(Objects::nonNull)   // an item without an "age" attribute leaves a null cell
          .mapToDouble(Number::doubleValue)
          .average()
          .orElse(0.0);
  System.out.println("Average age: " + avgAge);
  ```
- **See also:** `#list(QueryRequest)`, `#stream(QueryRequest)`
##### stream(...) -> Stream<T>
- **Signature:** `public Stream<T> stream(final QueryRequest queryRequest) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Executes a query operation and returns the results as a Stream for memory-efficient processing.
- **Contract:**
  - If no table name is specified in the request, the mapper's configured table name is used.
  - Important: Streams should be closed after use to release resources.
- **Parameters:**
  - `queryRequest` (`QueryRequest`) — the QueryRequest containing query parameters, must not be `null`
- **Returns:** Stream of entities matching the query conditions with lazy evaluation and automatic pagination; fetching or converting items can fail during stream traversal
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the request specifies a different table than configured, or if queryRequest is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  QueryRequest request = new QueryRequest()
      .withKeyConditionExpression("userId = :id")
      .withExpressionAttributeValues(Map.of(
          ":id", new AttributeValue().withS("123")
      ));

  try (Stream<User> stream = mapper.stream(request)) {
      // Find first active user (a Stream allows only ONE terminal operation)
      Optional<User> firstActive = stream
          .filter(u -> u.isActive())
          .findFirst();
  }

  // Counting matching items needs its own stream:
  try (Stream<User> stream = mapper.stream(request)) {
      long count = stream.filter(u -> u.getAge() > 18).count();
  }
  ```
- **See also:** `#list(QueryRequest)`
##### scan(...) -> Stream<T>
- **Signature:** `public Stream<T> scan(final List<String> attributesToGet)`
- **Summary:** Performs a full table scan with projection to retrieve only specified attributes.
- **Contract:**
  - Consider using Query operations with indexes instead of Scan when possible.
- **Parameters:**
  - `attributesToGet` (`List<String>`) — list of attribute names to retrieve; `null` or empty retrieves all attributes
- **Returns:** Stream of all entities in the table with specified attributes, providing lazy evaluation; fetching or converting items can fail during stream traversal
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<String> attrs = Arrays.asList("id", "name", "email");
  try (Stream<User> stream = mapper.scan(attrs)) {
      stream.limit(100)  // Process only first 100 items
          .forEach(System.out::println);
  }
  ```
- **See also:** `#scan(ScanRequest)`
- **Signature:** `public Stream<T> scan(final Map<String, Condition> scanFilter)`
- **Summary:** Performs a table scan with filter conditions applied to results.
- **Parameters:**
  - `scanFilter` (`Map<String, Condition>`) — map of attribute names to `Condition` objects for filtering results, or `null` to apply no filter (scans all items)
- **Returns:** Stream of entities matching the filter conditions; fetching or converting items can fail during stream traversal
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, Condition> filter = new HashMap<>();
  filter.put("age", new Condition()
      .withComparisonOperator(ComparisonOperator.GT)
      .withAttributeValueList(new AttributeValue().withN("18")));

  try (Stream<User> stream = mapper.scan(filter)) {
      stream.forEach(System.out::println);
  }
  ```
- **See also:** `#scan(ScanRequest)`
- **Signature:** `public Stream<T> scan(final List<String> attributesToGet, final Map<String, Condition> scanFilter)`
- **Summary:** Performs a table scan with both attribute projection and filter conditions.
- **Parameters:**
  - `attributesToGet` (`List<String>`) — list of attribute names to retrieve; `null` or empty retrieves all attributes
  - `scanFilter` (`Map<String, Condition>`) — map of attribute names to `Condition` objects for filtering results, or `null` to apply no filter (scans all items)
- **Returns:** Stream of entities with specified attributes matching the filter conditions; fetching or converting items can fail during stream traversal
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<String> attrs = Arrays.asList("id", "name", "email");

  Map<String, Condition> filter = new HashMap<>();
  filter.put("status", new Condition()
      .withComparisonOperator(ComparisonOperator.EQ)
      .withAttributeValueList(new AttributeValue("active")));

  try (Stream<User> stream = mapper.scan(attrs, filter)) {
      stream.limit(50)  // Process first 50 matching items
          .forEach(System.out::println);
  }
  ```
- **See also:** `#scan(ScanRequest)`
- **Signature:** `public Stream<T> scan(final ScanRequest scanRequest) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Performs a table scan using a custom ScanRequest for maximum control.
- **Contract:**
  - If no table name is specified in the request, the mapper's configured table name is used.
- **Parameters:**
  - `scanRequest` (`ScanRequest`) — the ScanRequest containing scan parameters, must not be `null`
- **Returns:** Stream of entities matching the scan parameters with lazy evaluation and automatic pagination; fetching or converting items can fail during stream traversal
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the request specifies a different table than configured, or if scanRequest is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  ScanRequest request = new ScanRequest()
      .withLimit(100)
      .withFilterExpression("age > :min AND #status = :active")
      .withExpressionAttributeNames(Map.of("#status", "status", "#name", "name"))
      .withExpressionAttributeValues(Map.of(
          ":min", new AttributeValue().withN("18"),
          ":active", new AttributeValue("ACTIVE")
      ))
      .withProjectionExpression("id, #name, email")
      .withReturnConsumedCapacity(ReturnConsumedCapacity.TOTAL);

  try (Stream<User> stream = mapper.scan(request)) {
      stream.forEach(System.out::println);
  }
  ```
- **See also:** `#scan(List, Map)`

### Class ConditionBuilder (com.landawn.abacus.da.aws.dynamodb.DynamoDBExecutor.ConditionBuilder)
Fluent builder that accumulates per-attribute `Condition`s into a single `Map<String, Condition>` suitable for v1 `ScanRequest.withScanFilter(...)` or `QueryRequest.withQueryFilter(...)`.

**Thread-safety:** not thread-safe
**Nullability:** unspecified

- (none)

- **Summary:** Creates a new ConditionBuilder instance.
- **Deprecated:** yes — Use `Filters#builder()` instead.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** a new ConditionBuilder instance
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, Condition> filters = ConditionBuilder.create().eq("status", "ACTIVE").build();
  ```

#### Public Instance Methods
##### eq(...) -> ConditionBuilder
- **Signature:** `public ConditionBuilder eq(final String attrName, final Object attrValue) throws NullPointerException, IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Adds an equality condition for the specified attribute.
- **Parameters:**
  - `attrName` (`String`) — the name of the attribute to compare
  - `attrValue` (`Object`) — the value to compare against
- **Returns:** this builder for method chaining
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if `#build()` has already detached this builder's condition map
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `attrName` is null or empty, or a condition value is a floating-point NaN or infinity
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if a value converter or an entity property accessor fails while encoding an attribute value
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, Condition> filter = Filters.builder().eq("status", "active").build();
  // filter.get("status") -> Condition with EQ operator and one value "active"

  // Chains with other conditions; returns the same builder for fluent use.
  ConditionBuilder b = Filters.builder().eq("status", "active").gt("age", 18);
  ```
##### ne(...) -> ConditionBuilder

- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, Condition> filter = Filters.builder().ne("status", "deleted").build();

  Map<String, Condition> f = Filters.builder().eq("x", 1).ne("x", 2).build();
  ```
