##### batchWriteItem(...) -> BatchWriteItemResponse
- **Signature:** `public BatchWriteItemResponse batchWriteItem(final Map<String, List<WriteRequest>> requestItems) throws DynamoDbException, SdkException`
- **Summary:** Performs batch write operations (puts and deletes) across multiple tables.
- **Parameters:**
  - `requestItems` (`Map<String, List<WriteRequest>>`) — map of table names to lists of write requests (puts/deletes). Must not be null.
- **Returns:** a `BatchWriteItemResponse` containing any unprocessed items (consumed capacity is not requested by this overload)
- **Throws:**
  - `software.amazon.awssdk.services.dynamodb.model.DynamoDbException` — if DynamoDB rejects the request (a null `requestItems` or a batch exceeding DynamoDB's limits fails with a service `ValidationException`)
  - `software.amazon.awssdk.core.exception.SdkException` — if the SDK cannot send the batchWriteItem request or DynamoDB rejects it because of credentials, table/key data, conditions, or service limits
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<WriteRequest> userWrites = Arrays.asList(
      WriteRequest.builder()
          .putRequest(PutRequest.builder()
              .item(asItem("userId", "user1", "name", "Alice"))
              .build())
          .build(),
      WriteRequest.builder()
          .putRequest(PutRequest.builder()
              .item(asItem("userId", "user2", "name", "Bob"))
              .build())
          .build(),
      WriteRequest.builder()
          .deleteRequest(DeleteRequest.builder()
              .key(asKey("userId", "user3"))
              .build())
          .build()
  );

  Map<String, List<WriteRequest>> requestItems = Map.of("Users", userWrites);

  BatchWriteItemResponse result = executor.batchWriteItem(requestItems);
  if (!result.unprocessedItems().isEmpty()) {
      // Retry unprocessed items
      executor.batchWriteItem(result.unprocessedItems());
  }
  ```
- **See also:** `#batchWriteItem(BatchWriteItemRequest)`

- **Signature:** `public UpdateItemResponse updateItem(final String tableName, final Map<String, AttributeValue> key, final Map<String, AttributeValueUpdate> attributeUpdates) throws DynamoDbException, SdkException`
- **Summary:** Updates specific attributes of an existing item in DynamoDB.
- **Parameters:**
  - `tableName` (`String`) — the name of the DynamoDB table. Must not be null or empty.
  - `key` (`Map<String, AttributeValue>`) — the primary key identifying the item to update. Must not be null.
  - `attributeUpdates` (`Map<String, AttributeValueUpdate>`) — map of attribute names to update actions. A `null` or empty map is not rejected: the request then updates nothing, and DynamoDB creates an item holding only the key attributes when none exists
- **Returns:** an `UpdateItemResponse` containing operation metadata

  - `software.amazon.awssdk.services.dynamodb.model.DynamoDbException` — if DynamoDB rejects the request (a null/empty `tableName` or a null `key` fails service-side validation)

  ```java
  Map<String, AttributeValue> key = asKey("userId", "user123");
  ```

- **Signature:** `public UpdateItemResponse updateItem(final UpdateItemRequest updateItemRequest) throws IllegalArgumentException, SdkException`

- **Returns:** an `UpdateItemResponse` containing operation results

  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `updateItemRequest` is null

##### list(...) -> varies by overload
- **Signature:** `public List<Map<String, Object>> list(final QueryRequest queryRequest) throws IllegalArgumentException, SdkException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Lists items from the specified DynamoDB table using a QueryRequest.
- **Contract:**
  - When the caller has not set `exclusiveStartKey` on the request, all pages are fetched and concatenated; if the caller did set `exclusiveStartKey`, only the single page returned by DynamoDB is materialized.
- **Parameters:**
  - `queryRequest` (`QueryRequest`) — the QueryRequest containing the table name and query parameters. Must not be null.
- **Returns:** a list of maps representing the items retrieved by the query. Never null.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if queryRequest is null
  - `software.amazon.awssdk.core.exception.SdkException` — if the SDK cannot send the list request or DynamoDB rejects it because of credentials, table/key data, conditions, or service limits
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if a returned attribute cannot be converted to the requested result type, or a result bean or container cannot be constructed or populated
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  QueryRequest queryRequest = QueryRequest.builder()
      .tableName("Users")
      .keyConditionExpression("userId = :v1")
      .expressionAttributeValues(Map.of(":v1", AttributeValue.builder().s("user123").build()))
      .build();
  List<Map<String, Object>> results = executor.list(queryRequest);
  ```
- **Signature:** `public <T> List<T> list(final QueryRequest queryRequest, final Class<T> targetClass) throws IllegalArgumentException, SdkException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Lists items from the specified DynamoDB table using a QueryRequest and converts the results to entities of the specified type.
- **Contract:**
  - If the query result is paginated and no exclusive start key was set on the request, this method automatically fetches and aggregates all remaining pages.
  - When the caller has already set `exclusiveStartKey`, only the single returned page is materialized.
- **Parameters:**
  - `queryRequest` (`QueryRequest`) — the QueryRequest containing the table name and query parameters. Must not be null.
  - `targetClass` (`Class<T>`) — the class of the entities to convert to. Must not be null.
- **Returns:** a list of entities aggregated across all pages (when pagination is auto-driven), never `null`; empty when the query matches nothing (or the client returns no response at all). A null response ends the result there: for the first page the list is empty, for a later page the list holds the rows of the pages before it and no further page is requested
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `queryRequest` or `targetClass` is null, or a returned item cannot be converted to `targetClass`
  - `software.amazon.awssdk.core.exception.SdkException` — if the SDK cannot send the list request or DynamoDB rejects it because of credentials, table/key data, conditions, or service limits
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if a returned attribute cannot be converted to the requested result type, or a result bean or container cannot be constructed or populated
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  QueryRequest queryRequest = QueryRequest.builder()
      .tableName("Users")
      .keyConditionExpression("userId = :v1")
      .expressionAttributeValues(Map.of(":v1", AttributeValue.builder().s("user123").build()))
      .build();
  List<User> results = executor.list(queryRequest, User.class);
  ```
##### query(...) -> Dataset
- **Signature:** `public Dataset query(final QueryRequest queryRequest) throws IllegalArgumentException, SdkException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Queries items from the specified DynamoDB table using a QueryRequest and returns the results as a Dataset.
- **Contract:**
  - Automatic pagination: When the caller has not set `exclusiveStartKey` on the request, all pages are fetched and concatenated into the returned Dataset.
  - If the caller did set `exclusiveStartKey`, only the single page returned by DynamoDB is materialized.
- **Parameters:**
  - `queryRequest` (`QueryRequest`) — the QueryRequest containing the table name and query parameters. Must not be null.
- **Returns:** a Dataset containing the items retrieved by the query, never `null`; empty when the query matches nothing, and also when no returned item has any attribute (for example a projection of attributes the items lack), because a Dataset without columns has no rows
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if queryRequest is null
  - `software.amazon.awssdk.core.exception.SdkException` — if the SDK cannot send the query request or DynamoDB rejects it because of credentials, table/key data, conditions, or service limits
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if a returned attribute cannot be converted to the requested result type, or a result bean or container cannot be constructed or populated
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  QueryRequest queryRequest = QueryRequest.builder()
      .tableName("Users")
      .keyConditionExpression("userId = :v1")
      .expressionAttributeValues(Map.of(":v1", AttributeValue.builder().s("user123").build()))
      .build();
  Dataset results = executor.query(queryRequest);
  ```
- **Signature:** `public Dataset query(final QueryRequest queryRequest, final Class<?> targetClass) throws IllegalArgumentException, SdkException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Queries items from the specified DynamoDB table using a QueryRequest and converts the results to a Dataset.
- **Contract:**
  - If `targetClass` is a `Map` type, the Dataset is built directly from the raw item attributes.
  - If the query result is paginated and no exclusive start key was set on the request, this method automatically fetches and aggregates all remaining pages.
- **Parameters:**
  - `queryRequest` (`QueryRequest`) — the QueryRequest containing the table name and query parameters. Must not be null.
  - `targetClass` (`Class<?>`) — the row type to convert each item to; must not be null. Pass a `Map` subtype (e.g. `Map.class`) to keep rows as raw attribute maps instead of mapped entities. Any other type must be a bean class, whose properties become the columns: an array, collection or single-value type is rejected before the query request is sent, because such rows have no column names (use `#list(QueryRequest, Class)` for them).
- **Returns:** a Dataset built from the query results. Never null. When the query matches nothing the Dataset is empty and has no columns, for a bean class too (its properties become the columns only of a non-empty result). For a `Map` type it is empty also when no returned item has any attribute, because a Dataset without columns has no rows.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `queryRequest` or `targetClass` is null, `targetClass` is neither a `Map` type nor a bean class (checked before any request is sent, even if the query would match nothing), or a returned item cannot be converted to `targetClass`
  - `software.amazon.awssdk.core.exception.SdkException` — if the SDK cannot send the query request or DynamoDB rejects it because of credentials, table/key data, conditions, or service limits
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if a returned attribute cannot be converted to the requested result type, or a result bean or container cannot be constructed or populated
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  QueryRequest queryRequest = QueryRequest.builder()
      .tableName("Users")
      .keyConditionExpression("userId = :v1")
      .expressionAttributeValues(Map.of(":v1", AttributeValue.builder().s("user123").build()))
      .build();
  Dataset results = executor.query(queryRequest, User.class);
  ```

- **Signature:** `public <T> Stream<T> stream(final QueryRequest queryRequest, final Class<T> targetClass) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Streams items from the specified DynamoDB table using a QueryRequest and converts the results to entities of the specified type.
- **Contract:**
  - Unlike `#list(QueryRequest, Class)` and `#query(QueryRequest, Class)`, which return a single page when the request sets `exclusiveStartKey`, the stream only starts from that key and still continues to the last page; a `limit` on the request is the page size, not a cap on the streamed rows (use `Stream.limit` for that).
- **Parameters:**
  - `queryRequest` (`QueryRequest`) — the QueryRequest containing the table name and query parameters. Must not be null.
  - `targetClass` (`Class<T>`) — the class of the entities to convert to. Must not be null.
- **Returns:** a lazy stream of entities that auto-paginates via `lastEvaluatedKey`. Never null; fetching or converting items can fail during stream traversal
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if queryRequest or targetClass is null
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  QueryRequest queryRequest = QueryRequest.builder()
      .tableName("Users")
      .keyConditionExpression("userId = :v1")
      .expressionAttributeValues(Map.of(":v1", AttributeValue.builder().s("user123").build()))
      .build();
  Stream<User> results = executor.stream(queryRequest, User.class);
  results.forEach(System.out::println);
  ```

##### close(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `public void close()`
- **Summary:** Closes this DynamoDB executor and releases all associated resources using AWS SDK v2.
- **Contract:**
  - Best Practices: Always call close() when finished with the executor Call close() from a finally block for guaranteed cleanup Ensure all operations complete before closing Don't share closed executors between threads Usage Examples:
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  DynamoDbClient client = DynamoDbClient.builder()
      .region(Region.US_EAST_1)
      .build();

  DynamoDBExecutor executor = new DynamoDBExecutor(client);
  try {
      Map<String, Object> item = executor.getItem(tableName, key);
  } finally {
      executor.close();   // Ensure cleanup
  }
  ```
- **See also:** `DynamoDbClient#close()`

##### getItem(...) -> T
- **Signature:** `public T getItem(final T entity) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException, SdkException`
- **Summary:** Retrieves an item from DynamoDB using the key values extracted from the provided entity.
- **Contract:**
  - The entity parameter should have its key fields populated.
- **Parameters:**
  - `entity` (`T`) — an entity instance with populated key fields
- **Returns:** the retrieved entity with all attributes populated, or null if not found
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `entity` is null or an ID is null, empty, or not a supported scalar key value
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if an entity property accessor or value converter fails while constructing the request or mapping a returned item
  - `software.amazon.awssdk.core.exception.SdkException` — if the SDK cannot send the getItem request or DynamoDB rejects it because of credentials, table/key data, conditions, or service limits
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  User keyEntity = new User();
  keyEntity.setUserId("12345");
  User fullUser = userMapper.getItem(keyEntity);
  ```
- **Signature:** `public T getItem(final T entity, final Boolean consistentRead) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException, SdkException`
- **Summary:** Retrieves an item from DynamoDB with optional consistent read guarantee.
- **Contract:**
  - When consistentRead is true, DynamoDB returns the most recent data reflecting all writes that received a successful response prior to the read.
- **Parameters:**
  - `entity` (`T`) — an entity instance with populated key fields
  - `consistentRead` (`Boolean`) — true for strongly consistent read, `false` for eventually consistent, null to use default
- **Returns:** the retrieved entity with all attributes populated, or null if not found
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `entity` is null or an ID is null, empty, or not a supported scalar key value
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if an entity property accessor or value converter fails while constructing the request or mapping a returned item
  - `software.amazon.awssdk.core.exception.SdkException` — if the SDK cannot send the getItem request or DynamoDB rejects it because of credentials, table/key data, conditions, or service limits
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  User keyEntity = new User();
  keyEntity.setUserId("12345");
  User user = userMapper.getItem(keyEntity, true);   // Consistent read
  ```

  - `software.amazon.awssdk.core.exception.SdkException` — if the SDK cannot send the batchDeleteItem request or DynamoDB rejects it because of credentials, table/key data, conditions, or service limits
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<User> usersToDelete = Arrays.asList(
      new User("12345"),
      new User("67890"),
      new User("11111")
  );
  BatchWriteItemResponse response = userMapper.batchDeleteItem(usersToDelete);
  ```
##### batchWriteItem(...) -> BatchWriteItemResponse
- **Signature:** `public BatchWriteItemResponse batchWriteItem(final BatchWriteItemRequest batchWriteItemRequest) throws IllegalArgumentException, SdkException`
- **Summary:** Performs a batch write operation using a fully configured BatchWriteItemRequest.
- **Parameters:**
  - `batchWriteItemRequest` (`BatchWriteItemRequest`) — the fully configured batch request
- **Returns:** the response containing information about unprocessed items if any
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `batchWriteItemRequest` is null or specifies a different table than this mapper's table
  - `software.amazon.awssdk.core.exception.SdkException` — if the SDK cannot send the batchWriteItem request or DynamoDB rejects it because of credentials, table/key data, conditions, or service limits
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, List<WriteRequest>> requestItems = new HashMap<>();
  requestItems.put(tableName, Arrays.asList(
      WriteRequest.builder().putRequest(PutRequest.builder().item(item1).build()).build(),
      WriteRequest.builder().deleteRequest(DeleteRequest.builder().key(key2).build()).build()
  ));
  BatchWriteItemRequest request = BatchWriteItemRequest.builder()
      .requestItems(requestItems)
      .build();
  BatchWriteItemResponse response = userMapper.batchWriteItem(request);
  ```
##### list(...) -> List<T>
- **Signature:** `public List<T> list(final QueryRequest queryRequest) throws IllegalArgumentException, SdkException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Executes a query and returns the results as a list of entities.
- **Contract:**
  - When the request has no `exclusiveStartKey`, all pages are loaded into memory; a request that sets one materializes only the single page DynamoDB returns (see `DynamoDBExecutor#list(QueryRequest, Class)`).
  - If the request names no table, this mapper's table is used.
- **Parameters:**
  - `queryRequest` (`QueryRequest`) — the query request with key conditions and other parameters
- **Returns:** a list of entities matching the query; empty list if no matches found
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `queryRequest` is null or specifies a different table than this mapper's table
  - `software.amazon.awssdk.core.exception.SdkException` — if the SDK cannot send the list request or DynamoDB rejects it because of credentials, table/key data, conditions, or service limits
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if a returned attribute cannot be converted to the requested result type, or a result bean or container cannot be constructed or populated
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  QueryRequest request = QueryRequest.builder()
      .keyConditionExpression("userId = :userId")
      .expressionAttributeValues(Map.of(":userId", AttributeValue.builder().s("12345").build()))
      .build();
  List<User> users = userMapper.list(request);
  ```
##### query(...) -> Dataset
- **Signature:** `public Dataset query(final QueryRequest queryRequest) throws IllegalArgumentException, SdkException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Executes a query and returns the results as a Dataset.
- **Contract:**
  - Pages are materialized as by `#list(QueryRequest)`: all of them when the request has no `exclusiveStartKey`, otherwise only the single returned page.
  - If the request names no table, this mapper's table is used.
- **Parameters:**
  - `queryRequest` (`QueryRequest`) — the query request with key conditions and other parameters
- **Returns:** a Dataset containing the query results, never `null`; its columns are the entity properties, except that a query matching nothing returns an empty Dataset without any columns
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `queryRequest` is null or specifies a different table than this mapper's table
  - `software.amazon.awssdk.core.exception.SdkException` — if the SDK cannot send the query request or DynamoDB rejects it because of credentials, table/key data, conditions, or service limits
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if a returned attribute cannot be converted to the requested result type, or a result bean or container cannot be constructed or populated
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  QueryRequest request = QueryRequest.builder()
      .keyConditionExpression("userId = :userId")
      .expressionAttributeValues(Map.of(":userId", AttributeValue.builder().s("12345").build()))
      .build();
  Dataset dataset = userMapper.query(request);
  // Use Dataset methods for further processing
  ```
##### stream(...) -> Stream<T>
- **Signature:** `public Stream<T> stream(final QueryRequest queryRequest) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Executes a query and returns the results as a Stream of entities.
- **Contract:**
  - The stream will automatically handle pagination, fetching additional pages as needed when elements are consumed from the stream.
  - If the request names no table, this mapper's table is used.
- **Parameters:**
  - `queryRequest` (`QueryRequest`) — the query request with key conditions and other parameters
- **Returns:** a Stream of entities; the stream should be closed after use; fetching or converting items can fail during stream traversal
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `queryRequest` is null or specifies a different table than this mapper's table
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  QueryRequest request = QueryRequest.builder()
      .keyConditionExpression("userId = :userId")
      .expressionAttributeValues(Map.of(":userId", AttributeValue.builder().s("12345").build()))
      .build();
  userMapper.stream(request)
      .filter(user -> user.getAge() > 18)
      .forEach(user -> System.out.println(user.getName()));
  ```
##### scan(...) -> Stream<T>
- **Signature:** `public Stream<T> scan(final List<String> attributesToGet)`
- **Summary:** Performs a table scan with optional attribute projection.
- **Parameters:**
  - `attributesToGet` (`List<String>`) — list of attribute names to retrieve; null or empty to get all attributes
- **Returns:** a Stream of entities from the scan operation; fetching or converting items can fail during stream traversal
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<String> attributes = Arrays.asList("userId", "userName", "email");
  Stream<User> users = userMapper.scan(attributes);
  users.forEach(user -> System.out.println(user.getUserName()));
  ```
- **Signature:** `public Stream<T> scan(final Map<String, Condition> scanFilter)`
- **Summary:** Performs a filtered table scan.
- **Parameters:**
  - `scanFilter` (`Map<String, Condition>`) — map of attribute names to conditions for filtering results, or null for no filter
- **Returns:** a Stream of entities matching the filter conditions; fetching or converting items can fail during stream traversal
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, Condition> filter = Filters.gt("age", 18);
  Stream<User> adults = userMapper.scan(filter);
  adults.forEach(System.out::println);
  ```
- **Signature:** `public Stream<T> scan(final List<String> attributesToGet, final Map<String, Condition> scanFilter)`
- **Summary:** Performs a filtered table scan with attribute projection.
- **Parameters:**
  - `attributesToGet` (`List<String>`) — list of attribute names to retrieve; null or empty to get all attributes
  - `scanFilter` (`Map<String, Condition>`) — map of attribute names to conditions for filtering results, or null for no filter
- **Returns:** a Stream of entities matching the filter with only specified attributes; fetching or converting items can fail during stream traversal
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<String> attributes = Arrays.asList("userId", "userName");
  Map<String, Condition> filter = Filters.eq("status", "ACTIVE");
  Stream<User> activeUsers = userMapper.scan(attributes, filter);
  activeUsers.forEach(System.out::println);
  ```
- **Signature:** `public Stream<T> scan(final ScanRequest scanRequest) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Performs a scan using a fully configured ScanRequest.
- **Contract:**
  - If the table name is not specified in the request, it will be automatically set to this mapper's table.
- **Parameters:**
  - `scanRequest` (`ScanRequest`) — the fully configured scan request
- **Returns:** a Stream of entities from the scan operation; fetching or converting items can fail during stream traversal
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `scanRequest` is null or specifies a different table than this mapper's table
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  ScanRequest request = ScanRequest.builder()
      .filterExpression("age > :minAge")
      .expressionAttributeValues(Map.of(":minAge", AttributeValue.builder().n("18").build()))
      .projectionExpression("userId, userName, age")
      .build();
  Stream<User> users = userMapper.scan(request);
  users.forEach(System.out::println);
  ```

### Class ConditionBuilder (com.landawn.abacus.da.aws.dynamodb.v2.DynamoDBExecutor.ConditionBuilder)
A builder class for constructing complex DynamoDB filter conditions using a fluent API.

**Since:** 1.0
**Thread-safety:** not thread-safe
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Public Constructors
- (none)

#### Public Static Methods
##### create(...) -> ConditionBuilder
- **Signature:** `@Deprecated public static ConditionBuilder create()`
- **Summary:** Creates a new ConditionBuilder instance.
- **Deprecated:** yes — Use `Filters#builder()` instead.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** a new ConditionBuilder instance
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, Condition> cond = ConditionBuilder.create()
      .eq("status", "active")
      .gt("age", 18)
      .build();                                  // 2 conditions: EQ status, GT age

  // Prefer Filters.builder() (this factory is deprecated)
  Map<String, Condition> same = Filters.builder().eq("status", "active").build();

  // build() empties the builder; a second build() returns null
  ConditionBuilder b = ConditionBuilder.create().eq("x", 1);
  Map<String, Condition> first = b.build();      // non-null, size 1
  Map<String, Condition> second = b.build();     // returns null
  ```

## com.landawn.abacus.da.azure
### Class CosmosContainerExecutor (com.landawn.abacus.da.azure.CosmosContainerExecutor)
Comprehensive executor for Azure Cosmos DB container operations providing a high-level, simplified interface for document database operations with built-in query building capabilities.

**Thread-safety:** thread-safe
**Nullability:** unspecified
**Annotations:** @Beta

#### Public Constructors
- `public CosmosContainerExecutor(final CosmosContainer cosmosContainer) throws IllegalArgumentException` — Constructs a new CosmosContainerExecutor with the default naming policy.
  - **Throws:**
    - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `cosmosContainer` is null
  ```java
  CosmosContainer container = client.getDatabase("ecommerce").getContainer("products");

  // Typical: wrap a container; the wrapped instance is exposed via cosmosContainer()
  CosmosContainerExecutor executor = new CosmosContainerExecutor(container);
  executor.cosmosContainer(); // returns the same 'container' instance (==)

  // Edge: null container is rejected eagerly
  new CosmosContainerExecutor((CosmosContainer) null); // throws IllegalArgumentException: "cosmosContainer cannot be null"
  ```
- `public CosmosContainerExecutor(final CosmosContainer cosmosContainer, final NamingPolicy namingPolicy) throws IllegalArgumentException` — Constructs a new CosmosContainerExecutor with the specified naming policy.
  - **Throws:**
    - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `cosmosContainer` or `namingPolicy` is null, or if `namingPolicy` is not one of the three supported policies
  ```java
  CosmosContainer container = client.getDatabase("ecommerce").getContainer("products");

  // Typical: SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE renders e.g. firstName -> FIRST_NAME in generated SQL
  CosmosContainerExecutor executor =
      new CosmosContainerExecutor(container, NamingPolicy.SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE);
  executor.cosmosContainer(); // returns the same 'container' instance (==)

  // Typical: CAMEL_CASE keeps property names as-is in generated SQL
  new CosmosContainerExecutor(container, NamingPolicy.CAMEL_CASE);

  // Edge: null container is rejected
  new CosmosContainerExecutor(null, NamingPolicy.SNAKE_CASE); // throws IllegalArgumentException: "cosmosContainer cannot be null"

  // Edge: null naming policy is rejected
  new CosmosContainerExecutor(container, (NamingPolicy) null); // throws IllegalArgumentException: "namingPolicy cannot be null"
  ```

#### Public Static Methods
- (none)

#### Public Instance Methods
##### cosmosContainer(...) -> CosmosContainer

- **Summary:** Returns the underlying Cosmos DB container.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the underlying CosmosContainer instance
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  CosmosContainer container = client.getDatabase("ecommerce").getContainer("products");
  CosmosContainerExecutor executor = new CosmosContainerExecutor(container);

  // Returns the exact same instance passed to the constructor (never null)
  CosmosContainer raw = executor.cosmosContainer(); // raw == container

  // Use for SDK operations not wrapped by this executor
  raw.read(); // direct CosmosContainer call
  ```
##### createItem(...) -> CosmosItemResponse<T>
- **Signature:** `public <T> CosmosItemResponse<T> createItem(final T item) throws IllegalArgumentException, CosmosException`
- **Summary:** Creates a new item in the container.
- **Parameters:**
  - `item` (`T`) — the item to create (must not be null)
- **Returns:** a CosmosItemResponse containing the created item and metadata including RU consumption
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `item` is null or the default Cosmos serializer cannot convert it to a JSON document, including failure of an item property getter
  - `com.azure.cosmos.CosmosException` — if Cosmos rejects the create request because the item already exists, its data or partition key is invalid, or authorization fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Define a product entity
  Product product = new Product();
  product.setId("prod123");
  product.setName("Laptop");
  product.setCategory("Electronics"); // Assuming category is the partition key
  product.setPrice(999.99);

  // Create the item
  CosmosItemResponse<Product> response = executor.createItem(product);

  // Access response metadata
  System.out.println("Request charge: " + response.getRequestCharge() + " RUs");
  System.out.println("Status code: " + response.getStatusCode());
  System.out.println("ETag: " + response.getETag());

  // Get the created item
  Product createdProduct = response.getItem();
  ```
- **Signature:** `public <T> CosmosItemResponse<T> createItem(final T item, final PartitionKey partitionKey, final CosmosItemRequestOptions options) throws IllegalArgumentException, CosmosException`
- **Summary:** Creates a new item in the container with explicit partition key and options.
- **Contract:**
  - This is useful when you need to override automatic partition key detection or when you want fine-grained control over the operation behavior.
- **Parameters:**
  - `item` (`T`) — the item to create (must not be null)
  - `partitionKey` (`PartitionKey`) — the partition key for the item (may be null, in which case the partition key is extracted from the item content by the Azure Cosmos SDK)
  - `options` (`CosmosItemRequestOptions`) — additional options for the create operation (can be null for default behavior)
- **Returns:** a CosmosItemResponse containing the created item and metadata
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `item` is null or the default Cosmos serializer cannot convert it to a JSON document, including failure of an item property getter
  - `com.azure.cosmos.CosmosException` — if Cosmos rejects the create request because the item already exists, its data or partition key is invalid, or authorization fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Product product = new Product("prod123", "Laptop", "Electronics", 999.99);

  // Create with explicit partition key
  PartitionKey partitionKey = new PartitionKey("Electronics");

  // Configure request options
  CosmosItemRequestOptions options = new CosmosItemRequestOptions();
  options.setConsistencyLevel(ConsistencyLevel.STRONG);

  // createItem already rejects an existing id in the same partition with HTTP 409.
  // If-None-Match is ignored for writes; no conditional-create header is needed.

  // Create the item
  CosmosItemResponse<Product> response = executor.createItem(
      product,
      partitionKey,
      options
  );

  System.out.println("Created with RU charge: " + response.getRequestCharge());
  ```
- **Signature:** `public <T> CosmosItemResponse<T> createItem(final T item, final CosmosItemRequestOptions options) throws IllegalArgumentException, CosmosException`
- **Summary:** Creates a new item in the container with specified options.
- **Contract:**
  - Useful when you need to control aspects like consistency level or an indexing directive without explicitly specifying the partition key.
- **Parameters:**
  - `item` (`T`) — the item to create (must not be null)
  - `options` (`CosmosItemRequestOptions`) — additional options for the create operation (can be null for default behavior). Do not reuse an options object passed to an operation with a partition key: the SDK stored that key in it, and the key would be used instead of the item's (see the class documentation).
- **Returns:** a CosmosItemResponse containing the created item and metadata
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `item` is null or the default Cosmos serializer cannot convert it to a JSON document, including failure of an item property getter
  - `com.azure.cosmos.CosmosException` — if Cosmos rejects the create request because the item already exists, its data or partition key is invalid, or authorization fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Product product = new Product("prod456", "Mouse", "Electronics", 29.99);

  // Configure options without explicit partition key
  CosmosItemRequestOptions options = new CosmosItemRequestOptions();
  options.setContentResponseOnWriteEnabled(false);           // Reduce the response payload
  options.setIndexingDirective(IndexingDirective.EXCLUDE);   // Skip indexing for this item

  CosmosItemResponse<Product> response = executor.createItem(product, options);

  System.out.println("Item created, RU charge: " + response.getRequestCharge());
  ```
##### upsertItem(...) -> CosmosItemResponse<T>
- **Signature:** `public <T> CosmosItemResponse<T> upsertItem(final T item) throws IllegalArgumentException, CosmosException`
- **Summary:** Creates or updates an item in the container (upsert operation).
- **Contract:**
  - If an item with the same id and partition key exists, it will be replaced.
  - If it doesn't exist, a new item will be created.
- **Parameters:**
  - `item` (`T`) — the item to create or update (must not be null)
- **Returns:** a CosmosItemResponse containing the upserted item and metadata
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `item` is null or the default Cosmos serializer cannot convert it to a JSON document, including failure of an item property getter
  - `com.azure.cosmos.CosmosException` — if Cosmos rejects the upsert request because its data or partition key is invalid, its access condition fails, or authorization fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Create or update a product
  Product product = new Product();
  product.setId("prod789");
  product.setName("Keyboard");
  product.setCategory("Electronics");
  product.setPrice(79.99);
  product.setLastUpdated(System.currentTimeMillis());

  // Upsert - will create if new, replace if exists
  CosmosItemResponse<Product> response = executor.upsertItem(product);

  // Check if it was created (201) or replaced (200)
  int statusCode = response.getStatusCode();
  if (statusCode == 201) {
      System.out.println("New item created");
  } else if (statusCode == 200) {
      System.out.println("Existing item updated");
  }

  System.out.println("RU consumed: " + response.getRequestCharge());
  ```
- **See also:** `#createItem(Object)` for create-only operations, `#replaceItem(String, PartitionKey, Object, CosmosItemRequestOptions)` for replace-only operations
- **Signature:** `public <T> CosmosItemResponse<T> upsertItem(final T item, final PartitionKey partitionKey, final CosmosItemRequestOptions options) throws IllegalArgumentException, CosmosException`
- **Summary:** Creates or updates an item with explicit partition key and options.
- **Contract:**
  - This is useful when you need to override the automatic partition key detection or when you want to specify options like consistency level, an indexing directive, or conditional updates.
  - An If-Match ETag is checked only when the upsert replaces an existing item.
  - If the item is absent, the service creates it without checking that ETag.
  - Use `#replaceItem(String, PartitionKey, Object, CosmosItemRequestOptions)` when a concurrent deletion must cause failure.
- **Parameters:**
  - `item` (`T`) — the item to create or update (must not be null)
  - `partitionKey` (`PartitionKey`) — the partition key for the item (may be null, in which case the partition key is extracted from the item content by the Azure Cosmos SDK)
  - `options` (`CosmosItemRequestOptions`) — additional options for the upsert operation (can be null for default behavior)
- **Returns:** a CosmosItemResponse containing the upserted item and metadata
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `item` is null or the default Cosmos serializer cannot convert it to a JSON document, including failure of an item property getter
  - `com.azure.cosmos.CosmosException` — if Cosmos rejects the upsert request because its data or partition key is invalid, its access condition fails, or authorization fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  PartitionKey partitionKey = new PartitionKey("Electronics");
  CosmosItemResponse<Product> current =
      executor.readItem("prod999", partitionKey, Product.class);
  Product product = current.getItem();
  product.setPrice(299.99);

  // Configure upsert options
  CosmosItemRequestOptions options = new CosmosItemRequestOptions();
  options.setConsistencyLevel(ConsistencyLevel.SESSION);

  // Check the ETag when replacing an existing item. If it was deleted, upsert creates it again.
  options.setIfMatchETag(current.getETag());

  try {
      CosmosItemResponse<Product> response = executor.upsertItem(
          product,
          partitionKey,
          options
      );
      System.out.println("Upsert successful, RU: " + response.getRequestCharge());
  } catch (CosmosException e) {
      if (e.getStatusCode() == 412) {
          System.out.println("Precondition failed - item was modified");
      }
  }
  ```
- **Signature:** `public <T> CosmosItemResponse<T> upsertItem(final T item, final CosmosItemRequestOptions options) throws IllegalArgumentException, CosmosException`
- **Summary:** Creates or updates an item with specified options.
- **Parameters:**
  - `item` (`T`) — the item to create or update (must not be null)
  - `options` (`CosmosItemRequestOptions`) — additional options for the upsert operation (can be null for default behavior). Do not reuse an options object passed to an operation with a partition key: the SDK stored that key in it, and the key would be used instead of the item's (see the class documentation).
- **Returns:** a CosmosItemResponse containing the upserted item and metadata
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `item` is null or the default Cosmos serializer cannot convert it to a JSON document, including failure of an item property getter
  - `com.azure.cosmos.CosmosException` — if Cosmos rejects the upsert request because its data or partition key is invalid, its access condition fails, or authorization fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Product product = new Product("prod555", "Headphones", "Electronics", 149.99);

  // Omit the item body from the write response
  CosmosItemRequestOptions options = new CosmosItemRequestOptions();
  options.setContentResponseOnWriteEnabled(false); // Don't return the document body

  CosmosItemResponse<Product> response = executor.upsertItem(product, options);

  // Response will not contain the item, but metadata is available
  System.out.println("Upsert completed with RU: " + response.getRequestCharge());
  System.out.println("Status: " + response.getStatusCode());
  ```
##### replaceItem(...) -> CosmosItemResponse<T>
- **Signature:** `public <T> CosmosItemResponse<T> replaceItem(final String oldItemId, final PartitionKey partitionKey, final T newItem, final CosmosItemRequestOptions options) throws IllegalArgumentException, CosmosException`
- **Summary:** Replaces an existing item with a new item.
- **Contract:**
  - The item must exist or the operation will fail.
  - This is different from upsert which will create the item if it doesn't exist.
- **Parameters:**
  - `oldItemId` (`String`) — the id of the existing item to replace (must not be null)
  - `partitionKey` (`PartitionKey`) — the partition key of the item to replace (may be null, in which case the partition key is extracted from `newItem` by the Azure Cosmos SDK)
  - `newItem` (`T`) — the new item that will replace the existing one (must not be null)
  - `options` (`CosmosItemRequestOptions`) — additional options for the replace operation (can be null for default behavior)
- **Returns:** a `CosmosItemResponse` containing the replaced item and metadata such as RU charge, ETag, and status code
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `oldItemId` or `newItem` is null, or the default Cosmos serializer cannot convert `newItem` to a JSON document
  - `com.azure.cosmos.CosmosException` — if the item is absent, an ETag condition fails, or Cosmos rejects the replacement data or partition key
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  PartitionKey partitionKey = new PartitionKey("Electronics");
  CosmosItemResponse<Product> current =
      executor.readItem("prod123", partitionKey, Product.class);
  Product existingProduct = current.getItem();

  // Modify the product
  Product updatedProduct = new Product(existingProduct.getId(),
                                      "Updated Laptop",
                                      "Electronics",
                                      1099.99);

  // Replace with ETag for optimistic concurrency
  CosmosItemRequestOptions options = new CosmosItemRequestOptions()
      .setIfMatchETag(current.getETag());

  CosmosItemResponse<Product> response = executor.replaceItem(
      "prod123",
      partitionKey,
      updatedProduct,
      options
  );
  ```
- **See also:** `#upsertItem(Object)` for create-or-replace operations
##### patchItem(...) -> CosmosItemResponse<T>
- **Signature:** `public <T> CosmosItemResponse<T> patchItem(final String itemId, final PartitionKey partitionKey, final CosmosPatchOperations cosmosPatchOperations, final Class<T> targetClass) throws IllegalArgumentException, CosmosException`
- **Summary:** Performs partial updates on an item using patch operations.
- **Parameters:**
  - `itemId` (`String`) — the id of the item to patch (must not be null)
  - `partitionKey` (`PartitionKey`) — the partition key of the item (must not be null)
  - `cosmosPatchOperations` (`CosmosPatchOperations`) — the patch operations to apply (must not be null)
  - `targetClass` (`Class<T>`) — the class type for deserializing the response (must not be null)
- **Returns:** a CosmosItemResponse containing the patched item and metadata
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `itemId`, `partitionKey`, `cosmosPatchOperations`, or `targetClass` is null. The SDK stores the result type without checking it, so a null type would otherwise only fail later, when `getItem()` is called.
  - `com.azure.cosmos.CosmosException` — if the item or patch path is absent, an access condition fails, or Cosmos rejects the patch operations
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  String itemId = "prod123";
  PartitionKey partitionKey = new PartitionKey("Electronics");

  // Create patch operations
  CosmosPatchOperations patchOps = CosmosPatchOperations.create();

  // Update price
  patchOps.replace("/price", 899.99);

  // Increment view count
  patchOps.increment("/viewCount", 1);

  // Add new field
  patchOps.add("/tags", Arrays.asList("sale", "featured"));

  // Remove a field
  patchOps.remove("/deprecated");

  // Execute patch
  CosmosItemResponse<Product> response = executor.patchItem(
      itemId,
      partitionKey,
      patchOps,
      Product.class
  );

  Product patchedProduct = response.getItem();
  System.out.println("Patched price: " + patchedProduct.getPrice());
  System.out.println("RU consumed: " + response.getRequestCharge());
  ```
- **See also:** `CosmosPatchOperations` for available patch operations
- **Signature:** `public <T> CosmosItemResponse<T> patchItem(final String itemId, final PartitionKey partitionKey, final CosmosPatchOperations cosmosPatchOperations, final CosmosPatchItemRequestOptions options, final Class<T> targetClass) throws IllegalArgumentException, CosmosException`
- **Summary:** Performs partial updates on an item using patch operations with additional options.
- **Parameters:**
  - `itemId` (`String`) — the id of the item to patch (must not be null)
  - `partitionKey` (`PartitionKey`) — the partition key of the item (must not be null)
  - `cosmosPatchOperations` (`CosmosPatchOperations`) — the patch operations to apply (must not be null)
  - `options` (`CosmosPatchItemRequestOptions`) — additional options for the patch operation (can be null for default behavior)
  - `targetClass` (`Class<T>`) — the class type for deserializing the response (must not be null)
- **Returns:** a CosmosItemResponse containing the patched item and metadata
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `itemId`, `partitionKey`, `cosmosPatchOperations`, or `targetClass` is null. The SDK stores the result type without checking it, so a null type would otherwise only fail later, when `getItem()` is called.
  - `com.azure.cosmos.CosmosException` — if the item or patch path is absent, an access condition fails, or Cosmos rejects the patch operations
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  String itemId = "prod456";
  PartitionKey partitionKey = new PartitionKey("Electronics");
  String existingETag = executor.readItem(itemId, partitionKey, Product.class).getETag();

  // Create patch operations
  CosmosPatchOperations patchOps = CosmosPatchOperations.create()
      .replace("/price", 799.99)
      .increment("/stockQuantity", -1);

  // Configure patch options with conditional update
  CosmosPatchItemRequestOptions options = new CosmosPatchItemRequestOptions();
  options.setIfMatchETag(existingETag);                             // Only patch if ETag matches
  options.setFilterPredicate("from c where c.stockQuantity > 0");   // Conditional logic

  try {
      CosmosItemResponse<Product> response = executor.patchItem(
          itemId,
          partitionKey,
          patchOps,
          options,
          Product.class
      );
      System.out.println("Patch successful, new stock: " + response.getItem().getStockQuantity());
  } catch (CosmosException e) {
      if (e.getStatusCode() == 412) {
  ```

- **Signature:** `public CosmosItemResponse<Object> deleteItem(final Object item, final CosmosItemRequestOptions options) throws IllegalArgumentException, CosmosException`
- **Summary:** Deletes an item from the container using the item object.
- **Parameters:**
  - `item` (`Object`) — the item object containing id and partition key information (must not be null)
  - `options` (`CosmosItemRequestOptions`) — additional options for the delete operation (can be null for default behavior)
- **Returns:** a CosmosItemResponse with metadata about the delete operation

- **Examples:**
  ```java

      "prod123", new PartitionKey("Electronics"), Product.class);
  Product productToDelete = current.getItem();

  CosmosItemResponse<Object> response = executor.deleteItem(productToDelete, null);
  System.out.println("Delete RU cost: " + response.getRequestCharge());

      }
  }
  ```

##### get(...) -> Optional<T>
- **Signature:** `public <T> Optional<T> get(final String itemId, final PartitionKey partitionKey, final Class<T> targetClass) throws IllegalArgumentException, CosmosException, IllegalStateException`
- **Summary:** Reads a single item by id and partition key, returning an empty `Optional` when the item does not exist.
- **Contract:**
  - This is the absence-tolerant counterpart to `#readItem(String, PartitionKey, Class)`: instead of letting a `CosmosException` with a `404 Not Found` status propagate when the document is missing, this method returns `Optional#empty()`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `itemId` (`String`) — the id of the item to read (must not be null)
  - `partitionKey` (`PartitionKey`) — the partition key of the item (must not be null)
  - `targetClass` (`Class<T>`) — the class type for deserializing the response (must not be null)
- **Returns:** an `Optional` holding the item if it exists, or `Optional#empty()` if no item exists for the given id/partition key (404)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `itemId`, `partitionKey`, or `targetClass` is null (rejected by `#readItem(String, PartitionKey, Class)` before the request is sent; without that check a null id would be swallowed by the 404 handling and reported as an empty result)
  - `com.azure.cosmos.CosmosException` — if the read request fails with an HTTP status other than 404, such as an authorization or throttling failure
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the default Cosmos item serializer cannot convert the returned document to `targetClass`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Optional<Product> product = executor.get("prod123", new PartitionKey("Electronics"), Product.class);

  product.ifPresentOrElse(
      p -> System.out.println("Found: " + p.getName()),
      () -> System.out.println("No such product"));    // taken when the id/partition-key has no item (404)
  ```
- **See also:** `#readItem(String, PartitionKey, Class)`, `#get(String, PartitionKey, CosmosItemRequestOptions, Class)`, `#gett(String, PartitionKey, Class)`

  - `options` (`CosmosItemRequestOptions`) — additional options for the read operation (can be null for default behavior)
  - `targetClass` (`Class<T>`) — the class type for deserializing the response (must not be null)
- **Returns:** an `Optional` holding the item if it exists, or `Optional#empty()` if no item exists for the given id/partition key (404)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `itemId`, `partitionKey`, or `targetClass` is null (rejected by `#readItem(String, PartitionKey, CosmosItemRequestOptions, Class)` before the request is sent; without that check a null id would be swallowed by the 404 handling and reported as an empty result)
  - `com.azure.cosmos.CosmosException` — if the read request fails with an HTTP status other than 404, such as an authorization or throttling failure
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the default Cosmos item serializer cannot convert the returned document to `targetClass`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  CosmosItemRequestOptions options = new CosmosItemRequestOptions();
  options.setConsistencyLevel(ConsistencyLevel.STRONG);

  Optional<Product> product = executor.get("prod456", new PartitionKey("Electronics"), options, Product.class);
  ```
- **See also:** `#readItem(String, PartitionKey, CosmosItemRequestOptions, Class)`, `#get(String, PartitionKey, Class)`, `#gett(String, PartitionKey, CosmosItemRequestOptions, Class)`

##### readItem(...) -> CosmosItemResponse<T>
- **Signature:** `public <T> CosmosItemResponse<T> readItem(final String itemId, final PartitionKey partitionKey, final Class<T> targetClass) throws IllegalArgumentException, CosmosException`
- **Summary:** Reads a single item from the container by id and partition key.
- **Contract:**
  - This is the most efficient way to retrieve a document when you know both the id and partition key.
- **Parameters:**
  - `itemId` (`String`) — the id of the item to read (must not be null)
  - `partitionKey` (`PartitionKey`) — the partition key of the item (must not be null)
  - `targetClass` (`Class<T>`) — the class type for deserializing the response (must not be null)
- **Returns:** a CosmosItemResponse containing the item and metadata
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `itemId`, `partitionKey`, or `targetClass` is null. None of the three is checked by the SDK: a null id is reported as a 404 CosmosException, a null partition key as an UnsupportedOperationException, and a null target class only fails later, when `getItem()` is called.
  - `com.azure.cosmos.CosmosException` — if the item is absent or Cosmos rejects the read request because of authorization, throttling, or an invalid partition key
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Read a product by id and partition key
  String itemId = "prod123";
  PartitionKey partitionKey = new PartitionKey("Electronics");

  CosmosItemResponse<Product> response = executor.readItem(
      itemId,
      partitionKey,
      Product.class
  );

  // Access the item
  Product product = response.getItem();
  System.out.println("Product: " + product.getName());
  System.out.println("Price: $" + product.getPrice());

  // Access metadata
  System.out.println("RU consumed: " + response.getRequestCharge());
  System.out.println("ETag: " + response.getETag());
  System.out.println("Activity ID: " + response.getActivityId());
  ```
- **Signature:** `public <T> CosmosItemResponse<T> readItem(final String itemId, final PartitionKey partitionKey, final CosmosItemRequestOptions options, final Class<T> targetClass) throws IllegalArgumentException, CosmosException`
- **Summary:** Reads a single item with additional options.
- **Contract:**
  - Useful when you need specific consistency guarantees or want to optimize for specific scenarios.
- **Parameters:**
  - `itemId` (`String`) — the id of the item to read (must not be null)
  - `partitionKey` (`PartitionKey`) — the partition key of the item (must not be null)
  - `options` (`CosmosItemRequestOptions`) — additional options for the read operation (can be null for default behavior)
  - `targetClass` (`Class<T>`) — the class type for deserializing the response (must not be null)
- **Returns:** a CosmosItemResponse containing the item and metadata
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `itemId`, `partitionKey`, or `targetClass` is null. None of the three is checked by the SDK: a null id is reported as a 404 CosmosException, a null partition key as an UnsupportedOperationException, and a null target class only fails later, when `getItem()` is called.
  - `com.azure.cosmos.CosmosException` — if the item is absent or Cosmos rejects the read request because of authorization, throttling, or an invalid partition key
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  String itemId = "prod456";
  PartitionKey partitionKey = new PartitionKey("Electronics");

  // Configure read options
  CosmosItemRequestOptions options = new CosmosItemRequestOptions();

  // Set strong consistency for critical reads
  options.setConsistencyLevel(ConsistencyLevel.STRONG);

  // Read the item
  CosmosItemResponse<Product> response = executor.readItem(
      itemId,
      partitionKey,
      options,
      Product.class
  );

  Product product = response.getItem();
  System.out.println("Read with strong consistency: " + product.getName());
  System.out.println("Session token: " + response.getSessionToken());
  ```
##### readMany(...) -> FeedResponse<T>
- **Signature:** `public <T> FeedResponse<T> readMany(final List<CosmosItemIdentity> itemIdentityList, final Class<T> targetClass) throws IllegalArgumentException, CosmosException`
- **Summary:** Reads multiple items in a single request using their identities.
- **Parameters:**
  - `itemIdentityList` (`List<CosmosItemIdentity>`) — list of item identities (id and partition key pairs, must not be null)
  - `targetClass` (`Class<T>`) — the class type for deserializing the response items (must not be null)
- **Returns:** a FeedResponse containing all found items (items not found will be omitted)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `itemIdentityList` or `targetClass` is null. The SDK dereferences the list only after the container metadata has been resolved, so an unchecked null would fail after a round trip rather than at the call site.
  - `com.azure.cosmos.CosmosException` — if Cosmos rejects the batch-read request because of invalid item identities, authorization, or throttling
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Create list of item identities to read
  List<CosmosItemIdentity> identities = Arrays.asList(
      new CosmosItemIdentity(new PartitionKey("Electronics"), "prod123"),
      new CosmosItemIdentity(new PartitionKey("Electronics"), "prod456"),
      new CosmosItemIdentity(new PartitionKey("Books"), "book789")
  );

  // Read multiple items at once
  FeedResponse<Product> response = executor.readMany(identities, Product.class);

  // Process results
  List<Product> products = response.getResults();
  System.out.println("Retrieved " + products.size() + " items");

  for (Product product : products) {
      System.out.println("Product: " + product.getName());
  }

  // Check total RU consumed
  System.out.println("Total RU: " + response.getRequestCharge());

  // Note: Items not found will not be included in results
  // Check count to see if all items were found
  if (products.size() < identities.size()) {
      System.out.println("Some items were not found");
  }
  ```
- **See also:** `CosmosItemIdentity` for item identity specification
- **Signature:** `public <T> FeedResponse<T> readMany(final List<CosmosItemIdentity> itemIdentityList, final String sessionToken, final Class<T> targetClass) throws IllegalArgumentException, CosmosException`
- **Summary:** Reads multiple items with session token for consistency.
- **Parameters:**
  - `itemIdentityList` (`List<CosmosItemIdentity>`) — list of item identities (id and partition key pairs, must not be null)
  - `sessionToken` (`String`) — the session token for consistency (can be null for default consistency)
  - `targetClass` (`Class<T>`) — the class type for deserializing the response items (must not be null)
- **Returns:** a FeedResponse containing all found items
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `itemIdentityList` or `targetClass` is null. The SDK dereferences the list only after the container metadata has been resolved, so an unchecked null would fail after a round trip rather than at the call site.
  - `com.azure.cosmos.CosmosException` — if Cosmos rejects the batch-read request because of invalid item identities, authorization, or throttling
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // First, perform a write and capture its session token
  Product newProduct = new Product("prod789", "Keyboard", "Electronics", 79.99);
  CosmosItemResponse<Product> writeResponse = executor.createItem(newProduct);
  String sessionToken = writeResponse.getSessionToken();

  // Now read multiple items using the session token
  List<CosmosItemIdentity> identities = Arrays.asList(
      new CosmosItemIdentity(new PartitionKey("Electronics"), "prod789"),
      new CosmosItemIdentity(new PartitionKey("Electronics"), "prod123"),
      new CosmosItemIdentity(new PartitionKey("Electronics"), "prod456")
  );

  // Read with session consistency
  FeedResponse<Product> response = executor.readMany(
      identities,
      sessionToken,
      Product.class
  );

  // The token preserves read-your-writes consistency for the applicable partition
  List<Product> products = response.getResults();
  System.out.println("Read " + products.size() + " items with session consistency");
  ```
##### readAllItems(...) -> CosmosPagedIterable<T>
- **Signature:** `public <T> CosmosPagedIterable<T> readAllItems(final PartitionKey partitionKey, final Class<T> targetClass) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Reads all items within a specific partition.
- **Parameters:**
  - `partitionKey` (`PartitionKey`) — the partition key identifying the partition to scan (must not be null)
  - `targetClass` (`Class<T>`) — the class type for deserializing the response items (must not be null)
- **Returns:** a CosmosPagedIterable for iterating through all items; Cosmos service failures are raised as `CosmosException` when the returned results are consumed.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `partitionKey` or `targetClass` is null. Neither is checked eagerly by the SDK, so an unchecked null would only fail once the result is consumed.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Read all products in Electronics category
  PartitionKey partitionKey = new PartitionKey("Electronics");
  CosmosPagedIterable<Product> pagedResults = executor.readAllItems(
      partitionKey,
      Product.class
  );

  // Iterate through all items (handles pagination automatically)
  for (Product product : pagedResults) {
      System.out.println("Product: " + product.getName());
  }

  // Or iterate by pages for more control
  pagedResults.iterableByPage().forEach(page -> {
      System.out.println("Page RU charge: " + page.getRequestCharge());
      page.getResults().forEach(product -> {
          System.out.println("  - " + product.getName());
      });
  });
  ```
- **See also:** `#streamAllItems(PartitionKey, Class)` for stream-based processing
- **Signature:** `public <T> CosmosPagedIterable<T> readAllItems(final PartitionKey partitionKey, final CosmosQueryRequestOptions options, final Class<T> targetClass) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Reads all items within a partition with query options.
- **Parameters:**
  - `partitionKey` (`PartitionKey`) — the partition key identifying the partition to scan (must not be null)
  - `options` (`CosmosQueryRequestOptions`) — query options controlling the scan behavior (can be null for default behavior). The SDK stores `partitionKey` into a non-null `options` object, so reusing that object for a later query scopes the query to this partition.
  - `targetClass` (`Class<T>`) — the class type for deserializing the response items (must not be null)
- **Returns:** a CosmosPagedIterable for iterating through all items; Cosmos service failures are raised as `CosmosException` when the returned results are consumed.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `partitionKey` or `targetClass` is null. Neither is checked eagerly by the SDK, so an unchecked null would only fail once the result is consumed.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  PartitionKey partitionKey = new PartitionKey("Electronics");

  // Configure query options
  CosmosQueryRequestOptions options = new CosmosQueryRequestOptions();
  options.setMaxDegreeOfParallelism(4);   // Parallel query execution
  options.setMaxBufferedItemCount(100);   // Buffer size

  CosmosPagedIterable<Product> pagedResults = executor.readAllItems(
      partitionKey,
      options,
      Product.class
  );

  // Process with pagination control
  int pageCount = 0;
  for (FeedResponse<Product> page : pagedResults.iterableByPage()) {
      pageCount++;
      System.out.println("Page " + pageCount + ": " +
          page.getResults().size() + " items, " +
          page.getRequestCharge() + " RUs");
  }
  ```

- **Signature:** `@Beta public <T> Stream<T> streamAllItems(final PartitionKey partitionKey, final Class<T> targetClass) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Annotations:** @Beta

  - `targetClass` (`Class<T>`) — the class type for deserializing the items (must not be null)

- **Examples:**
  ```java
  PartitionKey partitionKey = new PartitionKey("Electronics");

  // Stream and process items functionally
  List<String> expensiveProducts = executor.streamAllItems(partitionKey, Product.class)
      .filter(p -> p.getPrice() > 500)
      .map(Product::getName)
      .sorted()
      .collect(Collectors.toList());

  System.out.println("Expensive products: " + expensiveProducts);

  // Calculate statistics
  DoubleSummaryStatistics stats = executor.streamAllItems(partitionKey, Product.class)
      .mapToDouble(Product::getPrice)
      .summaryStatistics();

  System.out.println("Average price: $" + stats.getAverage());
  System.out.println("Max price: $" + stats.getMax());
  System.out.println("Total products: " + stats.getCount());
  ```

  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `partitionKey` or `targetClass` is null. Neither is checked eagerly by the SDK, so an unchecked null would only fail once the result is consumed.

  ```java
  // Simple query
  String query = "SELECT * FROM c WHERE c.category = 'Electronics' AND c.price > 100";
  CosmosPagedIterable<Product> results = executor.queryItems(query, Product.class);

  for (Product product : results) {
      System.out.println(product.getName() + ": $" + product.getPrice());
  }

  // Query with ORDER BY and projection
  String query2 = "SELECT c.id, c.name, c.price FROM c " +
                  "WHERE c.inStock = true " +
                  "ORDER BY c.price DESC";

  CosmosPagedIterable<Product> topProducts = executor.queryItems(query2, Product.class);

  // Track RU consumption by page
  for (FeedResponse<Product> page : topProducts.iterableByPage()) {
      System.out.println("Retrieved " + page.getResults().size() +
          " items, RU: " + page.getRequestCharge());
  }
  ```
- **Signature:** `public <T> CosmosPagedIterable<T> queryItems(final String query, final CosmosQueryRequestOptions options, final Class<T> targetClass) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Executes a SQL query with additional query options.
- **Parameters:**
  - `query` (`String`) — the SQL query string (must not be null)
  - `options` (`CosmosQueryRequestOptions`) — query options controlling execution behavior (can be null for default behavior)
  - `targetClass` (`Class<T>`) — the class type for deserializing the query results (must not be null)
- **Returns:** a CosmosPagedIterable for iterating through query results; Cosmos service failures are raised as `CosmosException` when the returned results are consumed.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `query` or `targetClass` is null. Neither is checked eagerly by the SDK, so an unchecked null would only fail once the result is consumed. The SDK also throws it, when the query is created, if `options` sets both a partition key and a feed range.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  String query = "SELECT * FROM c WHERE c.price BETWEEN 100 AND 500";

  // Configure query options
  CosmosQueryRequestOptions options = new CosmosQueryRequestOptions();

  // Single partition query for better performance
  options.setPartitionKey(new PartitionKey("Electronics"));

  // Control parallelism and buffering
  options.setMaxDegreeOfParallelism(4);
  options.setMaxBufferedItemCount(1000);

  // Execute query
  CosmosPagedIterable<Product> results = executor.queryItems(
      query,
      options,
      Product.class
  );

  // Cross-partition query example
  CosmosQueryRequestOptions crossPartitionOptions = new CosmosQueryRequestOptions();
  // Enable cross-partition by not setting partition key
  crossPartitionOptions.setMaxDegreeOfParallelism(-1); // Auto parallelism

  String globalQuery = "SELECT * FROM c WHERE c.featured = true";
  CosmosPagedIterable<Product> featuredProducts = executor.queryItems(
      globalQuery,
      crossPartitionOptions,
      Product.class
  );
  ```

  - `options` (`CosmosQueryRequestOptions`) — query options controlling execution behavior (can be null for defaults)
  - `targetClass` (`Class<T>`) — the class type for deserializing the query results (must not be null)
- **Returns:** a CosmosPagedIterable for iterating through query results; Cosmos service failures are raised as `CosmosException` when the returned results are consumed.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `querySpec` or `targetClass` is null. Neither is checked eagerly by the SDK, so an unchecked null would only fail once the result is consumed. The SDK also throws it, when the query is created, if `options` sets both a partition key and a feed range.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  SqlQuerySpec spec = new SqlQuerySpec(
      "SELECT * FROM c WHERE c.category = @cat AND c.price > @min"
  ).setParameters(Arrays.asList(
      new SqlParameter("@cat", "Electronics"),
      new SqlParameter("@min", 100.0)));

  // Typical: scope the query to a single partition for efficiency
  CosmosQueryRequestOptions options = new CosmosQueryRequestOptions();
  options.setPartitionKey(new PartitionKey("Electronics"));
  CosmosPagedIterable<Product> results = executor.queryItems(spec, options, Product.class);
  for (Product p : results) {
      System.out.println(p.getName());
  }

  // Typical: null options uses cross-partition defaults
  CosmosPagedIterable<Product> all = executor.queryItems(spec, (CosmosQueryRequestOptions) null, Product.class);

  // Edge: a malformed query is only validated when the iterable is enumerated
  SqlQuerySpec bad = new SqlQuerySpec("SELECT * FROM"); // no error here
  for (Product p : executor.queryItems(bad, options, Product.class)) { } // throws CosmosException on iteration
  ```

- **Summary:** Streams query results for functional processing.

- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Stream query results and process functionally
  String query = "SELECT * FROM c WHERE c.category = 'Electronics'";

  List<String> productNames = executor.streamItems(query, Product.class)
      .filter(p -> p.getPrice() > 100)
      .map(Product::getName)
      .sorted()
      .collect(Collectors.toList());

  System.out.println("Products over $100: " + productNames);

  // Calculate aggregates
  String allQuery = "SELECT * FROM c";
  double averagePrice = executor.streamItems(allQuery, Product.class)
      .mapToDouble(Product::getPrice)
      .average()
      .orElse(0.0);

  System.out.println("Average price: $" + averagePrice);

  // Count with condition

      .filter(p -> p.getPrice() > 500)
      .count();
  ```

- **Signature:** `@Beta public final <T> Stream<T> streamItems(final Condition whereClause, final Class<T> targetClass) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Annotations:** @Beta
- **Summary:** Streams items matching a condition using the query builder.
- **Contract:**
  - The FROM source is the entity's table name when that name is a plain identifier that is not a reserved word.
  - a: b`) in a `Filters.expr(...)` or in a subquery's SQL text; when the condition also carries parameter values, the counts then differ and the call fails with an `IllegalArgumentException`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `whereClause` (`Condition`) — the condition object defining the WHERE clause (can be null for no filter)
  - `targetClass` (`Class<T>`) — the class type for deserializing the results (must not be null)
- **Returns:** a Stream of items matching the condition; Cosmos service failures are raised as `CosmosException` when the returned results are consumed.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetClass` is null (rejected before any query is built or sent) or is not a bean class with properties, such as `Map` or `JsonNode` (the query builder derives the FROM source and property names from it), if `whereClause` has a null operator or is or contains a `Criteria`, standalone `SubQuery`, SQL clause, JOIN, `ON`/`USING` connector, quantified-subquery operand, or blank or comment-only `SqlExpression` (rejected by `SqlBuilder.where(Condition)`), if the generated query has a different number of positional placeholders and parameter values when the parameter list is nonempty, or if the Cosmos SDK's default JSON serializer cannot convert a condition value (for example a bean without properties or a `java.util.Optional`); values are converted when the query is created
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  import static com.landawn.abacus.query.Filters.*;

  // Simple condition query
  Condition condition = and(
      eq("category", "Electronics"),
      gt("price", 100.0),
      eq("featured", true));

  List<Product> results = executor.streamItems(condition, Product.class)
      .collect(Collectors.toList());

  // Complex condition with multiple operators
  Condition complexCond = and(
      eq("category", "Electronics"),
      between("price", 50.0, 500.0),
      in("brand", Arrays.asList("Apple", "Samsung", "Sony")),
      notEqual("status", "discontinued"));

  executor.streamItems(complexCond, Product.class)
      .forEach(p -> System.out.println(p.getName() + ": $" + p.getPrice()));

  // Condition with OR logic
  Condition orCond = or(
      eq("featured", true),
      gt("rating", 4.5));

  long featuredCount = executor.streamItems(orCond, Product.class).count();
  ```
- **See also:** `Condition` for condition construction, `com.landawn.abacus.query.Filters` for available filter operations

- **Returns:** a Stream of items matching the condition; Cosmos service failures are raised as `CosmosException` when the returned results are consumed.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetClass` is null (rejected before any query is built or sent) or is not a bean class with properties, such as `Map` or `JsonNode` (the query builder derives the FROM source and property names from it), if `whereClause` has a null operator or is or contains a `Criteria`, standalone `SubQuery`, SQL clause, JOIN, `ON`/`USING` connector, quantified-subquery operand, or blank or comment-only `SqlExpression` (rejected by `SqlBuilder.where(Condition)`), if the generated query has a different number of positional placeholders and parameter values when the parameter list is nonempty, if the Cosmos SDK's default JSON serializer cannot convert a condition value (for example a bean without properties or a `java.util.Optional`), or if `options` sets both a partition key and a feed range (rejected by the SDK); all of these are detected when the query is created

  ```java
  import static com.landawn.abacus.query.Filters.*;

  List<Product> midRangeProducts = executor.streamItems(condition, options, Product.class)
      .sorted(Comparator.comparing(Product::getPrice))
      .collect(Collectors.toList());
  ```

- **Annotations:** @Beta
- **Summary:** Streams selected properties of items matching a condition.
- **Parameters:**

  - `whereClause` (`Condition`) — the condition object defining the WHERE clause (can be null for no filter)

- **Returns:** a Stream of items with only selected properties populated; Cosmos service failures are raised as `CosmosException` when the returned results are consumed.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetClass` is null (rejected before any query is built or sent) or is not a bean class with properties, such as `Map` or `JsonNode` (the query builder derives the FROM source and property names from it), if `selectPropNames` contains a null, empty, or blank element, if `whereClause` has a null operator or is or contains a `Criteria`, standalone `SubQuery`, SQL clause, JOIN, `ON`/`USING` connector, quantified-subquery operand, or blank or comment-only `SqlExpression` (rejected by `SqlBuilder.where(Condition)`), if the generated query has a different number of positional placeholders and parameter values when the parameter list is nonempty, or if the Cosmos SDK's default JSON serializer cannot convert a condition value (for example a bean without properties or a `java.util.Optional`); values are converted when the query is created
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the generated selected-property expressions cannot be converted to a Cosmos projection
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  import static com.landawn.abacus.query.Filters.*;

  // Select specific fields to reduce the response payload
  Collection<String> selectFields = Arrays.asList("id", "name", "price");
  Condition condition = and(
      eq("category", "Electronics"),
      eq("featured", true));

  // Stream with projection
  List<Product> products = executor.streamItems(selectFields, condition, Product.class)
      .collect(Collectors.toList());

  // Only id, name, and price fields will be populated
  products.forEach(p ->
      System.out.println(p.getId() + ": " + p.getName() + " - $" + p.getPrice())
  );

  // Projection for report generation
  Collection<String> reportFields = Arrays.asList("name", "price", "category");
  Condition reportCond = gt("price", 100.0);

  executor.streamItems(reportFields, reportCond, Product.class)
      .forEach(p -> generateReport(p));
  ```

- **Annotations:** @Beta
- **Summary:** Streams selected properties with condition and query options.
- **Parameters:**
