##### queryForSingleNonNull(...) -> ContinuableFuture<Optional<V>>
- **Signature:** `public <V> ContinuableFuture<Optional<V>> queryForSingleNonNull(final Class<?> targetClass, final Class<V> valueClass, final String propName, final Condition whereClause) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Asynchronously selects a single non-null column value of the named property, coerced to `valueClass`, from the first row matching `whereClause`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `targetClass` (`Class<?>`) — the entity class identifying the target table
  - `valueClass` (`Class<V>`) — the type to convert the column value to
  - `propName` (`String`) — the property whose value is selected
  - `whereClause` (`Condition`) — the WHERE condition selecting at most one row
- **Returns:** a future whose payload is an `Optional` holding the value, or empty if no row matches; if a row was returned but the converted column value is `null`, `get()` throws an `ExecutionException` whose cause is a `NullPointerException`, since `Optional` cannot hold `null`
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetClass` is `null`, `valueClass` is `null`, `propName` is `null` or empty, the supplied condition contains a relation unsupported by CQL, or a condition value is rejected when converted to its column's type (see Bind Value Conversion in `CassandraExecutorBase`)
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if synchronous CQL preparation or parameter binding fails, or the driver rejects request submission; failures after submission are reported by the returned future
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if `whereClause` already carries a `LIMIT` (see Row Limits in `CassandraExecutorBase`); thrown at the call site, before any future is created
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  AsyncCassandraExecutor async = executor.async();

  // Typical: read a column known to be non-null when present.
  Optional<String> name = async.queryForSingleNonNull(User.class, String.class, "name", Filters.eq("id", 1L)).get();
  String n = name.orElse("");

  // Typical: numeric coercion of a required column.
  Optional<Long> id = async.queryForSingleNonNull(User.class, Long.class, "id", Filters.eq("email", "a@b.com")).get();

  // Edge: no matching row -> the future completes with an empty Optional (no exception).
  boolean empty = async.queryForSingleNonNull(User.class, String.class, "name", Filters.eq("id", -1L)).get().isEmpty(); // returns true

  // Edge: a row whose column value is SQL NULL cannot be held by Optional; the mapping runs
  // inside get(), which reports the failure as an ExecutionException caused by NullPointerException.
  try {
      async.queryForSingleNonNull(User.class, String.class, "nullableCol", Filters.eq("id", 1L)).get(); // throws ExecutionException
  } catch (ExecutionException ex) {
      // ex.getCause() is a NullPointerException: the selected column value was null
  }
  ```
- **Signature:** `public <V> ContinuableFuture<Optional<V>> queryForSingleNonNull(final Class<V> valueClass, final String query, final Object... parameters) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Asynchronously executes the supplied CQL query and returns the first column of the first row coerced to `valueClass`, requiring a non-null value when a row is present.
- **Parameters:**
  - `valueClass` (`Class<V>`) — the type to convert the column value to (must not be `null`)
  - `query` (`String`) — the parameterized CQL SELECT statement
  - `parameters` (`Object...`) — the parameter values to bind
- **Returns:** a future whose payload is an `Optional` holding the value, or empty if the query returned no row; if a row was returned but the converted column value is `null`, `get()` throws an `ExecutionException` whose cause is a `NullPointerException`, since `Optional` cannot hold `null`
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `valueClass` or `query` is `null`, the CQL contains malformed or mixed parameter markers, the supplied parameter count or names do not match the prepared statement, or a parameter value is rejected when converted to its column's type (see Bind Value Conversion in `CassandraExecutorBase`)
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if synchronous CQL preparation or parameter binding fails, or the driver rejects request submission; failures after submission are reported by the returned future
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  AsyncCassandraExecutor async = executor.async();

  // Typical: read a column that is non-null when a row is present.
  Optional<String> name = async.queryForSingleNonNull(String.class, "SELECT name FROM users WHERE id = ?", 1L).get();
  String n = name.orElse("");

  // Typical: numeric coercion of a required column.
  Optional<Long> id = async.queryForSingleNonNull(Long.class, "SELECT id FROM users WHERE email = ?", "a@b.com").get();

  // Edge: no matching row -> the future completes with an empty Optional (no exception).
  boolean empty = async.queryForSingleNonNull(String.class, "SELECT name FROM users WHERE id = ?", -1L).get().isEmpty(); // returns true

  // Edge: a row whose value is SQL NULL cannot be held by Optional; the mapping runs inside
  // get(), which reports the failure as an ExecutionException caused by NullPointerException.
  try {
      async.queryForSingleNonNull(String.class, "SELECT null_col FROM users WHERE id = ?", 1L).get(); // throws ExecutionException
  } catch (ExecutionException ex) {
      // ex.getCause() is a NullPointerException: the selected column value was null
  }
  ```
##### execute(...) -> ContinuableFuture<RS>
- **Signature:** `public abstract ContinuableFuture<RS> execute(final String query) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Asynchronously executes a CQL statement without parameters.
- **Parameters:**
  - `query` (`String`) — the CQL statement to execute
- **Returns:** a future that completes with the result set from the query execution
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `query` is `null`, the CQL contains malformed or mixed parameter markers, or the supplied parameter count or names do not match the prepared statement
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if synchronous CQL preparation or parameter binding fails, or the driver rejects request submission; failures after submission are reported by the returned future
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  AsyncCassandraExecutor async = executor.async();

  // Typical: run a parameterless statement and block for the result set.
  ResultSet rs = async.execute("SELECT * FROM users").get();

  // Typical: run a DDL/maintenance statement asynchronously.
  async.execute("TRUNCATE users").thenRunAsync(() -> log.info("truncated")); // runs after the statement completes

  // Edge: the statement is prepared synchronously before the async call is issued, so a
  // malformed statement throws directly from the call site (no future is created).
  async.execute("SELECT FROM"); // throws the driver parse failure synchronously

  // Edge: a statement against a missing table likewise fails during the synchronous preparation.
  async.execute("SELECT * FROM no_such_table"); // throws the driver failure synchronously
  ```
- **Signature:** `public abstract ContinuableFuture<RS> execute(final String query, final Object... parameters) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Asynchronously executes a parameterized CQL statement.
- **Parameters:**
  - `query` (`String`) — the parameterized CQL statement
  - `parameters` (`Object...`) — the parameter values (can be individual values, arrays, collections, maps, or entities)
- **Returns:** a future that completes with the result set from the query execution
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `query` is `null`, the CQL contains malformed or mixed parameter markers, the supplied parameter count or names do not match the prepared statement, or a parameter value is rejected when converted to its column's type (see Bind Value Conversion in `CassandraExecutorBase`)
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if synchronous CQL preparation or parameter binding fails, or the driver rejects request submission; failures after submission are reported by the returned future
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  AsyncCassandraExecutor async = executor.async();

  // Typical: bind positional parameters and block for the result set.
  ResultSet rs = async.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?", 1L).get();

  // Typical: run a parameterized write.
  async.execute("UPDATE users SET name = ? WHERE id = ?", "Alice", 1L).get();

  // Edge: an UPDATE without IF EXISTS creates the row when its primary key is absent.
  async.execute("UPDATE users SET name = ? WHERE id = ?", "x", -1L).get(); // creates id=-1 with name="x" if absent

  // Edge: the statement is prepared synchronously before the async call is issued, so a
  // malformed statement throws directly from the call site (no future is created).
  async.execute("SELECT FROM", 1L); // throws the driver parse failure synchronously
  ```
- **Signature:** `public abstract ContinuableFuture<RS> execute(String query, Map<String, Object> parameters) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Asynchronously executes a CQL statement with named parameters provided as a Map.
- **Parameters:**
  - `query` (`String`) — the parameterized CQL statement with named parameters
  - `parameters` (`Map<String, Object>`) — a Map containing parameter names as keys and parameter values as values
- **Returns:** a future that completes with the result set from the query execution
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `query` is `null`, the CQL contains malformed or mixed parameter markers, the supplied parameter count or names do not match the prepared statement, or a parameter value is rejected when converted to its column's type (see Bind Value Conversion in `CassandraExecutorBase`)
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if synchronous CQL preparation or parameter binding fails, or the driver rejects request submission; failures after submission are reported by the returned future
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  AsyncCassandraExecutor async = executor.async();

  // Typical: bind named parameters from a Map.
  Map<String, Object> params = new HashMap<>();
  params.put("id", 1L);
  ResultSet rs = async.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = :id", params).get();

  // Edge: an empty parameter map supplies no values, so a parameterless statement runs normally.
  ResultSet all = async.execute("SELECT * FROM users", new HashMap<String, Object>()).get(); // same as execute("SELECT * FROM users")

  // Edge: the statement is prepared and bound synchronously before the async call is issued,
  // so a missing named parameter throws directly from the call site (no future is created).
  async.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = :id", new HashMap<String, Object>()); // throws IllegalArgumentException synchronously

  // Edge: a malformed statement likewise fails during the synchronous preparation.
  async.execute("SELECT FROM", params); // throws the driver parse failure synchronously
  ```
- **Signature:** `public abstract ContinuableFuture<RS> execute(final ST statement) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Asynchronously executes a pre-configured CQL statement.
- **Parameters:**
  - `statement` (`ST`) — the configured CQL statement to execute (must not be `null`)
- **Returns:** a future that completes with the result set from the statement execution
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `statement` is `null` (enforced by the shipped executors)
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the driver rejects request submission; failures after submission, including execution on a closed session, are reported by the returned future
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  AsyncCassandraExecutor async = executor.async();

  // Typical: run a fully-built driver statement.
  Statement<?> stmt = SimpleStatement.newInstance("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?", 1L);
  ResultSet rs = async.execute(stmt).get();

  // Typical: apply per-statement options (e.g. page size) before executing.
  Statement<?> paged = SimpleStatement.newInstance("SELECT * FROM users").setPageSize(500);
  async.execute(paged).thenRunAsync(pagedRs -> System.out.println(pagedRs)); // prints the result set when ready

  // Edge: a null statement is rejected synchronously at the call site (no future is created).
  async.execute((Statement<?>) null); // throws IllegalArgumentException immediately

  // Edge: a statement against a missing table completes the future exceptionally.
  try {
      async.execute(SimpleStatement.newInstance("SELECT * FROM no_such_table")).get(); // throws ExecutionException
  } catch (ExecutionException ex) {
      // ex.getCause() is the driver failure
  }
  ```

### Class CassandraExecutor (com.landawn.abacus.da.cassandra.CassandraExecutor)
Primary Cassandra database executor providing high-level CQL operations and result mapping.

**Thread-safety:** thread-safe
**Nullability:** unspecified
**Extends:** `CassandraExecutorBase<Row, ResultSet, Statement<?>, PreparedStatement, BatchType>`

#### Public Constructors
- `public CassandraExecutor(final CqlSession session) throws IllegalArgumentException` — Creates a new CassandraExecutor with the specified Cassandra session.
  - **Throws:**
    - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `session` is `null`
  ```java
  CqlSession session = CqlSession.builder()
      .addContactPoint(new InetSocketAddress("127.0.0.1", 9042))
      .withLocalDatacenter("datacenter1")
      .withKeyspace("my_keyspace")
      .build();
  CassandraExecutor executor = new CassandraExecutor(session); // ready to use; null session throws IllegalArgumentException
  ```
- `public CassandraExecutor(final CqlSession session, final StatementSettings settings) throws IllegalArgumentException` — Creates a new CassandraExecutor with the specified session and statement settings.
  - **Throws:**
    - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `session` is `null`
  ```java
  StatementSettings settings = StatementSettings.builder()
      .consistency(ConsistencyLevel.QUORUM)
      .timeout(Duration.ofSeconds(30))
      .fetchSize(1000)
      .build();
  CassandraExecutor executor = new CassandraExecutor(session, settings); // settings may be null (driver defaults are used)
  ```
- `public CassandraExecutor(final CqlSession session, final StatementSettings settings, final CqlMapper cqlMapper) throws IllegalArgumentException` — Creates a new CassandraExecutor with session, settings, and CQL mapper.
  - **Throws:**
    - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `session` is `null`
  ```java
  CqlMapper cqlMapper = CqlMapper.loadFrom("queries/user-queries.cql");
  CassandraExecutor executor = new CassandraExecutor(session, settings, cqlMapper); // settings and cqlMapper may both be null
  // Pass the mapper KEY (id) as the query; the executor resolves it via the CqlMapper:
  ResultSet rs = executor.execute("findActiveUsers"); // "findActiveUsers" is looked up in cqlMapper
  ```
- `public CassandraExecutor(final CqlSession session, final StatementSettings settings, final CqlMapper cqlMapper, final NamingPolicy namingPolicy) throws IllegalArgumentException` — Creates a new CassandraExecutor with full configuration options.
  - **Throws:**
    - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `namingPolicy` is not `SNAKE_CASE`, `SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE` or `CAMEL_CASE` (checked before `session`), or `session` is `null`
  ```java
  StatementSettings settings = StatementSettings.builder().consistency(ConsistencyLevel.QUORUM).build();
  CqlMapper cqlMapper = CqlMapper.loadFrom("queries/user-queries.cql");

  CassandraExecutor executor = new CassandraExecutor(
      session, settings, cqlMapper, NamingPolicy.SNAKE_CASE); // entity prop firstName maps to column first_name

  // All four arguments except session are optional:
  CassandraExecutor plain = new CassandraExecutor(
      session, null, null, null);                             // no settings/mapper; null namingPolicy defaults to SNAKE_CASE
  ```

#### Public Static Methods
##### registerTypeCodec(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `public static void registerTypeCodec(final MutableCodecRegistry codecRegistry, final Class<?> javaClazz) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Registers a custom type codec for the specified Java class in the given codec registry.
- **Parameters:**
  - `codecRegistry` (`MutableCodecRegistry`) — the mutable codec registry to register the codec in
  - `javaClazz` (`Class<?>`) — the Java class for which to register a type codec
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `codecRegistry` or `javaClazz` is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  MutableCodecRegistry registry = (MutableCodecRegistry) session.getContext().getCodecRegistry();
  CassandraExecutor.registerTypeCodec(registry, CustomAddress.class); // CustomAddress now (de)serializes as a JSON TEXT column

  CassandraExecutor.registerTypeCodec(registry, null);                                   // throws IllegalArgumentException (null class)
  CassandraExecutor.registerTypeCodec((MutableCodecRegistry) null, CustomAddress.class); // throws IllegalArgumentException (null registry)
  ```
##### extractData(...) -> Dataset
- **Signature:** `public static Dataset extractData(final ResultSet resultSet) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Extracts all data from a Cassandra ResultSet into a Dataset.
- **Contract:**
  - This is useful for analytical operations or when you need to work with result data in a tabular format.
  - If decoding a row fails, that row has been consumed, but later rows are not drained.
- **Parameters:**
  - `resultSet` (`ResultSet`) — the Cassandra ResultSet to extract data from
- **Returns:** a Dataset containing all rows and columns from the result set
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `resultSet` is `null`
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if fetching a remaining result page or decoding a column value fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  ResultSet resultSet = session.execute("SELECT id, name, age FROM users");
  Dataset dataset = CassandraExecutor.extractData(resultSet); // returns a Dataset with raw driver values, no type conversion
  dataset.println();                                          // Print dataset in tabular format

  CassandraExecutor.extractData((ResultSet) null); // throws IllegalArgumentException (null result set)
  ```
- **See also:** `Dataset`
- **Signature:** `public static Dataset extractData(final ResultSet resultSet, final Class<?> targetClass) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Extracts data from a Cassandra ResultSet with type-aware column mapping.
- **Contract:**
  - When a target class is provided, the method will inspect the class properties to determine appropriate column types and perform necessary conversions.
  - When `targetClass` is `null`, `Map.class` (or any `Map` subtype), or a non-bean type, scalar values retain their driver types.
  - Nested `Row` values become maps for a map target, or `Object[]` when no bean-property type is available.
  - If mapping a row fails, that row has been consumed, but later rows are not drained.
- **Parameters:**
  - `resultSet` (`ResultSet`) — the Cassandra ResultSet to extract data from
  - `targetClass` (`Class<?>`) — the entity class used to determine target column types; a map class, other non-bean class, or `null` keeps scalar driver values unchanged
- **Returns:** a Dataset with type-converted data based on the target class
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `resultSet` is `null`
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the driver fails to fetch a remaining result page, decoding a column value fails, or a column value cannot be converted to the type of the matching `targetClass` property
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  ResultSet resultSet = session.execute("SELECT id, name, age FROM users");
  Dataset dataset = CassandraExecutor.extractData(resultSet, User.class); // column values converted to User property types

  // With Map.class (or null) no per-column conversion is performed:
  ResultSet rs2 = session.execute("SELECT id, name, age FROM users");
  Dataset raw = CassandraExecutor.extractData(rs2, Map.class);            // raw driver values, no conversion

  // Edge case: a null result set throws IllegalArgumentException
  CassandraExecutor.extractData((ResultSet) null, User.class); // throws IllegalArgumentException
  ```
##### toList(...) -> List<T>
- **Signature:** `public static <T> List<T> toList(final ResultSet resultSet, final Class<T> targetClass) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Converts a Cassandra ResultSet to a typed List of objects.
- **Contract:**
  - For raw-row targets, the list returned by `ResultSet#all()` is returned unchanged: when no row remains, that is the driver's immutable empty list (`Collections.emptyList()`), and otherwise a new mutable list of the remaining rows.
  - Other targets are mapped as pages are consumed, without first collecting the driver rows (into a new mutable list, also when empty).
  - If mapping a row fails, that row has been consumed, but later rows are not drained.
- **Parameters:**
  - `resultSet` (`ResultSet`) — the Cassandra ResultSet to convert
  - `targetClass` (`Class<T>`) — the target type each row is converted to (entity class, `Map.class`, `Row.class`, an object array class, a collection class, or a basic single-value type, including a primitive array class); must not be `null`
- **Returns:** a List containing all rows converted to the specified type
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `resultSet` or `targetClass` is `null`, if `targetClass` is a single-value type but the result set does not have exactly one column, or if a map or collection `targetClass` rejects a column value (a `NULL` column in a `ConcurrentHashMap` or an `ArrayBlockingQueue`, for example)
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the driver fails to fetch a remaining result page, a column value cannot be converted to the requested Java type, a bean property cannot be read or written, or a bean cannot be created (see `#toEntity(Row, Class)`)
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  ResultSet resultSet = session.execute("SELECT id, name, email FROM users");

  // Convert to entity list
  List<User> users = CassandraExecutor.toList(resultSet, User.class); // one User per row

  // Convert to map list (a ResultSet is single-pass, so re-execute rather than reuse 'resultSet')
  ResultSet resultSet2 = session.execute("SELECT id, name, email FROM users");
  List<Map> userMaps = CassandraExecutor.toList(resultSet2, Map.class); // one Map<String,Object> per row

  // Convert single column to value list
  ResultSet names = session.execute("SELECT name FROM users");
  List<String> nameList = CassandraExecutor.toList(names, String.class); // one String per row

  // Single-value type but multiple columns selected -> error
  ResultSet multi = session.execute("SELECT id, name FROM users");
  CassandraExecutor.toList(multi, String.class); // throws IllegalArgumentException (more than one column)

  // Edge case: a null result set throws IllegalArgumentException
  CassandraExecutor.toList((ResultSet) null, User.class); // throws IllegalArgumentException
  ```
##### toEntity(...) -> T
- **Signature:** `public static <T> T toEntity(final Row row, final Class<T> entityClass) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Converts a single Cassandra Row to an entity object.
- **Contract:**
  - The method handles: Direct mapping: Column names matching property names exactly Name variants: a column name also matches a property case-insensitively or in its snake_case form (e.g., `first_name` to `firstName`), as the bean metadata resolves it, or by the property's declared `@Column` name (see `QueryUtil#columnToPropNameMap(Class)`); no executor naming policy is involved, since this method is static Nested properties: Dot-notation property paths (e.g., `"address.city"`) when no direct property is found; the value is converted for the path's last property as a top-level column value is, and a path that does not resolve, or whose last property is read-only, is ignored.
  - A missing intermediate bean is created through its no-argument constructor and assigned first, and the value is written into the instance its owner then holds (the created one when the getter returns a new copy on every read), so a setter that stores a copy of its argument keeps the value Type conversion: Automatic conversion between compatible types (see the class documentation for the `timestamp`, `date`, `inet` and `blob` rules; a `blob` read into a `String` property is the base64 text of its bytes, one read into a property declared as a collection of an element type is that collection of the blob converted to the element type, one read into an `Optional`, `Nullable` or `Holder` property is that wrapper of the blob converted to its element type (an `Optional<ByteBuffer>` the buffer, a `Nullable<byte[]>` its bytes), and one read into a number, date/time, `UUID` or other property without a blob form fails the row), for top-level and nested properties alike.
  - A collection or map column read into a property declared as a parameterized collection or map (for example `List<byte[]>` or `Map<String, String>`) or as an object array has each element, key and value converted by the same rules for the declared element type, nested containers included (a `list<timestamp>` into a `List<LocalDateTime>`, a `set<inet>` into a `Set<String>`); the driver's collection is set unchanged when every element already has its declared type, and otherwise a new one of the declared kind holding the converted elements in the driver's order.
- **Parameters:**
  - `row` (`Row`) — the Cassandra Row containing the data
  - `entityClass` (`Class<T>`) — the target entity class with getter/setter methods (must not be `null`)
- **Returns:** a new instance of the entity class populated with row data
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `row` or `entityClass` is `null`, or `entityClass` is not a bean class (it has no property getter/setter methods or public fields, or it is a `Map` type, including an `@Entity`-annotated `Map` subclass; use `#toMap(Row, IntFunction)` for a map)
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if a column value cannot be converted to the requested Java type or a bean property cannot be read or written, or the entity cannot be created: an `UnsupportedOperationException` for a class with neither a no-argument constructor, a builder, nor a constructor taking all its properties, and an `IllegalArgumentException` for a dotted column whose intermediate property is unset and of a class without a no-argument constructor (such as a record)
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  ResultSet resultSet = session.execute("SELECT id, name, email FROM users WHERE id = ?", userId);
  Row row = resultSet.one();

  if (row != null) {
      User user = CassandraExecutor.toEntity(row, User.class); // returns a populated User (never null for a non-null row)
      System.out.println("User: " + user.getName());
  }

  // For nested properties (if supported by entity structure)
  // Column 'address.street' maps to user.getAddress().setStreet(value)

  // Edge case: a null row throws IllegalArgumentException
  CassandraExecutor.toEntity((Row) null, User.class); // throws IllegalArgumentException

  // Edge case: a null entity class is rejected as an illegal argument
  CassandraExecutor.toEntity(row, (Class<User>) null); // throws IllegalArgumentException ('entityClass' cannot be null)
  ```
##### toMap(...) -> Map<String, Object>
- **Signature:** `public static Map<String, Object> toMap(final Row row) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Converts a Cassandra Row to a Map with column names as keys.
- **Parameters:**
  - `row` (`Row`) — the Cassandra Row to convert
- **Returns:** a Map containing all column names and values from the row
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `row` is `null`
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if reading the row metadata or decoding a column value fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  ResultSet resultSet = session.execute("SELECT id, name, email, address FROM users WHERE id = ?", userId);
  Row row = resultSet.one();

  if (row != null) {
      Map<String, Object> userMap = CassandraExecutor.toMap(row); // returns a HashMap of column name -> value (column order NOT preserved)
      System.out.println("User ID: " + userMap.get("id"));
      System.out.println("Name: " + userMap.get("name"));

      // Only nested Row values are recursively converted to nested Maps
      // (a UDT column surfaces as a UdtValue and is kept as-is).
  }

  CassandraExecutor.toMap((Row) null); // throws IllegalArgumentException (null row)
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static Map<String, Object> toMap(final Row row, final IntFunction<? extends Map<String, Object>> supplier) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException, NullPointerException`
- **Summary:** Converts a Cassandra Row to a Map using a custom Map supplier.
- **Contract:**
  - This is useful when you need specific Map characteristics like ordering (LinkedHashMap) or concurrent access (ConcurrentHashMap, which rejects a `NULL` column with `IllegalArgumentException`).
- **Parameters:**
  - `row` (`Row`) — the Cassandra Row to convert
  - `supplier` (`IntFunction<? extends Map<String, Object>>`) — a function that creates a new Map instance with the specified initial capacity
- **Returns:** a Map of the specified type containing all column names and values from the row
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `row` or `supplier` is `null`, or the supplied map rejects a column entry (a `NULL` column in a `ConcurrentHashMap` or `Hashtable`, for example), with the map's exception as the cause
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if reading the row metadata, creating a map with `supplier`, decoding a column value, or adding a column entry to the supplied map fails
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if `supplier` returns `null` for a nonempty row
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  ResultSet resultSet = session.execute("SELECT id, name, email FROM users WHERE id = ?", userId);
  Row row = resultSet.one();

  if (row != null) {
      // Use LinkedHashMap to preserve column order
      Map<String, Object> orderedMap = CassandraExecutor.toMap(row, size -> new LinkedHashMap<>()); // column order preserved

      // Use TreeMap for sorted keys
      Map<String, Object> sortedMap = CassandraExecutor.toMap(row, size -> new TreeMap<>());        // keys sorted

      // Use specific initial capacity
      Map<String, Object> sizedMap = CassandraExecutor.toMap(row, HashMap::new);                    // HashMap sized to column count
  }

  CassandraExecutor.toMap((Row) null, size -> new HashMap<>()); // throws IllegalArgumentException (null row)
  ```

#### Public Instance Methods
##### session(...) -> CqlSession
- **Signature:** `public CqlSession session()`
- **Summary:** Returns the underlying Cassandra session used by this executor.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the Cassandra session instance
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  CqlSession session = executor.session(); // returns the underlying CqlSession (never null)
  Metadata metadata = session.getMetadata();
  metadata.getKeyspaces().forEach((name, ks) -> System.out.println("Keyspace: " + name));
  ```
##### async(...) -> AsyncCassandraExecutor
- **Signature:** `public AsyncCassandraExecutor async()`
- **Summary:** Returns an asynchronous facade for this executor.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the `AsyncCassandraExecutor` bound to this executor's session
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  AsyncCassandraExecutor async = executor.async(); // returns the same facade on every call (executor.async() == executor.async())

  ContinuableFuture<List<User>> future = async.list(User.class,
      "SELECT * FROM users WHERE status = ?", "active"); // non-blocking; resolve with future.get()
  ```
##### registerTypeCodec(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `public void registerTypeCodec(final Class<?> javaClazz) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Registers a custom type codec for the specified Java class.
- **Parameters:**
  - `javaClazz` (`Class<?>`) — the Java class for which to register a type codec
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the session exposes a read-only codec registry (checked before `javaClazz`)
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `javaClazz` is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Register codec for custom class
  executor.registerTypeCodec(Address.class); // Address now (de)serializes as a JSON TEXT column

  // Now Address objects can be used directly in CQL operations
  User user = new User();
  user.setAddress(new Address("123 Main St", "City", "12345"));
  executor.insert(user);   // Address will be automatically serialized

  executor.registerTypeCodec(null); // throws IllegalArgumentException (null class)
  ```
- **See also:** `#registerTypeCodec(MutableCodecRegistry, Class)`
##### gett(...) -> T
- **Signature:** `public <T> T gett(final Class<T> targetClass, final Collection<String> selectPropNames, final Condition whereClause) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException, DuplicateResultException`
- **Summary:** Retrieves at most one entity matching the given WHERE condition (the "get-typed" contract).
- **Contract:**
  - If no row matches, returns `null`.
  - If two or more rows match, a `DuplicateResultException` is thrown.
- **Parameters:**
  - `targetClass` (`Class<T>`) — the entity class to map the result row to
  - `selectPropNames` (`Collection<String>`) — the property names to select, or `null` to select all entity properties
  - `whereClause` (`Condition`) — the WHERE condition
- **Returns:** an instance of `targetClass` populated with data from the single matching row, or `null` when no row matches
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetClass` is `null`, the selected properties cannot be mapped, `whereClause` contains a relation unsupported by CQL, or a condition value is rejected when converted to its column's type (see Number and Blob Conversion in the class documentation)
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if preparing, binding, executing, or fetching the CQL fails; or a returned column cannot be converted to the requested Java type or assigned to a mapped bean property
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.DuplicateResultException` — if more than one row matches the WHERE condition
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if `whereClause` already carries a `LIMIT` (this method appends its own `LIMIT 2`; see Row Limits in `CassandraExecutorBase`)
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Find user by email (selecting all properties)
  User user = executor.gett(User.class, null, Filters.eq("email", email)); // returns the single matching User, or null if none

  // Select only specific properties
  User partial = executor.gett(User.class, Arrays.asList("id", "name"), Filters.eq("id", userId)); // only id and name populated

  // If more than one row matches the condition:
  executor.gett(User.class, null, Filters.eq("status", "active")); // throws DuplicateResultException when >1 match
  ```
##### queryForSingleValue(...) -> Nullable<V>
- **Signature:** `public <V> Nullable<V> queryForSingleValue(final Class<V> valueClass, final String query, final Object... parameters) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Executes the given CQL query and returns the first column of the first row converted to `valueClass`.
- **Contract:**
  - present semantics: `Nullable.empty()` is returned only when the query produces no rows.
  - If a row exists but the column is `NULL`, a wrapper or other reference `valueClass` yields a present-but-null `Nullable` (`Nullable.of(null)`).
- **Parameters:**
  - `valueClass` (`Class<V>`) — the Java class the column value is converted to (must not be `null`)
  - `query` (`String`) — the CQL query string with `?` placeholders for parameters
  - `parameters` (`Object...`) — the values to bind, in declaration order
- **Returns:** a present `Nullable<V>` holding the converted column value (for a `NULL` column, the default value of `valueClass`: the primitive default, the empty value of an `Optional`-like type, or `null`) when at least one row is returned; `Nullable.empty()` when the query returns no rows
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `valueClass` or `query` is `null`, the CQL contains malformed or mixed parameter markers, the supplied parameter count or names do not match the prepared statement, or a parameter value is rejected when converted to its column's type (see Number and Blob Conversion in the class documentation)
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if preparing, binding, executing, or fetching the CQL fails; or a returned column cannot be converted to the requested Java type or assigned to a mapped bean property
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Nullable<Long> userCount = executor.queryForSingleValue(
      Long.class, "SELECT count(*) FROM users"); // present Nullable holding the count

  // No rows matched -> Nullable.empty()
  Nullable<String> userName = executor.queryForSingleValue(
      String.class, "SELECT name FROM users WHERE id = ?", unknownId); // returns Nullable.empty() when no row matches

  // Row matched but column is NULL -> present-but-null (NOT empty)
  Nullable<String> nick = executor.queryForSingleValue(
      String.class, "SELECT nickname FROM users WHERE id = ?", userId); // Nullable.of(null) when the row exists but column is NULL
  ```
- **See also:** `#queryForSingleNonNull(Class, String, Object...)`
##### queryForSingleNonNull(...) -> Optional<V>
- **Signature:** `public <V> Optional<V> queryForSingleNonNull(final Class<V> valueClass, final String query, final Object... parameters) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException, NullPointerException`
- **Summary:** Executes the given CQL query and returns the first column of the first row converted to `valueClass`, wrapped in an `Optional` that is guaranteed to be non-null when present.
- **Contract:**
  - present semantics: `Optional.empty()` is returned only when the query produces no rows.
  - When a row is returned, the converted column value is wrapped in the `Optional` via `Optional#of(Object)`, which does not accept a null payload.
  - If conversion to `valueClass` yields `null`, this method throws `NullPointerException` rather than returning `Optional.empty()`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `valueClass` (`Class<V>`) — the Java class the column value is converted to (must not be `null`)
  - `query` (`String`) — the CQL query string with `?` placeholders for parameters
  - `parameters` (`Object...`) — the values to bind, in declaration order
- **Returns:** a present `Optional<V>` holding the converted non-null value when at least one row is returned; `Optional.empty()` when the query returns no rows
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `valueClass` or `query` is `null`, the CQL contains malformed or mixed parameter markers, the supplied parameter count or names do not match the prepared statement, or a parameter value is rejected when converted to its column's type (see Number and Blob Conversion in the class documentation)
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if preparing, binding, executing, or fetching the CQL fails; or a returned column cannot be converted to the requested Java type or assigned to a mapped bean property
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if a row is returned but the converted column value is `null`, because `Optional#of(Object)` rejects a null payload
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Optional<Long> activeUsers = executor.queryForSingleNonNull(
      Long.class, "SELECT count(*) FROM users WHERE status = 'active'"); // present Optional holding the count

  Optional<String> email = executor.queryForSingleNonNull(
      String.class, "SELECT email FROM users WHERE id = ?", userId); // present Optional holding the email

  // No rows matched -> Optional.empty()
  Optional<String> none = executor.queryForSingleNonNull(
      String.class, "SELECT email FROM users WHERE id = ?", unknownId); // returns Optional.empty() when no row matches

  // Row matched but column is NULL -> throws (Optional cannot hold null)
  executor.queryForSingleNonNull(String.class,
      "SELECT nickname FROM users WHERE id = ?", userId); // throws NullPointerException when the matched value is NULL
  ```
- **See also:** `#queryForSingleValue(Class, String, Object...)`
##### findFirst(...) -> Optional<T>
- **Signature:** `public <T> Optional<T> findFirst(final Class<T> targetClass, final String query, final Object... parameters) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException, NullPointerException`
- **Summary:** Executes the given CQL query and returns the first row mapped to an instance of `targetClass`.
- **Contract:**
  - present semantics: `Optional.empty()` is returned only when the query produces no rows.
  - When a row is found, the mapped value is returned as a present `Optional`.
  - Because `Optional` cannot carry a `null` payload, the mapped value itself must be non-null.
- **Parameters:**
  - `targetClass` (`Class<T>`) — an entity class with getter/setter methods, `Map.class`, a collection, an object array class, or a single-value type (must not be `null`)
  - `query` (`String`) — the CQL query string with `?` placeholders for parameters
  - `parameters` (`Object...`) — the values to bind, in declaration order
- **Returns:** a present `Optional<T>` holding the first mapped row when at least one row is returned; `Optional.empty()` when the query returns no rows
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetClass` or `query` is `null`, the CQL contains malformed or mixed parameter markers, the supplied parameter count or names do not match the prepared statement, a parameter value is rejected when converted to its column's type (see Number and Blob Conversion in the class documentation), `targetClass` is a single-value type but the first row does not have exactly one column, or a map or collection `targetClass` rejects a column value (a `NULL` column in a `ConcurrentHashMap` or an `ArrayBlockingQueue`, for example)
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if preparing, binding, executing, or fetching the CQL fails; or a returned column cannot be converted to the requested Java type or assigned to a mapped bean property
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if the first row maps to a null value, which `Optional#of(Object)` cannot contain
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Optional<User> user = executor.findFirst(User.class,
      "SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = ? LIMIT 1", email); // present Optional with the first matching User

  // No rows matched -> Optional.empty()
  Optional<User> none = executor.findFirst(User.class,
      "SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = ?", unknownEmail); // returns Optional.empty() when no row matches

  Optional<Map> userData = executor.findFirst(Map.class,
      "SELECT name, email FROM users WHERE id = ?", userId); // present Optional holding a Map of the row

  Optional<Object[]> row = executor.findFirst(Object[].class,
      "SELECT count(*), max(created_at) FROM events"); // present Optional holding an Object[] of the columns
  ```
- **See also:** `#findFirst(String, Object...)`, `#findFirst(Class, Condition)`
##### stream(...) -> Stream<T>
- **Signature:** `public <T> Stream<T> stream(final String query, final BiFunction<ColumnDefinitions, Row, T> rowMapper, final Object... parameters) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Executes a CQL query and returns a Stream with a custom row mapper.
- **Parameters:**
  - `query` (`String`) — the CQL query string
  - `rowMapper` (`BiFunction<ColumnDefinitions, Row, T>`) — a function that maps column definitions and rows to result objects
  - `parameters` (`Object...`) — the query parameters
- **Returns:** a Stream of mapped objects
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `query` or `rowMapper` is `null`, the CQL contains malformed or mixed parameter markers, the supplied parameter count or names do not match the prepared statement, or a parameter value is rejected when converted to its column's type (see Number and Blob Conversion in the class documentation)
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the driver rejects CQL or a bound value, the session is closed, or preparing, executing, or fetching the query fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Custom mapping with column inspection
  BiFunction<ColumnDefinitions, Row, UserSummary> mapper = (columns, row) -> {
      UserSummary summary = new UserSummary();

      for (int i = 0; i < columns.size(); i++) {
          String columnName = columns.get(i).getName().asInternal();
          Object value = row.getObject(i);

          // Custom logic based on column names and values
          switch (columnName) {
              case "full_name" -> summary.setDisplayName((String) value);
              case "created_at" -> summary.setAge(calculateAge((Instant) value));
              case "status" -> summary.setActive("active".equals(value));
          }
      }
      return summary;
  };

  try (Stream<UserSummary> summaries = executor.stream(
          "SELECT full_name, created_at, status FROM users WHERE department = ?",
          mapper, "engineering")) {

      List<UserSummary> activeSummaries = summaries
          .filter(UserSummary::isActive)
          .toList();
  }

  // A null rowMapper is rejected eagerly
  executor.stream("SELECT * FROM users", (BiFunction<ColumnDefinitions, Row, User>) null); // throws IllegalArgumentException
  ```
- **See also:** `#stream(Class, String, Object...)`
- **Signature:** `public <T> Stream<T> stream(final Statement<?> statement, final BiFunction<ColumnDefinitions, Row, T> rowMapper) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Executes a pre-configured CQL Statement and returns a Stream with a custom row mapper.
- **Contract:**
  - This is useful when you need fine-grained control over statement configuration (consistency levels, timeouts, etc.) or when working with complex prepared statements.
- **Parameters:**
  - `statement` (`Statement<?>`) — the configured CQL Statement to execute
  - `rowMapper` (`BiFunction<ColumnDefinitions, Row, T>`) — a function that maps column definitions and rows to result objects
- **Returns:** a Stream of mapped objects
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `statement` or `rowMapper` is `null`
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the session is closed or the driver rejects request submission or statement execution
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Create a custom statement with specific settings
  PreparedStatement preparedStatement = session.prepare(
      "SELECT id, name, last_login FROM users WHERE status = ?");

  BoundStatement statement = preparedStatement.bind("active")
      .setConsistencyLevel(ConsistencyLevel.LOCAL_QUORUM)
      .setTimeout(Duration.ofSeconds(30));

  // Custom mapper for user activity analysis
  BiFunction<ColumnDefinitions, Row, UserActivity> mapper = (columns, row) -> {
      UUID id = row.getUuid("id");
      String name = row.getString("name");
      Instant lastLogin = row.getInstant("last_login");

      return new UserActivity(id, name,
          lastLogin != null ? Duration.between(lastLogin, Instant.now()) : null);
  };

  try (Stream<UserActivity> activities = executor.stream(statement, mapper)) {
      activities.filter(activity -> activity.getDaysSinceLogin() > 30)
               .forEach(System.out::println);
  }

  // A null rowMapper is rejected eagerly
  executor.stream(statement, (BiFunction<ColumnDefinitions, Row, UserActivity>) null); // throws IllegalArgumentException
  ```
##### execute(...) -> ResultSet
- **Signature:** `public ResultSet execute(final String query) throws IllegalArgumentException, AllNodesFailedException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Executes a CQL statement without parameters and returns the raw ResultSet.
- **Contract:**
  - This is useful for DDL operations, simple queries without parameters, or when you need direct access to the ResultSet for custom processing.
- **Parameters:**
  - `query` (`String`) — the CQL statement to execute
- **Returns:** the raw ResultSet from Cassandra
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `query` is `null`, the CQL contains malformed or mixed parameter markers, or the supplied parameter count or names do not match the prepared statement
  - `com.datastax.oss.driver.api.core.AllNodesFailedException` — if every node tried by the driver fails to execute the request
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the driver rejects CQL or a bound value, the session is closed, or preparing, executing, or fetching the query fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Create table
  executor.execute("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (id UUID PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT)");

  // Simple query
  ResultSet results = executor.execute("SELECT * FROM users LIMIT 10");

  // Process results manually
  for (Row row : results) {
      UUID id = row.getUuid("id");
      String name = row.getString("name");
      // Process row...
  }
  ```
- **Signature:** `public ResultSet execute(final String query, final Object... parameters) throws IllegalArgumentException, AllNodesFailedException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Executes a parameterized CQL statement and returns the raw ResultSet.
- **Parameters:**
  - `query` (`String`) — the parameterized CQL statement
  - `parameters` (`Object...`) — the parameter values (can be individual values, arrays, collections, maps, or entities)
- **Returns:** the raw ResultSet from Cassandra
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `query` is `null`, the CQL contains malformed or mixed parameter markers, the supplied parameter count or names do not match the prepared statement, or a parameter value is rejected when converted to its column's type (see Number and Blob Conversion in the class documentation)
  - `com.datastax.oss.driver.api.core.AllNodesFailedException` — if every node tried by the driver fails to execute the request
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the driver rejects CQL or a bound value, the session is closed, or preparing, executing, or fetching the query fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Positional parameters
  ResultSet users = executor.execute(
      "SELECT * FROM users WHERE status = ? AND created_at > ?",
      "active", yesterday);

  // Named parameters with map
  Map<String, Object> params = new HashMap<>();
  params.put("email", "john@example.com");
  params.put("status", "active");
  ResultSet result = executor.execute(
      "SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = :email AND status = :status", params);

  // Entity parameters
  User searchCriteria = new User();
  searchCriteria.setStatus("active");
  searchCriteria.setDepartment("engineering");
  ResultSet engineeringUsers = executor.execute(
      "SELECT * FROM users WHERE status = :status AND department = :department",
      searchCriteria);
  ```
- **Signature:** `public ResultSet execute(final String query, final Map<String, Object> parameters) throws IllegalArgumentException, AllNodesFailedException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Executes a CQL statement with named parameters provided as a Map.
- **Contract:**
  - The parameter names in the query should match the keys in the provided Map.
- **Parameters:**
  - `query` (`String`) — the parameterized CQL statement
  - `parameters` (`Map<String, Object>`) — the query parameters
- **Returns:** the raw ResultSet from Cassandra
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `query` is `null`, the CQL contains malformed or mixed parameter markers, the supplied parameter count or names do not match the prepared statement, or a parameter value is rejected when converted to its column's type (see Number and Blob Conversion in the class documentation)
  - `com.datastax.oss.driver.api.core.AllNodesFailedException` — if every node tried by the driver fails to execute the request
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the driver rejects CQL or a bound value, the session is closed, or preparing, executing, or fetching the query fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Query with named parameters
  String query = "SELECT * FROM users WHERE department = :dept AND status = :status AND created_at > :since";

  Map<String, Object> params = new HashMap<>();
  params.put("dept", "engineering");
  params.put("status", "active");
  params.put("since", Instant.now().minus(Duration.ofDays(30)));

  ResultSet results = executor.execute(query, params);

  // Alternative using N.asMap utility
  ResultSet results2 = executor.execute(
      "SELECT * FROM orders WHERE user_id = :userId AND status = :status",
      N.asMap("userId", UUID.fromString("123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000"),
              "status", "pending"));
  ```
- **Signature:** `public ResultSet execute(final Statement<?> statement) throws IllegalArgumentException, AllNodesFailedException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Executes a pre-configured CQL Statement and returns the raw ResultSet.
- **Contract:**
  - This provides maximum flexibility when you need fine-grained control over statement configuration such as consistency levels, timeouts, or the execution profile.
- **Parameters:**
  - `statement` (`Statement<?>`) — the configured CQL Statement to execute
- **Returns:** the raw ResultSet from Cassandra
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `statement` is `null`
  - `com.datastax.oss.driver.api.core.AllNodesFailedException` — if every node tried by the driver fails to execute the request
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the session is closed or the driver rejects request submission or statement execution
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Execute a prepared statement with custom settings
  PreparedStatement preparedStatement = session.prepare(
      "INSERT INTO users (id, name, email) VALUES (?, ?, ?)");

  BoundStatement boundStatement = preparedStatement
      .bind(UUID.randomUUID(), "John Doe", "john@example.com")
      .setConsistencyLevel(ConsistencyLevel.QUORUM)
      .setTimeout(Duration.ofSeconds(10));

  ResultSet result = executor.execute(boundStatement);

  // Execute a batch statement
  BatchStatement batch = BatchStatement.newInstance(BatchType.LOGGED)
      .add(statement1)
      .add(statement2)
      .add(statement3);

  ResultSet batchResult = executor.execute(batch);

  // Execute a simple statement with custom settings
  SimpleStatement simpleStatement = SimpleStatement.builder(
          "SELECT * FROM users WHERE token(id) > token(?)")
      .addPositionalValue(lastId)
      .setPageSize(1000)
      .build();

  ResultSet pagedResults = executor.execute(simpleStatement);
  ```
##### close(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `public void close() throws RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Closes this executor and releases all associated resources.
- **Contract:**
  - After calling this method, the executor should not be used for further database operations.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the driver rejects closing the session (for example, when called on a driver I/O thread) or closing it fails; the prepared-statement cache is released in either case
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  CassandraExecutor executor = new CassandraExecutor(session);
  try {
      // Perform database operations
  } finally {
      executor.close();
  }
  ```

### Class UDTCodec (com.landawn.abacus.da.cassandra.CassandraExecutor.UDTCodec)
Abstract base class for creating custom User Defined Type (UDT) codecs.

**Thread-safety:** unspecified
**Nullability:** unspecified
**Implements:** `TypeCodec<T>`

#### Public Constructors
- (none)

#### Public Static Methods
##### create(...) -> UDTCodec<T>
- **Signature:** `public static <T> UDTCodec<T> create(final UserDefinedType userType, final Class<T> javaClazz) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates a new instance of a UDTCodec for the specified User Defined Type (UDT) and Java class.
- **Contract:**
  - When `javaClazz` is a `Collection` type, values are mapped positionally in UDT field order.
  - When `javaClazz` is a `Map` type, a value is written from the entries keyed by the exact (internal) field names, a missing field being written as `null` and other entries ignored, and decodes to a map keyed by the field names.
  - When it is a bean class, each field is bound to the property of that name (matched case-insensitively or in its snake_case form, as `CassandraExecutor#toEntity(Row, Class)` matches a column) or to the property declaring it as its `@Column` name.
  - A field without a matching property is written as `null` and ignored when decoding; a read-only (for example getter-only) property is written from its getter but ignored when decoding.
  - An entity property that holds a bean value of this codec (or a collection of them) must be annotated with `@Column` for the entity operations to write and read it: a bean-typed property without it is a sub-entity, which an entity `insert` or `update` and a query selecting all properties leave out without an error (see Entity-to-CQL mapping in `CassandraExecutorBase`).
  - If no registered codec accepts a `Date` or `Calendar` value, it is converted to `LocalTime` the same way ordinary parameter binding converts it.
  - Dates use the JVM default zone captured when Abacus's `com.landawn.abacus.type.AbstractTemporalType` is initialized; calendars use their own zone.
  - The `java.time` date-time types are not accepted when writing a TIME field unless a registered codec accepts them.
  - If no registered codec accepts another value, it is converted to an `Instant` as a value bound to a `timestamp` column is: a `LocalDateTime` or `LocalDate` in the JVM default zone (a `LocalDate` as the start of that day), a `ZonedDateTime` or `OffsetDateTime` as the instant it denotes, a `Date` (including `java.sql.Timestamp`) or `Calendar` as its instant, a `Long` as epoch milliseconds, and ISO-8601 instant text; a value that conversion rejects fails with the driver's `CodecNotFoundException`.
  - Usage Examples: The returned codec rejects unsupported Java types and collections with more elements than UDT fields when encoding or decoding a non-null value.
- **Parameters:**
  - `userType` (`UserDefinedType`) — the Cassandra User Defined Type to map
  - `javaClazz` (`Class<T>`) — the Java class to map the UDT to
- **Returns:** a new instance of `UDTCodec` for the specified UDT and Java class
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `javaClazz` is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  UserDefinedType userType = session.getMetadata()
      .getKeyspace("my_keyspace")
      .flatMap(ks -> ks.getUserDefinedType("my_udt"))
      .orElseThrow(() -> new IllegalArgumentException("UDT not found"));

  UDTCodec<MyClass> codec = UDTCodec.create(userType, MyClass.class); // returns a codec marshaling MyClass to/from the UDT
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static <T> UDTCodec<T> create(final Session session, final String keySpace, final String userTypeName, final Class<T> javaClazz) throws IllegalArgumentException, NoSuchElementException`
- **Summary:** Creates a new instance of a UDTCodec for the specified User Defined Type (UDT) and Java class.
- **Parameters:**
  - `session` (`Session`) — the Cassandra Session to use for metadata retrieval
  - `keySpace` (`String`) — the keyspace containing the UDT
  - `userTypeName` (`String`) — the name of the User Defined Type (UDT)
  - `javaClazz` (`Class<T>`) — the Java class to map the UDT to
- **Returns:** a new instance of `UDTCodec` for the specified UDT and Java class
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `session`, `keySpace`, `userTypeName`, or `javaClazz` is `null`, or `keySpace` or `userTypeName` is an unquoted CQL identifier that requires double quotes
  - `java.util.NoSuchElementException` — if `keySpace` or the named user type cannot be found in the session metadata
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  UDTCodec<MyClass> codec = UDTCodec.create(session, "my_keyspace", "my_udt", MyClass.class); // resolves the UDT via session metadata
  // throws NoSuchElementException if the keyspace or the UDT does not exist (orElseThrow)
  ```

#### Public Instance Methods
##### serialize(...) -> ByteBuffer
- **Signature:** `@Deprecated public ByteBuffer serialize(final T value, final ProtocolVersion protocolVersion) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecNotFoundException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Serializes the given value to a ByteBuffer using the UDT codec.
- **Deprecated:** yes — Use `#encode(Object, ProtocolVersion)` instead.
- **Parameters:**
  - `value` (`T`) — the value to serialize
  - `protocolVersion` (`ProtocolVersion`) — the protocol version to use for serialization
- **Returns:** a ByteBuffer containing the serialized value, or `null` for a `null` value
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the non-null value cannot be mapped to this UDT, including an unsupported Java type, a collection with more elements than UDT fields, or text for a `blob` field that is not valid base64
  - `com.datastax.oss.driver.api.core.type.codec.CodecNotFoundException` — if neither a registered codec nor a supported BLOB, TIME or TIMESTAMP conversion can map a non-null field value to its CQL type, or a field codec reports a missing codec while serializing
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if mapping the non-null value invokes a failing bean accessor, cannot create the target Java object, or a field codec rejects a value
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  UDTCodec<Address> codec = UDTCodec.create(addressUserType, Address.class);

  ByteBuffer bytes = codec.serialize(new Address("123 Main St"), ProtocolVersion.V4); // delegates to encode(...)

  ByteBuffer none = codec.serialize(null, ProtocolVersion.V4);                        // returns null for a null value
  ```
##### deserialize(...) -> T
- **Signature:** `@Deprecated public T deserialize(final ByteBuffer bytes, final ProtocolVersion protocolVersion) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Deserializes the given ByteBuffer to a value using the UDT codec.
- **Deprecated:** yes — Use `#decode(ByteBuffer, ProtocolVersion)` instead.
- **Parameters:**
  - `bytes` (`ByteBuffer`) — the ByteBuffer containing the serialized value
  - `protocolVersion` (`ProtocolVersion`) — the protocol version to use for deserialization
- **Returns:** the deserialized value, or `null` for a `null` payload
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the input cannot be decoded as this UDT or the non-null UDT cannot be mapped to the configured Java type
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if mapping the non-null value invokes a failing bean accessor, cannot create the target Java object, or a field codec rejects a value
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  UDTCodec<Address> codec = UDTCodec.create(addressUserType, Address.class);

  ByteBuffer bytes = codec.encode(new Address("123 Main St"), ProtocolVersion.V4);
  Address address = codec.deserialize(bytes, ProtocolVersion.V4); // delegates to decode(...); reconstructs the Address

  Address none = codec.deserialize(null, ProtocolVersion.V4);     // returns null for a null payload
  ```
##### encode(...) -> ByteBuffer
- **Signature:** `public ByteBuffer encode(final T value, final ProtocolVersion protocolVersion) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecNotFoundException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Encodes the given value to a ByteBuffer using the UDT codec.
- **Parameters:**
  - `value` (`T`) — the value to encode: a `T`, or a raw `UdtValue` of this codec's user type passed by caller code that resolved this codec by CQL type itself
  - `protocolVersion` (`ProtocolVersion`) — the protocol version to use for encoding
- **Returns:** a ByteBuffer containing the encoded value, or `null` for a `null` value
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the non-null value cannot be mapped to this UDT, including an unsupported Java type, a collection with more elements than UDT fields, or text for a `blob` field that is not valid base64
  - `com.datastax.oss.driver.api.core.type.codec.CodecNotFoundException` — if neither a registered codec nor a supported BLOB, TIME or TIMESTAMP conversion can map a non-null field value to its CQL type, or a field codec reports a missing codec while serializing
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if mapping the non-null value invokes a failing bean accessor, cannot create the target Java object, or a field codec rejects a value
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  UDTCodec<Address> codec = UDTCodec.create(addressUserType, Address.class);

  ByteBuffer bytes = codec.encode(new Address("123 Main St"), ProtocolVersion.V4); // returns the UDT binary form

  ByteBuffer none = codec.encode(null, ProtocolVersion.V4);                        // returns null for a null value
  ```
##### decode(...) -> T
- **Signature:** `public T decode(final ByteBuffer bytes, final ProtocolVersion protocolVersion) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Decodes the given ByteBuffer to a value using the UDT codec.
- **Parameters:**
  - `bytes` (`ByteBuffer`) — the ByteBuffer containing the serialized value
  - `protocolVersion` (`ProtocolVersion`) — the protocol version to use for decoding
- **Returns:** the deserialized value, or `null` for a `null` payload
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the input cannot be decoded as this UDT or the non-null UDT cannot be mapped to the configured Java type
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if mapping the non-null value invokes a failing bean accessor, cannot create the target Java object, or a field codec rejects a value
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  UDTCodec<Address> codec = UDTCodec.create(addressUserType, Address.class);

  ByteBuffer bytes = codec.encode(new Address("123 Main St"), ProtocolVersion.V4);
  Address address = codec.decode(bytes, ProtocolVersion.V4); // returns the reconstructed Address

  Address none = codec.decode(null, ProtocolVersion.V4);     // returns null for a null payload
  ```
##### parse(...) -> T
- **Signature:** `public T parse(final String value) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Parses a CQL UDT literal into a Java object of type `T`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `value` (`String`) — the CQL UDT literal to parse
- **Returns:** an instance of type `T`, or `null` if the input is empty or equal (case-insensitively) to `CassandraExecutorBase#NULL_STR`
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the input cannot be decoded as this UDT or the non-null UDT cannot be mapped to the configured Java type
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if mapping the non-null value invokes a failing bean accessor, cannot create the target Java object, or a field codec rejects a value
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  UDTCodec<Address> codec = UDTCodec.create(addressUserType, Address.class);

  Address a = codec.parse("{street:'123 Main St'}"); // returns the parsed Address

  Address empty = codec.parse("");     // returns null (empty input)
  Address nullS = codec.parse("NULL"); // returns null (the "NULL" sentinel)
  Address nullV = codec.parse(null);   // returns null (null input)
  ```
##### format(...) -> String
- **Signature:** `public String format(final T value) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecNotFoundException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Formats the given value as a CQL UDT literal.
- **Contract:**
  - If the value is null, this method returns `CassandraExecutorBase#NULL_STR`.
  - A driver `UdtValue`, which reaches this codec when it is looked up by CQL type only (`CodecRegistry.codecFor(DataType)`), is formatted as is by the driver's UDT codec.
- **Parameters:**
  - `value` (`T`) — the value to format
- **Returns:** a CQL UDT literal, or `CassandraExecutorBase#NULL_STR` if the value is null
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the non-null value cannot be mapped to this UDT, including an unsupported Java type, a collection with more elements than UDT fields, or text for a `blob` field that is not valid base64
  - `com.datastax.oss.driver.api.core.type.codec.CodecNotFoundException` — if neither a registered codec nor a supported BLOB, TIME or TIMESTAMP conversion can map a non-null field value to its CQL type, or a field codec reports a missing codec while serializing
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if mapping the non-null value invokes a failing bean accessor, cannot create the target Java object, or a field codec rejects a value
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  UDTCodec<Address> codec = UDTCodec.create(addressUserType, Address.class);

  String literal = codec.format(new Address("123 Main St")); // e.g. {street:'123 Main St'}

  String nullStr = codec.format(null);                    // returns "NULL"
  ```
##### getJavaType(...) -> GenericType<T>
- **Signature:** `public GenericType<T> getJavaType()`
- **Summary:** Returns the Java type of this codec.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the Java type of this codec
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  UDTCodec<Address> codec = UDTCodec.create(addressUserType, Address.class);

  GenericType<Address> type = codec.getJavaType();      // GenericType wrapping Address.class
  Class<?> raw = type.getRawType();                     // returns Address.class
  ```

- **Signature:** `public DataType getCqlType()`
- **Summary:** Returns the CQL type of this codec.

  ```java
  DataType cqlType = codec.getCqlType(); // returns the UserDefinedType this codec was created against
  ```

### Class StatementSettings (com.landawn.abacus.da.cassandra.CassandraExecutor.StatementSettings)
Configuration settings applied to every CQL statement built by a `CassandraExecutor`.

**Thread-safety:** unspecified
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Public Constructors
- `public StatementSettings()` — Creates an empty `StatementSettings` with every field `null` (i.e. no driver defaults overridden).
  ```java
  StatementSettings settings = new StatementSettings(); // every field is null (driver defaults)
  settings.consistency(ConsistencyLevel.QUORUM)         // fluent setters return the same instance
          .fetchSize(1000);
  CassandraExecutor executor = new CassandraExecutor(session, settings);
  ```
- `public StatementSettings(final ConsistencyLevel consistency, final ConsistencyLevel serialConsistency, final Integer fetchSize, final Duration timeout, final Boolean traceQuery)` — Creates a `StatementSettings` with all fields populated.
  ```java
  StatementSettings settings = new StatementSettings(
      ConsistencyLevel.QUORUM, ConsistencyLevel.SERIAL, 1000, Duration.ofSeconds(30), Boolean.TRUE);
  // settings.consistency() == QUORUM, settings.fetchSize() == 1000, settings.traceQuery() == true

  // Leave individual settings at the driver default by passing null:
  StatementSettings minimal = new StatementSettings(
      ConsistencyLevel.QUORUM, null, null, null, null); // only consistency overridden
  ```

### Class CassandraExecutorBase (com.landawn.abacus.da.cassandra.CassandraExecutorBase)
Driver-agnostic base class shared by the synchronous `CassandraExecutor` (DataStax 4.x driver) and the legacy `com.landawn.abacus.da.cassandra.v3.CassandraExecutor` (DataStax 3.x driver), as well as their `Async*` counterparts.

**Thread-safety:** thread-safe
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Public Constructors
- (none)

#### Public Static Methods
##### registerKeys(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `@Deprecated public static void registerKeys(final Class<?> entityClass, final Collection<String> keyNames) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Registers primary key field names for the specified entity class.
- **Deprecated:** yes — Define or annotate the key/id field with `@Id` instead.
- **Contract:**
  - New code should use `@Id` annotations on entity fields or `javax.persistence.Id` annotations instead of manual registration.
- **Parameters:**
  - `entityClass` (`Class<?>`) — the entity class
  - `keyNames` (`Collection<String>`) — collection of property names that comprise the primary key: a name resolved by the property's getter, or for a property backed only by a public field, by the entity's bean properties
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `entityClass` is `null`, or `keyNames` is null or empty, contains a `null` name, or contains a name that cannot be resolved to a readable property of `entityClass` (including when `entityClass` is not a bean class)
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Legacy approach (deprecated)
  CassandraExecutorBase.registerKeys(User.class, Arrays.asList("userId", "tenantId"));
  // post-state: getKeyNames(User.class) now returns ["userId", "tenantId"]

  CassandraExecutorBase.registerKeys(User.class, Arrays.asList("userId"));
  // post-state: a single-column key; getKeyNames(User.class) returns ["userId"]

  CassandraExecutorBase.registerKeys(User.class, null);              // throws IllegalArgumentException
  CassandraExecutorBase.registerKeys(User.class, new ArrayList<>()); // throws IllegalArgumentException (empty)
  CassandraExecutorBase.registerKeys(null, Arrays.asList("userId")); // throws IllegalArgumentException (null entityClass)

  // Preferred approach
  public class User {
      @Id
      private String userId;

      @Id  // Composite key
      private String tenantId;

      // other fields...
  }
  ```
- **See also:** `com.landawn.abacus.annotation.Id`

#### Public Instance Methods
##### get(...) -> Optional<T>
- **Signature:** `public final <T> Optional<T> get(final Class<T> targetClass, final Object... ids) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException, DuplicateResultException`
- **Summary:** Retrieves an entity by its primary key values.
- **Contract:**
  - Returns Optional.empty() if no entity is found.
  - For the nullable counterpart that returns the entity directly (or `null` when no row matches) instead of an `Optional`, use `#gett(Class, Object...)`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `targetClass` (`Class<T>`) — the entity class
  - `ids` (`Object...`) — the primary key values
- **Returns:** an Optional containing the entity if found, otherwise empty
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetClass` is `null`, `ids` is null or empty, `targetClass` is not a bean class, `ids` contains a `null` or empty character-sequence key value, its length does not match the registered/annotated key columns of `targetClass`, or an id value is rejected when converted to its column's type (see Bind Value Conversion in the class documentation)
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if preparing, binding, executing, or fetching the CQL fails; or a returned column cannot be converted to the requested Java type or assigned to a mapped bean property
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.DuplicateResultException` — if more than one entity is found
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // single-key entity
  Optional<User> user = executor.get(User.class, "user123"); // returns present Optional<User> when one row matches
  user.ifPresent(u -> System.out.println("Found: " + u.getName()));

  Optional<User> missing = executor.get(User.class, "nope");  // returns Optional.empty() when no row matches

  executor.get(User.class);              // throws IllegalArgumentException (ids is empty)
  executor.get(User.class, "a", "b");    // throws IllegalArgumentException (id count != single key column)
  ```
- **See also:** `#gett(Class, Object...)`
- **Signature:** `public final <T> Optional<T> get(final Class<T> targetClass, final Collection<String> selectPropNames, final Object... ids) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException, DuplicateResultException`
- **Summary:** Retrieves specific properties of an entity by its primary key values.
- **Contract:**
  - This is useful for optimizing queries when only certain fields are needed.
- **Parameters:**
  - `targetClass` (`Class<T>`) — the entity class
  - `selectPropNames` (`Collection<String>`) — the property names to select (null for all properties)
  - `ids` (`Object...`) — the primary key values
- **Returns:** an Optional containing the entity if found, otherwise empty
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetClass` is `null`, `ids` is null or empty, `targetClass` is not a bean class, `ids` contains a `null` or empty character-sequence key value, its length does not match the registered/annotated key columns of `targetClass`, or an id value is rejected when converted to its column's type (see Bind Value Conversion in the class documentation)
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if preparing, binding, executing, or fetching the CQL fails; or a returned column cannot be converted to the requested Java type or assigned to a mapped bean property
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.DuplicateResultException` — if more than one entity is found
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Optional<User> user = executor.get(User.class,
      Arrays.asList("name", "email"), "user123"); // returns present Optional with only name/email populated

  Optional<User> all = executor.get(User.class,
      (Collection<String>) null, "user123");      // returns present Optional with all properties populated

  executor.get(User.class, Arrays.asList("name"));            // throws IllegalArgumentException (ids is empty)
  executor.get(User.class, Arrays.asList("name"), "a", "b");  // throws IllegalArgumentException (id count mismatch)
  ```

  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.DuplicateResultException` — if more than one entity is found
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if `whereClause` already carries a `LIMIT` (see Row Limits in the class documentation)
- **Examples:**
