##### gett(...) -> T
- **Signature:** `public final <T> T gett(final Class<T> targetClass, final Object... ids) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException, DuplicateResultException`
- **Summary:** Retrieves an entity by its primary key values through the nullable `gett` variant.
- **Contract:**
  - It returns the entity directly or `null` when no row matches, while still throwing `DuplicateResultException` if multiple rows are returned.
- **Parameters:**
  - `targetClass` (`Class<T>`) — the entity class
  - `ids` (`Object...`) — the primary key values
- **Returns:** the entity if found, otherwise null
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetClass` is `null`, `ids` is null or empty, `targetClass` is not a bean class, `ids` contains a `null` or empty character-sequence key value, its length does not match the registered/annotated key columns of `targetClass`, or an id value is rejected when converted to its column's type (see Bind Value Conversion in the class documentation)
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if preparing, binding, executing, or fetching the CQL fails; or a returned column cannot be converted to the requested Java type or assigned to a mapped bean property
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.DuplicateResultException` — if more than one entity is found
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  User user = executor.gett(User.class, "user123"); // returns the mapped User, or null when no row matches
  if (user != null) {
      System.out.println("Found: " + user.getName());
  }

  executor.gett(User.class);            // throws IllegalArgumentException (ids is empty)
  executor.gett(User.class, "a", "b");  // throws IllegalArgumentException (id count != single key column)
  ```

##### insert(...) -> RS
- **Signature:** `public RS insert(final Object entity) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Inserts an entity into the database.
- **Contract:**
  - All non-null insertable properties of the entity will be included in the INSERT statement, primary-key properties too, also when a key value is `0`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `entity` (`Object`) — the entity to insert
- **Returns:** the result set from the INSERT operation
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `entity` is `null`, is not a supported bean, or exposes no insertable properties, or a property value is rejected when converted to its column's type (see Bind Value Conversion in the class documentation)
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the driver rejects CQL or a bound value, the session is closed, or preparing, executing, or fetching the query fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  User user = new User();
  user.setUserId("user123");
  user.setName("John Doe");
  user.setEmail("john@example.com");

  ResultSet result = executor.insert(user); // returns the driver ResultSet for the INSERT

  executor.insert((Object) null);           // throws IllegalArgumentException (entity is null)
  ```
- **Signature:** `public RS insert(final Class<?> targetClass, final Map<String, Object> props) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Inserts a new record with the specified properties.
- **Contract:**
  - This is useful when you don't have a full entity object but just the properties to insert.
- **Parameters:**
  - `targetClass` (`Class<?>`) — the entity class
  - `props` (`Map<String, Object>`) — the properties to insert
- **Returns:** the result set from the INSERT operation
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if targetClass is null or is not a bean class, props is null or empty, or a value in props is rejected when converted to its column's type (see Bind Value Conversion in the class documentation)
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the driver rejects CQL or a bound value, the session is closed, or preparing, executing, or fetching the query fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, Object> props = new HashMap<>();
  props.put("userId", "user123");
  props.put("name", "John Doe");
  props.put("email", "john@example.com");

  ResultSet result = executor.insert(User.class, props); // returns the driver ResultSet for the INSERT

  executor.insert(User.class, new HashMap<>());          // throws IllegalArgumentException (props is empty)
  ```
##### batchInsert(...) -> RS
- **Signature:** `public RS batchInsert(final Collection<?> entities, final BT type) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException, IllegalStateException`
- **Summary:** Performs a batch insert of multiple entities.
- **Contract:**
  - All entities must be of the same type.
- **Parameters:**
  - `entities` (`Collection<?>`) — the collection of entities to insert
  - `type` (`BT`) — the batch type; `null` is treated as `LOGGED` by the shipped executors
- **Returns:** the result set from the batch INSERT operation
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `entities` is `null` or empty, contains a `null` element, or contains an entity that is not a supported bean or exposes no insertable properties (enforced by the shipped executors' batch-statement builders), or a property value is rejected when converted to its column's type (see Bind Value Conversion in the class documentation)
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the driver rejects CQL or a bound value, the session is closed, or preparing, executing, or fetching the query fails
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if `entities` has more than 65,535 elements, the driver's per-batch statement limit (thrown by the shipped executors' batch-statement builders)
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<User> users = Arrays.asList(user1, user2, user3);
  ResultSet result = executor.batchInsert(users, BatchType.LOGGED); // returns the driver ResultSet for the batch

  executor.batchInsert(new ArrayList<>(), BatchType.LOGGED); // throws IllegalArgumentException (entities is empty)
  ```
- **Signature:** `public RS batchInsert(final Class<?> targetClass, final Collection<? extends Map<String, Object>> propsList, final BT type) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException, IllegalStateException`
- **Summary:** Performs a batch insert of multiple records using property maps.
- **Parameters:**
  - `targetClass` (`Class<?>`) — the entity class
  - `propsList` (`Collection<? extends Map<String, Object>>`) — the collection of property maps to insert
  - `type` (`BT`) — the batch type; `null` is treated as `LOGGED` by the shipped executors
- **Returns:** the result set from the batch INSERT operation
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetClass` is `null`, or `propsList` is `null` or empty or contains a `null` or empty map (enforced by the shipped executors' batch-statement builders), or a map value is rejected when converted to its column's type (see Bind Value Conversion in the class documentation)
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the driver rejects CQL or a bound value, the session is closed, or preparing, executing, or fetching the query fails
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if `propsList` has more than 65,535 elements, the driver's per-batch statement limit (thrown by the shipped executors' batch-statement builders)
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<Map<String, Object>> propsList = new ArrayList<>();
  propsList.add(Map.of("userId", "user1", "name", "Alice"));
  propsList.add(Map.of("userId", "user2", "name", "Bob"));

  ResultSet result = executor.batchInsert(User.class, propsList, BatchType.LOGGED); // returns the driver ResultSet for the batch

  executor.batchInsert(User.class, new ArrayList<>(), BatchType.LOGGED); // throws IllegalArgumentException (propsList is empty)
  ```
##### update(...) -> RS
- **Signature:** `public RS update(final Object entity) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Updates an entity in the database.
- **Parameters:**
  - `entity` (`Object`) — the entity to update
- **Returns:** the result set from the UPDATE operation
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if entity is null, if the entity's class is not a bean class, declares no updatable non-key property (for a `Map` entity: it has no non-key entry) or declares no key, if a key value is missing, or if a property or key value is rejected when converted to its column's type (see Bind Value Conversion in the class documentation)

- **Examples:**
  ```java
  User user = executor.gett(User.class, "user123");
  user.setEmail("newemail@example.com");
  user.setLastModified(new Date());

  ResultSet result = executor.update(user); // returns the driver ResultSet for the UPDATE (all non-key props)

  executor.update((Object) null);           // throws IllegalArgumentException (entity is null)
  ```
- **Signature:** `public RS update(final Object entity, final Collection<String> propNamesToUpdate) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`

  - `propNamesToUpdate` (`Collection<String>`) — the property names to update

  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the driver rejects CQL or a bound value, the session is closed, or preparing, executing, or fetching the query fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  User user = new User();
  user.setUserId("user123");
  user.setEmail("newemail@example.com");
  user.setLastModified(new Date());

  executor.update(user, new ArrayList<>());    // throws IllegalArgumentException (propNamesToUpdate is empty)
  ```
- **Signature:** `public RS update(final Class<?> targetClass, final Map<String, Object> props, final Condition whereClause) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Updates records based on a custom WHERE condition.
- **Parameters:**
  - `targetClass` (`Class<?>`) — the entity class
  - `props` (`Map<String, Object>`) — the properties to update
  - `whereClause` (`Condition`) — the WHERE condition
- **Returns:** the result set from the UPDATE operation
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if targetClass is null or is not a bean class, if props is null or empty, if `props` contains a primary-key property, if whereClause is null or contains a relation unsupported by CQL, or if a value in props or the condition is rejected when converted to its column's type (see Bind Value Conversion in the class documentation)

- **Examples:**
  ```java

  props.put("status", "inactive");
  props.put("lastModified", new Date());

  ResultSet result = executor.update(User.class, props, where); // returns the driver ResultSet for the UPDATE

  executor.update(User.class, new HashMap<>(), where);          // throws IllegalArgumentException (props is empty)

- **Signature:** `public RS update(final String query, final Object... parameters) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Executes a custom UPDATE query with parameters.

  ```

- **Throws:**

  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the driver rejects CQL or a bound value, the session is closed, or preparing, executing, or fetching the query fails
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if `parametersList` has more than 65,535 elements, the driver's per-batch statement limit (thrown by the shipped executors' batch-statement builders)
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  String query = "UPDATE users SET status = ? WHERE user_id = ?";
  List<Object[]> params = Arrays.asList(
      new Object[] {"active", "user1"},
      new Object[] {"inactive", "user2"}
  );

  ResultSet result = executor.batchUpdate(query, params, BatchType.LOGGED); // returns the driver ResultSet for the batch

  executor.batchUpdate(query, new ArrayList<>(), BatchType.LOGGED); // throws IllegalArgumentException (parametersList is empty)
  ```
##### delete(...) -> RS
- **Signature:** `public RS delete(final Object entity) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Deletes an entity from the database.
- **Parameters:**
  - `entity` (`Object`) — the entity to delete (must have primary key values set)
- **Returns:** the result set from the DELETE operation
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if entity is null, if the entity's class is not a bean class or declares no key, if a key value is missing, or if a key value is rejected when converted to its column's type (see Bind Value Conversion in the class documentation)
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the driver rejects CQL or a bound value, the session is closed, or preparing, executing, or fetching the query fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  User user = new User();
  user.setUserId("user123");

  ResultSet result = executor.delete(user); // returns the driver ResultSet for the DELETE (entire row)

  executor.delete((Object) null);           // throws IllegalArgumentException (entity is null)
  ```
- **Signature:** `public RS delete(final Object entity, final Collection<String> propNamesToDelete) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Deletes specific properties of an entity from the database.
- **Contract:**
  - If propNamesToDelete is null, the entire row is deleted; an empty (non-null) collection is rejected.
- **Parameters:**
  - `entity` (`Object`) — the entity identifying the row to delete from
  - `propNamesToDelete` (`Collection<String>`) — the property names to delete (null for entire row)
- **Returns:** the result set from the DELETE operation
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if entity is null, if propNamesToDelete is empty (but not null), if the entity's class is not a bean class or declares no key, if a key value is missing, if a primary-key property is requested for deletion, or if a key value is rejected when converted to its column's type (see Bind Value Conversion in the class documentation)
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the driver rejects CQL or a bound value, the session is closed, or preparing, executing, or fetching the query fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  User user = new User();
  user.setUserId("user123");

  // Delete only specific columns
  ResultSet result = executor.delete(user, Arrays.asList("email", "phone")); // returns the driver ResultSet (clears email/phone)

  // Delete the entire row (null prop names)
  ResultSet whole = executor.delete(user, (Collection<String>) null);        // returns the driver ResultSet (entire row removed)

  executor.delete(user, new ArrayList<>()); // throws IllegalArgumentException (propNamesToDelete is empty, not null)
  ```
- **Signature:** `public final RS delete(final Class<?> targetClass, final Object... ids) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Deletes a record by its primary key values.
- **Parameters:**
  - `targetClass` (`Class<?>`) — the entity class
  - `ids` (`Object...`) — the primary key values, in the order of the declared key columns
- **Returns:** the result set from the DELETE operation
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetClass` is `null`, `ids` is null or empty, `targetClass` is not a bean class, `ids` contains a `null` or empty character-sequence key value, its length does not match the registered/annotated key columns of `targetClass`, or an id value is rejected when converted to its column's type (see Bind Value Conversion in the class documentation)
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the driver rejects CQL or a bound value, the session is closed, or preparing, executing, or fetching the query fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  ResultSet result = executor.delete(User.class, "user123"); // returns the driver ResultSet for the DELETE

  executor.delete(User.class, new Object[0]); // throws IllegalArgumentException (ids is empty)
  executor.delete(User.class, "a", "b");      // throws IllegalArgumentException (id count != single key column)
  ```
- **Signature:** `public final RS delete(final Class<?> targetClass, final Collection<String> propNamesToDelete, final Object... ids) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Deletes specific properties or entire record by primary key values.
- **Contract:**
  - If propNamesToDelete is specified, only those column values are deleted (set to null).
  - If propNamesToDelete is null, the entire row is deleted; an empty (non-null) collection is rejected.
- **Parameters:**
  - `targetClass` (`Class<?>`) — the entity class
  - `propNamesToDelete` (`Collection<String>`) — the property names to delete; pass `null` to delete the entire row
  - `ids` (`Object...`) — the primary key values, in the order of the declared key columns
- **Returns:** the result set from the DELETE operation
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetClass` is `null`, if `propNamesToDelete` is non-null but empty, if `ids` is null or empty, if `targetClass` is not a bean class, if `ids` contains a `null` or empty character-sequence key value or its length does not match the registered/annotated key columns of `targetClass`, if `propNamesToDelete` contains a primary-key property, or if an id value is rejected when converted to its column's type (see Bind Value Conversion in the class documentation)
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the driver rejects CQL or a bound value, the session is closed, or preparing, executing, or fetching the query fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Delete specific columns
  ResultSet result = executor.delete(User.class,
      Arrays.asList("email", "phone"), "user123"); // returns the driver ResultSet (clears email/phone)

  // Delete entire row
  ResultSet whole = executor.delete(User.class, null, "user123"); // returns the driver ResultSet (entire row removed)

  executor.delete(User.class, new ArrayList<>(), "user123"); // throws IllegalArgumentException (propNamesToDelete empty, not null)
  executor.delete(User.class, Arrays.asList("email"), new Object[0]); // throws IllegalArgumentException (ids is empty)
  ```
- **Signature:** `public RS delete(final Class<?> targetClass, final Condition whereClause) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Deletes records based on a custom WHERE condition.
- **Parameters:**
  - `targetClass` (`Class<?>`) — the entity class
  - `whereClause` (`Condition`) — the WHERE condition
- **Returns:** the result set from the DELETE operation
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if targetClass is null or is not a bean class, whereClause is null or contains a relation unsupported by CQL, or a condition value is rejected when converted to its column's type (see Bind Value Conversion in the class documentation)
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the driver rejects CQL or a bound value, the session is closed, or preparing, executing, or fetching the query fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Condition where = Filters.in("userId", Arrays.asList("user1", "user2"));
  ResultSet result = executor.delete(User.class, where); // returns the driver ResultSet for the DELETE
  ```
- **Signature:** `public RS delete(final Class<?> targetClass, final Collection<String> propNamesToDelete, final Condition whereClause) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Deletes specific properties or entire records based on a WHERE condition.
- **Contract:**
  - If propNamesToDelete is specified, only those column values are deleted (set to null) in the matching rows.
  - If propNamesToDelete is null, the entire matching rows are deleted; an empty (non-null) collection is rejected.
- **Parameters:**
  - `targetClass` (`Class<?>`) — the entity class
  - `propNamesToDelete` (`Collection<String>`) — the property names to delete (null for entire rows)
  - `whereClause` (`Condition`) — the WHERE condition
- **Returns:** the result set from the DELETE operation
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if targetClass is null or is not a bean class, if propNamesToDelete is empty (but not null) or contains a primary-key property, if whereClause is null or contains a relation unsupported by CQL, or if a condition value is rejected when converted to its column's type (see Bind Value Conversion in the class documentation)
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the driver rejects CQL or a bound value, the session is closed, or preparing, executing, or fetching the query fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Condition where = Filters.in("userId", Arrays.asList("user1", "user2")); // DELETE must restrict the primary key

  // Delete specific columns in matching rows
  ResultSet result = executor.delete(User.class,
      Arrays.asList("lastLogin", "sessionToken"), where);     // returns the driver ResultSet (clears those columns)

  // Delete the entire matching rows (null prop names)
  ResultSet whole = executor.delete(User.class, null, where); // returns the driver ResultSet (entire rows removed)

  executor.delete(User.class, new ArrayList<>(), where); // throws IllegalArgumentException (propNamesToDelete empty, not null)
  ```
##### batchDelete(...) -> RS
- **Signature:** `public RS batchDelete(final Collection<?> entities) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Performs a batch delete of multiple entities.
- **Contract:**
  - Each entity must have its primary key values set.
- **Parameters:**
  - `entities` (`Collection<?>`) — the collection of entities to delete
- **Returns:** the result set from the batch DELETE operation
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if entities is null or empty, if any element is null or is not an instance of the first entity's class, if the entity's class is not a bean class or has no single-column key, if a key value is missing, or if a key value is rejected when converted to its column's type (see Bind Value Conversion in the class documentation)
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the driver rejects CQL or a bound value, the session is closed, or preparing, executing, or fetching the query fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<User> usersToDelete = Arrays.asList(user1, user2, user3);
  ResultSet result = executor.batchDelete(usersToDelete); // returns the driver ResultSet for the batch DELETE

  executor.batchDelete(new ArrayList<>());                // throws IllegalArgumentException (entities is empty)
  ```
- **Signature:** `public RS batchDelete(final Collection<?> entities, final Collection<String> propNamesToDelete) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Performs a batch delete of specific properties from multiple entities.
- **Contract:**
  - If propNamesToDelete is null, entire rows are deleted.
- **Parameters:**
  - `entities` (`Collection<?>`) — the collection of entities to delete from
  - `propNamesToDelete` (`Collection<String>`) — the property names to delete (null for entire rows)
- **Returns:** the result set from the batch DELETE operation
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if entities is null or empty, if propNamesToDelete is empty (but not null), if any element of entities is null or is not an instance of the first entity's class, if the entity's class is not a bean class or has no single-column key, if a key value is missing, if propNamesToDelete contains a primary-key property, or if a key value is rejected when converted to its column's type (see Bind Value Conversion in the class documentation)
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the driver rejects CQL or a bound value, the session is closed, or preparing, executing, or fetching the query fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<User> users = Arrays.asList(user1, user2, user3);
  ResultSet result = executor.batchDelete(users, Arrays.asList("email", "phone")); // returns the driver ResultSet (clears email/phone)

  // null prop names -> entire rows removed
  ResultSet whole = executor.batchDelete(users, (Collection<String>) null);        // returns the driver ResultSet (entire rows removed)

  executor.batchDelete(new ArrayList<>(), Arrays.asList("email")); // throws IllegalArgumentException (entities is empty)
  executor.batchDelete(users, new ArrayList<>());                  // throws IllegalArgumentException (propNamesToDelete empty, not null)
  ```
##### exists(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `public final boolean exists(final Class<?> targetClass, final Object... ids) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Checks if a record exists by its primary key values.
- **Parameters:**
  - `targetClass` (`Class<?>`) — the entity class
  - `ids` (`Object...`) — the primary key values, in the order of the declared key columns
- **Returns:** `true` if a record exists with the given primary key, `false` otherwise
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetClass` is `null`, `ids` is null or empty, `targetClass` is not a bean class, `ids` contains a `null` or empty character-sequence key value, its length does not match the registered/annotated key columns of `targetClass`, or an id value is rejected when converted to its column's type (see Bind Value Conversion in the class documentation)
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the driver rejects CQL or a bound value, the session is closed, or preparing, executing, or fetching the query fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  boolean exists = executor.exists(User.class, "user123"); // returns true if a row with that key exists, else false
  if (exists) {
      System.out.println("User exists");
  }

  executor.exists(User.class);            // throws IllegalArgumentException (ids is empty)
  executor.exists(User.class, "a", "b");  // throws IllegalArgumentException (id count != single key column)
  ```
- **Signature:** `public boolean exists(final Class<?> targetClass, final Condition whereClause) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Checks if any records exist matching the specified condition.
- **Parameters:**
  - `targetClass` (`Class<?>`) — the entity class whose table is queried
  - `whereClause` (`Condition`) — the WHERE condition; pass `null` to check whether the table has at least one row
- **Returns:** `true` if at least one record matches the condition, `false` otherwise
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetClass` is `null` or is not a bean class, `whereClause` contains a relation unsupported by CQL, or a condition value is rejected when converted to its column's type (see Bind Value Conversion in the class documentation)
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the driver rejects CQL or a bound value, the session is closed, or preparing, executing, or fetching the query fails
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if `whereClause` already carries a `LIMIT` (see Row Limits in the class documentation)
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Condition where = Filters.eq("email", "user@example.com");
  boolean exists = executor.exists(User.class, where);     // returns true if at least one row matches, else false

  boolean any = executor.exists(User.class, (Condition) null); // returns true if the table has at least one row
  ```
- **Signature:** `public final boolean exists(final String query, final Object... parameters) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Executes the given CQL query and returns whether it produced at least one row.
- **Parameters:**
  - `query` (`String`) — the CQL query string with `?` placeholders for parameters
  - `parameters` (`Object...`) — the values to bind, in declaration order
- **Returns:** `true` if the query returned at least one row, `false` otherwise
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `query` is `null`, the CQL contains malformed or mixed parameter markers, the supplied parameter count or names do not match the prepared statement, or a parameter value is rejected when converted to its column's type (see Bind Value Conversion in the class documentation)
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the driver rejects CQL or a bound value, the session is closed, or preparing, executing, or fetching the query fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  boolean exists = executor.exists(
  "SELECT email FROM users WHERE email = ? LIMIT 1",
  "user@example.com"); // returns true if the query yields at least one row, else false
  ```
##### count(...) -> long
- **Signature:** `public long count(final Class<?> targetClass, final Condition whereClause) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Counts the number of records matching the specified condition.
- **Parameters:**
  - `targetClass` (`Class<?>`) — the entity class whose table is queried
  - `whereClause` (`Condition`) — the WHERE condition; pass `null` to count all rows in the table
- **Returns:** the count of records matching the condition, or `0` if no rows match
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetClass` is `null`, the selected properties cannot be mapped, the supplied condition contains a relation unsupported by CQL, or a condition value is rejected when converted to its column's type (see Bind Value Conversion in the class documentation)
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the driver rejects CQL or a bound value, the session is closed, or preparing, executing, or fetching the query fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Condition where = Filters.eq("status", "active");
  long activeUsers = executor.count(User.class, where);     // returns the matching row count (0 when none match)
  System.out.println("Active users: " + activeUsers);

  long total = executor.count(User.class, (Condition) null); // returns the total row count of the table
  ```
- **Signature:** `@Deprecated public final long count(final String query, final Object... parameters) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Executes the given CQL query (assumed to be a `SELECT count(*)` / `SELECT sum(...)` or similar single-value aggregate) and returns the first column of the first row as a `long`.
- **Deprecated:** yes — prefer `#queryForLong(String, Object...)` with a `COUNT(*)` query and `.orElse(0L)` for the same behavior. Slated for removal in a future release.
- **Contract:**
  - If the query produces no rows (or the aggregate returns `NULL`) this method returns `0L`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `query` (`String`) — the CQL query to execute (typically a `COUNT(*)` aggregate)
  - `parameters` (`Object...`) — the values to bind, in declaration order
- **Returns:** the aggregate value, or `0L` if no row is returned
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `query` is `null`, the CQL contains malformed or mixed parameter markers, the supplied parameter count or names do not match the prepared statement, or a parameter value is rejected when converted to its column's type (see Bind Value Conversion in the class documentation)
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the driver rejects CQL or a bound value, the session is closed, or preparing, executing, or fetching the query fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  long active = executor.count(
  "SELECT count(*) FROM users WHERE status = ?", "active"); // returns the COUNT(*) value, or 0L if no row/NULL
  ```
- **See also:** `#queryForLong(String, Object...)`, `#count(Class, Condition)`
##### findFirst(...) -> varies by overload
- **Signature:** `public <T> Optional<T> findFirst(final Class<T> targetClass, final Condition whereClause) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Builds a `SELECT... LIMIT 1` CQL query from the given condition and returns the first matching row mapped to an instance of `targetClass`.
- **Contract:**
  - present semantics: `Optional.empty()` is returned only when the query produces no rows.
  - When a row is found, the mapped entity is returned as a present `Optional`.
  - Because `Optional` cannot carry a `null` payload, the mapped entity itself must be non-null.
- **Parameters:**
  - `targetClass` (`Class<T>`) — the entity class with getter/setter methods matching column names
  - `whereClause` (`Condition`) — the WHERE condition used to build the CQL query (may be `null`)
- **Returns:** a present `Optional<T>` holding the first mapped row when at least one row is returned; `Optional.empty()` when the query returns no rows
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetClass` is `null`, the selected properties cannot be mapped, the supplied condition contains a relation unsupported by CQL, or a condition value is rejected when converted to its column's type (see Bind Value Conversion in the class documentation)
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if preparing, binding, executing, or fetching the CQL fails; or a returned column cannot be converted to the requested Java type or assigned to a mapped bean property
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if `whereClause` already carries a `LIMIT` (see Row Limits in the class documentation)
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Optional<User> user = executor.findFirst(User.class,
      Filters.eq("email", "user@example.com")); // returns present Optional<User> for the first match

  Optional<User> none = executor.findFirst(User.class,
      Filters.eq("email", "missing@example.com")); // returns Optional.empty() when no row matches
  ```
- **See also:** `#findFirst(Class, Collection, Condition)`, `#findFirst(Class, String, Object...)`
- **Signature:** `public <T> Optional<T> findFirst(final Class<T> targetClass, final Collection<String> selectPropNames, final Condition whereClause) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Builds a `SELECT <selectPropNames>... LIMIT 1` CQL query from the given condition and returns the first matching row mapped to an instance of `targetClass`.
- **Contract:**
  - The generated CQL projects only the requested properties (or all properties when `selectPropNames` is `null`).
  - present semantics: `Optional.empty()` is returned only when the query produces no rows.
  - When a row is found, the mapped entity is returned as a present `Optional`.
  - Because `Optional` cannot carry a `null` payload, the mapped entity itself must be non-null.
- **Parameters:**
  - `targetClass` (`Class<T>`) — the entity class with getter/setter methods matching column names
  - `selectPropNames` (`Collection<String>`) — the property names to select, or `null` for all properties
  - `whereClause` (`Condition`) — the WHERE condition used to build the CQL query (may be `null`)
- **Returns:** a present `Optional<T>` holding the first mapped row when at least one row is returned; `Optional.empty()` when the query returns no rows
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetClass` is `null`, the selected properties cannot be mapped, the supplied condition contains a relation unsupported by CQL, or a condition value is rejected when converted to its column's type (see Bind Value Conversion in the class documentation)
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if preparing, binding, executing, or fetching the CQL fails; or a returned column cannot be converted to the requested Java type or assigned to a mapped bean property
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if `whereClause` already carries a `LIMIT` (see Row Limits in the class documentation)
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Optional<User> user = executor.findFirst(User.class,
      Arrays.asList("userId", "name"),
      Filters.eq("status", "active")); // returns present Optional<User> (only userId/name set) for the first match

  Optional<User> all = executor.findFirst(User.class, null,
      Filters.eq("status", "active")); // returns present Optional with all properties, or empty when no row matches
  ```
- **See also:** `#findFirst(Class, Condition)`, `#findFirst(Class, String, Object...)`
- **Signature:** `public final Optional<Map<String, Object>> findFirst(final String query, final Object... parameters) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Executes the given CQL query and returns the first row as a `Map<String, Object>` keyed by column name.
- **Contract:**
  - present semantics: `Optional.empty()` is returned only when the query produces no rows.
  - When a row is found, the map is returned as a present `Optional` — individual column values within the map may themselves be `null`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `query` (`String`) — the CQL query string with `?` placeholders for parameters
  - `parameters` (`Object...`) — the values to bind, in declaration order
- **Returns:** a present `Optional` holding the first row as a `Map<String, Object>` when at least one row is returned; `Optional.empty()` when the query returns no rows
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `query` is `null`, the CQL contains malformed or mixed parameter markers, the supplied parameter count or names do not match the prepared statement, or a parameter value is rejected when converted to its column's type (see Bind Value Conversion in the class documentation)
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if preparing, binding, executing, or fetching the CQL fails; or a returned column cannot be converted to the requested Java type or assigned to a mapped bean property
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Optional<Map<String, Object>> user = executor.findFirst(
  "SELECT * FROM users WHERE status = ? LIMIT 1", "active"); // returns present Optional holding the first row as a Map; empty when no row matches
  ```
- **See also:** `#findFirst(Class, String, Object...)`
- **Signature:** `public abstract <T> Optional<T> findFirst(final Class<T> targetClass, final String query, final Object... parameters) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException, NullPointerException`
- **Summary:** Executes the given CQL query and returns the first row mapped to an instance of `targetClass`.
- **Contract:**
  - present semantics: `Optional.empty()` is returned only when the query produces no rows.
  - When a row is found, the mapped value is returned as a present `Optional`.
  - Because `Optional` cannot carry a `null` payload, the mapped value itself must be non-null.
- **Parameters:**
  - `targetClass` (`Class<T>`) — an entity class with getter/setter methods, `Map.class`, a collection, an object array class, or a single-value type (including a primitive array class) (must not be `null`)
  - `query` (`String`) — the CQL query string with `?` placeholders for parameters
  - `parameters` (`Object...`) — the values to bind, in declaration order
- **Returns:** a present `Optional<T>` holding the first mapped row when at least one row is returned; `Optional.empty()` when the query returns no rows
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetClass` or `query` is `null`, the CQL contains malformed or mixed parameter markers, the supplied parameter count or names do not match the prepared statement, a parameter value is rejected when converted to its column's type (see Bind Value Conversion in the class documentation), or `targetClass` is a single-value type but the first row does not have exactly one column
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if preparing, binding, executing, or fetching the CQL fails; or a returned column cannot be converted to the requested Java type or assigned to a mapped bean property
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if the first row maps to a null value, which `Optional#of(Object)` cannot contain
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Optional<User> user = executor.findFirst(User.class,
      "SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = ? LIMIT 1", email); // returns present Optional<User>; empty when no row matches

  Optional<Map> userData = executor.findFirst(Map.class,
      "SELECT name, email FROM users WHERE id = ?", userId); // returns present Optional holding a Map; empty when no row matches

  Optional<Object[]> row = executor.findFirst(Object[].class,
      "SELECT count(*), max(created_at) FROM events"); // returns present Optional holding an Object[] of the two aggregates
  ```
- **See also:** `#findFirst(String, Object...)`, `#findFirst(Class, Condition)`
##### list(...) -> varies by overload
- **Signature:** `public <T> List<T> list(final Class<T> targetClass, final Condition whereClause) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Lists all entities matching the specified condition.
- **Parameters:**
  - `targetClass` (`Class<T>`) — the entity class with getter/setter methods matching column names
  - `whereClause` (`Condition`) — the WHERE condition (may be `null` to select every row)
- **Returns:** a list of all matching entities; empty if no row matches
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetClass` is `null`, the selected properties cannot be mapped, the supplied condition contains a relation unsupported by CQL, or a condition value is rejected when converted to its column's type (see Bind Value Conversion in the class documentation)
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if preparing, binding, executing, or fetching the CQL fails; or a returned column cannot be converted to the requested Java type or assigned to a mapped bean property
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Condition where = Filters.eq("status", "active");
  List<User> activeUsers = executor.list(User.class, where); // returns a (possibly empty) mutable List of matches

  ```
- **Signature:** `public <T> List<T> list(final Class<T> targetClass, final Collection<String> selectPropNames, final Condition whereClause) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Lists entities with specific properties matching the condition.
- **Parameters:**
  - `targetClass` (`Class<T>`) — the entity class with getter/setter methods matching column names
  - `selectPropNames` (`Collection<String>`) — the property names to select; pass `null` for all properties
  - `whereClause` (`Condition`) — the WHERE condition (may be `null` to select every row)
- **Returns:** a list of all matching entities; empty if no row matches
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetClass` is `null`, the selected properties cannot be mapped, the supplied condition contains a relation unsupported by CQL, or a condition value is rejected when converted to its column's type (see Bind Value Conversion in the class documentation)
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if preparing, binding, executing, or fetching the CQL fails; or a returned column cannot be converted to the requested Java type or assigned to a mapped bean property
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Condition where = Filters.ge("age", 18);
  List<User> adults = executor.list(User.class,
      Arrays.asList("userId", "name", "age"), where); // returns a (possibly empty) List with only those 3 props set

  List<User> allProps = executor.list(User.class, null, where); // returns matches with all properties populated
  ```
- **Signature:** `public final List<Map<String, Object>> list(final String query, final Object... parameters) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Executes the given CQL query and returns every row as a `Map<String, Object>` keyed by column name.
- **Parameters:**
  - `query` (`String`) — the CQL query string with `?` placeholders for parameters
  - `parameters` (`Object...`) — the values to bind, in declaration order
- **Returns:** a list of result rows, each as a `Map<String, Object>` keyed by column name
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `query` is `null`, the CQL contains malformed or mixed parameter markers, the supplied parameter count or names do not match the prepared statement, or a parameter value is rejected when converted to its column's type (see Bind Value Conversion in the class documentation)
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if preparing, binding, executing, or fetching the CQL fails; or a returned column cannot be converted to the requested Java type or assigned to a mapped bean property
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<Map<String, Object>> rows = executor.list(
  "SELECT name, email FROM users WHERE status = ?", "active"); // returns a (possibly empty) mutable List of row maps
  ```
- **See also:** `#list(Class, String, Object...)`
- **Signature:** `public final <T> List<T> list(final Class<T> targetClass, final String query, final Object... parameters) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Executes the given CQL query and returns every row mapped to an instance of `targetClass`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `targetClass` (`Class<T>`) — an entity class with getter/setter methods matching column names, `Map.class`, or a basic single-value type (must not be `null`)
  - `query` (`String`) — the CQL query string with `?` placeholders for parameters
  - `parameters` (`Object...`) — the values to bind, in declaration order
- **Returns:** a list of result rows mapped to `targetClass`
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetClass` or `query` is `null`, the CQL contains malformed or mixed parameter markers, the supplied parameter count or names do not match the prepared statement, a parameter value is rejected when converted to its column's type (see Bind Value Conversion in the class documentation), or `targetClass` is a single-value type but the result set does not have exactly one column
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if preparing, binding, executing, or fetching the CQL fails; or a returned column cannot be converted to the requested Java type or assigned to a mapped bean property
- **Examples:**
  ```java

  "SELECT * FROM users WHERE status = ?", "active"); // returns a (possibly empty) mutable List<User>
  ```

##### queryForBoolean(...) -> OptionalBoolean
- **Signature:** `@Beta public OptionalBoolean queryForBoolean(final Class<?> targetClass, final String propName, final Condition whereClause) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Annotations:** @Beta
- **Summary:** Builds a `SELECT <propName>... LIMIT 1` CQL query from the given condition and returns the value of `propName` from the first row as a boolean.
- **Contract:**
  - present semantics: `OptionalBoolean.empty()` is returned only when the query produces no rows.
  - If a row exists but the column is `NULL`, the returned `OptionalBoolean` is present and holds the primitive default `false`.
  - Use `#queryForSingleValue(Class, Class, String, Condition)` with `Boolean.class` if you need to distinguish `NULL` from a real `false`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `targetClass` (`Class<?>`) — the entity class used to derive the table/column mapping
  - `propName` (`String`) — the property name (column) whose value is returned
  - `whereClause` (`Condition`) — the WHERE condition used to build the CQL query
- **Returns:** a present `OptionalBoolean` holding the column value (or `false` for `NULL`) when at least one row is returned; `OptionalBoolean.empty()` when the query returns no rows
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetClass` is `null`, `propName` is `null` or empty, `whereClause` contains a relation unsupported by CQL, or a condition value is rejected when converted to its column's type (see Bind Value Conversion in the class documentation); or the value read cannot be converted to `boolean` (for example a `bigint` or `double` value, an `int` other than `1`, `0` or `-1`, or text other than `1`/`0`/`-1`/ `y`/`n`/`true`/`false` once its padding is removed — blank text converts to `false`; see Boolean Conversion in the class documentation)
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if preparing, binding, executing, or fetching the CQL fails; or a returned column cannot be converted to the requested Java type or assigned to a mapped bean property
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if `whereClause` already carries a `LIMIT` (see Row Limits in the class documentation)
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  OptionalBoolean isActive = executor.queryForBoolean(User.class, "is_active",
  Filters.eq("id", userId)); // returns present OptionalBoolean (false when the column is NULL); empty when no row matches
  ```
- **See also:** `#queryForBoolean(String, Object...)`, `#queryForSingleValue(Class, Class, String, Condition)`
