  - `0L`, which is returned.) Use `#queryForSingleValue(Class, Class, String, Condition)` (which returns `Nullable`) when the column may legitimately be `NULL`.

  - `targetClass` (`Class<?>`) — the class representing the target BigQuery table
  - `valueClass` (`Class<V>`) — the expected class of the returned value, used for type conversion
  - `propName` (`String`) — the property/column name to select
  - `whereClause` (`Condition`) — the condition to filter records, or `null` to omit the WHERE clause
- **Returns:** a present `Optional<V>` holding the (non-null) column value when at least one row is returned with a non-null value; `Optional.empty()` when the query returns no rows

  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if parameter conversion fails, BigQuery rejects the query or fetching a result page fails, the waiting thread is interrupted, or a returned value cannot be decoded or mapped to the requested Java type
  - `java.lang.ArithmeticException` — if a row is returned and the column value overflows an integral `valueClass`
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if a row is returned but the column value (or its conversion) is `null`, because `Optional#of(Object)` rejects a null payload
- **Examples:**

  Condition condition = Filters.eq("customerId", "CUST123");
  Optional<String> email = executor.queryForSingleNonNull(
          Customer.class, String.class, "email", condition);   // present with the email when a row matches

  email.isPresent();          // returns true when at least one row matched with a non-null value
  email.orElse("n/a");        // returns the column value, or "n/a" when no row matched

  // Edge: no matching row -> Optional.empty()
  Optional<String> none = executor.queryForSingleNonNull(
          Customer.class, String.class, "email", Filters.eq("customerId", "MISSING"));
  none.isPresent();           // returns false

##### query(...) -> Dataset
- **Signature:** `public Dataset query(final Class<?> targetClass, final Condition whereClause) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException, ArithmeticException`
- **Summary:** Queries a BigQuery table and returns results as a Dataset using a condition.
- **Parameters:**
  - `targetClass` (`Class<?>`) — the class representing the target table
  - `whereClause` (`Condition`) — the condition to filter records, or `null` to select all rows
- **Returns:** a Dataset containing all matching records in columnar format
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetClass` is null or declares no selectable property, or if `whereClause` has a null operator or is or contains a `Criteria`, SQL clause, JOIN, or other non-predicate condition rejected by the SQL builder
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if parameter conversion fails, BigQuery rejects the query or fetching a result page fails, the waiting thread is interrupted, or a returned value cannot be decoded or mapped to the requested Java type
  - `java.lang.ArithmeticException` — if the result has a schema and its reported row count exceeds `Integer#MAX_VALUE`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Query for dataset with condition
  Condition condition = Filters.eq("status", "active");
  Dataset dataset = executor.query(Customer.class, condition);   // returns a columnar Dataset of matching rows
  dataset.size();                                                // returns the number of matching rows

  // Access columns by name
  ImmutableList<String> names = dataset.getColumn("name");
  ImmutableList<String> emails = dataset.getColumn("email");

  // A null condition selects all rows (the read path omits the WHERE clause)
  Dataset all = executor.query(Customer.class, (Condition) null);   // returns every row in the table
  ```
- **See also:** `#query(Class, Collection, Condition)`, `Dataset`
- **Signature:** `public Dataset query(final Class<?> targetClass, final Collection<String> selectPropNames, final Condition whereClause) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException, ArithmeticException`
- **Summary:** Queries specific columns from a BigQuery table and returns results as a Dataset.
- **Contract:**
  - If selectPropNames is null or empty, all columns are selected.
- **Parameters:**
  - `targetClass` (`Class<?>`) — the class representing the target table
  - `selectPropNames` (`Collection<String>`) — the collection of property/column names to select, or null for all columns
  - `whereClause` (`Condition`) — the condition to filter records, or `null` to select all rows
- **Returns:** a Dataset containing matching records for the selected columns in columnar format
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetClass` is null; if `selectPropNames` contains a null, empty, or blank element; if `selectPropNames` is null or empty and `targetClass` declares no selectable property; or if `whereClause` has a null operator or is or contains a `Criteria`, SQL clause, JOIN, or other non-predicate condition rejected by the SQL builder
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if parameter conversion fails, BigQuery rejects the query or fetching a result page fails, the waiting thread is interrupted, or a returned value cannot be decoded or mapped to the requested Java type
  - `java.lang.ArithmeticException` — if the result has a schema and its reported row count exceeds `Integer#MAX_VALUE`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Query specific columns
  Collection<String> columns = Arrays.asList("customerId", "name", "email");
  Condition condition = Filters.eq("status", "active");
  Dataset dataset = executor.query(Customer.class, columns, condition);   // returns a Dataset with exactly those 3 columns
  dataset.columnCount();                                                  // returns 3
  dataset.size();                                                         // returns the number of matching rows

  // Access specific columns by name
  ImmutableList<String> customerIds = dataset.getColumn("customerId");
  ImmutableList<String> names = dataset.getColumn("name");

  // null selectPropNames selects all columns (equivalent to query(Class, Condition))
  Dataset full = executor.query(Customer.class, (Collection<String>) null, condition);
  ```
- **See also:** `#query(Class, String, Object...)`
- **Signature:** `public final Dataset query(final Class<?> targetClass, final String query, final Object... parameters) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException, ArithmeticException`
- **Summary:** Executes a custom BigQuery SQL query and returns results as a Dataset.
- **Parameters:**
  - `targetClass` (`Class<?>`) — the target class for result conversion (entity class with getter/setter methods or Map.class) used for type information and conversion
  - `query` (`String`) — the SQL query string with? parameter placeholders
  - `parameters` (`Object...`) — the parameter values to bind to the query
- **Returns:** a Dataset containing query results in columnar format
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `query` is null or empty, or any positional parameter is an untyped null (wrap SQL nulls in a typed `QueryParameterValue`)
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if parameter conversion fails, BigQuery rejects the query or fetching a result page fails, the waiting thread is interrupted, or a returned value cannot be decoded or mapped to the requested Java type
  - `java.lang.ArithmeticException` — if the result has a schema and its reported row count exceeds `Integer#MAX_VALUE`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Execute custom SQL query
  String sql = "SELECT customer_id, name, email FROM customers " +
               "WHERE status = ? AND created_date > ?";
  Dataset dataset = executor.query(Customer.class, sql,
      "active", java.sql.Date.valueOf(LocalDate.now().minusMonths(6)));   // java.sql.Date binds as a native DATE parameter

  // Process results
  dataset.size();                                  // returns the number of rows
  dataset.getColumn("name").forEach(System.out::println);

  // Complex query with aggregation
  String aggQuery = "SELECT status, COUNT(*) as count, AVG(order_amount) as avg_amount " +
                    "FROM orders WHERE order_date >= ? GROUP BY status";
  Dataset aggDataset = executor.query(Map.class, aggQuery,
      java.sql.Date.valueOf(LocalDate.now().minusMonths(1)));   // returns a Dataset
  ```
- **See also:** `#execute(String, Object...)`, `Dataset`
##### list(...) -> List<T>
- **Signature:** `public <T> List<T> list(final Class<T> targetClass, final Condition whereClause) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException, ArithmeticException`
- **Summary:** Queries a BigQuery table and returns results as a List using a condition.
- **Parameters:**
  - `targetClass` (`Class<T>`) — the entity class used both to derive the table name and to map result rows
  - `whereClause` (`Condition`) — the condition to filter records, or `null` to select all rows
- **Returns:** a List containing all matching records converted to the target type, empty list if no matches
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetClass` is null or declares no selectable property, or if `whereClause` has a null operator or is or contains a `Criteria`, SQL clause, JOIN, or other non-predicate condition rejected by the SQL builder
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if parameter conversion fails, BigQuery rejects the query or fetching a result page fails, the waiting thread is interrupted, or a returned value cannot be decoded or mapped to the requested Java type
  - `java.lang.ArithmeticException` — if the result has a schema and its reported row count exceeds `Integer#MAX_VALUE`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // List all active customers
  Condition condition = Filters.eq("status", "active");
  List<Customer> customers = executor.list(Customer.class, condition);   // returns a List of matching entities (empty if none)

  customers.forEach(customer -> {
      System.out.println(customer.getName() + ": " + customer.getEmail());
  });

  // List with complex condition
  Condition complexCond = Filters.and(
      Filters.eq("status", "active"),
      Filters.gt("orderCount", 10),
      Filters.between("lastOrderDate", startDate, endDate)
  );
  List<Customer> vipCustomers = executor.list(Customer.class, complexCond);   // returns a List of matching entities

  // A null condition selects all rows
  List<Customer> everyone = executor.list(Customer.class, (Condition) null);  // returns every row in the table
  ```
- **See also:** `com.landawn.abacus.query.Filters`, `#list(Class, Collection, Condition)`
- **Signature:** `public <T> List<T> list(final Class<T> targetClass, final Collection<String> selectPropNames, final Condition whereClause) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException, ArithmeticException`
- **Summary:** Queries specific columns from a BigQuery table and returns results as a List.
- **Contract:**
  - If selectPropNames is null or empty, all columns are selected.
- **Parameters:**
  - `targetClass` (`Class<T>`) — the entity class used both to derive the table name and to map result rows
  - `selectPropNames` (`Collection<String>`) — the collection of property/column names to select, or null for all columns
  - `whereClause` (`Condition`) — the condition to filter records, or `null` to select all rows
- **Returns:** a List containing matching records for the selected columns converted to the target type
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetClass` is null; if `selectPropNames` contains a null, empty, or blank element; if `selectPropNames` is null or empty and `targetClass` declares no selectable property; or if `whereClause` has a null operator or is or contains a `Criteria`, SQL clause, JOIN, or other non-predicate condition rejected by the SQL builder
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if parameter conversion fails, BigQuery rejects the query or fetching a result page fails, the waiting thread is interrupted, or a returned value cannot be decoded or mapped to the requested Java type
  - `java.lang.ArithmeticException` — if the result has a schema and its reported row count exceeds `Integer#MAX_VALUE`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Select specific columns
  Collection<String> columns = Arrays.asList("customerId", "name", "email");
  Condition condition = Filters.eq("status", "active");
  List<Customer> customers = executor.list(Customer.class, columns, condition);   // returns a List of entities populated from the 3 columns

  // Map and scalar targets require the raw-SQL overload because this overload derives the
  // table from targetClass.
  List<LinkedHashMap<String, Object>> results = executor.list(com.landawn.abacus.util.Clazz.PROPS_MAP,
      "SELECT customer_id, name FROM customers WHERE status = ?", "active");
  List<String> customerIds = executor.list(String.class,
      "SELECT customer_id FROM customers WHERE status = ?", "active");
  ```
- **See also:** `com.landawn.abacus.query.Filters`, `#list(Class, String, Object...)`
- **Signature:** `public final <T> List<T> list(final Class<T> targetClass, final String query, final Object... parameters) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException, ArithmeticException`
- **Summary:** Executes a custom BigQuery SQL query and returns results as a List.
- **Parameters:**
  - `targetClass` (`Class<T>`) — the target class for result conversion (entity class with getter/setter methods, Map.class, or supported basic types)
  - `query` (`String`) — the SQL query string with? parameter placeholders
  - `parameters` (`Object...`) — the parameter values to bind to the query
- **Returns:** a List containing all query results converted to the target type, empty list if no results
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `query` is null or empty, or any positional parameter is an untyped null (wrap SQL nulls in a typed `QueryParameterValue`)
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if parameter conversion fails, BigQuery rejects the query or fetching a result page fails, the waiting thread is interrupted, or a returned value cannot be decoded or mapped to the requested Java type
  - `java.lang.ArithmeticException` — if the result has a schema and its reported row count exceeds `Integer#MAX_VALUE`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Execute SQL query with parameters
  String sql = "SELECT * FROM customers WHERE status = ? AND created_date > ?";
  List<Customer> customers = executor.list(Customer.class, sql,
      "active", java.sql.Date.valueOf(LocalDate.now().minusMonths(6)));   // java.sql.Date binds as a native DATE parameter

  // Complex JOIN query
  String joinSql = "SELECT c.customer_id, c.name, COUNT(o.order_id) as order_count " +
                   "FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id " +
                   "WHERE c.status = ? GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.name";
  List<LinkedHashMap<String, Object>> results = executor.list(
      com.landawn.abacus.util.Clazz.PROPS_MAP, joinSql, "active");   // returns one Map per row

  // Query returning single values (single-column result -> scalar conversion)
  String idQuery = "SELECT customer_id FROM customers WHERE status = ?";
  List<String> activeIds = executor.list(String.class, idQuery, "active");   // returns one String per row
  ```
- **See also:** `#execute(String, Object...)`, `#toList(TableResult, Class)`
##### stream(...) -> varies by overload
- **Signature:** `public <T> Stream<T> stream(final Class<T> targetClass, final Condition whereClause) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Queries a BigQuery table and returns results as a Stream using a condition.
- **Parameters:**
  - `targetClass` (`Class<T>`) — the entity class used both to derive the table name and to map result rows
  - `whereClause` (`Condition`) — the condition to filter records, or `null` to select all rows
- **Returns:** a Stream containing all matching records converted to the target type; later page-fetch and row-conversion failures are raised during stream traversal
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetClass` is null or declares no selectable property, or if `whereClause` has a null operator or is or contains a `Criteria`, SQL clause, JOIN, or other non-predicate condition rejected by the SQL builder
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if BigQuery rejects the SQL or query job, or the calling thread is interrupted while waiting for the job
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Stream and process records
  Condition condition = Filters.eq("status", "active");
  Stream<Customer> customerStream = executor.stream(Customer.class, condition);   // query completed; row conversion is deferred

  customerStream
      .filter(c -> c.getOrderCount() > 10)
      .map(Customer::getEmail)
      .forEach(System.out::println);

  // Stream with aggregation (abacus Stream)
  BigDecimal totalAmount = executor.stream(Order.class, Filters.eq("status", "completed"))
      .map(Order::getAmount)
      .reduce(BigDecimal.ZERO, BigDecimal::add);   // returns the summed amount

  // Avoid eagerly materialising converted rows
  long count = executor.stream(Customer.class, Filters.between("createdDate", start, end))
      .count();                                    // returns the number of matching rows
  ```
- **See also:** `com.landawn.abacus.query.Filters`, `#stream(Class, Collection, Condition)`
- **Signature:** `public <T> Stream<T> stream(final Class<T> targetClass, final Collection<String> selectPropNames, final Condition whereClause) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Queries specific columns from a BigQuery table and returns results as a Stream.
- **Contract:**
  - If selectPropNames is null or empty, all columns are selected.
- **Parameters:**
  - `targetClass` (`Class<T>`) — the entity class used both to derive the table name and to map result rows
  - `selectPropNames` (`Collection<String>`) — the collection of property/column names to select, or null for all columns
  - `whereClause` (`Condition`) — the condition to filter records, or `null` to select all rows
- **Returns:** a Stream containing matching records for the selected columns converted to the target type; later page-fetch and row-conversion failures are raised during stream traversal
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetClass` is null; if `selectPropNames` contains a null, empty, or blank element; if `selectPropNames` is null or empty and `targetClass` declares no selectable property; or if `whereClause` has a null operator or is or contains a `Criteria`, SQL clause, JOIN, or other non-predicate condition rejected by the SQL builder
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if BigQuery rejects the SQL or query job, or the calling thread is interrupted while waiting for the job
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Stream specific columns
  Collection<String> columns = Arrays.asList("customerId", "email");
  Condition condition = Filters.eq("status", "active");

  List<String> emails = executor.stream(Customer.class, columns, condition)
      .map(Customer::getEmail)
      .filter(email -> email.endsWith("@example.com"))
      .toList();                                   // returns the matching emails as a List

  // Stream and group by (abacus Stream collector)
  Map<String, List<Customer>> byStatus = executor.stream(Customer.class,
          Arrays.asList("customerId", "status"), Filters.isNotNull("status"))
      .groupTo(Customer::getStatus);              // returns a Map keyed by status
  ```
- **See also:** `com.landawn.abacus.query.Filters`, `#stream(Class, String, Object...)`
- **Signature:** `public final <T> Stream<T> stream(final Class<T> targetClass, final String query, final Object... parameters) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Executes a custom BigQuery SQL query and returns results as a Stream.
- **Parameters:**
  - `targetClass` (`Class<T>`) — the target class for result conversion (entity class with getter/setter methods, Map.class, or supported basic types)
  - `query` (`String`) — the SQL query string with? parameter placeholders
  - `parameters` (`Object...`) — the parameter values to bind to the query
- **Returns:** a Stream containing all query results converted to the target type; later page-fetch and row-conversion failures are raised during stream traversal
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `query` is null or empty, or any positional parameter is an untyped null (wrap SQL nulls in a typed `QueryParameterValue`)
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if BigQuery rejects the SQL or query job, or the calling thread is interrupted while waiting for the job
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Stream query results
  String sql = "SELECT * FROM customers WHERE status = ? AND created_date > ?";
  Stream<Customer> stream = executor.stream(Customer.class, sql,
      "active", java.sql.Date.valueOf(LocalDate.now().minusMonths(6)));   // java.sql.Date binds as a native DATE parameter

  // Process stream with filtering and mapping (abacus Stream)
  List<String> premiumEmails = stream
      .filter(c -> c.getOrderCount() > 100)
      .map(Customer::getEmail)
      .toList();                                   // returns the matching emails as a List

  // Stream for analytics
  String analyticsSql = "SELECT order_date, SUM(amount) as total FROM orders " +
                        "WHERE order_date >= ? GROUP BY order_date";
  executor.stream(Map.class, analyticsSql, java.sql.Date.valueOf(LocalDate.now().minusDays(30)))
      .forEach(row -> System.out.println(row.get("order_date") + ": " + row.get("total")));
  ```
- **See also:** `#execute(String, Object...)`, `Stream`
- **Signature:** `public final <T> Stream<T> stream(final Class<T> targetClass, final QueryJobConfiguration queryConfig) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Executes a BigQuery job using the provided configuration and returns results as a Stream.
- **Parameters:**
  - `targetClass` (`Class<T>`) — the target class for result conversion (entity class with getter/setter methods, Map.class, or basic single value types)
  - `queryConfig` (`QueryJobConfiguration`) — the BigQuery QueryJobConfiguration with query and job settings; must not be `null`
- **Returns:** a Stream containing all query results converted to the target type; later page-fetch and row-conversion failures are raised during stream traversal
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `queryConfig` is `null`
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if BigQuery rejects `queryConfig` or its query job, the job fails or is cancelled, or the calling thread is interrupted while waiting for the job
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Advanced query with custom job configuration
  QueryJobConfiguration config = QueryJobConfiguration.newBuilder(
      "SELECT * FROM customers WHERE status = 'active'")
      .setUseLegacySql(false)
      .setPriority(QueryJobConfiguration.Priority.INTERACTIVE)
      .setMaximumBytesBilled(10000000L)
      .setLabels(Map.of("environment", "production"))
      .build();

  Stream<Customer> stream = executor.stream(Customer.class, config);   // query completed; row conversion is deferred
  long count = stream.count();                                         // returns the number of rows produced by the job

  // Query with caching disabled
  QueryJobConfiguration noCacheConfig = QueryJobConfiguration.newBuilder(
      "SELECT * FROM realtime_data")
      .setUseQueryCache(false)
      .build();

  executor.stream(Map.class, noCacheConfig)
      .forEach(System.out::println);
  ```
- **See also:** `QueryJobConfiguration`, `#stream(QueryJobConfiguration)`
- **Signature:** `public final Stream<FieldValueList> stream(final QueryJobConfiguration queryConfig) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Executes a BigQuery job and returns raw results as a Stream of FieldValueList.
- **Contract:**
  - This is useful when you need full control over result processing or when working with complex nested data structures.
- **Parameters:**
  - `queryConfig` (`QueryJobConfiguration`) — the BigQuery QueryJobConfiguration with query and job settings; must not be `null`
- **Returns:** a Stream containing raw FieldValueList objects from the query results; later page-fetch and row-conversion failures are raised during stream traversal
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `queryConfig` is `null`
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if BigQuery rejects `queryConfig` or its query job, the job fails or is cancelled, or the calling thread is interrupted while waiting for the job
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Stream raw FieldValueList for custom processing
  QueryJobConfiguration config = QueryJobConfiguration.newBuilder(
      "SELECT * FROM customers")
      .build();

  Stream<FieldValueList> rawStream = executor.stream(config);   // query completed; raw-row iteration is deferred

  rawStream.forEach(row -> {
      // Access fields by index or name
      String id = row.get("customer_id").getStringValue();
      String name = row.get("name").getStringValue();
      System.out.println(id + ": " + name);
  });

  // Handle complex nested structures
  QueryJobConfiguration nestedConfig = QueryJobConfiguration.newBuilder(
      "SELECT id, STRUCT(name, email) as contact FROM customers")
      .build();

  executor.stream(nestedConfig)
      .forEach(row -> {
          FieldValueList contactStruct = (FieldValueList) row.get("contact").getValue();
          // Process nested structure
      });
  ```
- **See also:** `QueryJobConfiguration`, `FieldValueList`, `#stream(Class, QueryJobConfiguration)`
##### execute(...) -> TableResult
- **Signature:** `public final TableResult execute(final String query, final Object... parameters) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Submits an arbitrary BigQuery SQL statement (SELECT/DML/DDL) as a query job with positional parameters and blocks the calling thread until it completes.
- **Parameters:**
  - `query` (`String`) — the SQL statement with `?` positional placeholders; must not be `null`
  - `parameters` (`Object...`) — values bound to the placeholders, in order; may be omitted entirely if the statement has no parameters
- **Returns:** the `TableResult` returned by BigQuery; for SELECT statements this contains the rows, for DML the affected-row count via `TableResult#getNumDmlAffectedRows()` (not `TableResult#getTotalRows()`, which the client sets to that count only when the statement completes within the initial `jobs.query` call or results are read in the Arrow format, and otherwise to the result's row count, `0`), for DDL a result with no schema
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `query` is null or empty, or any positional parameter is an untyped null (wrap SQL nulls in a typed `QueryParameterValue`)
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if parameter conversion fails, BigQuery rejects the SQL, the query job fails or is cancelled, or the calling thread is interrupted while waiting for its result
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // SELECT (java.sql.Date binds as a native DATE parameter; a raw LocalDate would bind as STRING)
  TableResult result = executor.execute(
      "SELECT * FROM customers WHERE status = ? AND created_date > ?",
      "active", java.sql.Date.valueOf(LocalDate.now().minusMonths(6)));   // returns a TableResult holding the selected rows

  // DML (returned TableResult exposes the affected-row count via getNumDmlAffectedRows())
  TableResult updated = executor.execute(
      "UPDATE customers SET status = ? WHERE last_order_date < ?",
      "inactive", java.sql.Date.valueOf(LocalDate.now().minusYears(1)));   // returns a TableResult; getNumDmlAffectedRows() is the affected-row count

  // DDL (no parameters; returned TableResult has no schema)
  executor.execute("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS test_table (id STRING, name STRING)");   // returns a TableResult
  ```
- **See also:** `#stream(Class, String, Object...)`, `#list(Class, String, Object...)`

## com.landawn.abacus.da.hadoop
## com.landawn.abacus.da.hbase
### Class AnyAppend (com.landawn.abacus.da.hbase.AnyAppend)
Fluent builder wrapper for HBase `Append` operations.

**Thread-safety:** unspecified
**Nullability:** unspecified
**Implements:** `Row`

#### Public Constructors
- (none)

#### Public Static Methods
##### of(...) -> AnyAppend
- **Signature:** `public static AnyAppend of(final Object rowKey) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Creates a new AnyAppend instance for the specified row key.
- **Parameters:**
  - `rowKey` (`Object`) — the row key to append data to; converted to bytes automatically
- **Returns:** a new AnyAppend instance configured for the specified row
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `rowKey` is `null`, an HBase operation or `Any*` wrapper, bare or held by a present value wrapper (not a row-key value), or an empty value wrapper (such as an empty `Optional`, which converts to no bytes), or its byte representation is empty or exceeds 32,767 bytes
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if converting `rowKey` to bytes invokes a failing string conversion
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  AnyAppend append = AnyAppend.of("user123");            // returns a new AnyAppend; row = "user123"
  append.addColumn("logs", "activity", "login;");        // returns the same AnyAppend (for chaining); queues the append

  AnyAppend numKey = AnyAppend.of(1001L);                // returns a new AnyAppend; numeric key encoded to bytes
  AnyAppend.of((Object) null);                           // throws IllegalArgumentException (null row key)
  AnyAppend.of(Optional.empty());                        // throws IllegalArgumentException (converts to no bytes)
  ```
- **See also:** `#addColumn(String, String, Object)`
- **Signature:** `public static AnyAppend of(final byte[] rowKey) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates a new AnyAppend instance for the specified byte array row key.
- **Contract:**
  - This is more efficient than the Object version when you already have the row key in byte array format, as it avoids the conversion overhead.
- **Parameters:**
  - `rowKey` (`byte[]`) — the row key as a byte array; must not be `null` or empty
- **Returns:** a new AnyAppend instance configured for the specified row
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `rowKey` is `null`, empty, or longer than 32,767 bytes
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  byte[] keyBytes = Bytes.toBytes("user123");
  AnyAppend append = AnyAppend.of(keyBytes);             // returns a new AnyAppend; row = a copy of keyBytes
  append.addColumn("logs", "activity", "login;");        // returns the same AnyAppend (for chaining)

  AnyAppend.of((byte[]) null);                           // throws IllegalArgumentException (null row key)
  AnyAppend.of(new byte[0]);                             // throws IllegalArgumentException (empty row key)
  ```
- **See also:** `#of(Object)`
- **Signature:** `public static AnyAppend of(final byte[] rowKey, final int rowOffset, final int rowLength) throws IllegalArgumentException, NegativeArraySizeException, ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException`
- **Summary:** Creates a new AnyAppend instance using a portion of the specified byte array as the row key.
- **Contract:**
  - This is useful when the row key is part of a larger byte array, allowing you to specify exactly which portion to use without creating a new array.
- **Parameters:**
  - `rowKey` (`byte[]`) — the source byte array containing the row key
  - `rowOffset` (`int`) — the starting position within the byte array (0-based)
  - `rowLength` (`int`) — the number of bytes to use for the row key
- **Returns:** a new AnyAppend instance configured for the specified row key portion
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `rowKey` is `null`, or `rowLength` is zero or exceeds 32,767 bytes
  - `java.lang.NegativeArraySizeException` — if `rowLength` is negative
  - `java.lang.ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException` — if `rowOffset` is negative or the selected slice extends beyond the end of `rowKey`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  byte[] data = "prefix:user123:suffix".getBytes();
  AnyAppend append = AnyAppend.of(data, 7, 7);           // returns a new AnyAppend; row = "user123"
  append.addColumn("logs", "activity", "login;");        // returns the same AnyAppend (for chaining)

  AnyAppend.of((byte[]) null, 0, 1);                     // throws IllegalArgumentException ("Row buffer is null")
  AnyAppend.of(Bytes.toBytes("abc"), 1, 5);              // throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException (offset+length > 3)
  AnyAppend.of(Bytes.toBytes("abc"), -1, 2);             // throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException (negative offset)
  ```
- **See also:** `#of(byte[])`
- **Signature:** `public static AnyAppend of(final Object rowKey, final int rowOffset, final int rowLength) throws IllegalArgumentException, NegativeArraySizeException, ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Creates a new AnyAppend instance using a portion of the row key object's byte representation.
- **Parameters:**
  - `rowKey` (`Object`) — the row key object whose byte representation will be sliced
  - `rowOffset` (`int`) — the starting position within the converted row-key bytes (0-based)
  - `rowLength` (`int`) — the number of bytes to use for the row key
- **Returns:** a new AnyAppend instance configured for the specified row key portion
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `rowKey` converts to `null` or is an HBase operation or `Any*` wrapper (bare or held by a present value wrapper), or `rowLength` is zero or exceeds 32,767 bytes
  - `java.lang.NegativeArraySizeException` — if `rowLength` is negative
  - `java.lang.ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException` — if `rowOffset` is negative or the selected slice extends beyond the converted row bytes
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if converting `rowKey` to bytes invokes a failing string conversion
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  AnyAppend append = AnyAppend.of("prefix:user123:suffix", 7, 7);   // returns a new AnyAppend; row = "user123"
  append.addColumn("logs", "activity", "login;");                   // returns the same AnyAppend (for chaining)

  AnyAppend.of((Object) null, 0, 1);      // throws IllegalArgumentException ("Row buffer is null")
  AnyAppend.of("abc", 1, 5);              // throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException (offset+length > 3)
  ```
- **See also:** `#of(byte[], int, int)`
- **Signature:** `public static AnyAppend of(final byte[] rowKey, final long timestamp, final NavigableMap<byte[], List<Cell>> familyMap) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates a new AnyAppend instance with pre-configured data and timestamp.
- **Contract:**
  - This is typically used for bulk operations or when reconstructing append operations from existing data structures.
- **Parameters:**
  - `rowKey` (`byte[]`) — the row key as a byte array; must not be `null` or empty
  - `timestamp` (`long`) — the default timestamp for subsequently added columns (milliseconds since epoch); a negative value is retained without validation, unlike `#setTimestamp(long)`
  - `familyMap` (`NavigableMap<byte[], List<Cell>>`) — a map of column family names to lists of cells to append; retained by reference. Order it by `Bytes.BYTES_COMPARATOR`, as HBase's own family maps are: with a naturally ordered map (a plain `new TreeMap<>()`) every later `addColumn`, `add`, `has` and `get` call throws `ClassCastException`
- **Returns:** a new AnyAppend instance configured with the specified data
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `rowKey` or `familyMap` is `null`, or `rowKey` is empty
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  long ts = System.currentTimeMillis();
  NavigableMap<byte[], List<Cell>> familyMap = new TreeMap<>(Bytes.BYTES_COMPARATOR);
  AnyAppend append = AnyAppend.of(Bytes.toBytes("user123"), ts, familyMap);
  // returns a new AnyAppend; row = "user123", timestamp = ts

  AnyAppend.of(Bytes.toBytes("k"), ts, null);            // throws IllegalArgumentException (familyMap is null)
  AnyAppend.of(new byte[0], ts, familyMap);              // throws IllegalArgumentException (empty row key)
  ```
- **See also:** `#of(Object)`, `org.apache.hadoop.hbase.Cell`
- **Signature:** `public static AnyAppend of(final Append appendToCopy) throws IllegalArgumentException, NullPointerException`
- **Summary:** Creates a new AnyAppend instance by copying an existing HBase Append operation.
- **Contract:**
  - Attributes (including the TTL, cluster ids, ACL, cell visibility and the return-results flag) and the priority are copied as well, but the Durability is not: HBase's copy constructor leaves it at `Durability.USE_DEFAULT`, so re-apply setDurability on the copy when the source used a non-default level.
- **Parameters:**
  - `appendToCopy` (`Append`) — the existing HBase `Append` to copy; must not be `null`
- **Returns:** a new AnyAppend instance backed by a fresh Append copied from `appendToCopy`
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `appendToCopy` is `null`
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if `appendToCopy`'s mutable family-cell map contains a null cell list, or it carries an attribute with a `null` name
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Append existingAppend = new Append(Bytes.toBytes("user123"));
  existingAppend.addColumn(Bytes.toBytes("logs"), Bytes.toBytes("activity"),
                           Bytes.toBytes("login;"));

  AnyAppend append = AnyAppend.of(existingAppend);       // returns a new AnyAppend wrapping a fresh copy
  assert append.val() != existingAppend;                 // true: the wrapped Append is a distinct copy
  append.addColumn("logs", "activity", "logout;");       // returns the same AnyAppend; does not mutate existingAppend

  AnyAppend.of((Append) null);                           // throws IllegalArgumentException
  ```
- **See also:** `org.apache.hadoop.hbase.client.Append`

#### Public Instance Methods
##### val(...) -> Append
- **Signature:** `public Append val()`
- **Summary:** Returns the underlying HBase Append object for direct access to native HBase operations.
- **Contract:**
  - Use this method when you need to access HBase-specific functionality or when integrating with existing HBase code.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the underlying HBase Append object
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  AnyAppend anyAppend = AnyAppend.of("user123")
                                 .addColumn("logs", "activity", "login;");
  Append hbaseAppend = anyAppend.val();                  // returns the wrapped Append; row = "user123"
  table.append(hbaseAppend);                             // use with the native HBase API

  assert anyAppend.val() == anyAppend.val();             // true: always returns the same wrapped instance
  ```
- **See also:** `Append`
##### setTimeRange(...) -> AnyAppend
- **Signature:** `public AnyAppend setTimeRange(final long minStamp, final long maxStamp) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Sets the TimeRange used by the Get that HBase performs before the append.
- **Contract:**
  - Caution: if the time range does not cover the latest cells the server will append against an older version, effectively rewriting it rather than the current value.
- **Parameters:**
  - `minStamp` (`long`) — minimum timestamp value, inclusive
  - `maxStamp` (`long`) — maximum timestamp value, exclusive
- **Returns:** this AnyAppend instance, to allow fluent method chaining
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `minStamp` or `maxStamp` is negative or if `maxStamp < minStamp`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Append into the cell version recorded during the current hour
  long hourStart = System.currentTimeMillis() / 3600000 * 3600000;
  long hourEnd = hourStart + 3600000;
  AnyAppend append = AnyAppend.of("hourly_log")
                              .setTimeRange(hourStart, hourEnd)   // returns the same AnyAppend; range = [hourStart, hourEnd)
                              .addColumn("logs", "events", "evt;");

  AnyAppend.of("k").setTimeRange(-1L, 10L);              // throws IllegalArgumentException (negative minStamp)
  AnyAppend.of("k").setTimeRange(200L, 100L);            // throws IllegalArgumentException (maxStamp < minStamp)
  ```
- **See also:** `#getTimeRange()`, `org.apache.hadoop.hbase.io.TimeRange`
##### getTimeRange(...) -> TimeRange
- **Signature:** `public TimeRange getTimeRange()`
- **Summary:** Returns the time range used by the pre-append read for this append operation.
- **Contract:**
  - If no time range has been set, this method returns the underlying `Append`'s default `TimeRange` (covering all timestamps).
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the configured `TimeRange`, or the default `TimeRange` if no specific range is set; never `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  AnyAppend append = AnyAppend.of("user123");
  append.getTimeRange().getMin();                        // returns 0 (default: covers all timestamps)
  append.getTimeRange().getMax();                        // returns Long.MAX_VALUE

  append.setTimeRange(100L, 200L);
  TimeRange range = append.getTimeRange();               // returns the configured TimeRange; never null
  range.getMin();                                        // returns 100
  range.getMax();                                        // returns 200
  ```
- **See also:** `#setTimeRange(long, long)`, `org.apache.hadoop.hbase.io.TimeRange`
##### setReturnResults(...) -> AnyAppend
- **Signature:** `public AnyAppend setReturnResults(final boolean returnResults)`
- **Summary:** Sets whether to return results after the append operation.
- **Parameters:**
  - `returnResults` (`boolean`) — `true` to return the post-append values (HBase's historical default for `Append`); `false` to skip the response payload and improve throughput
- **Returns:** this AnyAppend instance, to allow fluent method chaining
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Disable result return for better performance
  AnyAppend highThroughput = AnyAppend.of("log_key")
                                      .addColumn("logs", "events", "evt;")
                                      .setReturnResults(false);   // returns the same AnyAppend; isReturnResults() now false

  // Enable result return to inspect the concatenated value
  Object someData = "v;";
  AnyAppend withResults = AnyAppend.of("important_key")
                                   .addColumn("data", "value", someData)
                                   .setReturnResults(true);       // returns the same AnyAppend; isReturnResults() now true
  ```
- **See also:** `#isReturnResults()`
##### isReturnResults(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `public boolean isReturnResults() throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns whether this append operation is configured to return results.
- **Contract:**
  - This method returns `true` if the append operation is set to return the updated values after the operation.
  - If false, the operation will not return results, optimizing performance for scenarios where results are not needed.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** `true` if results will be returned, `false` otherwise
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the stored return-results attribute is not exactly one byte
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  AnyAppend append = AnyAppend.of("user123")
                              .addColumn("logs", "activity", "login;")
                              .setReturnResults(false);
  boolean returnsResults = append.isReturnResults();    // returns false

  AnyAppend fresh = AnyAppend.of("k");
  fresh.isReturnResults();                              // returns true (default for a new Append)
  ```
- **See also:** `#setReturnResults(boolean)`
##### addColumn(...) -> AnyAppend
- **Signature:** `public AnyAppend addColumn(final byte[] family, final byte[] qualifier, final byte[] value) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Adds the specified column and value to this append operation using byte array identifiers.
- **Contract:**
  - This is more efficient than the String version when you already have the data in byte array format, as it avoids conversion overhead.
- **Parameters:**
  - `family` (`byte[]`) — the column-family name as a byte array; must not be null or empty
  - `qualifier` (`byte[]`) — the column-qualifier name as a byte array; may be `null` to denote an empty qualifier
  - `value` (`byte[]`) — the byte array to append to the existing cell value; may be `null`
- **Returns:** this AnyAppend instance, to allow fluent method chaining
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `family` is null or empty (validated by the underlying `Append`), or the encoded family exceeds 127 bytes or the cell exceeds HBase's maximum size
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  byte[] familyBytes = Bytes.toBytes("logs");
  byte[] qualifierBytes = Bytes.toBytes("activity");
  byte[] valueBytes = Bytes.toBytes("login_event");

  AnyAppend append = AnyAppend.of("user123")
                              .addColumn(familyBytes, qualifierBytes, valueBytes);   // returns the same AnyAppend; queues the cell

  append.addColumn(familyBytes, (byte[]) null, valueBytes);       // ok: null qualifier means empty qualifier
  append.addColumn(familyBytes, qualifierBytes, (byte[]) null);   // ok: null value accepted
  append.addColumn((byte[]) null, qualifierBytes, valueBytes);    // throws IllegalArgumentException (null family)
  append.addColumn(new byte[0], qualifierBytes, valueBytes);      // throws IllegalArgumentException (empty family)
  ```
- **See also:** `#addColumn(String, String, Object)`
- **Signature:** `public AnyAppend addColumn(final String family, final String qualifier, final Object value) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Adds the specified column and value to this append operation using string identifiers.
- **Parameters:**
  - `family` (`String`) — the column-family name; converted via `HBaseExecutor#toFamilyQualifierBytes(String)`
  - `qualifier` (`String`) — the column-qualifier name; converted via `HBaseExecutor#toFamilyQualifierBytes(String)`
  - `value` (`Object`) — the value whose encoded bytes will be appended; converted via `HBaseExecutor#toValueBytes(Object)`; `null`, or a value with no string form such as an empty `Optional`, is stored like `null`, so no bytes are appended
- **Returns:** this AnyAppend instance, to allow fluent method chaining
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `family` is null or empty (validated by the underlying `Append`), or the encoded family exceeds 127 bytes or the cell exceeds HBase's maximum size
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if converting `value` to bytes invokes a failing string conversion
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  AnyAppend append = AnyAppend.of("user123");
  append.addColumn("logs", "activity", "login;");         // returns the same AnyAppend (for chaining); queues the cell
  append.addColumn("audit", "trail", "ACTION:LOGIN;");    // returns the same AnyAppend; second cell queued
  append.addColumn("settings", "history", "theme=dark;"); // returns the same AnyAppend; three families now present

  append.addColumn("metrics", "count", 12345);           // ok: non-string value encoded via toValueBytes
  ```
- **See also:** `#addColumn(byte[], byte[], byte[])`, `AnyIncrement`
##### add(...) -> AnyAppend
- **Signature:** `public AnyAppend add(final Cell cell) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Adds a pre-constructed `Cell` carrying bytes to concatenate.
- **Contract:**
  - Useful when an existing cell (for example one read out of an `org.apache.hadoop.hbase.CellScanner`) already encodes the value to append; for ordinary use prefer `#addColumn(String, String, Object)`.
  - The cell's row key must match this append's row key.
- **Parameters:**
  - `cell` (`Cell`) — the non-null `Cell` to add to this append operation
- **Returns:** this AnyAppend instance, to allow fluent method chaining
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `cell` is null, its row does not match this append's row, or its family is null or empty
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  byte[] row = Bytes.toBytes("user123");
  AnyAppend append = AnyAppend.of("user123");

  Cell cell = new KeyValue(row, Bytes.toBytes("logs"),
                           Bytes.toBytes("activity"), Bytes.toBytes("login;"));

  append.add(cell);                                      // returns the same AnyAppend (for chaining); cell queued
  ```
- **See also:** `org.apache.hadoop.hbase.Cell`, `#addColumn(String, String, Object)`
##### setAttribute(...) -> AnyAppend
- **Signature:** `public AnyAppend setAttribute(final String name, final byte[] value)`
- **Summary:** Sets a custom attribute on this append using a raw byte-array value.
- **Parameters:**
  - `name` (`String`) — the attribute name
  - `value` (`byte[]`) — the attribute value as a raw byte array; may be `null` to clear it
- **Returns:** this AnyAppend instance, to allow fluent method chaining
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  AnyAppend append = AnyAppend.of("user123");
  append.setAttribute("trace_id", Bytes.toBytes("trace-12345"));   // returns the same AnyAppend; getAttribute("trace_id") -> "trace-12345" bytes
  append.setAttribute("priority", Bytes.toBytes("high"));          // returns the same AnyAppend; attribute stored

  append.setAttribute("trace_id", (byte[]) null);       // returns the same AnyAppend; clears the "trace_id" attribute
  ```
- **See also:** `#getAttribute(String)`, `AnyOperationWithAttributes#setAttribute(String, Object)`
- **Signature:** `public AnyAppend setAttribute(final String name, final Object value) throws RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Sets or replaces an attribute on this operation.
- **Parameters:**
  - `name` (`String`) — the attribute name; null/blank handling is delegated to the underlying `OperationWithAttributes`, which is not validated here
  - `value` (`Object`) — the attribute value, converted to bytes via `HBaseExecutor#toValueBytes(Object)`. A `null` value is forwarded as a `null` byte array, which per the `OperationWithAttributes#setAttribute(String, byte[])` contract removes any attribute previously stored under `name`. An empty value wrapper such as `Optional.empty()` or an empty `Nullable` converts to `null` bytes and so removes the attribute too.
- **Returns:** this instance, to allow fluent method chaining
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if converting `value` to bytes invokes a failing string conversion
- **See also:** `#getAttribute(String)`, `HBaseExecutor#toValueBytes(Object)`
##### hashCode(...) -> int
- **Signature:** `public int hashCode()`
- **Summary:** Returns the hash code value for this AnyAppend instance.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the hash code value for this AnyAppend
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  AnyAppend a = AnyAppend.of("rowKey").addColumn("cf", "qualifier", "v");
  assert a.hashCode() == a.hashCode();   // true (stable; delegates to the wrapped HBase Append)

  // equals/hashCode are identity-based on the wrapped Append, so two distinct instances
  // built the same way are not equal and need not share a hash code:
  AnyAppend b = AnyAppend.of("rowKey").addColumn("cf", "qualifier", "v");
  a.equals(b);                    // returns false
  ```
- **See also:** `#equals(Object)`
##### equals(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `@SuppressFBWarnings public boolean equals(final Object obj)`
- **Summary:** Compares this AnyAppend instance with another object for equality.
- **Contract:**
  - The comparison is delegated to the underlying HBase `Append#equals(Object)`, which is identity-based: two separately constructed AnyAppend instances are not equal even when they wrap Appends with the same row key and identical columns.
- **Parameters:**
  - `obj` (`Object`) — the object to compare with
- **Returns:** `true` if the specified object is an `AnyAppend` whose underlying `Append` is equal to this one's, `false` otherwise
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  AnyAppend a = AnyAppend.of("rowKey").addColumn("cf", "qualifier", "v");
  a.equals(a);                    // returns true (same instance)

  // Two separately built appends are NOT equal, even with identical row and columns:
  AnyAppend b = AnyAppend.of("rowKey").addColumn("cf", "qualifier", "v");
  a.equals(b);                    // returns false

  a.equals(null);                 // returns false
  a.equals("not an AnyAppend");   // returns false
  ```
- **See also:** `#hashCode()`
##### toString(...) -> String
- **Signature:** `public String toString() throws NullPointerException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns a string representation of this AnyAppend instance.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** a string representation of the append operation
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if a wrapped mutation has a null cell list or a null cell that falls within the column-description limit
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the stored TTL attribute is shorter than eight bytes
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  AnyAppend a = AnyAppend.of("rowKey").addColumn("cf", "qualifier", "v");
  String s = a.toString();        // delegates to Append.toString(); never null
  s.contains("rowKey");           // returns true (the row key appears in the description)
  ```
- **Signature:** `public String toString(final int maxCols) throws NullPointerException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns a human-readable string representation of this operation using `maxCols` as HBase's total-column truncation budget.
- **Parameters:**
  - `maxCols` (`int`) — HBase's total-column truncation budget for the string representation
- **Returns:** a string representation generated with the requested truncation budget; never `null`
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if a wrapped mutation has a null cell list or a null cell that falls within the column-description limit
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the wrapped operation is a mutation whose stored TTL attribute is shorter than eight bytes
- **See also:** `#toString()`

##### getDurability(...) -> Durability
- **Signature:** `public Durability getDurability()`
- **Summary:** Returns the durability level currently set for this mutation.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the current durability level (defaults to `Durability#USE_DEFAULT` when none has been set explicitly, meaning the table-level default is applied)
- **See also:** `#setDurability(Durability)`, `Durability`
##### setDurability(...) -> AnyAppend
- **Signature:** `public AnyAppend setDurability(final Durability durability) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Sets the durability level for this mutation, trading throughput against persistence guarantees.
- **Contract:**
  - The supported levels are: SKIP_WAL: fastest, bypasses the write-ahead log (data-loss risk) ASYNC_WAL: fast, asynchronous WAL append SYNC_WAL: synchronous WAL append FSYNC_WAL: strongest, forces filesystem sync USE_DEFAULT: use the table-level setting `null` is rejected here rather than forwarded: the wrapped HBase `Mutation` would store it silently and only fail — with a bare `NullPointerException` raised deep inside HBase's request encoder — when the mutation is finally executed.
- **Parameters:**
  - `durability` (`Durability`) — the durability level to apply; must not be `null`
- **Returns:** this mutation instance, to allow fluent method chaining
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `durability` is `null`
- **See also:** `#getDurability()`, `Durability`

- **Signature:** `public AnyAppend setTimestamp(final long timestamp) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Sets this mutation's default timestamp, used as the version for cells added subsequently without their own explicit timestamp.
- **Contract:**

- **Parameters:**

- **Returns:** this mutation instance, to allow fluent method chaining
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `timestamp` is negative
- **See also:** `#getTimestamp()`, `System#currentTimeMillis()`

##### setACL(...) -> AnyAppend
- **Signature:** `public AnyAppend setACL(final String user, final Permission perms) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Grants the specified `Permission` to a single user on the data written by this mutation.
- **Parameters:**
  - `user` (`String`) — the username to grant permissions to; must not be `null`
  - `perms` (`Permission`) — the `Permission` defining the allowed actions; must not be `null`
- **Returns:** this mutation instance, to allow fluent method chaining
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `user` or `perms` is `null`
- **See also:** `#getACL()`, `#setACL(Map)`, `Permission`
- **Signature:** `public AnyAppend setACL(final Map<String, Permission> perms) throws IllegalArgumentException, NullPointerException`
- **Summary:** Grants the specified `Permission`s to multiple users on the data written by this mutation.
- **Parameters:**
  - `perms` (`Map<String, Permission>`) — a map of username to `Permission`; must not be `null`
- **Returns:** this mutation instance, to allow fluent method chaining
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `perms` is `null`
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if a username key or a permission value in `perms` is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  import org.apache.hadoop.hbase.security.access.Permission;
  import java.util.HashMap;
  import java.util.Map;

  Map<String, Permission> acl = new HashMap<>();
  acl.put("alice", new Permission(Permission.Action.READ, Permission.Action.WRITE));
  acl.put("bob", new Permission(Permission.Action.READ));
  mutation.setACL(acl);

  // Edge: a null map is rejected.
  mutation.setACL((Map<String, Permission>) null);   // throws IllegalArgumentException
  ```

- **Summary:** Sets the Time-To-Live (TTL), in milliseconds, for cells written by this mutation.

##### get(...) -> List<Cell>
- **Signature:** `public List<Cell> get(final String family, final String qualifier) throws NullPointerException`
- **Summary:** Returns every `Cell` already queued by this mutation that matches the given column family and qualifier.
- **Parameters:**
  - `family` (`String`) — the column-family name
  - `qualifier` (`String`) — the column-qualifier name
- **Returns:** a (possibly empty) list of matching `Cell`s; never `null`
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if traversal of the requested family reaches a null cell in the mutable family-cell map
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  AnyPut put = AnyPut.of("user123");
  put.addColumn("profile", "name", "Alice");
  put.addColumn("profile", "name", System.currentTimeMillis() - 1000, "Alice_Old");

  // Get all cells for the "name" column (may include multiple versions)
  List<Cell> cells = put.get("profile", "name");
  System.out.println("Number of versions: " + cells.size());
  ```
- **See also:** `#get(byte[], byte[])`, `#has(String, String)`, `Cell`
- **Signature:** `public List<Cell> get(final byte[] family, final byte[] qualifier) throws NullPointerException`
- **Summary:** Byte-array variant of `get(String, String)`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `family` (`byte[]`) — the column-family name as a byte array
  - `qualifier` (`byte[]`) — the column-qualifier name as a byte array
- **Returns:** a (possibly empty) list of matching `Cell`s; never `null`
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if traversal of the requested family reaches a null cell in the mutable family-cell map
- **See also:** `#get(String, String)`, `#has(byte[], byte[])`, `Cell`
##### has(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `public boolean has(final String family, final String qualifier) throws NullPointerException`
- **Summary:** Returns `true` if at least one `Cell` already queued by this mutation matches the given family and qualifier.
- **Parameters:**
  - `family` (`String`) — the column-family name
  - `qualifier` (`String`) — the column-qualifier name
- **Returns:** `true` if at least one matching cell is present; `false` otherwise
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if traversal of the requested family reaches a null cell in the mutable family-cell map
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  AnyPut put = AnyPut.of("user123");
  put.addColumn("profile", "name", "Alice");

  if (put.has("profile", "name")) {
      System.out.println("Mutation will update the name column");
  }
  ```
- **See also:** `#has(String, String, long)`, `#has(String, String, Object)`, `#get(String, String)`
- **Signature:** `public boolean has(final String family, final String qualifier, final long ts) throws NullPointerException`
- **Summary:** Returns `true` if a queued `Cell` matches the given family, qualifier, and timestamp.
- **Contract:**
  - All three components must match exactly.
- **Parameters:**
  - `family` (`String`) — the column-family name
  - `qualifier` (`String`) — the column-qualifier name
  - `ts` (`long`) — the cell timestamp, in milliseconds since the epoch; any primitive `byte`, `short`, `char`, `int` or `long` third argument selects this overload, even one meant as a cell value (see `#has(String, String, Object)`)
- **Returns:** `true` if a matching cell is queued; `false` otherwise
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if traversal of the requested family reaches a null cell in the mutable family-cell map
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  long timestamp = System.currentTimeMillis();
  AnyPut put = AnyPut.of("user123");
  put.addColumn("profile", "name", timestamp, "Alice");

  // Check for specific version
  if (put.has("profile", "name", timestamp)) {
      System.out.println("Mutation contains this specific version");
  }
  ```
- **See also:** `#has(String, String)`, `#has(String, String, long, Object)`
- **Signature:** `public boolean has(final String family, final String qualifier, final Object value) throws NullPointerException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Returns `true` if a queued `Cell` matches the given family, qualifier, and value.
- **Parameters:**
  - `family` (`String`) — the column-family name
  - `qualifier` (`String`) — the column-qualifier name
  - `value` (`Object`) — the value to look for; encoded via `HBaseExecutor#toValueBytes(Object)`, so an empty value wrapper such as `Optional.empty()` encodes to `null` bytes like `null`. A primitive `byte`, `short`, `char`, `int` or `long` argument does not reach this overload: it selects `#has(String, String, long)`, which compares it with the cell timestamp; pass a boxed value instead. A boxed number is encoded as its decimal text, so it never matches an `AnyIncrement` amount (queued as an 8-byte long): pass `Bytes.toBytes(amount)` for that
- **Returns:** `true` if a matching cell is queued; `false` otherwise
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if `value` is `null` or an empty value wrapper and a queued cell matches `family` and `qualifier` (raised by `Mutation#has(byte[], byte[], byte[])` while comparing values), or traversal of the requested family reaches a null cell
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the family is present and converting `value` to bytes invokes a failing string conversion
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  AnyPut put = AnyPut.of("user123");
  put.addColumn("profile", "name", "Alice");

  // Check if mutation will write specific value
  if (put.has("profile", "name", "Alice")) {
      System.out.println("Mutation will write 'Alice' to name column");
  }

  // This would return false
  boolean hasBob = put.has("profile", "name", "Bob");

  // Trap: a primitive byte, short, char, int or long argument selects has(String, String, long) and is compared
  // with the cell timestamp, not the value. Box it to look for a numeric value.
  AnyPut counter = AnyPut.of("user123").addColumn("stats", "visits", 5);
  counter.has("stats", "visits", 5);                    // returns false (timestamp 5)
  counter.has("stats", "visits", Integer.valueOf(5));   // returns true

  // Trap: a boxed number is encoded as its decimal text, as AnyPut stored it above, but an AnyIncrement queues its
  // amounts as 8-byte longs. Look for an increment amount by its bytes.
  AnyIncrement increment = AnyIncrement.of("user123").addColumn("stats", "visits", 5L);
  increment.has("stats", "visits", Long.valueOf(5));    // returns false (the text "5" is one byte)
  increment.has("stats", "visits", Bytes.toBytes(5L));  // returns true
  ```
- **See also:** `#has(String, String)`, `#has(String, String, long, Object)`
- **Signature:** `public boolean has(final String family, final String qualifier, final long ts, final Object value) throws NullPointerException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Returns `true` if a queued `Cell` matches all four of family, qualifier, timestamp, and value.
- **Parameters:**
  - `family` (`String`) — the column-family name
  - `qualifier` (`String`) — the column-qualifier name
  - `ts` (`long`) — the cell timestamp, in milliseconds since the epoch
  - `value` (`Object`) — the value to look for; encoded via `HBaseExecutor#toValueBytes(Object)`, so an empty value wrapper such as `Optional.empty()` encodes to `null` bytes like `null`. A boxed number is encoded as its decimal text, so it never matches an `AnyIncrement` amount (queued as an 8-byte long): pass `Bytes.toBytes(amount)` for that
- **Returns:** `true` if a matching cell is queued; `false` otherwise
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if `value` is `null` or an empty value wrapper and a queued cell matches `family` and `qualifier` (raised by `Mutation#has(byte[], byte[], long, byte[])` while comparing values), or traversal of the requested family reaches a null cell
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the family is present and converting `value` to bytes invokes a failing string conversion
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  long timestamp = System.currentTimeMillis();
  AnyPut put = AnyPut.of("user123");
  put.addColumn("profile", "name", timestamp, "Alice");

  // Check for exact match of all parameters
  if (put.has("profile", "name", timestamp, "Alice")) {
      System.out.println("Found exact cell match");
  }

  // Different timestamp would return false
  boolean hasDifferentTs = put.has("profile", "name", timestamp - 1000, "Alice");
  ```
- **See also:** `#has(String, String)`, `#has(String, String, long)`, `#has(String, String, Object)`

- **Returns:** this instance, to allow fluent method chaining
