- **Signature:** `public <T> ContinuableFuture<Stream<T>> stream(final Collection<String> selectPropNames, final Bson filter, final int offset, final int count, final Class<T> rowType) throws IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException, RejectedExecutionException`
- **Summary:** Asynchronously creates a stream with field projection and pagination.
- **Contract:**
  - Usage Examples: The returned future completes exceptionally if the delegated `stream` operation fails while converting documents or executing the MongoDB command.
  - This includes an `IllegalArgumentException` when `offset` or `count` is negative.
  - If cancellation of the returned future succeeds, any stream created by this operation is closed, including a stream created after cancellation.
  - Cancellation after successful completion returns `false` and does not close the delivered stream; the caller must close it after use.
- **Parameters:**
  - `selectPropNames` (`Collection<String>`) — the collection of BSON field names to include in the projection (null or empty for all fields); when `count` is positive, a null name in it fails the returned future with an `IllegalArgumentException` (the driver rejects it while encoding the query; a `count` of 0 sends no projection)
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — the query filter to match documents (must not be null)
  - `offset` (`int`) — the number of documents to skip
  - `count` (`int`) — the maximum number of documents to stream
  - `rowType` (`Class<T>`) — the Class object representing the row type
- **Returns:** a ContinuableFuture that completes with a paginated projected typed Stream
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null, or if `rowType` is null
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the backing AsyncExecutor has been shut down before task submission
  - `java.util.concurrent.RejectedExecutionException` — if the backing executor refuses the submitted task, for example because its queue is full or it has shut down
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  async.stream(Arrays.asList("userId", "action"), Filters.eq("type", "audit"),
         0, 1000, AuditLog.class)
  .thenRunAsync(stream -> archiveAuditLogs(stream));
  ```
- **See also:** `Stream`
- **Signature:** `public <T> ContinuableFuture<Stream<T>> stream(final Collection<String> selectPropNames, final Bson filter, final Bson sort, final Class<T> rowType) throws IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException, RejectedExecutionException`
- **Summary:** Asynchronously creates a stream with field projection and sorting.
- **Contract:**
  - When exactly one field is selected into a single-value `rowType`, that field's value is extracted directly (a dotted path such as `address.city` resolves the nested value), and a document that lacks the field yields a `null` element instead of its converted `_id`.
  - Usage Examples: The returned future completes exceptionally if the delegated `stream` operation fails while converting documents or executing the MongoDB command.
  - If cancellation of the returned future succeeds, any stream created by this operation is closed, including a stream created after cancellation.
  - Cancellation after successful completion returns `false` and does not close the delivered stream; the caller must close it after use.
- **Parameters:**
  - `selectPropNames` (`Collection<String>`) — the collection of BSON field names to include in the projection (null or empty for all fields); a null name in it fails the returned future with an `IllegalArgumentException` (the driver rejects it while encoding the query)
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — the query filter to match documents (must not be null)
  - `sort` (`Bson`) — the sort specification (null for natural order)
  - `rowType` (`Class<T>`) — the Class object representing the row type
- **Returns:** a ContinuableFuture that completes with a sorted projected typed Stream
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null, or if `rowType` is null
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the backing AsyncExecutor has been shut down before task submission
  - `java.util.concurrent.RejectedExecutionException` — if the backing executor refuses the submitted task, for example because its queue is full or it has shut down
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  async.stream(Arrays.asList("name", "highScore"), Filters.exists("highScore"),
         Sorts.descending("highScore"), Player.class)
  .thenRunAsync(stream -> displayLeaderboard(stream));
  ```
- **See also:** `Stream`, `com.mongodb.client.model.Sorts`
- **Signature:** `public <T> ContinuableFuture<Stream<T>> stream(final Collection<String> selectPropNames, final Bson filter, final Bson sort, final int offset, final int count, final Class<T> rowType) throws IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException, RejectedExecutionException`
- **Summary:** Asynchronously creates a stream with projection, sorting, and pagination.
- **Contract:**
  - When exactly one field is selected into a single-value `rowType`, that field's value is extracted directly (a dotted path such as `address.city` resolves the nested value), and a document that lacks the field yields a `null` element instead of its converted `_id`.
  - Usage Examples: The returned future completes exceptionally if the delegated `stream` operation fails while converting documents or executing the MongoDB command.
  - This includes an `IllegalArgumentException` when `offset` or `count` is negative.
  - If cancellation of the returned future succeeds, any stream created by this operation is closed, including a stream created after cancellation.
  - Cancellation after successful completion returns `false` and does not close the delivered stream; the caller must close it after use.
- **Parameters:**
  - `selectPropNames` (`Collection<String>`) — the collection of BSON field names to include in the projection (null or empty for all fields); when `count` is positive, a null name in it fails the returned future with an `IllegalArgumentException` (the driver rejects it while encoding the query; a `count` of 0 sends no projection)
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — the query filter to match documents (must not be null)
  - `sort` (`Bson`) — the sort specification (null for natural order)
  - `offset` (`int`) — the number of documents to skip
  - `count` (`int`) — the maximum number of documents to stream
  - `rowType` (`Class<T>`) — the Class object representing the row type
- **Returns:** a ContinuableFuture that completes with a fully configured typed Stream
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null, or if `rowType` is null
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the backing AsyncExecutor has been shut down before task submission
  - `java.util.concurrent.RejectedExecutionException` — if the backing executor refuses the submitted task, for example because its queue is full or it has shut down
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  async.stream(Arrays.asList("title", "views"), Filters.eq("published", true),
         Sorts.descending("views"), 0, 10, Article.class)
  .thenRunAsync(stream -> displayTopArticles(stream));
  ```
- **See also:** `Stream`
- **Signature:** `public <T> ContinuableFuture<Stream<T>> stream(final Bson projection, final Bson filter, final Bson sort, final Class<T> rowType) throws IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException, RejectedExecutionException`
- **Summary:** Asynchronously creates a stream with BSON projection and sorting.
- **Contract:**
  - Usage Examples: The returned future completes exceptionally if the delegated `stream` operation fails while converting documents or executing the MongoDB command.
  - If cancellation of the returned future succeeds, any stream created by this operation is closed, including a stream created after cancellation.
  - Cancellation after successful completion returns `false` and does not close the delivered stream; the caller must close it after use.
- **Parameters:**
  - `projection` (`Bson`) — the BSON projection specification (null for all fields)
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — the query filter to match documents (must not be null)
  - `sort` (`Bson`) — the sort specification (null for natural order)
  - `rowType` (`Class<T>`) — the Class object representing the row type
- **Returns:** a ContinuableFuture that completes with a projected and sorted typed Stream
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null, or if `rowType` is null
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the backing AsyncExecutor has been shut down before task submission
  - `java.util.concurrent.RejectedExecutionException` — if the backing executor refuses the submitted task, for example because its queue is full or it has shut down
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Bson projection = Projections.computed("fullName",
                                       new Document("$concat", Arrays.asList("$firstName", " ", "$lastName")));
  async.stream(projection, Filters.eq("active", true), Sorts.ascending("lastName"), User.class)
       .thenRunAsync(stream -> exportUserList(stream));
  ```
- **See also:** `Stream`, `com.mongodb.client.model.Projections`
- **Signature:** `public <T> ContinuableFuture<Stream<T>> stream(final Bson projection, final Bson filter, final Bson sort, final int offset, final int count, final Class<T> rowType) throws IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException, RejectedExecutionException`
- **Summary:** Asynchronously creates a stream with BSON projection, sorting, and pagination.
- **Contract:**
  - Usage Examples: The returned future completes exceptionally if the delegated `stream` operation fails while converting documents or executing the MongoDB command.
  - This includes an `IllegalArgumentException` when `offset` or `count` is negative.
  - If cancellation of the returned future succeeds, any stream created by this operation is closed, including a stream created after cancellation.
  - Cancellation after successful completion returns `false` and does not close the delivered stream; the caller must close it after use.
- **Parameters:**
  - `projection` (`Bson`) — the BSON projection specification (null for all fields)
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — the query filter to match documents (must not be null)
  - `sort` (`Bson`) — the sort specification (null for natural order)
  - `offset` (`int`) — the number of documents to skip
  - `count` (`int`) — the maximum number of documents to stream
  - `rowType` (`Class<T>`) — the Class object representing the row type
- **Returns:** a ContinuableFuture that completes with a fully configured typed Stream
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null, or if `rowType` is null
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the backing AsyncExecutor has been shut down before task submission
  - `java.util.concurrent.RejectedExecutionException` — if the backing executor refuses the submitted task, for example because its queue is full or it has shut down
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Bson projection = Projections.fields(
      Projections.include("title", "author"),
      Projections.elemMatch("reviews", Filters.gte("rating", 4))
  );

              0, 25, Book.class)
  ```

##### watch(...) -> varies by overload
- **Signature:** `public ContinuableFuture<ChangeStreamIterable<Document>> watch() throws IllegalStateException, RejectedExecutionException`
- **Summary:** Asynchronously creates a change stream to watch for changes in the collection.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** a ContinuableFuture that completes with a ChangeStreamIterable for Document changes
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the backing AsyncExecutor has been shut down before task submission
  - `java.util.concurrent.RejectedExecutionException` — if the backing executor refuses the submitted task, for example because its queue is full or it has shut down
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  async.watch()
  .thenRunAsync(changeStream -> changeStream.forEach(change ->
      System.out.println("Change detected: " + change.getOperationType())));
  ```
- **See also:** `ChangeStreamIterable`, `#watch(Class)`
- **Signature:** `public <T> ContinuableFuture<ChangeStreamIterable<T>> watch(final Class<T> rowType) throws IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException, RejectedExecutionException`
- **Summary:** Asynchronously creates a typed change stream to watch for changes.
- **Contract:**
  - Creating the iterable looks up the codec for `rowType`: the returned future completes exceptionally with a `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` if the collection's codec registry has none (possible for a collection passed to `MongoDB#collectionExecutor(com.mongodb.client.MongoCollection)` with its own registry).
- **Parameters:**
  - `rowType` (`Class<T>`) — the class to decode each change event's full document into
- **Returns:** a ContinuableFuture that completes with a typed ChangeStreamIterable
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `rowType` is null
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the backing AsyncExecutor has been shut down before task submission
  - `java.util.concurrent.RejectedExecutionException` — if the backing executor refuses the submitted task, for example because its queue is full or it has shut down
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  async.watch(Product.class)
  .thenRunAsync(changeStream -> changeStream.forEach(change ->
      updateInventoryCache(change.getFullDocument())));
  ```
- **See also:** `ChangeStreamIterable`, `#watch()`
- **Signature:** `public ContinuableFuture<ChangeStreamIterable<Document>> watch(final List<? extends Bson> pipeline) throws IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException, RejectedExecutionException`
- **Summary:** Asynchronously creates a change stream with an aggregation pipeline.
- **Contract:**
  - Likewise a `null` stage in `pipeline` does not fail the future: the driver throws an `IllegalArgumentException` when the cursor is opened.
- **Parameters:**
  - `pipeline` (`List<? extends Bson>`) — the aggregation pipeline to apply to change events
- **Returns:** a ContinuableFuture that completes with a filtered ChangeStreamIterable for Document changes
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `pipeline` is null
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the backing AsyncExecutor has been shut down before task submission
  - `java.util.concurrent.RejectedExecutionException` — if the backing executor refuses the submitted task, for example because its queue is full or it has shut down
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<Bson> pipeline = Arrays.asList(
      Aggregates.match(Filters.in("operationType", "insert", "update"))
  );
  async.watch(pipeline)
       .thenRunAsync(changeStream -> processFilteredChanges(changeStream));
  ```
- **See also:** `ChangeStreamIterable`, `com.mongodb.client.model.Aggregates`
- **Signature:** `public <T> ContinuableFuture<ChangeStreamIterable<T>> watch(final List<? extends Bson> pipeline, final Class<T> rowType) throws IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException, RejectedExecutionException`
- **Summary:** Asynchronously creates a typed change stream with an aggregation pipeline.
- **Contract:**
  - Creating the iterable looks up the codec for `rowType`: the returned future completes exceptionally with a `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` if the collection's codec registry has none (possible for a collection passed to `MongoDB#collectionExecutor(com.mongodb.client.MongoCollection)` with its own registry).
  - A `null` stage in `pipeline` does not fail the future: the driver throws an `IllegalArgumentException` when the cursor is opened.
- **Parameters:**
  - `pipeline` (`List<? extends Bson>`) — the aggregation pipeline to apply to change events
  - `rowType` (`Class<T>`) — the class to decode each change event's full document into
- **Returns:** a ContinuableFuture that completes with a filtered typed ChangeStreamIterable
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `pipeline` is null, or if `rowType` is null
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the backing AsyncExecutor has been shut down before task submission
  - `java.util.concurrent.RejectedExecutionException` — if the backing executor refuses the submitted task, for example because its queue is full or it has shut down
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<Bson> pipeline = Arrays.asList(
      Aggregates.match(Filters.eq("fullDocument.priority", "high"))
  );
  async.watch(pipeline, Task.class)
       .thenRunAsync(changeStream -> notifyHighPriorityChanges(changeStream));
  ```
- **See also:** `ChangeStreamIterable`, `com.mongodb.client.model.Aggregates`
##### insertOne(...) -> ContinuableFuture<InsertOneResult>
- **Signature:** `public ContinuableFuture<InsertOneResult> insertOne(final Object obj) throws IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException, RejectedExecutionException`
- **Summary:** Asynchronously inserts a single document into the collection.
- **Contract:**
  - Usage Examples: The returned future completes exceptionally if the delegated `insertOne` operation fails while converting documents or executing the MongoDB command.
- **Parameters:**
  - `obj` (`Object`) — the object to insert - can be Document, `Map<String, Object>`, or entity class with getter/setter methods
- **Returns:** a ContinuableFuture that completes with the `InsertOneResult` reported by the server
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `obj` is null
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the backing AsyncExecutor has been shut down before task submission
  - `java.util.concurrent.RejectedExecutionException` — if the backing executor refuses the submitted task, for example because its queue is full or it has shut down
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Insert a Document asynchronously:
  Document userDoc = new Document("name", "John")
                       .append("email", "john@example.com")
                       .append("age", 30);

  async.insertOne(userDoc)
       .thenRunAsync(result -> {
           System.out.println("User inserted successfully");
           // The generated _id (created by the driver when absent) is exposed via the result
           BsonValue userId = result.getInsertedId();
       });

  // Insert an entity and wait for completion:
  User user = new User("Jane", "jane@example.com", 25);
  InsertOneResult result = async.insertOne(user).get();
  ```
- **See also:** `#insertOne(Object, InsertOneOptions)`, `#insertMany(Collection)`
- **Signature:** `public ContinuableFuture<InsertOneResult> insertOne(final Object obj, final InsertOneOptions options) throws IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException, RejectedExecutionException`
- **Summary:** Asynchronously inserts a single document with custom options.
- **Contract:**
  - The document is converted via `MongoDBBase#toDocument(Object)` (or passed through when already a `Document`), and the insertion is executed on the thread pool.
  - Usage Examples: The returned future completes exceptionally if the delegated `insertOne` operation fails while converting documents or executing the MongoDB command.
- **Parameters:**
  - `obj` (`Object`) — the object to insert, which will be converted to a Document
  - `options` (`InsertOneOptions`) — the options to apply to the insert operation (null uses defaults)
- **Returns:** a ContinuableFuture that completes with the `InsertOneResult` reported by the server
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `obj` is null
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the backing AsyncExecutor has been shut down before task submission
  - `java.util.concurrent.RejectedExecutionException` — if the backing executor refuses the submitted task, for example because its queue is full or it has shut down
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  User newUser = new User("john", "john@example.com");
  InsertOneOptions options = new InsertOneOptions().bypassDocumentValidation(true);

  async.insertOne(newUser, options)
       .thenRunAsync(result -> System.out.println("User inserted with validation bypass: " + result.getInsertedId()));
  ```
- **See also:** `InsertOneOptions`, `#insertOne(Object)`

- **Signature:** `public ContinuableFuture<InsertManyResult> insertMany(final Collection<?> objList, final InsertManyOptions options) throws IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException, RejectedExecutionException`
- **Summary:** Asynchronously inserts multiple documents with custom options.
- **Contract:**
  - Usage Examples: The returned future completes exceptionally if the delegated `insertMany` operation fails while converting documents or executing the MongoDB command.
  - This includes an `IllegalArgumentException` when `objList` contains a null document.
- **Parameters:**
  - `objList` (`Collection<?>`) — the collection of objects to insert, each will be converted to a Document
  - `options` (`InsertManyOptions`) — the options to apply to the insert operation (null uses defaults)
- **Returns:** a ContinuableFuture that completes with the `InsertManyResult` reported by the server
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `objList` is null or empty
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the backing AsyncExecutor has been shut down before task submission
  - `java.util.concurrent.RejectedExecutionException` — if the backing executor refuses the submitted task, for example because its queue is full or it has shut down
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<Product> products = loadProductsFromCsv();
  InsertManyOptions options = new InsertManyOptions()
      .ordered(false)  // attempt every document even after one fails
      .bypassDocumentValidation(true);

  async.insertMany(products, options)
       .thenRunAsync(result -> System.out.println("Bulk product import completed: " + result.getInsertedIds()));
  // the callback runs only if every insert succeeded; otherwise the future fails with MongoBulkWriteException
  ```
- **See also:** `InsertManyOptions`, `#insertMany(Collection)`
##### updateOne(...) -> ContinuableFuture<UpdateResult>
- **Signature:** `public ContinuableFuture<UpdateResult> updateOne(final String objectId, final Object update) throws IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException, RejectedExecutionException`
- **Summary:** Asynchronously updates a single document identified by ObjectId string.
- **Contract:**
  - Usage Examples: The returned future completes exceptionally if the delegated `updateOne` operation fails while converting documents or executing the MongoDB command.
  - This includes an `IllegalArgumentException` when `objectId` is not a 24-character hexadecimal ObjectId.
- **Parameters:**
  - `objectId` (`String`) — the string representation of the ObjectId to identify the document
  - `update` (`Object`) — the update specification; can be Bson/Document/`Map<String, Object>`/entity class with getter/setter methods. A non-operator payload is wrapped in `$set` (use `replaceOne` to replace the whole document)
- **Returns:** a ContinuableFuture that completes with UpdateResult containing operation details
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `objectId` is null or empty, or if `update` is null
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the backing AsyncExecutor has been shut down before task submission
  - `java.util.concurrent.RejectedExecutionException` — if the backing executor refuses the submitted task, for example because its queue is full or it has shut down
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  String userId = "507f1f77bcf86cd799439011";
  Document update = new Document("$set", new Document("lastLogin", new Date()));

  async.updateOne(userId, update)
       .thenRunAsync(result -> {
           System.out.println("Modified count: " + result.getModifiedCount());
           if (result.getMatchedCount() == 0) {
               System.out.println("User not found");
           }
       });
  ```
- **See also:** `UpdateResult`, `#updateOne(ObjectId, Object)`, `com.mongodb.client.model.Updates`
- **Signature:** `public ContinuableFuture<UpdateResult> updateOne(final ObjectId objectId, final Object update) throws IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException, RejectedExecutionException`
- **Summary:** Asynchronously updates a single document identified by ObjectId.

  - Usage Examples: The returned future completes exceptionally if the delegated `updateOne` operation fails while converting documents or executing the MongoDB command.
- **Parameters:**
  - `objectId` (`ObjectId`) — the ObjectId to identify the document to update
  - `update` (`Object`) — the update specification; can be Bson/Document/`Map<String, Object>`/entity class with getter/setter methods. A non-operator payload is wrapped in `$set` (use `replaceOne` to replace the whole document)
- **Returns:** a ContinuableFuture that completes with UpdateResult containing operation details
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `objectId` is null, or if `update` is null
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the backing AsyncExecutor has been shut down before task submission
  - `java.util.concurrent.RejectedExecutionException` — if the backing executor refuses the submitted task, for example because its queue is full or it has shut down
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  ObjectId productId = new ObjectId();
  Bson update = Updates.combine(
      Updates.set("lastUpdated", new Date()),
      Updates.inc("version", 1)
  );

       .thenRunAsync(result -> {
  ```

- **Signature:** `public ContinuableFuture<UpdateResult> updateOne(final Bson filter, final Object update) throws IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException, RejectedExecutionException`
- **Summary:** Asynchronously updates a single document matching the specified filter.
- **Contract:**
  - Usage Examples: The returned future completes exceptionally if the delegated `updateOne` operation fails while converting documents or executing the MongoDB command.
- **Parameters:**
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — the query filter to select the document to update
  - `update` (`Object`) — the update specification; can be Bson/Document/`Map<String, Object>`/entity class with getter/setter methods. A non-operator payload is wrapped in `$set` (use `replaceOne` to replace the whole document)
- **Returns:** a ContinuableFuture that completes with UpdateResult containing operation details
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null, or if `update` is null
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the backing AsyncExecutor has been shut down before task submission
  - `java.util.concurrent.RejectedExecutionException` — if the backing executor refuses the submitted task, for example because its queue is full or it has shut down
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Bson filter = Filters.and(
      Filters.eq("status", "pending"),
      Filters.lt("createdAt", Date.from(Instant.now().minus(1, ChronoUnit.HOURS)))
  );
  Bson update = Updates.set("status", "expired");

  async.updateOne(filter, update)
       .thenRunAsync(result -> {
           System.out.println("Expired " + result.getModifiedCount() + " pending items");
       });
  ```

##### replaceOne(...) -> ContinuableFuture<UpdateResult>
- **Signature:** `public ContinuableFuture<UpdateResult> replaceOne(final String objectId, final Object replacement) throws IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException, RejectedExecutionException`
- **Summary:** Asynchronously replaces a single document by its ObjectId string representation.
- **Contract:**
  - When the replacement omits `_id`, MongoDB retains the matched document's value; a supplied `_id` must equal that value.
  - If no document exists with the given ObjectId, no operation is performed.
  - Usage Examples: The returned future completes exceptionally if the delegated `replaceOne` operation fails while converting documents or executing the MongoDB command.
  - This includes an `IllegalArgumentException` when `objectId` is not a 24-character hexadecimal ObjectId, or when the converted replacement has a top-level field name starting with `$`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `objectId` (`String`) — the string representation of the ObjectId to identify the document
  - `replacement` (`Object`) — the replacement document; an omitted `_id` is retained, while a supplied value must equal the matched document's `_id`
- **Returns:** a ContinuableFuture that completes with UpdateResult containing operation details
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `objectId` is null or empty, or if `replacement` is null
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the backing AsyncExecutor has been shut down before task submission
  - `java.util.concurrent.RejectedExecutionException` — if the backing executor refuses the submitted task, for example because its queue is full or it has shut down
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  User updatedUser = new User("John Doe", "john@example.com");
  async.replaceOne("507f1f77bcf86cd799439011", updatedUser)
       .thenRunAsync(result -> System.out.println("Replaced: " + result.getModifiedCount()));
  ```
- **See also:** `UpdateResult`, `#replaceOne(ObjectId, Object)`, `#replaceOne(Bson, Object)`
- **Signature:** `public ContinuableFuture<UpdateResult> replaceOne(final ObjectId objectId, final Object replacement) throws IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException, RejectedExecutionException`

  - If no document exists with the given ObjectId, no operation is performed.
  - Usage Examples: The returned future completes exceptionally if the delegated `replaceOne` operation fails while converting documents or executing the MongoDB command.
  - This includes an `IllegalArgumentException` when the converted replacement has a top-level field name starting with `$`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `objectId` (`ObjectId`) — the ObjectId to identify the document for replacement
  - `replacement` (`Object`) — the replacement document; an omitted `_id` is retained, while a supplied value must equal the matched document's `_id`
- **Returns:** a ContinuableFuture that completes with UpdateResult containing operation details
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `objectId` is null, or if `replacement` is null
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the backing AsyncExecutor has been shut down before task submission
  - `java.util.concurrent.RejectedExecutionException` — if the backing executor refuses the submitted task, for example because its queue is full or it has shut down
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  ObjectId id = new ObjectId("507f1f77bcf86cd799439011");

  async.replaceOne(id, newDoc).thenRunAsync(result -> System.out.println("Updated: " + result));
  ```
- **See also:** `UpdateResult`, `#replaceOne(String, Object)`, `#replaceOne(Bson, Object)`
- **Signature:** `public ContinuableFuture<UpdateResult> replaceOne(final Bson filter, final Object replacement) throws IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException, RejectedExecutionException`
- **Summary:** Asynchronously replaces a single document matching the specified filter.
- **Contract:**
  - An omitted `_id` is retained; a supplied value must equal the matched document's `_id`.
  - Usage Examples: The returned future completes exceptionally if the delegated `replaceOne` operation fails while converting documents or executing the MongoDB command.
  - This includes an `IllegalArgumentException` when the converted replacement has a top-level field name starting with `$`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — the query filter to select the document to replace
  - `replacement` (`Object`) — the replacement document; an omitted `_id` is retained, while a supplied value must equal the matched document's `_id`

- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null, or if `replacement` is null
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the backing AsyncExecutor has been shut down before task submission
  - `java.util.concurrent.RejectedExecutionException` — if the backing executor refuses the submitted task, for example because its queue is full or it has shut down
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Replace user document with updated profile:
  User updatedProfile = new User();
  updatedProfile.setName("John Doe Updated");
  updatedProfile.setEmail("john.updated@example.com");
  updatedProfile.setRole("senior_developer");

  Bson filter = Filters.eq("userId", "user123");

  async.replaceOne(filter, updatedProfile)
       .thenRunAsync(result -> {
           if (result.getMatchedCount() > 0) {
               System.out.println("User profile replaced successfully");
           } else {
               System.out.println("No user found with the specified ID");
           }
       });
  ```

- **See also:** `UpdateResult`, `#replaceOne(Bson, Object, ReplaceOptions)`, `#updateOne(Bson, Object)`
- **Signature:** `public ContinuableFuture<UpdateResult> replaceOne(final Bson filter, final Object replacement, final ReplaceOptions options) throws IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException, RejectedExecutionException`
- **Summary:** Asynchronously replaces a single document matching the specified filter with custom options.
- **Contract:**
  - You can specify whether to upsert (insert if no match found) and set other replacement behaviors.
  - For a matched document, an omitted `_id` is retained and a supplied value must equal the existing `_id`.
  - Usage Examples: The returned future completes exceptionally if the delegated `replaceOne` operation fails while converting documents or executing the MongoDB command.
  - This includes an `IllegalArgumentException` when the converted replacement has a top-level field name starting with `$`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — the query filter to select the document to replace
  - `replacement` (`Object`) — the replacement document; for a match, an omitted `_id` is retained while a supplied value must equal the matched document's `_id`
  - `options` (`ReplaceOptions`) — the options to apply to the replace operation (null uses defaults)
- **Returns:** a ContinuableFuture that completes with UpdateResult containing operation details
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null, or if `replacement` is null
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the backing AsyncExecutor has been shut down before task submission
  - `java.util.concurrent.RejectedExecutionException` — if the backing executor refuses the submitted task, for example because its queue is full or it has shut down
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  ReplaceOptions options = new ReplaceOptions().upsert(true);
  Document replacement = new Document("status", "active").append("updated", new Date());
  async.replaceOne(Filters.eq("userId", "123"), replacement, options)
       .thenRunAsync(result -> System.out.println("Upserted: " + result.getUpsertedId()));
  ```

##### deleteOne(...) -> ContinuableFuture<DeleteResult>
- **Signature:** `public ContinuableFuture<DeleteResult> deleteOne(final String objectId) throws IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException, RejectedExecutionException`
- **Summary:** Asynchronously deletes a single document by its ObjectId string representation.
- **Contract:**
  - The ObjectId string must be a valid 24-character hexadecimal representation.
  - Only one document is deleted, even if multiple documents somehow have the same _id.
  - Usage Examples: The returned future completes exceptionally if the delegated `deleteOne` operation fails while converting documents or executing the MongoDB command.
  - This includes an `IllegalArgumentException` when `objectId` is not a 24-character hexadecimal ObjectId.

- **Returns:** a ContinuableFuture that completes with DeleteResult containing operation details
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `objectId` is null or empty
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the backing AsyncExecutor has been shut down before task submission
  - `java.util.concurrent.RejectedExecutionException` — if the backing executor refuses the submitted task, for example because its queue is full or it has shut down
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  String userId = "507f1f77bcf86cd799439011";

  async.deleteOne(userId)
       .thenRunAsync(result -> {
           if (result.getDeletedCount() > 0) {
               System.out.println("User deleted successfully");
           } else {
               System.out.println("No user found with ID: " + userId);
           }
       });
  ```

  - `java.util.concurrent.RejectedExecutionException` — if the backing executor refuses the submitted task, for example because its queue is full or it has shut down

- **Signature:** `public ContinuableFuture<DeleteResult> deleteOne(final Bson filter, final DeleteOptions options) throws IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException, RejectedExecutionException`

  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null

- **Examples:**
  ```java

       .thenRunAsync(result -> System.out.println("Case-insensitive delete: " + result.getDeletedCount()));
  ```

- **Signature:** `public ContinuableFuture<BulkWriteResult> bulkInsert(final Collection<?> entities, final BulkWriteOptions options) throws IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException, RejectedExecutionException`
- **Summary:** Asynchronously performs a bulk insert of multiple documents with custom options.

  - You can specify whether the operations should be ordered (stop on first error) or unordered (continue despite errors), and control validation.
  - Usage Examples: The returned future completes exceptionally if the delegated `bulkInsert` operation fails while converting documents or executing the MongoDB command.
  - This includes an `IllegalArgumentException` when `entities` contains a null document.
- **Parameters:**

- **Throws:**

  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the backing AsyncExecutor has been shut down before task submission
  - `java.util.concurrent.RejectedExecutionException` — if the backing executor refuses the submitted task, for example because its queue is full or it has shut down
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  BulkWriteOptions options = new BulkWriteOptions().ordered(false).bypassDocumentValidation(true);
  async.bulkInsert(documents, options)
       .thenRunAsync(result -> System.out.println("Inserted " + result.getInsertedCount() + " documents (unordered)"));
  ```

- **Contract:**

  - Usage Examples: The returned future completes exceptionally if the delegated `bulkWrite` operation fails while converting documents or executing the MongoDB command.
  - This includes an `IllegalArgumentException` when `requests` contains a null write model.
- **Parameters:**
  - `requests` (`List<? extends WriteModel<? extends Document>>`) — the list of write operations to perform
  - `options` (`BulkWriteOptions`) — the options to apply to the bulk write operation (null uses defaults)
- **Returns:** a ContinuableFuture that completes with BulkWriteResult containing operation details
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `requests` is null or empty
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the backing AsyncExecutor has been shut down before task submission
  - `java.util.concurrent.RejectedExecutionException` — if the backing executor refuses the submitted task, for example because its queue is full or it has shut down
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  BulkWriteOptions options = new BulkWriteOptions().ordered(false);
  async.bulkWrite(operations, options).thenRunAsync(result -> {
      System.out.println("Inserted: " + result.getInsertedCount());
      System.out.println("Deleted: " + result.getDeletedCount());
  });
  // the callback runs only if every write succeeded; otherwise the future fails with MongoBulkWriteException
  ```
- **See also:** `BulkWriteResult`, `BulkWriteOptions`, `#bulkWrite(List)`

##### distinct(...) -> ContinuableFuture<Stream<T>>
- **Signature:** `public <T> ContinuableFuture<Stream<T>> distinct(final String fieldName, final Class<T> rowType) throws IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException, RejectedExecutionException`
- **Summary:** Asynchronously retrieves distinct values for a specified field.
- **Contract:**
  - Usage Examples: The returned future completes exceptionally if the delegated `distinct` operation fails while converting documents or executing the MongoDB command.
  - If cancellation of the returned future succeeds, any stream created by this operation is closed, including a stream created after cancellation.
  - Cancellation after successful completion returns `false` and does not close the delivered stream; the caller must close it after use.
- **Parameters:**
  - `fieldName` (`String`) — the field name to get distinct values for
  - `rowType` (`Class<T>`) — the class to deserialize the distinct values into
- **Returns:** a ContinuableFuture that completes with a Stream of distinct values
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `fieldName` is null or empty, or if `rowType` is null
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the backing AsyncExecutor has been shut down before task submission
  - `java.util.concurrent.RejectedExecutionException` — if the backing executor refuses the submitted task, for example because its queue is full or it has shut down
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  async.distinct("category", String.class)
  .thenRunAsync(stream -> stream.forEach(System.out::println));
  ```

- **Signature:** `public <T> ContinuableFuture<Stream<T>> distinct(final String fieldName, final Bson filter, final Class<T> rowType) throws IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException, RejectedExecutionException`
- **Summary:** Asynchronously retrieves distinct values for a specified field with a filter.
- **Contract:**
  - Usage Examples: The returned future completes exceptionally if the delegated `distinct` operation fails while converting documents or executing the MongoDB command.
  - If cancellation of the returned future succeeds, any stream created by this operation is closed, including a stream created after cancellation.
  - Cancellation after successful completion returns `false` and does not close the delivered stream; the caller must close it after use.
- **Parameters:**
  - `fieldName` (`String`) — the field name to get distinct values for
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — the query filter to apply before getting distinct values (must not be null)
  - `rowType` (`Class<T>`) — the class to deserialize the distinct values into
- **Returns:** a ContinuableFuture that completes with a Stream of distinct values
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `fieldName` is null or empty, or if `filter` is null, or if `rowType` is null
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the backing AsyncExecutor has been shut down before task submission
  - `java.util.concurrent.RejectedExecutionException` — if the backing executor refuses the submitted task, for example because its queue is full or it has shut down
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  async.distinct("department", Filters.eq("active", true), String.class)
  .thenRunAsync(stream -> stream.sorted().forEach(System.out::println));
  ```
- **See also:** `#distinct(String, Class)`
##### aggregate(...) -> varies by overload
- **Signature:** `public ContinuableFuture<Stream<Document>> aggregate(final List<? extends Bson> pipeline) throws IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException, RejectedExecutionException`
- **Summary:** Asynchronously executes an aggregation pipeline and returns results as Documents.
- **Contract:**
  - Usage Examples: The returned future completes exceptionally if the delegated `aggregate` operation fails while converting documents or executing the MongoDB command.
  - This includes the driver's `IllegalArgumentException` when `pipeline` contains a null stage (only a null `pipeline` itself is rejected at the call site).
  - If cancellation of the returned future succeeds, any stream created by this operation is closed, including a stream created after cancellation.
  - Cancellation after successful completion returns `false` and does not close the delivered stream; the caller must close it after use.
- **Parameters:**
  - `pipeline` (`List<? extends Bson>`) — the aggregation pipeline to execute
- **Returns:** a ContinuableFuture that completes with a Stream of result Documents
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `pipeline` is null
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the backing AsyncExecutor has been shut down before task submission
  - `java.util.concurrent.RejectedExecutionException` — if the backing executor refuses the submitted task, for example because its queue is full or it has shut down
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<Bson> pipeline = Arrays.asList(
      Aggregates.match(Filters.eq("status", "active")),
      Aggregates.group("$category", Accumulators.sum("total", 1))
  );
  async.aggregate(pipeline).thenRunAsync(stream ->
      stream.forEach(doc -> System.out.println(doc)));
  ```
- **See also:** `#aggregate(List, Class)`, `com.mongodb.client.model.Aggregates`
- **Signature:** `public <T> ContinuableFuture<Stream<T>> aggregate(final List<? extends Bson> pipeline, final Class<T> rowType) throws IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException, RejectedExecutionException`
- **Summary:** Asynchronously executes an aggregation pipeline with type conversion.
- **Contract:**
  - Useful when the aggregation output matches a known document structure.
  - Usage Examples: The returned future completes exceptionally if the delegated `aggregate` operation fails while converting documents or executing the MongoDB command.
  - This includes the driver's `IllegalArgumentException` when `pipeline` contains a null stage (only a null `pipeline` itself is rejected at the call site).
  - If cancellation of the returned future succeeds, any stream created by this operation is closed, including a stream created after cancellation.
  - Cancellation after successful completion returns `false` and does not close the delivered stream; the caller must close it after use.
- **Parameters:**
  - `pipeline` (`List<? extends Bson>`) — the aggregation pipeline to execute
  - `rowType` (`Class<T>`) — the class to deserialize the result documents into
- **Returns:** a ContinuableFuture that completes with a Stream of result objects
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `pipeline` is null, or if `rowType` is null
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the backing AsyncExecutor has been shut down before task submission
  - `java.util.concurrent.RejectedExecutionException` — if the backing executor refuses the submitted task, for example because its queue is full or it has shut down
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<Bson> pipeline = Arrays.asList(
      Aggregates.match(Filters.gte("score", 80)),
      Aggregates.sort(Sorts.descending("score"))
  );

      stream.limit(10).forEach(result -> System.out.println(result)));
  ```

- **Signature:** `@Beta public ContinuableFuture<Stream<Document>> groupByAndCount(final String fieldName) throws IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException, RejectedExecutionException`
- **Annotations:** @Beta
- **Summary:** Asynchronously groups documents by a single field and counts frequency in each group.
- **Contract:**
  - Usage Examples: The returned future completes exceptionally if the delegated `groupByAndCount` operation fails while converting documents or executing the MongoDB command.
  - If cancellation of the returned future succeeds, any stream created by this operation is closed, including a stream created after cancellation.
  - Cancellation after successful completion returns `false` and does not close the delivered stream; the caller must close it after use.
- **Parameters:**
  - `fieldName` (`String`) — the field name to group by and count. A path with an empty segment (such as `"a..b"`) is rejected by the delegated `groupByAndCount` operation and completes the returned future exceptionally
- **Returns:** a ContinuableFuture that completes with a Stream of Documents containing group keys and counts
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `fieldName` is null or empty
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the backing AsyncExecutor has been shut down before task submission
  - `java.util.concurrent.RejectedExecutionException` — if the backing executor refuses the submitted task, for example because its queue is full or it has shut down
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Count users by department:
  async.groupByAndCount("department")
       .thenRunAsync(stream -> {

                                ", Count: " + group.get("count"));
           });
       });

  async.groupByAndCount("category")
       .thenRunAsync(stream -> stream.forEach(System.out::println));
  ```

- **Contract:**
  - Usage Examples: The returned future completes exceptionally if the delegated `groupByAndCount` operation fails while converting documents or executing the MongoDB command.
  - If cancellation of the returned future succeeds, any stream created by this operation is closed, including a stream created after cancellation.

### Class MongoCollectionExecutor (com.landawn.abacus.da.mongodb.MongoCollectionExecutor)
Comprehensive MongoDB collection executor providing high-level CRUD operations, aggregation pipelines, and advanced query capabilities.

**Thread-safety:** thread-safe
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Public Constructors
- (none)

#### Public Static Methods
- (none)

#### Public Instance Methods
##### coll(...) -> MongoCollection<Document>
- **Signature:** `public MongoCollection<Document> coll()`
- **Summary:** Returns the underlying MongoDB collection instance for advanced operations.
- **Contract:**
  - This method provides direct access to the native MongoDB Java driver's `MongoCollection` for operations not exposed by this executor or when you need fine-grained control over MongoDB driver features like read preferences, write concerns, or custom codecs.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the underlying MongoCollection instance
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  MongoCollection<Document> collection = executor.coll();      // never null; same instance every call
  collection.withWriteConcern(WriteConcern.MAJORITY).insertOne(document); // document inserted with majority write concern
  ```
- **See also:** `MongoCollection`
##### async(...) -> AsyncMongoCollectionExecutor
- **Signature:** `public AsyncMongoCollectionExecutor async()`
- **Summary:** Returns an asynchronous version of this executor for non-blocking operations.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** an AsyncMongoCollectionExecutor for asynchronous operations
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  AsyncMongoCollectionExecutor asyncExecutor = executor.async(); // never null; shared async view of this executor
  ContinuableFuture<List<Document>> future = asyncExecutor.list(Filters.eq("status", "active"));
  ```

##### exists(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `public boolean exists(final String objectId) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException`
- **Summary:** Checks if a document exists in the collection by its ObjectId string representation (blocking operation).
- **Contract:**
  - The string must be a valid 24-character hexadecimal ObjectId.
- **Parameters:**
  - `objectId` (`String`) — the string representation of the ObjectId to check for existence
- **Returns:** `true` if a document with the specified ObjectId exists, `false` otherwise
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `objectId` is null or is not a 24-character hexadecimal ObjectId
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  if (executor.exists("507f1f77bcf86cd799439011")) {                                          // returns true only when a document with that _id exists
      executor.updateOne("507f1f77bcf86cd799439011", Updates.set("lastSeen", new Date()));    // returns an UpdateResult
  }

  executor.exists("");   // throws IllegalArgumentException (empty objectId)
  executor.exists((String) null); // throws IllegalArgumentException (null objectId)
  ```
- **See also:** `#exists(ObjectId)`, `#exists(Bson)`, `#async()`
- **Signature:** `public boolean exists(final ObjectId objectId) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException`
- **Summary:** Checks if a document exists in the collection by its ObjectId.

  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
- **Examples:**

  ```java
  ObjectId oid = new ObjectId();
  boolean exists = executor.exists(oid); // true if a document with _id == oid exists, false otherwise
  ```
- **See also:** `ObjectId`, `#exists(String)`
- **Signature:** `public boolean exists(final Bson filter) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException`
- **Summary:** Checks if any documents exist in the collection matching the specified filter.
- **Contract:**
  - It's more efficient than using `find().limit(1)` when you only need to know if matching documents exist without retrieving them.
- **Parameters:**
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — the query filter to match documents against (must not be null)
- **Returns:** `true` if any documents match the filter, `false` otherwise
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  boolean hasActiveUsers = executor.exists(Filters.eq("status", "active"));                  // true if at least one match
  boolean hasRecentUsers = executor.exists(Filters.gte("createdAt", Dates.parseToJUDate("2023-01-01"))); // true if any match
  executor.exists((Bson) null);                                                              // throws IllegalArgumentException (filter must not be null)
  ```
- **See also:** `com.mongodb.client.model.Filters`

  - For large collections, consider using `#estimatedDocumentCount()` for better performance when exact counts are not required.
- **Parameters:**

- **Returns:** the total number of documents in the collection
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
- **Examples:**
  ```java

  ```
- **See also:** `#count(Bson)`, `#estimatedDocumentCount()`, `#async()`
- **Signature:** `public long count(final Bson filter) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException`
- **Summary:** Returns the number of documents in the collection matching the specified filter.
- **Parameters:**
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — the query filter to count matching documents (must not be null; use `#count()` for an unfiltered count)
- **Returns:** the number of documents matching the filter
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  long activeUsers = executor.count(Filters.eq("status", "active"));         // number of matching documents (0 if none)
  long adultUsers = executor.count(Document.parse("{age: {$gte: 18}}"));     // number of matching documents
  executor.count((Bson) null);                                               // throws IllegalArgumentException (use count() for an unfiltered count)
  ```
- **See also:** `com.mongodb.client.model.Filters`, `#count(Bson, CountOptions)`
- **Signature:** `public long count(final Bson filter, final CountOptions options) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException`
- **Summary:** Returns the number of documents matching the filter with additional count options.
- **Parameters:**
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — the query filter to count matching documents (must not be null; use `#count()` for an unfiltered count)
  - `options` (`CountOptions`) — additional options for the count operation (null uses defaults)
- **Returns:** the number of documents matching the filter within the specified constraints
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  CountOptions options = new CountOptions().limit(1000);
  long limitedCount = executor.count(Filters.exists("email"), options); // at most 1000 (capped by the limit)
  long plainCount = executor.count(Filters.exists("email"), null);      // null options -> behaves like count(filter)
  ```
- **See also:** `CountOptions`, `com.mongodb.client.model.Filters`

- **Signature:** `public Optional<Document> get(final String objectId) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException`
- **Summary:** Retrieves a document by its ObjectId string representation.

  - The ObjectId string must be a valid 24-character hexadecimal representation.
  - For the nullable counterpart that returns the document directly (or `null` when not found) instead of an `Optional`, use `#gett(String)`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `objectId` (`String`) — the string representation of the ObjectId to search for

- **Throws:**

  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed

- **Examples:**

- **Summary:** Finds the first document matching the filter with field projection, sorting, and type conversion.
- **Contract:**
  - The sort parameter determines which document is considered "first" when multiple documents match the filter; only the specified fields are retrieved and the document is converted to the target type.
  - When exactly one field is selected for a scalar `rowType` (a BSON value type such as Binary, Code or Symbol is scalar here too), that named field is converted directly; a missing field yields `Optional#empty()` rather than converting MongoDB's implicit `_id` projection.
- **Parameters:**
  - `selectPropNames` (`Collection<String>`) — collection of field names to include in the projection (null for all fields)
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — the query filter to match documents against (must not be null)
  - `sort` (`Bson`) — the sort criteria for ordering results (null for no sorting)
  - `rowType` (`Class<T>`) — the Class representing the target type for conversion
- **Returns:** an Optional containing the first matching sorted converted object with projected fields, or empty if none found
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null, or if `rowType` is null, or if a returned document has multiple non-`_id` fields for a scalar result type or a value that cannot be converted to the requested type, or if `selectPropNames` contains a null name (the driver rejects it while encoding the query, whatever `rowType` is)
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
  - `java.lang.ArrayStoreException` — if the result type is a reference-array type and a returned document value is incompatible with its component type
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if a dotted property path traverses a non-null value that is not a Document
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if converting a result value overflows its target numeric range, a registered converter or type handler throws, or constructing or populating a result bean or map, or invoking a bean accessor, fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Collection<String> fields = Arrays.asList("name", "score", "createdAt");
  Optional<Student> topStudent = executor.findFirst(fields,
      Filters.eq("active", true),
      Sorts.descending("score"),
      Student.class); // highest-scoring active student (sort decides "first"), or empty if none
  ```
- **See also:** `com.mongodb.client.model.Projections`, `com.mongodb.client.model.Sorts`

- **Summary:** Finds the first document matching the filter with BSON projection, sorting, and type conversion.
- **Parameters:**
  - `projection` (`Bson`) — BSON projection specification for field selection (null for all fields)
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — the query filter to match documents against (must not be null)
  - `sort` (`Bson`) — the sort criteria for ordering results (null for no sorting)
  - `rowType` (`Class<T>`) — the Class representing the target type for conversion
- **Returns:** an Optional containing the first matching sorted converted object with projected fields, or empty if none found
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null, or if `rowType` is null, or if a returned document has multiple non-`_id` fields for a scalar result type or a value that cannot be converted to the requested type
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
  - `java.lang.ArrayStoreException` — if the result type is a reference-array type and a returned document value is incompatible with its component type
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if converting a result value overflows its target numeric range, a registered converter or type handler throws, or constructing or populating a result bean or map, or invoking a bean accessor, fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Bson projection = Projections.fields(
      Projections.include("name", "score"),
      Projections.excludeId()
  );
  Optional<Student> topStudent = executor.findFirst(projection,
      Filters.eq("active", true),
      Sorts.descending("score"),
      Student.class); // highest-scoring active student with _id excluded, or empty if none
  ```
- **See also:** `com.mongodb.client.model.Projections`, `com.mongodb.client.model.Sorts`

  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error

  ```java
  List<Document> activeUsers = executor.list(Filters.eq("status", "active")); // all matching docs; empty list (never null) if none
  ```

  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if converting a result value overflows its target numeric range, a registered converter or type handler throws, or constructing or populating a result bean or map, or invoking a bean accessor, fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Get second page of 20 active users:
  List<User> page2Users = executor.list(
      Filters.eq("status", "active"), 20, 20, User.class); // up to 20 users after skipping the first 20
  ```

  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if a dotted property path traverses a non-null value that is not a Document
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if converting a result value overflows its target numeric range, a registered converter or type handler throws, or constructing or populating a result bean or map, or invoking a bean accessor, fails
