- **See also:** `#list(Collection, Bson, Class)`, `#list(Collection, Bson, Bson, int, int, Class)`, `com.mongodb.client.model.Sorts`
- **Signature:** `public <T> List<T> list(final Collection<String> selectPropNames, final Bson filter, final Bson sort, final int offset, final int count, final Class<T> rowType) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException, ClassCastException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Retrieves a list of documents with field projection, filtering, sorting, and pagination support.
- **Contract:**
  - When exactly one field is selected into a scalar type (a BSON value type such as Binary, Code or Symbol included), that requested value is extracted directly; dotted paths such as `address.city` resolve the nested value, and a missing value becomes `null` instead of being mistaken for MongoDB's implicitly projected `_id`.
  - Unlike for a single field selected into a scalar type, a document that has only its `_id` yields `null` when another returned document has a non-`_id` field, but its converted `_id` when none does.
- **Parameters:**
  - `selectPropNames` (`Collection<String>`) — collection of field names to include in projection (null for all fields)
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — BSON filter criteria to match documents (must not be null)
  - `sort` (`Bson`) — BSON sort specification for result ordering (null for natural order)
  - `offset` (`int`) — number of documents to skip from the beginning of results (0 for no offset)
  - `count` (`int`) — maximum number of documents to return (Integer.MAX_VALUE for all matching)
  - `rowType` (`Class<T>`) — an entity class with getter/setter method, Map.class or basic single value type (Primitive/String/Date...)
- **Returns:** a list of documents converted to the specified type, may be empty but never null
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null, or if `offset` is negative, or if `count` is negative, or if `rowType` is null, or if a returned document has multiple non-`_id` fields for a scalar result type, inconsistent scalar projection fields, or a value that cannot be converted to the requested type, or if `selectPropNames` contains a null name and `count` is positive (the driver rejects it while encoding the query, whatever `rowType` is; a `count` of 0 sends no projection)
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if a dotted property path traverses a non-null value that is not a Document
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if converting a result value overflows its target numeric range, a registered converter or type handler throws, or constructing or populating a result bean or map, or invoking a bean accessor, fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Collection<String> fields = Arrays.asList("name", "email");
  Bson sort = Sorts.ascending("name");
  List<User> users = executor.list(fields, Filters.eq("status", "active"), sort, 0, 10, User.class); // first 10 active users by name; empty list if none
  ```
- **See also:** `#list(Bson, Bson, Bson, int, int, Class)`, `com.mongodb.client.model.Filters`, `com.mongodb.client.model.Sorts`
- **Signature:** `public <T> List<T> list(final Bson projection, final Bson filter, final Bson sort, final Class<T> rowType) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Retrieves all matching documents with BSON projection, filtering, and sorting.
- **Contract:**
  - This is suitable when you need all matching results or when the result set is expected to be manageable in size.
  - A document that has only its `_id` (for example because it lacks the projected field) yields `null` (the primitive default, such as `0`, for a primitive class token such as `int.class`) when another returned document has the projected field, but its converted `_id` when none does.
- **Parameters:**
  - `projection` (`Bson`) — BSON projection specification for field selection (null for all fields)
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — BSON filter criteria to match documents (must not be null)
  - `sort` (`Bson`) — BSON sort specification for result ordering (null for natural order)
  - `rowType` (`Class<T>`) — an entity class with getter/setter method, Map.class or basic single value type (Primitive/String/Date...)
- **Returns:** a list of all matching documents converted to the specified type, may be empty but never null
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null, or if `rowType` is null, or if a returned document has multiple non-`_id` fields for a scalar result type, inconsistent scalar projection fields, or a value that cannot be converted to the requested type
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if converting a result value overflows its target numeric range, a registered converter or type handler throws, or constructing or populating a result bean or map, or invoking a bean accessor, fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Bson projection = Projections.include("name", "email");
  Bson sort = Sorts.ascending("name");
  List<User> allActiveUsers = executor.list(projection, Filters.eq("status", "active"), sort, User.class); // all active users by name, only name/email; empty list if none
  ```
- **See also:** `#list(Bson, Bson, Bson, int, int, Class)`, `com.mongodb.client.model.Projections`
- **Signature:** `public <T> List<T> list(final Bson projection, final Bson filter, final Bson sort, final int offset, final int count, final Class<T> rowType) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Retrieves a list of documents with BSON projection, filtering, sorting, and pagination support.
- **Contract:**
  - A document that has only its `_id` (for example because it lacks the projected field) yields `null` (the primitive default, such as `0`, for a primitive class token such as `int.class`) when another returned document has the projected field, but its converted `_id` when none does.
- **Parameters:**
  - `projection` (`Bson`) — BSON projection specification for advanced field selection (null for all fields)
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — BSON filter criteria to match documents (must not be null)
  - `sort` (`Bson`) — BSON sort specification for result ordering (null for natural order)
  - `offset` (`int`) — number of documents to skip from the beginning of results (0 for no offset)
  - `count` (`int`) — maximum number of documents to return (Integer.MAX_VALUE for all matching)
  - `rowType` (`Class<T>`) — an entity class with getter/setter method, Map.class or basic single value type (Primitive/String/Date...)
- **Returns:** a list of documents converted to the specified type, may be empty but never null
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null, or if `offset` is negative, or if `count` is negative, or if `rowType` is null, or if a returned document has multiple non-`_id` fields for a scalar result type, inconsistent scalar projection fields, or a value that cannot be converted to the requested type
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if converting a result value overflows its target numeric range, a registered converter or type handler throws, or constructing or populating a result bean or map, or invoking a bean accessor, fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Bson projection = Projections.fields(
      Projections.include("name", "email"),
      Projections.slice("tags", 5)
  );
  Bson filter = Filters.and(
      Filters.eq("status", "active"),
      Filters.gte("lastLogin", thirtyDaysAgo)
  );
  List<User> recentUsers = executor.list(projection, filter, Sorts.descending("lastLogin"), 0, 50, User.class); // up to 50 most-recent active users; empty list if none
  ```
- **See also:** `com.mongodb.client.model.Projections`, `com.mongodb.client.model.Filters`, `com.mongodb.client.model.Sorts`
##### queryForBoolean(...) -> OptionalBoolean
- **Signature:** `@Beta public OptionalBoolean queryForBoolean(final String propName, final Bson filter) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException, ClassCastException, RuntimeException`
- **Annotations:** @Beta
- **Summary:** Executes a query and returns the value of `propName` from the first matching document as a boolean value.
- **Contract:**
  - present semantics: `OptionalBoolean.empty()` is returned only when no document matches the filter.
  - When a document is matched but has no field named `propName` (or the stored value is BSON null), the underlying `Nullable.of(null)` is unboxed via `ToBooleanFunction#UNBOX` to the primitive default `false`, so the returned `OptionalBoolean` is present and holds `false`.
  - Use `#queryForSingleValue(String, Bson, Class)` with `Boolean.class` if you need to distinguish a missing/null field from a real `false` value.
- **Parameters:**
  - `propName` (`String`) — the name of the field to retrieve the boolean value from
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — BSON filter criteria to match documents (must not be null)
- **Returns:** a present `OptionalBoolean` holding the converted field value (or `false` for a missing/null field, or for empty or whitespace-only text) when a document is matched; `OptionalBoolean.empty()` when no document matches the filter
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `propName` is null or empty, or if `filter` is null, or if the selected field value cannot be converted to `Boolean` (for example an int64, double or `Decimal128` value, an int32 other than `1`/`0`/`-1`, or text such as `"yes"` once its surrounding whitespace is ignored; see `MongoDBBase`)
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if a dotted property path traverses a non-null value that is not a Document
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if a registered converter or type handler throws while converting the selected value
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  OptionalBoolean isActive = executor.queryForBoolean("active", Filters.eq("userId", "u1")); // present (false for a missing/null field) if a doc matched; empty if none matched
  if (isActive.orElse(false)) {
      // user is active
  }
  ```
- **See also:** `#queryForSingleValue(String, Bson, Class)`
##### queryForChar(...) -> OptionalChar
- **Signature:** `@Beta public OptionalChar queryForChar(final String propName, final Bson filter) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException, ClassCastException, RuntimeException`
- **Annotations:** @Beta
- **Summary:** Executes a query and returns the value of `propName` from the first matching document as a char value.
- **Contract:**
  - present semantics: `OptionalChar.empty()` is returned only when no document matches the filter.
  - When a document is matched but has no field named `propName` (or the stored value is BSON null), the underlying `Nullable.of(null)` is unboxed via `ToCharFunction#UNBOX` to the primitive default `(char) 0`, so the returned `OptionalChar` is present and holds `(char) 0`.
  - Use `#queryForSingleValue(String, Bson, Class)` with `Character.class` if you need to distinguish a missing/null field from a real `(char) 0`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `propName` (`String`) — the name of the field to retrieve the character value from
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — BSON filter criteria to match documents (must not be null)
- **Returns:** a present `OptionalChar` holding the converted field value (or `(char) 0` for a missing/null field) when a document is matched; `OptionalChar.empty()` when no document matches the filter
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `propName` is null or empty, or if `filter` is null, or if the selected field value cannot be converted to the requested value type
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if a dotted property path traverses a non-null value that is not a Document
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if a registered converter or type handler throws while converting the selected value
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  OptionalChar grade = executor.queryForChar("grade", Filters.eq("studentId", "S12345")); // present ((char) 0 for a missing/null field) if a doc matched; empty if none
  char letter = grade.orElse(' ');
  ```
- **See also:** `#queryForSingleValue(String, Bson, Class)`

- **Signature:** `@Beta public Nullable<String> queryForString(final String propName, final Bson filter) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException, ClassCastException, RuntimeException`
- **Annotations:** @Beta
- **Summary:** Executes a query and returns the value of `propName` from the first matching document as a String value.
- **Contract:**
  - present semantics: `Nullable.empty()` is returned only when no document matches the filter.
  - When a document matches, the returned `Nullable` is present and holds the converted value — which itself may be `null` if the field is absent on the matched document or the stored field value is null (`Nullable.of(null)`).
- **Parameters:**
  - `propName` (`String`) — the name of the field to retrieve the string value from
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — BSON filter criteria to match documents (must not be null)
- **Returns:** a present `Nullable<String>` holding the field value (possibly `null` for a missing/null field) when a document is matched; `Nullable.empty()` when no document matches the filter
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `propName` is null or empty, or if `filter` is null, or if the selected field value cannot be converted to the requested value type
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if a dotted property path traverses a non-null value that is not a Document
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if a registered converter or type handler throws while converting the selected value
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Nullable<String> email = executor.queryForString("email", Filters.eq("userId", "u1")); // present (value may be null) if a doc matched; Nullable.empty() if none
  String userEmail = email.orElseIfNull(""); // "" if no doc matched OR the matched doc's email is missing/null (orElse("") would return null for the latter)
  ```
- **See also:** `#queryForSingleValue(String, Bson, Class)`

##### queryForSingleValue(...) -> Nullable<V>
- **Signature:** `public <V> Nullable<V> queryForSingleValue(final String propName, final Bson filter, final Class<V> valueType) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException, ClassCastException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Executes a query and returns the value of `propName` from the first matching document, converted to the specified type.
- **Contract:**
  - An embedded document requested as a bean class is read as the embedded document of a bean property is read (the elements of a `List<Long>` property become `Long`s, a `LocalDate` property is read in UTC, a `String` or `ObjectId` id property takes the document's own `id` field, if any, over its `_id`), and an array of embedded documents requested as a bean array likewise element by element.
  - present semantics: this method returns `Nullable.empty()` when no nonempty document is found.
- **Parameters:**
  - `propName` (`String`) — the name of the field to retrieve the value from
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — BSON filter criteria to match documents (must not be null)
  - `valueType` (`Class<V>`) — the target type for conversion of the field value
- **Returns:** a present `Nullable<V>` holding the converted field value (possibly `null` for a missing/null field) when a document is matched; `Nullable.empty()` when no nonempty document is found
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `propName` is null or empty, or if `filter` is null, or if `valueType` is null, or if the selected field value cannot be converted to the requested value type
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if a dotted property path traverses a non-null value that is not a Document
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if numeric conversion overflows the target range, or a registered converter or type handler throws while converting the selected value, or constructing or populating a result bean fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Nullable<String> email = executor.queryForSingleValue(
          "email", Filters.eq("userId", "u1"), String.class); // present (value may be null) if a doc matched; Nullable.empty() if none
  Nullable<BigDecimal> price = executor.queryForSingleValue(
          "price", Filters.eq("productId", "P001"), BigDecimal.class); // converted to BigDecimal; Nullable.empty() if no doc matched
  ```
- **See also:** `#queryForSingleNonNull(String, Bson, Class)`, `com.landawn.abacus.util.u.Nullable`
##### queryForSingleNonNull(...) -> Optional<V>
- **Signature:** `public <V> Optional<V> queryForSingleNonNull(final String propName, final Bson filter, final Class<V> valueType) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException, ClassCastException, RuntimeException, NullPointerException`
- **Summary:** Executes a query and returns the value of `propName` from the first matching document, converted to the specified type and wrapped in an `Optional` that never carries a null payload.
- **Contract:**
  - present semantics: this method returns `Optional.empty()` when no nonempty document is found.
  - If conversion yields `null`, this method throws `NullPointerException`.
  - Use `#queryForSingleValue(String, Bson, Class)` with a wrapper or reference type when a matched-but-null value must be represented.
- **Parameters:**
  - `propName` (`String`) — the name of the field to retrieve the value from
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — BSON filter criteria to match documents (must not be null)
  - `valueType` (`Class<V>`) — the target type for conversion of the field value
- **Returns:** a present `Optional<V>` holding the converted non-null value when a document is matched and conversion yields a non-null value; `Optional.empty()` when no nonempty document is found
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `propName` is null or empty, or if `filter` is null, or if `valueType` is null, or if the selected field value cannot be converted to the requested value type
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if a dotted property path traverses a non-null value that is not a Document
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if numeric conversion overflows the target range, or a registered converter or type handler throws while converting the selected value, or constructing or populating a result bean fails
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if a nonempty document is matched and conversion of its selected field to `valueType` yields `null`, because `Optional#of(Object)` rejects a null payload
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Optional<Integer> activeCount = executor.queryForSingleNonNull(
          "activeUsers", Filters.eq("type", "summary"), Integer.class); // present non-null value if matched; Optional.empty() if no doc matched
  activeCount.filter(c -> c > 100).ifPresent(c -> sendHighActivityAlert());

  // If a doc matches but "activeUsers" is absent/null, Optional.of(null) rejects it:
  executor.queryForSingleNonNull("activeUsers", Filters.eq("type", "summary"), Integer.class); // throws NullPointerException
  ```
- **See also:** `#queryForSingleValue(String, Bson, Class)`, `com.landawn.abacus.util.u.Optional`
##### query(...) -> Dataset
- **Signature:** `public Dataset query(final Bson filter) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException`
- **Summary:** Executes a query and returns the results as a Dataset with Document rows.
- **Parameters:**
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — BSON filter criteria to match documents (must not be null)
- **Returns:** a Dataset containing the query results with Document-based rows; its columns are the fields of the returned documents, so when no document matches it is empty and has no columns
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Get all active users as a Dataset:
  Dataset activeUsers = executor.query(Filters.eq("status", "active")); // non-null Dataset; 0 rows if no document matches

  // Export to CSV:
  activeUsers.toCsv(new File("active_users.csv"));

  // Print tabular format:
  activeUsers.println();

  // Access column data:
  List<String> userNames = activeUsers.getColumn("name");
  ```
- **See also:** `Dataset`, `#query(Bson, Class)`, `#query(Collection, Bson, Class)`
- **Signature:** `public Dataset query(final Bson filter, final Class<?> rowType) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Executes a query and returns the results as a Dataset with typed rows.
- **Parameters:**
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — BSON filter criteria to match documents (must not be null)
  - `rowType` (`Class<?>`) — the target type for conversion of each document
- **Returns:** a Dataset containing the query results with typed rows; when no document matches it is empty and has no columns (use `#query(Collection, Bson, Class)` to keep named columns)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null, or if `rowType` is null, or if `rowType` is neither a bean class nor a Map type, or if a returned document cannot be converted to a bean `rowType`
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if converting a result value overflows its target numeric range, a registered converter or type handler throws, or constructing or populating a result bean or map, or invoking a bean accessor, fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Get active users as a Dataset of User objects:
  Dataset userDataset = executor.query(Filters.eq("status", "active"), User.class); // non-null Dataset of User rows; 0 rows if none match

  // Access typed data:
  List<User> users = userDataset.toList(User.class);
  User firstUser = userDataset.getRow(0, User.class);

  // Get data as Maps for flexible processing:
  Dataset mapDataset = executor.query(Filters.eq("category", "electronics"), Map.class); // non-null Dataset of Map rows; 0 rows if none match

  // Export with type safety:
  userDataset.toCsv(new File("typed_users.csv"));
  ```

- **Signature:** `public Dataset query(final Bson filter, final int offset, final int count, final Class<?> rowType) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Executes a paginated query and returns the results as a Dataset with typed rows.
- **Parameters:**
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — BSON filter criteria to match documents (must not be null)
  - `offset` (`int`) — number of documents to skip from the beginning (0 for first page)
  - `count` (`int`) — maximum number of documents to return
  - `rowType` (`Class<?>`) — the target type for conversion of each document
- **Returns:** a Dataset containing the paginated query results with typed rows; when no document matches it is empty and has no columns (use `#query(Collection, Bson, int, int, Class)` to keep named columns)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null, or if `offset` is negative, or if `count` is negative, or if `rowType` is null, or if `rowType` is neither a bean class nor a Map type, or if a returned document cannot be converted to a bean `rowType`
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if converting a result value overflows its target numeric range, a registered converter or type handler throws, or constructing or populating a result bean or map, or invoking a bean accessor, fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Get page 2 of products (20 per page) as a Dataset:
  Dataset productPage = executor.query(Filters.eq("category", "electronics"), 20, 20, Map.class); // up to 20 rows after skipping 20; 0 rows if none match

  // Export paginated results:
  productPage.toCsv(new File("products_page2.csv"));

  // Process paginated User objects:
  Dataset userPage = executor.query(Filters.eq("type", "user"), 0, 50, User.class); // first 50 matching documents
  List<User> firstUsers = userPage.toList(User.class);
  ```

- **Signature:** `public Dataset query(final Bson projection, final Bson filter, final Bson sort, final Class<?> rowType) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Executes a query with BSON field projection, filtering, and sorting, returning all results as a Dataset with typed rows.

  - `rowType` (`Class<?>`) — the target type for conversion of each document
- **Returns:** a Dataset containing all matching query results with projected fields and typed rows; when no document matches it is empty and has no columns, since the field names inside a `Bson` projection are not known (use `#query(Collection, Bson, Bson, Class)` to keep the selected columns)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null, or if `rowType` is null, or if `rowType` is neither a bean class nor a Map type, or if a returned document cannot be converted to a bean `rowType`
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if converting a result value overflows its target numeric range, a registered converter or type handler throws, or constructing or populating a result bean or map, or invoking a bean accessor, fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Get all active users with selected fields:
  Bson projection = Projections.fields(Projections.include("userId", "name", "email"));
  Bson filter = Filters.eq("status", "active");
  Bson sort = Sorts.ascending("name");
  Dataset users = executor.query(projection, filter, sort, User.class); // all active users by name, only the projected fields; 0 rows and NO columns if none match

  // Export sorted projected data:
  users.toCsv(new File("active_users.csv"));

  // Process data (when nothing matched, getColumn throws IllegalArgumentException: the Dataset has no columns):
  List<String> emails = users.getColumn("email");
  ```

- **Signature:** `public Stream<Document> stream() throws CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException`
- **Summary:** Creates a stream of all documents in the collection.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** a Stream of Document objects representing all documents in the collection
- **Throws:**
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Process all documents in the collection:
  executor.stream() // returns a lazy Stream over every document; closing it (or completing a terminal op) releases the cursor
          .filter(doc -> doc.getInteger("age", 0) > 18)
          .limit(100)
          .forEach(doc -> processAdultDocument(doc));

  // Count documents with functional operations:
  long activeCount = executor.stream()
                            .filter(doc -> "active".equals(doc.getString("status")))
                            .count();

  // Transform and collect:
  List<String> names = executor.stream()
                               .map(doc -> doc.getString("name"))
                               .filter(Objects::nonNull)
                               .collect(Collectors.toList());
  ```
- **See also:** `Stream`, `#stream(Class)`, `#stream(Bson)`
- **Signature:** `public <T> Stream<T> stream(final Class<T> rowType) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException`
- **Summary:** Creates a typed stream of all documents in the collection with automatic conversion.
- **Parameters:**
  - `rowType` (`Class<T>`) — the target type for conversion of each document
- **Returns:** a Stream of typed objects representing all documents in the collection
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `rowType` is null
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Process all users with type safety:
  executor.stream(User.class) // returns a lazy Stream of every document converted to User
          .filter(User::isActive)
          .map(User::getEmail)
          .filter(Objects::nonNull)
          .forEach(email -> sendNotification(email));

  executor.stream((Class<User>) null); // throws IllegalArgumentException (rowType must not be null; no cursor opened)

  // Collect typed results:
  List<User> activeAdults = executor.stream(User.class)
                                   .filter(user -> user.getAge() > 18)
                                   .filter(User::isActive)
                                   .collect(Collectors.toList());

  // Use with Maps for flexible processing:
  executor.stream(Map.class)
          .filter(map -> "premium".equals(map.get("tier")))
          .forEach(this::processPremiumAccount);
  ```
- **See also:** `Stream`, `#stream()`, `#stream(Bson, Class)`
- **Signature:** `public Stream<Document> stream(final Bson filter) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException`
- **Summary:** Creates a filtered stream of documents from the collection.
- **Parameters:**
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — BSON filter criteria to match documents (must not be null)
- **Returns:** a Stream of Document objects matching the filter criteria
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Process active users:
  Bson activeFilter = Filters.eq("status", "active");
  executor.stream(activeFilter) // returns a lazy Stream of the matching documents
          .filter(doc -> doc.getDate("lastLogin").after(thirtyDaysAgo))
          .forEach(doc -> updateActivityScore(doc));

  // Find and process premium accounts:
  Bson premiumFilter = Filters.eq("accountType", "premium");
  Optional<Document> firstExpired = executor.stream(premiumFilter)
                                           .filter(doc -> doc.getDate("expiresAt").before(new Date()))
                                           .findFirst();

  // Aggregate data with streams:
  double avgAge = executor.stream(Filters.exists("age"))
                         .mapToInt(doc -> doc.getInteger("age", 0))
                         .average()
                         .orElse(0.0);
  ```

- **Signature:** `public <T> Stream<T> stream(final Bson filter, final Class<T> rowType) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException`
- **Summary:** Creates a filtered, typed stream of documents with automatic conversion.
- **Parameters:**
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — BSON filter criteria to match documents (must not be null)
  - `rowType` (`Class<T>`) — the target type for conversion of each document
- **Returns:** a Stream of typed objects matching the filter criteria
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null, or if `rowType` is null
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Process active users with type safety:
  Bson activeFilter = Filters.eq("status", "active");
  executor.stream(activeFilter, User.class)
          .filter(user -> user.getLastLoginDate().after(recentDate))
          .map(User::getEmail)
          .forEach(this::sendWelcomeBackEmail);

  // Find high-value orders:
  Bson highValueFilter = Filters.gte("total", 1000.0);

                                       .filter(order -> order.getStatus() == OrderStatus.PENDING)

          .limit(10)
          .forEach(this::processHighRatedProduct);
  ```

  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null, or if `offset` is negative, or if `count` is negative, or if `rowType` is null, or if `selectPropNames` contains a null name and `count` is positive (the driver rejects it while encoding the query; a `count` of 0 sends no projection)
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Get specific fields with pagination
  List<String> fields = Arrays.asList("name", "status");
  executor.stream(fields, filter, 0, 100, User.class)
          .collect(Collectors.toList());
  ```
- **Signature:** `public <T> Stream<T> stream(final Collection<String> selectPropNames, final Bson filter, final Bson sort, final Class<T> rowType) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException`
- **Summary:** Creates a sorted stream with projection and filtering.
- **Contract:**
  - When exactly one field is selected into a single-value `rowType`, that field's value is extracted directly (a dotted path such as `address.city` resolves the nested value), and a document that lacks the field yields a `null` element instead of its converted `_id`.
  - The selected scalar field is captured when the stream is created.
- **Parameters:**
  - `selectPropNames` (`Collection<String>`) — collection of field names to include in projection (null for all fields)
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — BSON filter criteria to match documents (must not be null)
  - `sort` (`Bson`) — BSON sort criteria (null for no sorting)
  - `rowType` (`Class<T>`) — the target type for conversion of each document
- **Returns:** a sorted Stream of typed objects
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null, or if `rowType` is null, or if `selectPropNames` contains a null name (the driver rejects it while encoding the query)
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Get users sorted by creation date
  Bson sort = Sorts.descending("createdAt");
  executor.stream(fields, filter, sort, User.class)
          .limit(10)
          .forEach(this::displayRecentUser);
  ```
- **Signature:** `public <T> Stream<T> stream(final Collection<String> selectPropNames, final Bson filter, final Bson sort, final int offset, final int count, final Class<T> rowType) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException`
- **Summary:** Creates a fully-featured stream with projection, filtering, sorting, and pagination.
- **Contract:**
  - The selected scalar field is captured when the stream is created.
  - When exactly one field is selected into a single-value `rowType`, that field's value is extracted directly (a dotted path such as `address.city` resolves the nested value), and a document that lacks the field yields a `null` element instead of its converted `_id`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `selectPropNames` (`Collection<String>`) — collection of field names to include in projection (null for all fields)
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — BSON filter criteria to match documents (must not be null)
  - `sort` (`Bson`) — BSON sort criteria (null for no sorting)
  - `offset` (`int`) — number of documents to skip
  - `count` (`int`) — maximum number of documents to return
  - `rowType` (`Class<T>`) — the target type for conversion of each document
- **Returns:** a Stream of typed objects matching the projection, filter, sort, and pagination constraints
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null, or if `offset` is negative, or if `count` is negative, or if `rowType` is null, or if `selectPropNames` contains a null name and `count` is positive (the driver rejects it while encoding the query; a `count` of 0 sends no projection)
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Complex query with all features
  List<String> fields = Arrays.asList("name", "email", "score");
  Bson filter = Filters.gte("score", 80);
  Bson sort = Sorts.descending("score");
  executor.stream(fields, filter, sort, 0, 50, Student.class)
          .forEach(this::awardHonor);
  ```
- **Signature:** `public <T> Stream<T> stream(final Bson projection, final Bson filter, final Bson sort, final Class<T> rowType) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException`
- **Summary:** Creates a stream with BSON projection, filtering, and sorting.
- **Parameters:**
  - `projection` (`Bson`) — BSON projection document (null for all fields)
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — BSON filter criteria to match documents (must not be null)
  - `sort` (`Bson`) — BSON sort criteria (null for no sorting)
  - `rowType` (`Class<T>`) — the target type for conversion of each document
- **Returns:** a Stream of typed objects with the specified projection applied
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null, or if `rowType` is null
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Complex projection with nested fields
  Bson projection = Projections.fields(
      Projections.include("name", "address.city"),
      Projections.excludeId()
  );
  executor.stream(projection, filter, sort, User.class)
          .forEach(this::processUser);
  ```
- **Signature:** `public <T> Stream<T> stream(final Bson projection, final Bson filter, final Bson sort, final int offset, final int count, final Class<T> rowType) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException`
- **Summary:** Creates a fully-featured stream with BSON projection.
- **Parameters:**
  - `projection` (`Bson`) — BSON projection document (null for all fields)
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — BSON filter criteria to match documents (must not be null)
  - `sort` (`Bson`) — BSON sort criteria (null for no sorting)
  - `offset` (`int`) — number of documents to skip
  - `count` (`int`) — maximum number of documents to return
  - `rowType` (`Class<T>`) — the target type for conversion of each document
- **Returns:** a Stream of typed objects matching the projection, filter, sort, and pagination constraints
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null, or if `offset` is negative, or if `count` is negative, or if `rowType` is null
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Advanced query with all features
  Bson projection = Projections.fields(
      Projections.include("scores"),
      Projections.elemMatch("scores", Filters.gte("value", 90))
  );
  executor.stream(projection, filter, sort, 0, 10, Student.class)
          .forEach(this::processTopScorer);
  ```
##### watch(...) -> varies by overload
- **Signature:** `public ChangeStreamIterable<Document> watch()`
- **Summary:** Creates a change stream to monitor all changes in the collection.
- **Contract:**
  - Usage Examples: The returned change-stream iterable executes when its cursor is opened or consumed.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** a ChangeStreamIterable for monitoring collection changes
- **Performance:** Change streams allow applications to access real-time data changes without the complexity and risk of tailing the oplog.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  executor.watch() // returns a ChangeStreamIterable; iterating it (e.g. forEach) blocks and yields change events as they occur
  .forEach(change -> System.out.println("Change: " + change));
  ```
- **See also:** `ChangeStreamIterable`
- **Signature:** `public <T> ChangeStreamIterable<T> watch(final Class<T> rowType) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException`
- **Summary:** Creates a typed change stream to monitor collection changes.
- **Contract:**
  - Usage Examples: The returned change-stream iterable executes when its cursor is opened or consumed.
- **Parameters:**
  - `rowType` (`Class<T>`) — the class to decode each change event's full document into (must not be null)
- **Returns:** a typed ChangeStreamIterable
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `rowType` is null
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if the codec registry of the underlying collection has no codec for `rowType` (the driver looks it up when it creates the iterable, so this call throws before any server is contacted; the `MongoDBBase` registry of a collection obtained by name has one for every class)
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  executor.watch(UserChange.class) // returns a ChangeStreamIterable whose fullDocument is decoded as UserChange
  .forEach(change -> processUserChange(change));
  ```
- **Signature:** `public ChangeStreamIterable<Document> watch(final List<? extends Bson> pipeline) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates a change stream with an aggregation pipeline.
- **Contract:**
  - Usage Examples: The returned change-stream iterable executes when its cursor is opened or consumed.
  - A `null` stage in `pipeline` is not rejected by this call: the driver throws an `IllegalArgumentException` when the cursor is opened, before contacting a server.
- **Parameters:**
  - `pipeline` (`List<? extends Bson>`) — aggregation pipeline to apply to change events (must not be null)
- **Returns:** a filtered ChangeStreamIterable
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `pipeline` is null
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<Bson> pipeline = Arrays.asList(
      Aggregates.match(Filters.in("operationType", "insert", "update"))
  );
  executor.watch(pipeline) // returns a ChangeStreamIterable emitting only insert/update change events
      .forEach(change -> processChange(change));
  ```
- **Signature:** `public <T> ChangeStreamIterable<T> watch(final List<? extends Bson> pipeline, final Class<T> rowType) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException`
- **Summary:** Creates a typed change stream with an aggregation pipeline.
- **Contract:**
  - Usage Examples: The returned change-stream iterable executes when its cursor is opened or consumed.
  - A `null` stage in `pipeline` is not rejected by this call: the driver throws an `IllegalArgumentException` when the cursor is opened, before contacting a server.
- **Parameters:**
  - `pipeline` (`List<? extends Bson>`) — aggregation pipeline to apply (must not be null)
  - `rowType` (`Class<T>`) — the class to decode each change event's full document into (must not be null)
- **Returns:** a filtered and typed ChangeStreamIterable
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `pipeline` is null, or if `rowType` is null
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if the codec registry of the underlying collection has no codec for `rowType` (the driver looks it up when it creates the iterable, so this call throws before any server is contacted; the `MongoDBBase` registry of a collection obtained by name has one for every class)
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<Bson> pipeline = Arrays.asList(
      Aggregates.match(Filters.eq("fullDocument.status", "critical"))
  );
  executor.watch(pipeline, Alert.class) // returns a ChangeStreamIterable of critical-status change events whose fullDocument is decoded as Alert
      .forEach(change -> sendNotification(change.getFullDocument()));
  ```
##### insertOne(...) -> InsertOneResult
- **Signature:** `public InsertOneResult insertOne(final Object obj) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoWriteException, MongoException`
- **Summary:** Inserts a single document into the collection (blocking operation).
- **Parameters:**
  - `obj` (`Object`) — the object to insert (must not be null) - can be Document, `Map<String, Object>`, or entity class with getter/setter methods
- **Returns:** the `InsertOneResult` reported by the server (e.g. the generated `_id` via `InsertOneResult#getInsertedId()`)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `obj` is null, or if a document value cannot be converted from a Map, bean, or array of String name/value pairs
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if a bean accessor, BSON implementation, codec, or value converter throws during request or result conversion
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoWriteException` — if the server rejects the write, for example because a unique index or document validation rule is violated
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Insert a Document:
  Document userDoc = new Document("name", "John")
                       .append("email", "john@example.com")
                       .append("age", 30);
  InsertOneResult result = executor.insertOne(userDoc); // userDoc is inserted (an _id is generated if absent); result.getInsertedId() exposes it

  // Insert an entity:
  User user = new User("Jane", "jane@example.com", 25);
  executor.insertOne(user); // entity is converted to a Document and inserted (null properties dropped)
  ```
- **See also:** `#insertOne(Object, InsertOneOptions)`, `#insertMany(Collection)`, `#async()`
- **Signature:** `public InsertOneResult insertOne(final Object obj, final InsertOneOptions options) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoWriteException, MongoException`
- **Summary:** Inserts a single document into the collection with additional options.
- **Parameters:**
  - `obj` (`Object`) — the object to insert (must not be null) - can be Document, `Map<String, Object>`, or entity class with getter/setter methods
  - `options` (`InsertOneOptions`) — additional options for the insert operation (null uses defaults)
- **Returns:** the `InsertOneResult` reported by the server (e.g. the generated `_id` via `InsertOneResult#getInsertedId()`)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `obj` is null, or if a document value cannot be converted from a Map, bean, or array of String name/value pairs
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if a bean accessor, BSON implementation, codec, or value converter throws during request or result conversion
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoWriteException` — if the server rejects the write, for example because a unique index or document validation rule is violated
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  User user = new User("Alice", "alice@example.com", 28);

  // Insert with custom options:
  InsertOneOptions options = new InsertOneOptions().bypassDocumentValidation(true);
  InsertOneResult result = executor.insertOne(user, options); // document inserted bypassing schema validation
  ```
- **See also:** `InsertOneOptions`, `#insertOne(Object)`
##### insertMany(...) -> InsertManyResult
- **Signature:** `public InsertManyResult insertMany(final Collection<?> objList) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoBulkWriteException, MongoException`
- **Summary:** Inserts multiple documents into the collection in a single operation (blocking operation).
- **Parameters:**
  - `objList` (`Collection<?>`) — collection of objects to insert - each can be Document, `Map<String, Object>`, or entity class with getter/setter methods
- **Returns:** the `InsertManyResult` reported by the server (e.g. the generated `_id`s via `InsertManyResult#getInsertedIds()`)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `objList` is null or empty or contains a null document, or if a document value cannot be converted from a Map, bean, or array of String name/value pairs
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if a bean accessor, BSON implementation, codec, or value converter throws during request or result conversion
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoBulkWriteException` — if the server reports a write or write-concern error for one or more requests in the batch
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Insert multiple entities:
  List<User> users = Arrays.asList(
      new User("John", "john@example.com", 30),
      new User("Jane", "jane@example.com", 25),
      new User("Bob", "bob@example.com", 35)
  );
  InsertManyResult result = executor.insertMany(users); // all 3 users inserted in one batch; result.getInsertedIds() exposes the generated _ids
  executor.insertMany(List.of()); // throws IllegalArgumentException (objList must not be empty)
  ```
- **See also:** `#insertMany(Collection, InsertManyOptions)`, `#insertOne(Object)`, `#async()`
- **Signature:** `public InsertManyResult insertMany(final Collection<?> objList, final InsertManyOptions options) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoBulkWriteException, MongoException`
- **Summary:** Inserts multiple documents into the collection with additional options.
- **Parameters:**
  - `objList` (`Collection<?>`) — collection of objects to insert - each can be Document, `Map<String, Object>`, or entity class with getter/setter methods
  - `options` (`InsertManyOptions`) — additional options for the insert operation (null uses defaults)
- **Returns:** the `InsertManyResult` reported by the server (e.g. the generated `_id`s via `InsertManyResult#getInsertedIds()`)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `objList` is null or empty or contains a null document, or if a document value cannot be converted from a Map, bean, or array of String name/value pairs
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if a bean accessor, BSON implementation, codec, or value converter throws during request or result conversion
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoBulkWriteException` — if the server reports a write or write-concern error for one or more requests in the batch
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<User> users = Arrays.asList(
      new User("John", "john@example.com", 30),
      new User("Jane", "jane@example.com", 25)
  );

  // Insert with unordered execution (faster for large batches):
  InsertManyOptions options = new InsertManyOptions().ordered(false);
  InsertManyResult result = executor.insertMany(users, options); // every user is attempted; if any insert fails, the call still throws MongoBulkWriteException
  ```
- **See also:** `InsertManyOptions`, `#insertMany(Collection)`
##### updateOne(...) -> UpdateResult
- **Signature:** `public UpdateResult updateOne(final String objectId, final Object update) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoWriteException, MongoException`
- **Summary:** Updates a single document identified by ObjectId string with the specified update operations (blocking operation).
- **Contract:**
  - If the payload is empty after conversion (no non-null updatable properties besides `_id`), an `IllegalArgumentException` is thrown — this executor requires at least one updatable field.
- **Parameters:**
  - `objectId` (`String`) — the string representation of the ObjectId identifying the document to update
  - `update` (`Object`) — the update operations - can be Bson, Document with update operators, `Map<String, Object>`, or entity class with getter/setter methods
- **Returns:** UpdateResult containing information about the update operation
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `objectId` is null or is not a 24-character hexadecimal ObjectId, or if `update` is null, or if an update document has a null field name, mixes operator and ordinary field names, or has no updatable fields after removing `_id`, or if an update value cannot be converted from a Map, bean, or array of String name/value pairs
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if a bean accessor, BSON implementation, codec, or value converter throws during request or result conversion
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoWriteException` — if the server rejects the write, for example because a unique index or document validation rule is violated
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  String userId = "507f1f77bcf86cd799439011";

  // Update with MongoDB update operators:
  UpdateResult result1 = executor.updateOne(userId,
      Updates.combine(Updates.set("status", "active"), Updates.inc("loginCount", 1))); // returns UpdateResult; matchedCount 0..1

  // Update with entity (automatically wrapped in $set):
  User updatedUser = new User();
  updatedUser.setStatus("inactive");
  UpdateResult result2 = executor.updateOne(userId, updatedUser); // returns UpdateResult; matchedCount 0..1, modifiedCount 0..1
  ```
- **See also:** `UpdateResult`, `#updateOne(ObjectId, Object)`, `com.mongodb.client.model.Updates`, `#async()`
- **Signature:** `public UpdateResult updateOne(final ObjectId objectId, final Object update) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoWriteException, MongoException`
- **Summary:** Updates a single document identified by ObjectId.
- **Parameters:**
  - `objectId` (`ObjectId`) — the ObjectId of the document to update
  - `update` (`Object`) — can be Bson/Document/`Map<String, Object>`/entity class with getter/setter methods
- **Returns:** UpdateResult containing update operation details
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `objectId` is null, or if `update` is null, or if an update document has a null field name, mixes operator and ordinary field names, or has no updatable fields after removing `_id`, or if an update value cannot be converted from a Map, bean, or array of String name/value pairs
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if a bean accessor, BSON implementation, codec, or value converter throws during request or result conversion
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoWriteException` — if the server rejects the write, for example because a unique index or document validation rule is violated
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  ObjectId id = new ObjectId("507f1f77bcf86cd799439011");
  executor.updateOne(id, Updates.set("lastModified", new Date())); // returns UpdateResult; matchedCount 1 if the document exists, else 0
  ```
- **See also:** `#updateOne(String, Object)`
- **Signature:** `public UpdateResult updateOne(final Bson filter, final Object update) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoWriteException, MongoException`

- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null, or if `update` is null, or if an update document has a null field name, mixes operator and ordinary field names, or has no updatable fields after removing `_id`, or if an update value cannot be converted from a Map, bean, or array of String name/value pairs
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if a bean accessor, BSON implementation, codec, or value converter throws during request or result conversion
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoWriteException` — if the server rejects the write, for example because a unique index or document validation rule is violated
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error

- **Signature:** `public UpdateResult updateOne(final Bson filter, final Object update, final UpdateOptions options) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoWriteException, MongoException`

- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null, or if `update` is null, or if an update document has a null field name, mixes operator and ordinary field names, or has no updatable fields after removing `_id`, or if an update value cannot be converted from a Map, bean, or array of String name/value pairs
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if a bean accessor, BSON implementation, codec, or value converter throws during request or result conversion
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoWriteException` — if the server rejects the write, for example because a unique index or document validation rule is violated
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error

  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoWriteException` — if the server rejects the write, for example because a unique index or document validation rule is violated
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
- **Examples:**

  ```java
      Updates.set("status", "processed"),
      Updates.set("processedAt", new Date())
  );
  executor.updateOne(filter, updates); // returns UpdateResult; applies the aggregation-pipeline updates to the first match
  ```

##### replaceOne(...) -> UpdateResult
- **Signature:** `public UpdateResult replaceOne(final String objectId, final Object replacement) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoWriteException, MongoException`
- **Summary:** Replaces a document identified by ObjectId string.
- **Contract:**
  - The replacement must not contain MongoDB update operators (keys starting with `$`); if it does, the driver will reject the call.
  - If the replacement itself contains an `_id` that differs from the matched document's `_id`, the server rejects the operation.
  - If the replacement omits `_id`, the original is retained.
- **Parameters:**
  - `objectId` (`String`) — string representation of the ObjectId
  - `replacement` (`Object`) — can be Document/`Map<String, Object>`/entity class with getter/setter methods
- **Returns:** UpdateResult containing replace operation details
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `objectId` is null or is not a 24-character hexadecimal ObjectId, or if `replacement` is null, or if a document value cannot be converted from a Map, bean, or array of String name/value pairs, or if the converted replacement has a top-level field name starting with `$` (rejected by the driver before the command is sent)
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if a bean accessor, BSON implementation, codec, or value converter throws during request or result conversion
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoWriteException` — if the server rejects the write, for example because a unique index or document validation rule is violated
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  String id = "507f1f77bcf86cd799439011";
  User newUser = new User("John", "john@example.com");
  executor.replaceOne(id, newUser); // returns UpdateResult; matchedCount 1 if the document exists (its _id is retained), else 0
  ```
- **Signature:** `public UpdateResult replaceOne(final ObjectId objectId, final Object replacement) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoWriteException, MongoException`
- **Summary:** Replaces a document identified by ObjectId.
- **Contract:**
  - MongoDB retains the matched document's `_id` when the replacement omits it.
  - A replacement that supplies `_id` must supply the same value; see `#replaceOne(String, Object)` for the full rules and the prohibition on update operators in the replacement.
- **Parameters:**
  - `objectId` (`ObjectId`) — the ObjectId of the document to replace
  - `replacement` (`Object`) — can be Document/`Map<String, Object>`/entity class with getter/setter methods
- **Returns:** UpdateResult containing replace operation details
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `objectId` is null, or if `replacement` is null, or if a document value cannot be converted from a Map, bean, or array of String name/value pairs, or if the converted replacement has a top-level field name starting with `$` (rejected by the driver before the command is sent)
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if a bean accessor, BSON implementation, codec, or value converter throws during request or result conversion
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoWriteException` — if the server rejects the write, for example because a unique index or document validation rule is violated
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  ObjectId id = new ObjectId("507f1f77bcf86cd799439011");
  Document newDoc = new Document("name", "Jane").append("status", "active");
  executor.replaceOne(id, newDoc); // returns UpdateResult; whole document body is swapped, _id preserved
  ```

##### bulkInsert(...) -> BulkWriteResult
- **Signature:** `public BulkWriteResult bulkInsert(final Collection<?> entities) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoBulkWriteException, MongoException`
- **Summary:** Performs bulk insert of multiple entities.
- **Parameters:**
  - `entities` (`Collection<?>`) — collection of entities to insert
- **Returns:** the `BulkWriteResult` reported by the server (use `BulkWriteResult#getInsertedCount()` for the inserted count)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `entities` is null or empty or contains a null document, or if a document value cannot be converted from a Map, bean, or array of String name/value pairs
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if a bean accessor, BSON implementation, codec, or value converter throws during request or result conversion
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoBulkWriteException` — if the server reports a write or write-concern error for one or more requests in the batch
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<User> users = generateUsers(1000);
  BulkWriteResult result = executor.bulkInsert(users); // result.getInsertedCount() is e.g. 1000
  System.out.println("Inserted " + result.getInsertedCount() + " users");
  executor.bulkInsert(List.of()); // throws IllegalArgumentException (entities must not be empty)
  ```

  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoBulkWriteException` — if the server reports a write or write-concern error for one or more requests in the batch

- **Signature:** `public BulkWriteResult bulkWrite(final List<? extends WriteModel<? extends Document>> requests) throws IllegalArgumentException, UnsupportedOperationException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoBulkWriteException, MongoException`
- **Summary:** Executes bulk write operations.
- **Parameters:**
  - `requests` (`List<? extends WriteModel<? extends Document>>`) — list of write operations to execute
- **Returns:** BulkWriteResult containing operation details
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `requests` is null or empty, or contains a null write model
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if `requests` contains a WriteModel subtype that the MongoDB driver does not support
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoBulkWriteException` — if the server reports a write or write-concern error for one or more requests in the batch
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<WriteModel<Document>> operations = Arrays.asList(
      new InsertOneModel<>(doc1),
      new UpdateOneModel<>(filter, update),
      new DeleteOneModel<>(deleteFilter)
  );
  BulkWriteResult result = executor.bulkWrite(operations); // returns BulkWriteResult (insert/match/modify/delete counts) for all 3 ops
  executor.bulkWrite(List.of());                           // throws IllegalArgumentException (requests must not be empty)
  ```

  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if `requests` contains a WriteModel subtype that the MongoDB driver does not support
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
