  - `options` (`FindOneAndDeleteOptions`) — additional options (null uses defaults)
  - `rowType` (`Class<T>`) — class to convert the result to
- **Returns:** the deleted document as the specified type, or null if not found
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null, or if `rowType` is null, or if the returned document cannot be converted to `rowType` (the document has then already been deleted)
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
  - `java.lang.ArrayStoreException` — if the result type is a reference-array type and a returned document value is incompatible with its component type
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if converting a result value overflows its target numeric range, a registered converter or type handler throws, or constructing or populating a result bean or map, or invoking a bean accessor, fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  FindOneAndDeleteOptions options = new FindOneAndDeleteOptions()
      .projection(Projections.include("name", "email"));
  User deleted = executor.findOneAndDelete(filter, options, User.class); // deleted doc (only name/email) as User, or null if none matched
  ```
##### distinct(...) -> Stream<T>
- **Signature:** `public <T> Stream<T> distinct(final String fieldName, final Class<T> rowType) throws IllegalArgumentException, BsonInvalidOperationException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Returns a stream of distinct values for the specified field.
- **Contract:**
  - Usage Examples: The `distinct` command runs when this method is called and returns every value in one reply, which is decoded as `rowType` right away: a value that cannot be decoded (for example a string or fractional value requested as `Long`) makes this call throw, and consuming the returned stream sends no further command.
- **Parameters:**
  - `fieldName` (`String`) — the field to get distinct values for
  - `rowType` (`Class<T>`) — the class of the field values
- **Returns:** a Stream of distinct values
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `fieldName` is null or empty, or if `rowType` is null, or if a returned value cannot be converted to a `rowType` that has no driver codec (such as `int.class`, which the `MongoDBBase` codec registry converts)
  - `org.bson.BsonInvalidOperationException` — if a returned value cannot be decoded as `rowType`, for example a string or fractional value requested as `Long`, or a value that is not a document requested as a bean
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if a returned value overflows the numeric range of a `rowType` without a driver codec, or a registered converter or type handler throws while converting it
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  executor.distinct("category", String.class) // returns a lazy Stream of the unique "category" values (null included if a document stores the field as null)
  .forEach(category -> System.out.println("Category: " + category));
  ```
- **Signature:** `public <T> Stream<T> distinct(final String fieldName, final Bson filter, final Class<T> rowType) throws IllegalArgumentException, BsonInvalidOperationException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Returns a stream of distinct values with filtering.
- **Contract:**
  - Usage Examples: As with `#distinct(String, Class)`, the command runs and every returned value is decoded as `rowType` when this method is called, so a value that cannot be decoded makes this call throw; consuming the returned stream sends no further command.
- **Parameters:**
  - `fieldName` (`String`) — the field to get distinct values for
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — BSON filter to apply before getting distinct values (must not be null)
  - `rowType` (`Class<T>`) — the class of the field values
- **Returns:** a Stream of distinct values from filtered documents
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `fieldName` is null or empty, or if `filter` is null, or if `rowType` is null, or if a returned value cannot be converted to a `rowType` that has no driver codec (such as `int.class`, which the `MongoDBBase` codec registry converts)
  - `org.bson.BsonInvalidOperationException` — if a returned value cannot be decoded as `rowType`, for example a string or fractional value requested as `Long`, or a value that is not a document requested as a bean
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if a returned value overflows the numeric range of a `rowType` without a driver codec, or a registered converter or type handler throws while converting it
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Bson filter = Filters.gte("price", 100);
  executor.distinct("brand", filter, String.class) // returns a lazy Stream of unique "brand" values among matching docs
      .forEach(brand -> System.out.println("Premium brand: " + brand));
  ```

### Class MongoCollectionMapper (com.landawn.abacus.da.mongodb.MongoCollectionMapper)
Synchronous, strongly-typed façade over a MongoDB `MongoCollection<Document>`.

**Thread-safety:** thread-safe
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Public Constructors
- (none)

#### Public Static Methods
- (none)

#### Public Instance Methods
##### collectionExecutor(...) -> MongoCollectionExecutor
- **Signature:** `public MongoCollectionExecutor collectionExecutor()`
- **Summary:** Returns the underlying MongoCollectionExecutor for advanced operations.
- **Contract:**
  - This method provides access to the raw executor when you need operations not exposed by the mapper or when working with untyped Documents is more appropriate.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the underlying MongoCollectionExecutor instance
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  MongoCollectionMapper<User> userMapper = mongoDB.collectionMapper(User.class);
  MongoCollectionExecutor executor = userMapper.collectionExecutor(); // never null; same instance on each call
  // Use raw executor for operations not exposed by the mapper, e.g. an untyped aggregate:
  Document complexResult = executor.aggregate(complexPipeline).first().orElse(null); // raw Document, not the mapped entity
  ```
- **See also:** `MongoCollectionExecutor`
##### exists(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `public boolean exists(final String objectId) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException`
- **Summary:** Checks if an entity exists by its ObjectId string representation.
- **Contract:**
  - The ObjectId must be a valid 24-character hexadecimal representation.
- **Parameters:**
  - `objectId` (`String`) — the string representation of the ObjectId to check
- **Returns:** `true` if an entity with the specified ObjectId exists, `false` otherwise
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `objectId` is null or is not a 24-character hexadecimal ObjectId
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  MongoCollectionMapper<User> userMapper = mongoDB.collectionMapper(User.class);
  boolean present = userMapper.exists("507f1f77bcf86cd799439011"); // returns true if a doc with that _id exists
  boolean absent  = userMapper.exists("000000000000000000000000"); // returns false when nothing matches

  // A malformed (non-24-hex) string is rejected before any DB call:
  userMapper.exists("not-a-valid-id"); // throws IllegalArgumentException
  ```
- **See also:** `#exists(ObjectId)`
- **Signature:** `public boolean exists(final ObjectId objectId) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException`
- **Summary:** Checks if an entity exists by its ObjectId.
- **Parameters:**
  - `objectId` (`ObjectId`) — the ObjectId to check for existence
- **Returns:** `true` if an entity with the specified ObjectId exists, `false` otherwise
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `objectId` is null
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  MongoCollectionMapper<User> mapper = mongoDB.collectionMapper(User.class);
  ObjectId userId = new ObjectId("507f1f77bcf86cd799439011");
  boolean userExists = mapper.exists(userId);  // returns true / false depending on the collection

  boolean missing = mapper.exists(new ObjectId()); // returns false: a brand-new id is almost certainly absent
  ```
- **See also:** `ObjectId`
- **Signature:** `public boolean exists(final Bson filter) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException`
- **Summary:** Checks if any entities exist matching the specified filter criteria.
- **Contract:**
  - It's more efficient than retrieving entities when you only need to verify existence.
- **Parameters:**
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — the query filter to match entities against
- **Returns:** `true` if any entities match the filter, `false` otherwise
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  MongoCollectionMapper<User> mapper = mongoDB.collectionMapper(User.class);
  // Check if any active users exist:
  boolean hasActiveUsers = mapper.exists(Filters.eq("status", "active")); // returns true if >=1 match
  // Filters parsed from JSON must be wrapped in a Bson (Document.parse), not passed as a raw String:
  boolean hasRecent = mapper.exists(Document.parse(
      "{ \"createdAt\": { \"$gte\": { \"$date\": \"2023-01-01T00:00:00Z\" } } }"));
  boolean none = mapper.exists(Filters.eq("status", "no-such-status")); // returns false: empty match set
  ```
- **See also:** `com.mongodb.client.model.Filters`
##### count(...) -> long
- **Signature:** `public long count() throws IllegalStateException, MongoException`
- **Summary:** Returns the total number of entities in the collection (blocking operation).
- **Contract:**
  - For large collections, consider using `#collectionExecutor()`.`estimatedDocumentCount()` for better performance when exact counts are not required.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the total number of entities in the collection
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  MongoCollectionMapper<User> userMapper = mongoDB.collectionMapper(User.class);
  long totalUsers = userMapper.count();   // returns the exact document count, e.g. 1500
  // An empty collection counts as 0 (never negative, never null):
  long emptyCount = mongoDB.collectionMapper(Audit.class).count(); // returns 0L when nothing has been inserted
  ```
- **See also:** `#count(Bson)`, `#collectionExecutor()`
- **Signature:** `public long count(final Bson filter) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException`
- **Summary:** Returns the number of entities matching the specified filter.
- **Parameters:**
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — the query filter to count matching entities
- **Returns:** the number of entities matching the filter
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  MongoCollectionMapper<User> mapper = mongoDB.collectionMapper(User.class);
  long activeUsers = mapper.count(Filters.eq("status", "active")); // returns the number of active users
  // A JSON filter must be a Bson (Document.parse), not a raw String:
  long adults = mapper.count(Document.parse("{ age: { $gte: 18 } }"));
  long none = mapper.count(Filters.eq("status", "no-such-status")); // returns 0L when nothing matches
  ```
- **See also:** `com.mongodb.client.model.Filters`
- **Signature:** `public long count(final Bson filter, final CountOptions options) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException`
- **Summary:** Returns the count of entities matching the filter with additional count options.
- **Parameters:**
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — the query filter to count matching entities
  - `options` (`CountOptions`) — additional options for the count operation (null uses defaults)
- **Returns:** the number of entities matching the filter within the specified constraints
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  MongoCollectionMapper<User> mapper = mongoDB.collectionMapper(User.class);
  // Cap the count so a huge match set never costs more than scanning 1000 docs:
  CountOptions options = new CountOptions().limit(1000);
  long limitedCount = mapper.count(Filters.exists("email"), options); // returns at most 1000
  // skip() shifts the window: skip the first 10 matches before counting the rest:
  long afterSkip = mapper.count(Filters.exists("email"), new CountOptions().skip(10));
  ```
- **See also:** `CountOptions`
##### get(...) -> Optional<T>
- **Signature:** `public Optional<T> get(final String objectId) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException, ArrayStoreException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Retrieves an entity by its ObjectId string representation with automatic type conversion.
- **Contract:**
  - The ObjectId string must be a valid 24-character hexadecimal representation.
- **Parameters:**
  - `objectId` (`String`) — the string representation of the ObjectId to retrieve
- **Returns:** an Optional containing the entity if found, or empty if not found
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `objectId` is null or is not a 24-character hexadecimal ObjectId, or if a returned document has multiple non-`_id` fields for a scalar result type or a value that cannot be converted to the requested type
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
  - `java.lang.ArrayStoreException` — if the result type is a reference-array type and a returned document value is incompatible with its component type
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if converting a result value overflows its target numeric range, a registered converter or type handler throws, or constructing or populating a result bean or map, or invoking a bean accessor, fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  MongoCollectionMapper<User> mapper = mongoDB.collectionMapper(User.class);
  Optional<User> user = mapper.get("507f1f77bcf86cd799439011"); // returns Optional with the entity, or empty
  String name = user.map(User::getName).orElse("<unknown>");    // safe access without an explicit isPresent() check

  Optional<User> missing = mapper.get("000000000000000000000000"); // returns Optional.empty() when no match
  boolean absent = missing.isPresent() == false;                   // absent == true

  mapper.get("xyz"); // throws IllegalArgumentException: not a 24-hex ObjectId
  ```
- **See also:** `Optional`, `#get(ObjectId)`
- **Signature:** `public Optional<T> get(final ObjectId objectId) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException, ArrayStoreException, RuntimeException`

  - `java.lang.ArrayStoreException` — if the result type is a reference-array type and a returned document value is incompatible with its component type
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if converting a result value overflows its target numeric range, a registered converter or type handler throws, or constructing or populating a result bean or map, or invoking a bean accessor, fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  MongoCollectionMapper<User> mapper = mongoDB.collectionMapper(User.class);
  ObjectId userId = new ObjectId("507f1f77bcf86cd799439011");
  ```

  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
  - `java.lang.ArrayStoreException` — if the result type is a reference-array type and a returned document value is incompatible with its component type
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if a dotted property path traverses a non-null value that is not a Document
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if converting a result value overflows its target numeric range, a registered converter or type handler throws, or constructing or populating a result bean or map, or invoking a bean accessor, fails

##### gett(...) -> T
- **Signature:** `public T gett(final String objectId) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException, ArrayStoreException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Retrieves an entity by its ObjectId string representation, returning null if not found.
- **Contract:**
  - It returns `null` instead of an empty Optional when the entity is not found.
  - The `gett` name is preserved for API compatibility; prefer `#get(String)` when Optional-based handling is clearer.
- **Parameters:**
  - `objectId` (`String`) — the string representation of the ObjectId (24 hex characters)
- **Returns:** the matching entity, or `null` if not found
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `objectId` is null or is not a 24-character hexadecimal ObjectId, or if a returned document has multiple non-`_id` fields for a scalar result type or a value that cannot be converted to the requested type
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
  - `java.lang.ArrayStoreException` — if the result type is a reference-array type and a returned document value is incompatible with its component type
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if converting a result value overflows its target numeric range, a registered converter or type handler throws, or constructing or populating a result bean or map, or invoking a bean accessor, fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  MongoCollectionMapper<User> mapper = mongoDB.collectionMapper(User.class);
  User user = mapper.gett("507f1f77bcf86cd799439011"); // returns the entity, or null if absent
  if (user != null) {
      process(user);                                   // null guard required, unlike the Optional-based get
  }

  User missing = mapper.gett("000000000000000000000000"); // returns null: no document with that _id
  mapper.gett("bad");                                      // throws IllegalArgumentException: not 24-hex
  ```
- **See also:** `#get(String)`, `#gett(ObjectId)`

##### findFirst(...) -> Optional<T>
- **Signature:** `public Optional<T> findFirst(final Bson filter) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException, ArrayStoreException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Finds the first entity matching the specified filter criteria.
- **Parameters:**
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — the query filter to match entities against
- **Returns:** an Optional containing the first matching entity, or empty if none found
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null, or if a returned document has multiple non-`_id` fields for a scalar result type or a value that cannot be converted to the requested type
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
  - `java.lang.ArrayStoreException` — if the result type is a reference-array type and a returned document value is incompatible with its component type
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if converting a result value overflows its target numeric range, a registered converter or type handler throws, or constructing or populating a result bean or map, or invoking a bean accessor, fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  MongoCollectionMapper<User> mapper = mongoDB.collectionMapper(User.class);
  // Find the first active user (natural order; pass a sort overload for a stable "first"):
  Optional<User> user = mapper.findFirst(Filters.eq("status", "active")); // returns Optional, possibly empty
  user.ifPresent(u -> process(u));
  // Using a JSON filter (must be a Bson via Document.parse, not a raw String):
  Optional<User> recentUser = mapper.findFirst(Document.parse(
      "{ \"createdAt\": { \"$gte\": { \"$date\": \"2023-01-01T00:00:00Z\" } } }"));
  Optional<User> none = mapper.findFirst(Filters.eq("status", "no-such")); // returns Optional.empty()
  ```
- **See also:** `Optional`, `com.mongodb.client.model.Filters`
- **Signature:** `public Optional<T> findFirst(final Collection<String> selectPropNames, final Bson filter) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException, ArrayStoreException, ClassCastException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Finds the first entity matching the filter with field projection.
- **Contract:**
  - This is more efficient when you only need specific fields from the entity, reducing network bandwidth and memory usage.
- **Parameters:**
  - `selectPropNames` (`Collection<String>`) — collection of field names to include in the projection (null or empty for all fields)
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — the query filter to match entities against
- **Returns:** an Optional containing the first matching entity with projected fields, or empty if none found
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null, or if a returned document has multiple non-`_id` fields for a scalar result type or a value that cannot be converted to the requested type, or if `selectPropNames` contains a null name (the driver rejects it while encoding the query, whatever the mapped type is)
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
  - `java.lang.ArrayStoreException` — if the result type is a reference-array type and a returned document value is incompatible with its component type
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if a dotted property path traverses a non-null value that is not a Document
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if converting a result value overflows its target numeric range, a registered converter or type handler throws, or constructing or populating a result bean or map, or invoking a bean accessor, fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  MongoCollectionMapper<User> mapper = mongoDB.collectionMapper(User.class);
  Collection<String> fields = Arrays.asList("name", "email");
  // First active user, with only name/email (plus _id) populated:
  Optional<User> user = mapper.findFirst(fields, Filters.eq("status", "active")); // returns Optional, possibly empty
  String email = user.map(User::getEmail).orElse(null);
  // null fields means "all fields":
  Optional<User> full = mapper.findFirst(null, Filters.eq("status", "active"));
  ```
- **See also:** `#findFirst(Bson)`, `#findFirst(Collection, Bson, Bson)`
- **Signature:** `public Optional<T> findFirst(final Collection<String> selectPropNames, final Bson filter, final Bson sort) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException, ArrayStoreException, ClassCastException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Finds the first entity matching the filter with field projection and sorting.
- **Contract:**
  - The sorting determines which entity is considered "first" when multiple documents match the filter.
- **Parameters:**
  - `selectPropNames` (`Collection<String>`) — collection of field names to include in the projection (null or empty for all fields)
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — the query filter to match entities against
  - `sort` (`Bson`) — the sort specification to determine result ordering (null for the natural, unspecified order)
- **Returns:** an Optional containing the first matching entity with projected fields, or empty if none found
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null, or if a returned document has multiple non-`_id` fields for a scalar result type or a value that cannot be converted to the requested type, or if `selectPropNames` contains a null name (the driver rejects it while encoding the query, whatever the mapped type is)
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
  - `java.lang.ArrayStoreException` — if the result type is a reference-array type and a returned document value is incompatible with its component type
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if a dotted property path traverses a non-null value that is not a Document
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if converting a result value overflows its target numeric range, a registered converter or type handler throws, or constructing or populating a result bean or map, or invoking a bean accessor, fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  MongoCollectionMapper<Order> mapper = mongoDB.collectionMapper(Order.class);
  Collection<String> fields = Arrays.asList("orderId", "total", "status");
  Bson filter = Filters.eq("customerId", "CUST123");
  Bson sort = Sorts.descending("createdAt");   // Most recent first
  // Sort makes "first" deterministic: the newest order for this customer:
  Optional<Order> recentOrder = mapper.findFirst(fields, filter, sort);                    // returns Optional, possibly empty
  Optional<Order> oldest = mapper.findFirst(fields, filter, Sorts.ascending("createdAt")); // earliest instead
  ```
- **See also:** `#findFirst(Collection, Bson)`, `#findFirst(Bson, Bson, Bson)`, `com.mongodb.client.model.Sorts`

  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null, or if a returned document has multiple non-`_id` fields for a scalar result type or a value that cannot be converted to the requested type
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
  - `java.lang.ArrayStoreException` — if the result type is a reference-array type and a returned document value is incompatible with its component type
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if converting a result value overflows its target numeric range, a registered converter or type handler throws, or constructing or populating a result bean or map, or invoking a bean accessor, fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  MongoCollectionMapper<Article> mapper = mongoDB.collectionMapper(Article.class);
  Bson projection = Projections.fields(
      Projections.include("title", "author"),
      Projections.slice("tags", 5)
  );
  Bson filter = Filters.eq("status", "published");
  Bson sort = Sorts.descending("views");
  // Most-viewed published article, with tags trimmed to the first 5 entries:
  Optional<Article> popularArticle = mapper.findFirst(projection, filter, sort);              // returns Optional, possibly empty
  Optional<Article> none = mapper.findFirst(projection, Filters.eq("status", "draft"), sort); // empty if no drafts
  ```
- **See also:** `#findFirst(Collection, Bson, Bson)`, `com.mongodb.client.model.Projections`, `com.mongodb.client.model.Sorts`
##### list(...) -> List<T>
- **Signature:** `public List<T> list(final Bson filter) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Retrieves all entities matching the specified filter as a list.
- **Contract:**
  - Use this method when you need to retrieve all matching entities at once.
- **Parameters:**
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — the query filter to match entities against
- **Returns:** a List containing all matching entities (empty list if none found)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null, or if a returned document has multiple non-`_id` fields for a scalar result type, inconsistent scalar projection fields, or a value that cannot be converted to the requested type
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if converting a result value overflows its target numeric range, a registered converter or type handler throws, or constructing or populating a result bean or map, or invoking a bean accessor, fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  MongoCollectionMapper<User> mapper = mongoDB.collectionMapper(User.class);
  List<User> activeUsers = mapper.list(Filters.eq("status", "active")); // returns all matches, e.g. size 42
  activeUsers.forEach(user -> processUser(user));
  // No match yields an empty (never null) list:
  List<User> none = mapper.list(Filters.eq("status", "no-such")); // returns an empty List, none.isEmpty() == true
  ```
- **See also:** `#stream(Bson)`, `com.mongodb.client.model.Filters`
- **Signature:** `public List<T> list(final Bson filter, final int offset, final int count) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Retrieves a paginated list of entities matching the specified filter.
- **Parameters:**
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — the query filter to match entities against
  - `offset` (`int`) — the number of documents to skip from the beginning (0 for first page)
  - `count` (`int`) — the maximum number of entities to return (`0` yields an empty list; `Integer.MAX_VALUE` is effectively "no limit")
- **Returns:** a List containing the requested page of matching entities
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null, or if `offset` is negative, or if `count` is negative, or if a returned document has multiple non-`_id` fields for a scalar result type, inconsistent scalar projection fields, or a value that cannot be converted to the requested type
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if converting a result value overflows its target numeric range, a registered converter or type handler throws, or constructing or populating a result bean or map, or invoking a bean accessor, fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  MongoCollectionMapper<Product> mapper = mongoDB.collectionMapper(Product.class);
  Bson filter = Filters.eq("category", "electronics");
  List<Product> page1 = mapper.list(filter, 0, 20);  // returns up to 20 matches (the first page)
  List<Product> page2 = mapper.list(filter, 20, 20); // returns the next 20 (skip 20, limit 20)
  // Past the end of the result set yields an empty list:
  List<Product> empty = mapper.list(filter, 1_000_000, 20); // returns an empty List
  ```
- **See also:** `#list(Bson)`, `#list(Collection, Bson, int, int)`
- **Signature:** `public List<T> list(final Collection<String> selectPropNames, final Bson filter) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException, ClassCastException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Retrieves all entities matching the filter with field projection.
- **Contract:**
  - This reduces network bandwidth and memory usage when you don't need all fields from the entity.
- **Parameters:**
  - `selectPropNames` (`Collection<String>`) — collection of field names to include in the projection (null or empty for all fields)
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — the query filter to match entities against
- **Returns:** a List containing all matching entities with projected fields
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null, or if a returned document has multiple non-`_id` fields for a scalar result type, inconsistent scalar projection fields, or a value that cannot be converted to the requested type, or if `selectPropNames` contains a null name (the driver rejects it while encoding the query, whatever the mapped type is)
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if a dotted property path traverses a non-null value that is not a Document
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if converting a result value overflows its target numeric range, a registered converter or type handler throws, or constructing or populating a result bean or map, or invoking a bean accessor, fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  MongoCollectionMapper<User> mapper = mongoDB.collectionMapper(User.class);
  Collection<String> fields = Arrays.asList("name", "email", "status");
  // All active users with only name/email/status (plus _id) populated:
  List<User> users = mapper.list(fields, Filters.eq("status", "active")); // returns all matches (empty if none)
  // null fields means "all fields":
  List<User> full = mapper.list(null, Filters.eq("status", "active"));
  ```
- **See also:** `#list(Bson)`, `#list(Collection, Bson, int, int)`
- **Signature:** `public List<T> list(final Collection<String> selectPropNames, final Bson filter, final int offset, final int count) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException, ClassCastException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Retrieves entities matching the filter with field projection and pagination.

  - `offset` (`int`) — the number of entities to skip (0-based)
  - `count` (`int`) — the maximum number of entities to return
- **Returns:** a List containing the specified range of matching entities with projected fields
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null, or if `offset` is negative, or if `count` is negative, or if a returned document has multiple non-`_id` fields for a scalar result type, inconsistent scalar projection fields, or a value that cannot be converted to the requested type, or if `selectPropNames` contains a null name and `count` is positive (the driver rejects it while encoding the query, whatever the mapped type is; a `count` of 0 sends no projection)
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if a dotted property path traverses a non-null value that is not a Document
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if converting a result value overflows its target numeric range, a registered converter or type handler throws, or constructing or populating a result bean or map, or invoking a bean accessor, fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  MongoCollectionMapper<Product> mapper = mongoDB.collectionMapper(Product.class);
  Collection<String> fields = Arrays.asList("name", "price", "category");
  Bson filter = Filters.eq("inStock", true);
  // Second page of in-stock products, only name/price/category populated:
  List<Product> page2 = mapper.list(fields, filter, 20, 20); // returns up to 20 matches (skip 20, limit 20)
  List<Product> page1 = mapper.list(fields, filter, 0, 20);  // returns the first page
  ```
- **See also:** `#list(Collection, Bson)`, `#list(Bson, int, int)`
- **Signature:** `public List<T> list(final Collection<String> selectPropNames, final Bson filter, final Bson sort) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException, ClassCastException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Retrieves all entities matching the filter with field projection and sorting.
- **Parameters:**
  - `selectPropNames` (`Collection<String>`) — collection of field names to include in the projection (null or empty for all fields)
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — the query filter to match entities against
  - `sort` (`Bson`) — the sort specification for result ordering (null for the natural, unspecified order)
- **Returns:** a List containing all matching entities with projected fields in sorted order
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null, or if a returned document has multiple non-`_id` fields for a scalar result type, inconsistent scalar projection fields, or a value that cannot be converted to the requested type, or if `selectPropNames` contains a null name (the driver rejects it while encoding the query, whatever the mapped type is)
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if a dotted property path traverses a non-null value that is not a Document
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if converting a result value overflows its target numeric range, a registered converter or type handler throws, or constructing or populating a result bean or map, or invoking a bean accessor, fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  MongoCollectionMapper<Article> mapper = mongoDB.collectionMapper(Article.class);
  Collection<String> fields = Arrays.asList("title", "author", "publishedAt", "viewCount");
  Bson filter = Filters.eq("status", "published");
  Bson sort = Sorts.descending("viewCount");   // Most viewed first
  // Published articles, most-viewed first, only the listed props populated:
  List<Article> articles = mapper.list(fields, filter, sort);                            // returns all matches in sorted order (empty if none)
  List<Article> leastViewed = mapper.list(fields, filter, Sorts.ascending("viewCount")); // reverse order
  ```
- **See also:** `#list(Collection, Bson)`, `#list(Collection, Bson, Bson, int, int)`, `com.mongodb.client.model.Sorts`
- **Signature:** `public List<T> list(final Collection<String> selectPropNames, final Bson filter, final Bson sort, final int offset, final int count) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException, ClassCastException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Retrieves entities matching the filter with field projection, sorting, and pagination.
- **Parameters:**
  - `selectPropNames` (`Collection<String>`) — collection of field names to include in the projection (null or empty for all fields)
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — the query filter to match entities against
  - `sort` (`Bson`) — the sort specification for result ordering (null for the natural, unspecified order)
  - `offset` (`int`) — the number of entities to skip (0-based)
  - `count` (`int`) — the maximum number of entities to return
- **Returns:** a List containing the specified range of matching entities with projected fields in sorted order
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null, or if `offset` is negative, or if `count` is negative, or if a returned document has multiple non-`_id` fields for a scalar result type, inconsistent scalar projection fields, or a value that cannot be converted to the requested type, or if `selectPropNames` contains a null name and `count` is positive (the driver rejects it while encoding the query, whatever the mapped type is; a `count` of 0 sends no projection)
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if a dotted property path traverses a non-null value that is not a Document
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if converting a result value overflows its target numeric range, a registered converter or type handler throws, or constructing or populating a result bean or map, or invoking a bean accessor, fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  MongoCollectionMapper<User> mapper = mongoDB.collectionMapper(User.class);
  Collection<String> fields = Arrays.asList("username", "email", "lastLoginAt");
  Bson filter = Filters.eq("status", "active");
  Bson sort = Sorts.descending("lastLoginAt");
  // Second page (rows 26-50) of active users, most-recent login first:
  List<User> recentUsers = mapper.list(fields, filter, sort, 25, 25); // returns up to 25 matches (skip 25)
  List<User> firstPage = mapper.list(fields, filter, sort, 0, 25);    // returns the first 25
  ```
- **See also:** `#list(Collection, Bson, Bson)`, `#list(Collection, Bson, int, int)`, `com.mongodb.client.model.Sorts`
- **Signature:** `public List<T> list(final Bson projection, final Bson filter, final Bson sort) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Retrieves all entities matching the filter with BSON projection and sorting.
- **Contract:**
  - A document that has only its `_id` (for example because it lacks the projected field) yields `null` (the primitive default, such as `0`, for a primitive class token such as `int.class`) when another returned document has the projected field, but its converted `_id` when none does.
- **Parameters:**
  - `projection` (`Bson`) — the BSON projection specification for field selection and transformation (null for all fields)
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — the query filter to match entities against
  - `sort` (`Bson`) — the sort specification for result ordering (null for the natural, unspecified order)
- **Returns:** a List containing all matching entities with BSON-projected fields in sorted order
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null, or if a returned document has multiple non-`_id` fields for a scalar result type, inconsistent scalar projection fields, or a value that cannot be converted to the requested type
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if converting a result value overflows its target numeric range, a registered converter or type handler throws, or constructing or populating a result bean or map, or invoking a bean accessor, fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  MongoCollectionMapper<Order> mapper = mongoDB.collectionMapper(Order.class);
  Bson projection = Projections.fields(
      Projections.include("customerId", "items"),
      Projections.computed("totalAmount", new Document("$sum", "$items.price"))
  );
  Bson filter = Filters.gte("orderDate", LocalDate.now().minusDays(30));
  Bson sort = Sorts.descending("orderDate");
  // Last 30 days of orders, newest first, with a computed totalAmount per order:
  List<Order> recentOrders = mapper.list(projection, filter, sort); // returns all matches in sorted order
  // A computed field only surfaces on the entity if it has a matching property/setter.
  ```
- **See also:** `#list(Collection, Bson, Bson)`, `com.mongodb.client.model.Projections`, `com.mongodb.client.model.Sorts`
- **Signature:** `public List<T> list(final Bson projection, final Bson filter, final Bson sort, final int offset, final int count) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Retrieves entities matching the filter with BSON projection, sorting, and pagination.
- **Contract:**
  - A document that has only its `_id` (for example because it lacks the projected field) yields `null` (the primitive default, such as `0`, for a primitive class token such as `int.class`) when another returned document has the projected field, but its converted `_id` when none does.
- **Parameters:**
  - `projection` (`Bson`) — the BSON projection specification for field selection and transformation (null for all fields)
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — the query filter to match entities against
  - `sort` (`Bson`) — the sort specification for result ordering (null for the natural, unspecified order)
  - `offset` (`int`) — the number of entities to skip (0-based)
  - `count` (`int`) — the maximum number of entities to return
- **Returns:** a List containing the specified range of matching entities with BSON-projected fields in sorted order
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null, or if `offset` is negative, or if `count` is negative, or if a returned document has multiple non-`_id` fields for a scalar result type, inconsistent scalar projection fields, or a value that cannot be converted to the requested type
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if converting a result value overflows its target numeric range, a registered converter or type handler throws, or constructing or populating a result bean or map, or invoking a bean accessor, fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  MongoCollectionMapper<Product> mapper = mongoDB.collectionMapper(Product.class);
  Bson projection = Projections.fields(
      Projections.include("name", "category"),
      Projections.elemMatch("reviews", Filters.gte("rating", 4))
  );
  Bson filter = Filters.eq("category", "electronics");
  Bson sort = Sorts.descending("avgRating");
  // Top-rated electronics, first page of 20:
  List<Product> topRated = mapper.list(projection, filter, sort, 0, 20);  // returns up to 20 matches, sorted
  List<Product> nextPage = mapper.list(projection, filter, sort, 20, 20); // the following 20
  ```
- **See also:** `#list(Bson, Bson, Bson)`, `#list(Collection, Bson, Bson, int, int)`, `com.mongodb.client.model.Projections`
##### queryForBoolean(...) -> OptionalBoolean
- **Signature:** `@Beta public OptionalBoolean queryForBoolean(final String propName, final Bson filter) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException, ClassCastException, RuntimeException`
- **Annotations:** @Beta
- **Summary:** Returns the value of `propName` from the first document matching `filter`, as a boolean value.
- **Contract:**
  - present semantics: `OptionalBoolean.empty()` is returned only when no document matches the filter.
  - If a document is matched, the returned `OptionalBoolean` is present and holds the unboxed `Boolean` value — when the field is missing or stored as BSON `null`, the JDBC-style primitive default `false` may surface inside a present Optional.
  - Use `#queryForSingleValue(String, Bson, Class)` with `Boolean.class` if you need to distinguish a missing/`null` field from a real `false`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `propName` (`String`) — the name of the boolean property to retrieve
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — the query filter to match documents against (must not be null)
- **Returns:** a present `OptionalBoolean` holding the field value (or `false` for a missing/`null` field, or for empty or whitespace-only text) when at least one document is matched; `OptionalBoolean.empty()` when no document matches
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `propName` is null or empty, or if `filter` is null, or if the selected field value cannot be converted to `Boolean` (for example an int64, double or `Decimal128` value, an int32 other than `1`/`0`/`-1`, or text such as `"yes"` once its surrounding whitespace is ignored; see `MongoDBBase`)
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if a dotted property path traverses a non-null value that is not a Document
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if a registered converter or type handler throws while converting the selected value
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  MongoCollectionMapper<User> mapper = mongoDB.collectionMapper(User.class);
  OptionalBoolean isActive = mapper.queryForBoolean("active", Filters.eq("userId", "123"));
  boolean active = isActive.orElse(false); // present -> the field value; empty (no match) -> the false fallback
  // No matching document yields empty (NOT a present false):
  OptionalBoolean none = mapper.queryForBoolean("active", Filters.eq("userId", "missing"));
  boolean isEmpty = none.isPresent() == false; // isEmpty == true
  ```
- **See also:** `OptionalBoolean`, `#queryForSingleValue(String, Bson, Class)`
##### queryForChar(...) -> OptionalChar
- **Signature:** `@Beta public OptionalChar queryForChar(final String propName, final Bson filter) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException, ClassCastException, RuntimeException`
- **Annotations:** @Beta
- **Summary:** Returns the value of `propName` from the first document matching `filter`, as a char value.
- **Contract:**
  - present semantics: `OptionalChar.empty()` is returned only when no document matches the filter.
  - If a document is matched, the returned `OptionalChar` is present and holds the unboxed `Character` value — when the field is missing or stored as BSON `null`, the JDBC-style primitive default `(char) 0` (the NUL character) may surface inside a present Optional.
  - Use `#queryForSingleValue(String, Bson, Class)` with `Character.class` if you need to distinguish a missing/`null` field from a real `(char) 0`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `propName` (`String`) — the name of the character property to retrieve
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — the query filter to match documents against (must not be null)
- **Returns:** a present `OptionalChar` holding the field value (or the default `char` for a missing/`null` field) when at least one document is matched; `OptionalChar.empty()` when no document matches
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `propName` is null or empty, or if `filter` is null, or if the selected field value cannot be converted to the requested value type
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if a dotted property path traverses a non-null value that is not a Document
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if a registered converter or type handler throws while converting the selected value
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  MongoCollectionMapper<Entity> mapper = mongoDB.collectionMapper(Entity.class);
  OptionalChar grade = mapper.queryForChar("grade", Filters.eq("studentId", "456"));
  char g = grade.orElse('?'); // present -> the field value; empty (no match) -> the '?' fallback
  // No match yields empty:
  OptionalChar none = mapper.queryForChar("grade", Filters.eq("studentId", "missing"));
  boolean isEmpty = none.isPresent() == false; // isEmpty == true
  ```
- **See also:** `OptionalChar`, `#queryForSingleValue(String, Bson, Class)`
##### queryForByte(...) -> OptionalByte
- **Signature:** `@Beta public OptionalByte queryForByte(final String propName, final Bson filter) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException, ClassCastException, RuntimeException`
- **Annotations:** @Beta
- **Summary:** Returns the value of `propName` from the first document matching `filter`, as a byte value.

  - Use `#queryForSingleValue(String, Bson, Class)` with `Byte.class` if you need to distinguish a missing/`null` field from a real `0`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `propName` (`String`) — the name of the byte property to retrieve

- **Returns:** a present `OptionalByte` holding the field value (or `0` for a missing/`null` field) when at least one document is matched; `OptionalByte.empty()` when no document matches
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `propName` is null or empty, or if `filter` is null, or if the selected field value cannot be converted to the requested value type
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error

  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if numeric conversion overflows the target range, or a registered converter or type handler throws while converting the selected value
- **Examples:**

  ```java
  OptionalByte flags = mapper.queryForByte("flags", Filters.eq("deviceId", "789"));
  byte f = flags.orElse((byte) 0); // present -> the field value; empty (no match) -> the 0 fallback
  // No match yields empty:
  OptionalByte none = mapper.queryForByte("flags", Filters.eq("deviceId", "missing"));
  ```

##### queryForString(...) -> Nullable<String>
- **Signature:** `@Beta public Nullable<String> queryForString(final String propName, final Bson filter) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException, ClassCastException, RuntimeException`
- **Annotations:** @Beta
- **Summary:** Returns the value of `propName` from the first document matching `filter`, as a String value.

- **Parameters:**
  - `propName` (`String`) — the name of the string property to retrieve
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — the query filter to match documents against (must not be null)
- **Returns:** a present `Nullable<String>` holding the field value (possibly `null` for a missing/`null` field) when at least one document is matched; `Nullable.empty()` when no document matches
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `propName` is null or empty, or if `filter` is null, or if the selected field value cannot be converted to the requested value type
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if a dotted property path traverses a non-null value that is not a Document
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if a registered converter or type handler throws while converting the selected value
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  MongoCollectionMapper<User> mapper = mongoDB.collectionMapper(User.class);
  Nullable<String> email = mapper.queryForString("email", Filters.eq("userId", "user456"));
  String addr = email.orElseIfNull("unknown@example.com"); // fallback if empty OR present-but-null
  // No match yields empty; a matched doc with a null/absent "email" yields present-but-null:
  Nullable<String> none = mapper.queryForString("email", Filters.eq("userId", "missing"));
  boolean isEmpty = none.isPresent() == false; // isEmpty == true (no document matched)
  ```
- **See also:** `Nullable`, `#queryForSingleValue(String, Bson, Class)`

##### queryForSingleValue(...) -> Nullable<V>
- **Signature:** `public <V> Nullable<V> queryForSingleValue(final String propName, final Bson filter, final Class<V> valueType) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException, ClassCastException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Returns the value of `propName` from the first document matching `filter`, as the specified type.
- **Contract:**
  - An embedded document requested as a bean class is read as the embedded document of a bean property is read (the elements of a `List<Long>` property become `Long`s, a `LocalDate` property is read in UTC, a `String` or `ObjectId` id property takes the document's own `id` field, if any, over its `_id`), and an array of embedded documents requested as a bean array likewise element by element.
  - present semantics: this method returns `Nullable.empty()` when no nonempty document is found.
- **Parameters:**
  - `propName` (`String`) — the name of the property to retrieve
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — the query filter to match documents against (must not be null)
  - `valueType` (`Class<V>`) — the class of the type to convert to
- **Returns:** a present `Nullable<V>` holding the field value (possibly `null` for a missing or BSON `null` field) when at least one document is matched; `Nullable.empty()` when no nonempty document is found
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `propName` is null or empty, or if `filter` is null, or if `valueType` is null, or if the selected field value cannot be converted to the requested value type
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if a dotted property path traverses a non-null value that is not a Document
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if numeric conversion overflows the target range, or a registered converter or type handler throws while converting the selected value, or constructing or populating a result bean fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  MongoCollectionMapper<Product> mapper = mongoDB.collectionMapper(Product.class);
  Nullable<BigDecimal> price = mapper.queryForSingleValue("price",
      Filters.eq("productId", "PROD999"), BigDecimal.class);
  BigDecimal value = price.orElseIfNull(BigDecimal.ZERO); // ZERO if empty OR present-but-null
  // No match yields empty; a matched doc whose "price" is null/absent yields present-but-null:
  Nullable<BigDecimal> none = mapper.queryForSingleValue("price",
      Filters.eq("productId", "missing"), BigDecimal.class);
  boolean isEmpty = none.isPresent() == false; // isEmpty == true (no document matched)
  ```
- **See also:** `Nullable`

##### query(...) -> Dataset
- **Signature:** `public Dataset query(final Bson filter) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Executes a query and returns results as a Dataset.
- **Parameters:**
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — the query filter to match entities against
- **Returns:** a Dataset containing the query results
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null, or if the mapped type is neither a bean class nor a Map type, or if a returned document cannot be converted to the mapped type
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if converting a result value overflows its target numeric range, a registered converter or type handler throws, or constructing or populating a result bean or map, or invoking a bean accessor, fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  MongoCollectionMapper<Sales> mapper = mongoDB.collectionMapper(Sales.class);
  Dataset ds = mapper.query(Filters.gte("amount", 1000)); // returns a Dataset (one row per matching doc)
  int rows = ds.size();                                   // number of matching documents
  // No match yields a Dataset with zero rows (never null):
  Dataset none = mapper.query(Filters.gte("amount", Long.MAX_VALUE)); // none.size() == 0
  ```
- **See also:** `Dataset`
- **Signature:** `public Dataset query(final Bson filter, final int offset, final int count) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Executes a paginated query and returns results as a Dataset.
- **Parameters:**
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — the query filter to match entities against
  - `offset` (`int`) — the number of documents to skip (0-based)
  - `count` (`int`) — the maximum number of entities to return
- **Returns:** a Dataset containing the paginated query results
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null, or if `offset` is negative, or if `count` is negative, or if the mapped type is neither a bean class nor a Map type, or if a returned document cannot be converted to the mapped type
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if converting a result value overflows its target numeric range, a registered converter or type handler throws, or constructing or populating a result bean or map, or invoking a bean accessor, fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  MongoCollectionMapper<Sales> mapper = mongoDB.collectionMapper(Sales.class);
  Dataset page1 = mapper.query(Filters.gte("amount", 1000), 0, 100);   // returns up to 100 rows (first page)
  Dataset page2 = mapper.query(Filters.gte("amount", 1000), 100, 100); // the next 100 (skip 100, limit 100)
  ```
- **See also:** `Dataset`
- **Signature:** `public Dataset query(final Collection<String> selectPropNames, final Bson filter) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException, ClassCastException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Executes a query with field projection and returns results as a Dataset.
- **Parameters:**
  - `selectPropNames` (`Collection<String>`) — collection of field names to include in the projection (null or empty for all fields)
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — the query filter to match entities against
- **Returns:** a Dataset containing the query results with projected fields
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null, or if the mapped type is neither a bean class nor a Map type, or if a returned document cannot be converted to the mapped type, or if `selectPropNames` contains a null or duplicated name (each name is a Dataset column)
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if a dotted property path traverses a non-null value that is not a Document
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if converting a result value overflows its target numeric range, a registered converter or type handler throws, or constructing or populating a result bean or map, or invoking a bean accessor, fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  MongoCollectionMapper<Customer> mapper = mongoDB.collectionMapper(Customer.class);
  Collection<String> fields = Arrays.asList("name", "email", "city");
  // The Dataset has exactly one column per selected field (no _id column):
  Dataset ds = mapper.query(fields, Filters.eq("status", "active")); // returns a Dataset, possibly 0 rows
  List<String> columns = ds.columnNames();
  ```
- **See also:** `Dataset`
- **Signature:** `public Dataset query(final Collection<String> selectPropNames, final Bson filter, final int offset, final int count) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException, ClassCastException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Executes a paginated query with field projection and returns results as a Dataset.
- **Parameters:**

- **Returns:** a Dataset containing the paginated query results with projected fields
- **Throws:**

  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if a dotted property path traverses a non-null value that is not a Document
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if converting a result value overflows its target numeric range, a registered converter or type handler throws, or constructing or populating a result bean or map, or invoking a bean accessor, fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Collection<String> fields = Arrays.asList("orderId", "total", "status");
  Dataset orders = mapper.query(fields, Filters.gte("total", 1000), 20, 10);   // returns up to 10 rows (skip 20)
  Dataset firstPage = mapper.query(fields, Filters.gte("total", 1000), 0, 10); // the first 10 instead
  ```
