##### deleteMany(...) -> DeleteResult
- **Signature:** `public DeleteResult deleteMany(final Bson filter) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoWriteException, MongoException`
- **Summary:** Deletes all entities matching the specified filter (blocking operation).
- **Parameters:**
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — the query filter to match entities to delete
- **Returns:** DeleteResult containing information about the delete operation
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoWriteException` — if the server rejects the delete with a write error
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // EVERY matching document is deleted (contrast with deleteOne):
  DeleteResult result = mapper.deleteMany(
      Filters.lt("expiryDate", new Date())
  );                                       // returns DeleteResult; getDeletedCount() may be > 1
  long removed = result.getDeletedCount(); // e.g. 37; 0 when nothing matched
  ```
- **See also:** `#deleteOne(Bson)`, `DeleteResult`, `#collectionExecutor()`
- **Signature:** `public DeleteResult deleteMany(final Bson filter, final DeleteOptions options) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoWriteException, MongoException`
- **Summary:** Deletes all entities matching the filter with additional delete options.
- **Contract:**
  - Options enable collation for language-specific matching and index hints for performance optimization when deleting large numbers of documents.
- **Parameters:**
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — the query filter to match entities to delete
  - `options` (`DeleteOptions`) — additional options for the delete operation (null uses defaults)
- **Returns:** DeleteResult containing information about the delete operation
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoWriteException` — if the server rejects the delete with a write error
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  DeleteOptions options = new DeleteOptions()
      .hint(Indexes.ascending("status", "createdDate"));
  DeleteResult result = mapper.deleteMany(
      Filters.and(
          Filters.eq("status", "archived"),
          Filters.lt("createdDate", oneYearAgo)
      ), options); // returns DeleteResult; getDeletedCount() may be > 1
  ```
- **See also:** `#deleteMany(Bson)`, `DeleteOptions`
##### bulkInsert(...) -> BulkWriteResult
- **Signature:** `public BulkWriteResult bulkInsert(final Collection<? extends T> entities) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoBulkWriteException, MongoException`
- **Summary:** Inserts the supplied entities as a single MongoDB bulk-write of `InsertOneModel` entries and returns the `BulkWriteResult` reported by the server.
- **Parameters:**
  - `entities` (`Collection<? extends T>`) — collection of entities to insert in bulk
- **Returns:** the `BulkWriteResult` reported by the server (use `BulkWriteResult#getInsertedCount()` for the inserted count)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `entities` is null or empty or contains a null document, or if a document value cannot be converted from a Map, bean, or array of String name/value pairs
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if a bean accessor, BSON implementation, codec, or value converter throws during request or result conversion
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoBulkWriteException` — if the server reports a write or write-concern error for one or more requests in the batch
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<Product> products = loadLargeProductCatalog(); // e.g. 5000 products
  BulkWriteResult result = mapper.bulkInsert(products); // result.getInsertedCount() is e.g. 5000

  mapper.bulkInsert(Collections.emptyList());         // throws IllegalArgumentException: empty collection
  ```
- **See also:** `#bulkInsert(Collection, BulkWriteOptions)`, `#insertMany(Collection)`
- **Signature:** `public BulkWriteResult bulkInsert(final Collection<? extends T> entities, final BulkWriteOptions options) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoBulkWriteException, MongoException`
- **Summary:** Performs a bulk insert of entities with additional bulk write options.
- **Parameters:**
  - `entities` (`Collection<? extends T>`) — collection of entities to insert in bulk
  - `options` (`BulkWriteOptions`) — additional options for the bulk write operation (null uses defaults)
- **Returns:** the `BulkWriteResult` reported by the server (use `BulkWriteResult#getInsertedCount()` for the inserted count)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `entities` is null or empty or contains a null document, or if a document value cannot be converted from a Map, bean, or array of String name/value pairs
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if a bean accessor, BSON implementation, codec, or value converter throws during request or result conversion
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoBulkWriteException` — if the server reports a write or write-concern error for one or more requests in the batch
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  BulkWriteOptions options = new BulkWriteOptions()
      .ordered(false)  // unordered: attempt every insert even if some fail
      .bypassDocumentValidation(true);
  List<LogEntry> logs = collectLogEntries();
  BulkWriteResult result = mapper.bulkInsert(logs, options); // result.getInsertedCount() is the inserted count
  ```
- **See also:** `#bulkInsert(Collection)`, `BulkWriteOptions`
##### bulkWrite(...) -> BulkWriteResult
- **Signature:** `public BulkWriteResult bulkWrite(final List<? extends WriteModel<? extends Document>> requests) throws IllegalArgumentException, UnsupportedOperationException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoBulkWriteException, MongoException`
- **Summary:** Executes a bulk write operation with mixed write models.
- **Parameters:**
  - `requests` (`List<? extends WriteModel<? extends Document>>`) — list of write models defining the operations to perform
- **Returns:** BulkWriteResult containing detailed information about the bulk operation
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `requests` is null or empty, or contains a null write model
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if `requests` contains a WriteModel subtype that the MongoDB driver does not support
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoBulkWriteException` — if the server reports a write or write-concern error for one or more requests in the batch
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<WriteModel<Document>> operations = Arrays.asList(
      new InsertOneModel<>(doc1),
      new UpdateOneModel<>(filter1, update1),
      new DeleteOneModel<>(filter2)
  );
  BulkWriteResult result = mapper.bulkWrite(operations); // returns BulkWriteResult; never null
  int inserted = result.getInsertedCount();              // per-type counts available on the result
  ```
- **See also:** `#bulkWrite(List, BulkWriteOptions)`, `BulkWriteResult`
- **Signature:** `public BulkWriteResult bulkWrite(final List<? extends WriteModel<? extends Document>> requests, final BulkWriteOptions options) throws IllegalArgumentException, UnsupportedOperationException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoBulkWriteException, MongoException`
- **Summary:** Executes a bulk write operation with mixed write models and additional options.
- **Parameters:**
  - `requests` (`List<? extends WriteModel<? extends Document>>`) — list of write models defining the operations to perform
  - `options` (`BulkWriteOptions`) — additional options for the bulk write operation (null uses defaults)
- **Returns:** BulkWriteResult containing detailed information about the bulk operation
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `requests` is null or empty, or contains a null write model
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if `requests` contains a WriteModel subtype that the MongoDB driver does not support
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoBulkWriteException` — if the server reports a write or write-concern error for one or more requests in the batch
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  BulkWriteOptions options = new BulkWriteOptions()
      .ordered(true)  // ordered: stop at the first failing op (earlier ops stay applied)
      .bypassDocumentValidation(false);
  List<WriteModel<Document>> operations = createComplexBatch();
  BulkWriteResult result = mapper.bulkWrite(operations, options); // returns BulkWriteResult; never null
  ```
- **See also:** `#bulkWrite(List)`, `BulkWriteOptions`
##### findOneAndUpdate(...) -> T
- **Signature:** `public T findOneAndUpdate(final Bson filter, final T update) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException, ArrayStoreException`
- **Summary:** Atomically finds the first document matching `filter`, applies the supplied update, and returns the matched document as an entity.
- **Parameters:**
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — the query filter to match the entity to update
  - `update` (`T`) — the entity, or a driver-built `Bson` update expression, containing the update data
- **Returns:** the matched entity (pre-update by default), or `null` if no document matched
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null, or if `update` is null, or if an update document has a null field name, mixes operator and ordinary field names, or has no updatable fields after removing `_id`, or if an update value cannot be converted from a Map, bean, or array of String name/value pairs, or if the returned document cannot be converted to the mapped type
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if a bean accessor, BSON implementation, codec, or value converter throws during request or result conversion
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
  - `java.lang.ArrayStoreException` — if the result type is a reference-array type and a returned document value is incompatible with its component type
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  User updates = new User();
  updates.setLoginCount(5);
  // Returns the PRE-update entity by default (ReturnDocument.BEFORE):
  User user = mapper.findOneAndUpdate(
      Filters.eq("email", "user@example.com"), updates); // returns the matched entity, or null if none matched
  ```
- **See also:** `#findOneAndUpdate(Bson, Object, FindOneAndUpdateOptions)`
- **Signature:** `public T findOneAndUpdate(final Bson filter, final T update, final FindOneAndUpdateOptions options) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException, ArrayStoreException`
- **Summary:** Finds and updates a single entity atomically with additional update options.
- **Parameters:**
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — the query filter to match the entity to update
  - `update` (`T`) — the entity, or a driver-built `Bson` update expression, containing the update data
  - `options` (`FindOneAndUpdateOptions`) — additional options for the find and update operation (null uses defaults)
- **Returns:** the entity before or after the update (based on options), or null if not found
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null, or if `update` is null, or if an update document has a null field name, mixes operator and ordinary field names, or has no updatable fields after removing `_id`, or if an update value cannot be converted from a Map, bean, or array of String name/value pairs, or if the returned document cannot be converted to the mapped type
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if a bean accessor, BSON implementation, codec, or value converter throws during request or result conversion
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
  - `java.lang.ArrayStoreException` — if the result type is a reference-array type and a returned document value is incompatible with its component type
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  FindOneAndUpdateOptions options = new FindOneAndUpdateOptions()
      .returnDocument(ReturnDocument.AFTER)  // return the POST-update document instead of the default BEFORE
      .upsert(true)
      .projection(Projections.include("name", "status"));
  User updates = new User();
  updates.setLastSeen(new Date());
  User updatedUser = mapper.findOneAndUpdate(
      Filters.eq("email", "user@example.com"), updates, options); // returns the AFTER entity; upsert(true) guarantees non-null
  ```
- **See also:** `#findOneAndUpdate(Bson, Object)`, `FindOneAndUpdateOptions`
- **Signature:** `public T findOneAndUpdate(final Bson filter, final Collection<? extends T> objList) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException, ArrayStoreException`
- **Summary:** Finds and updates a single entity atomically using a pipeline of update operations.
- **Contract:**
  - If the mapper's row type itself implements `Bson`, an element passes through as a caller-built stage whose values are evaluated as aggregation expressions; an operator document must obey the stage restrictions below.
- **Parameters:**
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — the query filter to match the entity to update
  - `objList` (`Collection<? extends T>`) — collection of entities forming the update pipeline
- **Returns:** the entity before the update (default behavior), or null if not found
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null, or if `objList` is null or empty or contains a null element, or if an update document has a null field name, mixes operator and ordinary field names, or has no updatable fields after removing `_id`, or if an update value cannot be converted from a Map, bean, or array of String name/value pairs, or if the returned document cannot be converted to the mapped type
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if a bean accessor, BSON implementation, codec, or value converter throws during request or result conversion
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
  - `java.lang.ArrayStoreException` — if the result type is a reference-array type and a returned document value is incompatible with its component type
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  User visitUpdate = new User();
  visitUpdate.setVisitCount(5);  // Set visit count (literal $set assignment)
  User timestampUpdate = new User();
  timestampUpdate.setLastUpdated(new Date());
  List<User> updatePipeline = Arrays.asList(visitUpdate, timestampUpdate);
  // Pre-update entity by default (ReturnDocument.BEFORE):
  User user = mapper.findOneAndUpdate(
      Filters.eq("userId", "USER123"), updatePipeline); // returns the matched entity, or null if none matched
  ```
- **See also:** `#findOneAndUpdate(Bson, Object)`, `#findOneAndUpdate(Bson, Collection, FindOneAndUpdateOptions)`
- **Signature:** `public T findOneAndUpdate(final Bson filter, final Collection<? extends T> objList, final FindOneAndUpdateOptions options) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException, ArrayStoreException`
- **Summary:** Finds and updates a single entity atomically using a pipeline with additional options.
- **Parameters:**
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — the query filter to match the entity to update
  - `objList` (`Collection<? extends T>`) — collection of entities forming the update pipeline
  - `options` (`FindOneAndUpdateOptions`) — additional options for the find and update operation (null uses defaults)
- **Returns:** the entity before or after the update (based on options), or null if not found
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null, or if `objList` is null or empty or contains a null element, or if an update document has a null field name, mixes operator and ordinary field names, or has no updatable fields after removing `_id`, or if an update value cannot be converted from a Map, bean, or array of String name/value pairs, or if the returned document cannot be converted to the mapped type
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if a bean accessor, BSON implementation, codec, or value converter throws during request or result conversion
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
  - `java.lang.ArrayStoreException` — if the result type is a reference-array type and a returned document value is incompatible with its component type
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  FindOneAndUpdateOptions options = new FindOneAndUpdateOptions()
      .returnDocument(ReturnDocument.AFTER) // return the POST-update document
      .upsert(true);
  List<Product> pipeline = createPriceUpdatePipeline();
  Product updated = mapper.findOneAndUpdate(
      Filters.eq("sku", "PROD-456"), pipeline, options); // returns the AFTER entity (upsert guarantees non-null)
  ```
- **See also:** `#findOneAndUpdate(Bson, Collection)`, `FindOneAndUpdateOptions`
##### findOneAndReplace(...) -> T
- **Signature:** `public T findOneAndReplace(final Bson filter, final T replacement) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException, ArrayStoreException`
- **Summary:** Finds and replaces a single entity atomically.
- **Parameters:**
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — the query filter to match the entity to replace
  - `replacement` (`T`) — the new entity to replace the existing one
- **Returns:** the original entity before replacement, or null if not found
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null, or if `replacement` is null, or if a document value cannot be converted from a Map, bean, or array of String name/value pairs, or if the converted replacement has a top-level field name starting with `$` (rejected by the driver before the command is sent), or if the returned document cannot be converted to the mapped type
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if a bean accessor, BSON implementation, codec, or value converter throws during request or result conversion
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
  - `java.lang.ArrayStoreException` — if the result type is a reference-array type and a returned document value is incompatible with its component type
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  User replacement = new User("John Updated", "john.new@example.com", 32);
  // Returns the original (pre-replacement) entity by default:
  User originalUser = mapper.findOneAndReplace(
      Filters.eq("username", "john"), replacement); // returns the original entity, or null if no match
  ```
- **See also:** `#findOneAndReplace(Bson, Object, FindOneAndReplaceOptions)`, `#replaceOne(Bson, Object)`
- **Signature:** `public T findOneAndReplace(final Bson filter, final T replacement, final FindOneAndReplaceOptions options) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException, ArrayStoreException`
- **Summary:** Finds and replaces a single entity atomically with additional replace options.
- **Parameters:**
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — the query filter to match the entity to replace
  - `replacement` (`T`) — the new entity to replace the existing one
  - `options` (`FindOneAndReplaceOptions`) — additional options for the find and replace operation (null uses defaults)
- **Returns:** the entity before or after replacement (based on options), or null if not found
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null, or if `replacement` is null, or if a document value cannot be converted from a Map, bean, or array of String name/value pairs, or if the converted replacement has a top-level field name starting with `$` (rejected by the driver before the command is sent), or if the returned document cannot be converted to the mapped type
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if a bean accessor, BSON implementation, codec, or value converter throws during request or result conversion
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
  - `java.lang.ArrayStoreException` — if the result type is a reference-array type and a returned document value is incompatible with its component type
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  FindOneAndReplaceOptions options = new FindOneAndReplaceOptions()
      .returnDocument(ReturnDocument.AFTER)  // return the replacement document, not the original
      .upsert(true)
      .projection(Projections.exclude("_id"));
  Article newArticle = createUpdatedArticle();
  Article result = mapper.findOneAndReplace(
      Filters.eq("slug", "article-slug"), newArticle, options); // returns the AFTER entity (upsert -> non-null)
  ```
- **See also:** `#findOneAndReplace(Bson, Object)`, `FindOneAndReplaceOptions`
##### findOneAndDelete(...) -> T
- **Signature:** `public T findOneAndDelete(final Bson filter) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException, ArrayStoreException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Finds and deletes a single entity atomically.
- **Parameters:**
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — the query filter to match the entity to delete
- **Returns:** the deleted entity, or null if no entity matched the filter
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null, or if the returned document cannot be converted to the mapped type
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
  - `java.lang.ArrayStoreException` — if the result type is a reference-array type and a returned document value is incompatible with its component type
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if converting a result value overflows its target numeric range, a registered converter or type handler throws, or constructing or populating a result bean or map, or invoking a bean accessor, fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  User deletedUser = mapper.findOneAndDelete(
      Filters.and(
          Filters.eq("status", "inactive"),
          Filters.lt("lastLogin", thirtyDaysAgo)
      )
  ); // returns the just-deleted entity, or null if nothing matched
  if (deletedUser != null) {
      auditUserDeletion(deletedUser); // null guard: only the matched doc was removed
  }
  ```
- **See also:** `#findOneAndDelete(Bson, FindOneAndDeleteOptions)`, `#deleteOne(Bson)`
- **Signature:** `public T findOneAndDelete(final Bson filter, final FindOneAndDeleteOptions options) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException, ArrayStoreException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Finds and deletes a single entity atomically with additional delete options.
- **Parameters:**
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — the query filter to match the entity to delete
  - `options` (`FindOneAndDeleteOptions`) — additional options for the find and delete operation (null uses defaults)
- **Returns:** the deleted entity with projected fields, or null if no entity matched
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null, or if the returned document cannot be converted to the mapped type
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
  - `java.lang.ArrayStoreException` — if the result type is a reference-array type and a returned document value is incompatible with its component type
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if converting a result value overflows its target numeric range, a registered converter or type handler throws, or constructing or populating a result bean or map, or invoking a bean accessor, fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  FindOneAndDeleteOptions options = new FindOneAndDeleteOptions()
      .sort(Sorts.ascending("createdAt"))  // among matches, delete the oldest one
      .projection(Projections.include("email", "name"));
  // Only email/name (plus _id) are populated on the returned entity:
  User deletedUser = mapper.findOneAndDelete(
      Filters.eq("status", "pending"), options); // returns the deleted entity, or null if nothing matched
  ```
- **See also:** `#findOneAndDelete(Bson)`, `FindOneAndDeleteOptions`
##### distinct(...) -> Stream<T>
- **Signature:** `public Stream<T> distinct(final String fieldName) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException`
- **Summary:** Returns a stream of entities, each carrying one distinct value of the specified field across all entities.
- **Contract:**
  - Each distinct value is surfaced under `fieldName` on an entity of the mapped type, and is only readable if the entity declares a matching property.
- **Parameters:**
  - `fieldName` (`String`) — the name of the field to get distinct values from
- **Returns:** a Stream of entities containing only the distinct field values. Documents that lack the field contribute a null-valued entity for a non-primitive `T`, including a `null` element for a single-value reference `T`; a primitive `T` skips that null group instead of converting it to the primitive default
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `fieldName` is null, empty, or contains an empty path segment (such as `"a..b"`)
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Stream the unique "category" values across the whole collection:
  try (Stream<Product> categoryStream = mapper.distinct("category")) { // returns a lazy Stream of distinct values
      List<String> categories = categoryStream
          .map(Product::getCategory)
          .toList();
  }
  ```
- **See also:** `#distinct(String, Bson)`, `Stream`
- **Signature:** `public Stream<T> distinct(final String fieldName, final Bson filter) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException`
- **Summary:** Returns a stream of entities, each carrying one distinct value of the specified field from matching entities.
- **Contract:**
  - Each distinct value is surfaced under `fieldName` on an entity of the mapped type, and is only readable if the entity declares a matching property (a single-value `T` such as `String` gets no `$project` stage and receives each value directly, as in `#distinct(String)`).
- **Parameters:**
  - `fieldName` (`String`) — the name of the field to get distinct values from
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — the query filter to match entities before extracting distinct values
- **Returns:** a Stream of entities containing only the distinct field values from matching entities. Matching documents that lack the field follow the same primitive/reference null-group behavior as `#distinct(String)`
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `fieldName` is null, empty, or contains an empty path segment (such as `"a..b"`), or if `filter` is null
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Distinct "category" values, but only among active products:
  try (Stream<Product> stream = mapper.distinct("category",
          Filters.eq("active", true))) { // returns a lazy Stream of distinct values from matches only
      stream.map(Product::getCategory)
            .forEach(System.out::println);
  }
  ```
- **See also:** `#distinct(String)`, `Stream`
##### aggregate(...) -> Stream<T>
- **Signature:** `public Stream<T> aggregate(final List<? extends Bson> pipeline) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException`
- **Summary:** Executes an aggregation pipeline and returns a stream of transformed entities.
- **Parameters:**
  - `pipeline` (`List<? extends Bson>`) — list of aggregation pipeline stages to execute
- **Returns:** a Stream of entities representing the aggregation results
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `pipeline` is null, or if it contains a null stage (rejected by the driver when the cursor is opened by this call)
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<Bson> pipeline = Arrays.asList(
      Aggregates.match(Filters.gte("price", 100.0)),
      Aggregates.group("$category", Accumulators.avg("avgPrice", "$price")),
      // $group puts the group key in _id; expose it as "category" so it maps onto the entity property:
      Aggregates.project(Projections.fields(Projections.excludeId(),
          Projections.computed("category", "$_id"), Projections.include("avgPrice"))),
      Aggregates.sort(Sorts.descending("avgPrice"))
  );
  try (Stream<Product> results = mapper.aggregate(pipeline)) { // returns a lazy Stream of pipeline output docs
      results.forEach(stat -> System.out.println(
          stat.getCategory() + ": $" + stat.getAvgPrice()));
  }
  ```
- **See also:** `Stream`, `com.mongodb.client.model.Aggregates`, `com.mongodb.client.model.Accumulators`
##### groupBy(...) -> Stream<T>
- **Signature:** `@Beta public Stream<T> groupBy(final String fieldName) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException`
- **Annotations:** @Beta
- **Summary:** Returns a stream of entities, one per group, grouped by the specified field.
- **Contract:**
  - For a single-value row type, the null-key group is omitted if the mapper was created with a primitive class token (such as `int.class`); a wrapper or reference single-value type receives a `null` element.
- **Parameters:**
  - `fieldName` (`String`) — the field name to group entities by; a dotted path such as `"a.b"` groups by the nested field, and each segment must be nonempty
- **Returns:** a Stream of entities representing grouped results
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `fieldName` is null, empty, or contains an empty path segment (such as `"a..b"`)
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // One entity per distinct "department" value:
  try (Stream<User> groupedStream = mapper.groupBy("department")) { // returns a lazy Stream, one row per group
      groupedStream.forEach(group ->
          System.out.println("Department: " + group.getDepartment()));
  }
  ```
- **See also:** `#groupBy(Collection)`, `#groupByAndCount(String)`
- **Signature:** `@Beta public Stream<T> groupBy(final Collection<String> fieldNames) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException`
- **Annotations:** @Beta
- **Summary:** Returns a stream of entities, one per group, grouped by multiple fields.
- **Contract:**
  - In the result that field is present with the value `null` — inside `_id` when `T` is `Document`, otherwise as a field or property of the row — and a dotted path such as `"a.b"` appears as the nested document `{a: {b: <value>}}`.
  - If `fieldNames` contains only one distinct field and the mapper has a single-value row type, each group key is converted to that type.
- **Parameters:**
  - `fieldNames` (`Collection<String>`) — collection of field names to group entities by. Dotted paths produce nested key fields; paths must have nonempty segments, and no path may be an ancestor of another.
- **Returns:** a Stream of entities representing grouped results
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `fieldNames` is null or empty, contains a null path, an empty path segment or overlapping paths
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Collection<String> groupFields = Arrays.asList("department", "level");
  // One entity per unique (department, level) combination:
  try (Stream<Employee> groups = mapper.groupBy(groupFields)) { // returns a lazy Stream, one row per combination
      groups.forEach(group -> System.out.println(
          group.getDepartment() + "/" + group.getLevel()));
  }
  ```
- **See also:** `#groupBy(String)`, `#groupByAndCount(Collection)`
##### groupByAndCount(...) -> Stream<T>
- **Signature:** `@Beta public Stream<T> groupByAndCount(final String fieldName) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException`
- **Annotations:** @Beta
- **Summary:** Returns a stream of entities, one per group, grouped by the specified field, each carrying its count.
- **Contract:**
  - The count surfaces under a `count` field on the entity and is only readable if the entity declares a matching property.
- **Parameters:**
  - `fieldName` (`String`) — the field name to group entities by; a dotted path such as `"a.b"` groups by the nested field, and each segment must be nonempty
- **Returns:** a Stream of entities with group information and counts
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `fieldName` is null, empty, or contains an empty path segment (such as `"a..b"`), or if `fieldName` is `"count"` or starts with `"count."` (it would collide with the count column), and the mapped type is not `Document`
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // One entity per "status" group, each carrying its member count:
  try (Stream<Order> countedGroups = mapper.groupByAndCount("status")) { // returns a lazy Stream, one row per group
      countedGroups.forEach(group -> System.out.println(
          group.getStatus() + ": " + group.getCount() + " orders"));
  }
  ```
- **See also:** `#groupBy(String)`, `#groupByAndCount(Collection)`
- **Signature:** `@Beta public Stream<T> groupByAndCount(final Collection<String> fieldNames) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException`
- **Annotations:** @Beta
- **Summary:** Returns a stream of entities, one per group, grouped by multiple fields, each carrying its count.
- **Contract:**
  - The count surfaces under a `count` field on the entity and is only readable if the entity declares a matching property.
  - In the result that field is present with the value `null` — inside `_id` when `T` is `Document`, otherwise as a field or property of the row — and a dotted path such as `"a.b"` appears as the nested document `{a: {b: <value>}}`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `fieldNames` (`Collection<String>`) — collection of field names to group entities by. Dotted paths produce nested key fields; paths must have nonempty segments, and no path may be an ancestor of another.
- **Returns:** a Stream of entities with group information and counts
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `fieldNames` is null or empty, contains a null path, an empty path segment or overlapping paths, or if `fieldNames` contains `"count"` or a path starting with `"count."` (either would collide with the count column), and the mapped type is not `Document`
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Collection<String> fields = Arrays.asList("region", "productType");
  // One entity per (region, productType) combination, each carrying its count:
  try (Stream<Sale> stats = mapper.groupByAndCount(fields)) { // returns a lazy Stream, one row per combination
      stats.forEach(stat -> System.out.println(
          stat.getRegion() + "/" + stat.getProductType() + ": " +
          stat.getCount() + " sales"));
  }
  ```
- **See also:** `#groupBy(Collection)`, `#groupByAndCount(String)`
##### mapReduce(...) -> Stream<T>
- **Signature:** `@Deprecated public Stream<T> mapReduce(final String mapFunction, final String reduceFunction) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException, MongoException`
- **Summary:** Executes a MapReduce operation and returns a stream of entities representing the results.
- **Deprecated:** yes — Use `#aggregate(List)` with aggregation pipeline instead.
- **Contract:**
  - MapReduce operations are less efficient than aggregation pipelines and should be avoided in new code.
- **Parameters:**
  - `mapFunction` (`String`) — JavaScript map function as a string
  - `reduceFunction` (`String`) — JavaScript reduce function as a string
- **Returns:** a Stream of entities representing the MapReduce results
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `mapFunction` is null or empty, or if `reduceFunction` is null or empty
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or requested result type has no usable BSON codec
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
  - `com.mongodb.MongoException` — if the MongoDB command cannot complete because of a connection, authentication, server, or command error
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  String mapFunction = "function() { emit(this.category, this.price); }";
  String reduceFunction = "function(key, values) { return Array.sum(values); }";
  // Prefer the aggregate pipeline in new code; mapReduce is retained for legacy scripts:
  try (Stream<Product> results = mapper.mapReduce(mapFunction, reduceFunction)) { // returns a lazy Stream
      results.forEach(result -> System.out.println(result));
  }
  ```
- **See also:** `#aggregate(List)`, `com.mongodb.client.model.Aggregates`

### Class MongoDB (com.landawn.abacus.da.mongodb.MongoDB)
Synchronous MongoDB database executor that provides a simplified interface for MongoDB operations.

**Thread-safety:** unspecified
**Nullability:** unspecified
**Extends:** `MongoDBBase`

#### Public Constructors
- `public MongoDB(final MongoDatabase mongoDB) throws IllegalArgumentException` — Constructs a MongoDB executor with the specified database and the framework's default async executor.
  - **Throws:**
    - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `mongoDB` is `null`
  ```java
  MongoClient client = MongoClients.create("mongodb://localhost:27017");
  MongoDatabase database = client.getDatabase("myapp");
  MongoDB mongoDB = new MongoDB(database);                 // wraps "myapp", uses DEFAULT_ASYNC_EXECUTOR
  MongoDatabase wrapped = mongoDB.db();                    // codec-configured database (not necessarily the same instance passed in)

  // Edge case: a null database is rejected eagerly.
  MongoDB bad = new MongoDB((MongoDatabase) null);         // throws IllegalArgumentException
  ```
- `public MongoDB(final MongoDatabase mongoDB, final AsyncExecutor asyncExecutor) throws IllegalArgumentException` — Constructs a MongoDB executor with the specified database and custom async executor.
  - **Throws:**
    - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `mongoDB` or `asyncExecutor` is `null`
  ```java
  AsyncExecutor customExecutor = new AsyncExecutor(10, 50, 300L, TimeUnit.SECONDS);
  MongoDB mongoDB = new MongoDB(database, customExecutor); // both args wired in; collection executors use customExecutor for async wrappers

  // Edge cases: both arguments must be non-null.
  new MongoDB((MongoDatabase) null, customExecutor);       // throws IllegalArgumentException
  new MongoDB(database, (AsyncExecutor) null);             // throws IllegalArgumentException
  ```

##### db(...) -> MongoDatabase

- **Examples:**
  ```java
  MongoDatabase database = mongoDB.db();                  // never null; the codec-configured database backing this executor
  database.createCollection("newCollection");             // direct driver call, bypassing this wrapper

  // Successive calls return the same configured instance.
  boolean same = (mongoDB.db() == mongoDB.db());           // true
  ```

##### collection(...) -> varies by overload
- **Signature:** `public MongoCollection<Document> collection(final String collectionName) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns a MongoDB collection as a Document-based collection.
- **Contract:**
  - This is ideal for schema-less operations or when working with dynamic document structures.
- **Parameters:**
  - `collectionName` (`String`) — the name of the MongoDB collection to retrieve
- **Returns:** a MongoCollection configured for Document operations
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if collectionName is null or empty
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  MongoCollection<Document> users = mongoDB.collection("users");  // never null; a handle even if the collection does not yet exist
  users.insertOne(new Document("name", "John").append("age", 30));

  // The collection name is validated up front, consistent with collectionExecutor(String):
  mongoDB.collection(null);                               // throws IllegalArgumentException ("collectionName")
  ```
- **See also:** `Document`, `MongoCollection`
- **Signature:** `public <T> MongoCollection<T> collection(final String collectionName, final Class<T> rowType) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns a MongoDB collection configured for a specific Java type with automatic POJO mapping.
- **Parameters:**
  - `collectionName` (`String`) — the name of the MongoDB collection to retrieve
  - `rowType` (`Class<T>`) — the Class object representing the document type
- **Returns:** a MongoCollection configured for the specified type
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if collectionName is null or empty, or rowType is null
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  MongoCollection<User> userColl = mongoDB.collection("users", User.class); // never null; typed handle, POJO codec applied
  userColl.insertOne(new User("Alice", "alice@example.com"));

  // Document is just the special case where rowType is Document.class.
  MongoCollection<Document> raw = mongoDB.collection("users", Document.class); // equivalent to collection("users")

  // Both arguments are validated up front, consistent with collectionMapper(String, Class):
  mongoDB.collection(null, User.class);                  // throws IllegalArgumentException ("collectionName")
  mongoDB.collection("users", (Class<User>) null);       // throws IllegalArgumentException ("rowType")
  ```
- **See also:** `MongoCollection`
##### collectionExecutor(...) -> MongoCollectionExecutor
- **Signature:** `public MongoCollectionExecutor collectionExecutor(final String collectionName) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates a MongoCollectionExecutor for performing operations on the specified collection.
- **Parameters:**
  - `collectionName` (`String`) — the name of the MongoDB collection
- **Returns:** a MongoCollectionExecutor for the specified collection
- **Throws:**

- **Examples:**
  ```java
  MongoCollectionExecutor executor = mongoDB.collectionExecutor("users"); // never null; a fresh executor each call (not pooled)
  long count = executor.count(Filters.eq("status", "active"));
  ```
