##### bulkInsert(...) -> Mono<BulkWriteResult>
- **Signature:** `public Mono<BulkWriteResult> bulkInsert(final Collection<? extends T> entities) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException`
- **Summary:** Performs a bulk insert of multiple entities into the collection in a reactive manner.
- **Contract:**
  - A `Document` entity is wrapped as-is, so the driver writes a generated `_id` into that same document when this method builds the publisher.
  - Usage Examples: After subscription, the returned publisher signals a `MongoException` if the MongoDB write command fails.
- **Parameters:**
  - `entities` (`Collection<? extends T>`) — the collection of entities to insert (must not be null or empty)
- **Returns:** a `Mono` that, on subscription, emits exactly one `BulkWriteResult` (use `BulkWriteResult#getInsertedCount()` for the inserted count), then completes
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `entities` is null or empty or contains a null document, or if a document value cannot be converted from a Map, bean, or array of String name/value pairs
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if a bean accessor, BSON implementation, or codec throws while preparing the request before the publisher is returned
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or the document type has no usable BSON codec while the driver constructs the operation
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Typical: emits the BulkWriteResult (one inserted document per entity on success).
  List<User> newUsers = Arrays.asList(user1, user2, user3);
  userMapper.bulkInsert(newUsers)
      .subscribe(result -> System.out.println("Inserted " + result.getInsertedCount() + " users"));   // inserted 3

  // Edge: cold publisher — building it inserts nothing until subscribed.
  Mono<BulkWriteResult> pending = userMapper.bulkInsert(newUsers);   // nothing written yet

  // Negative: a null or empty collection -> IllegalArgumentException.
  userMapper.bulkInsert(Collections.emptyList());   // throws IllegalArgumentException

  // Negative: a per-document failure (e.g. duplicate _id) -> onError(MongoBulkWriteException).
  userMapper.bulkInsert(usersWithDuplicate)
      .subscribe(r -> {}, err -> System.err.println("Bulk insert failed: " + err));   // onError(MongoBulkWriteException)
  ```
- **See also:** `MongoCollectionExecutor#bulkInsert(Collection)`
- **Signature:** `public Mono<BulkWriteResult> bulkInsert(final Collection<? extends T> entities, final BulkWriteOptions options) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException`
- **Summary:** Performs a bulk insert with custom write options.
- **Contract:**
  - Usage Examples: After subscription, the returned publisher signals a `MongoException` if the MongoDB write command fails.
- **Parameters:**
  - `entities` (`Collection<? extends T>`) — the collection of entities to insert
  - `options` (`BulkWriteOptions`) — configuration options for the bulk write operation (may be null to use defaults)
- **Returns:** a Mono emitting the `BulkWriteResult` (use `BulkWriteResult#getInsertedCount()` for the inserted count)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `entities` is null or empty or contains a null document, or if a document value cannot be converted from a Map, bean, or array of String name/value pairs
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if a bean accessor, BSON implementation, or codec throws while preparing the request before the publisher is returned
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or the document type has no usable BSON codec while the driver constructs the operation
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  BulkWriteOptions options = new BulkWriteOptions().ordered(false);
  userMapper.bulkInsert(userList, options)
      .subscribe(result -> System.out.println("Bulk inserted: " + result.getInsertedCount()));
  ```
##### bulkWrite(...) -> Mono<BulkWriteResult>
- **Signature:** `public Mono<BulkWriteResult> bulkWrite(final List<? extends WriteModel<? extends Document>> requests) throws IllegalArgumentException, UnsupportedOperationException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException`
- **Summary:** Executes multiple write operations in a single bulk request.
- **Contract:**
  - This method provides maximum flexibility for complex bulk operations and ensures optimal performance when multiple different operations need to be executed.
  - Usage Examples: After subscription, the returned publisher signals a `MongoException` if the MongoDB write command fails.
- **Parameters:**
  - `requests` (`List<? extends WriteModel<? extends Document>>`) — list of write operations to execute (must not be null or empty)
- **Returns:** a Mono emitting BulkWriteResult with detailed operation statistics
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `requests` is null or empty, or if it contains a null element
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if `requests` contains a WriteModel subtype that the MongoDB driver does not support
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or the document type has no usable BSON codec while the driver constructs the operation
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Typical: mixed insert/update/delete in one round-trip; result.getModifiedCount() is one of
  // several per-type counts.
  List<WriteModel<Document>> operations = Arrays.asList(
      new InsertOneModel<>(doc1),
      new UpdateOneModel<>(filter, update),
      new DeleteOneModel<>(deleteFilter));
  userMapper.bulkWrite(operations).subscribe(result ->
      System.out.println("Modified: " + result.getModifiedCount()));   // emits one BulkWriteResult

  // Edge: cold publisher — building it writes nothing until subscribed.
  Mono<BulkWriteResult> pending = userMapper.bulkWrite(operations);   // nothing written yet

  // Negative: a null or empty request list -> IllegalArgumentException.
  userMapper.bulkWrite(Collections.emptyList());   // throws IllegalArgumentException

  // Negative: a failing operation (e.g. duplicate _id on insert) -> onError(MongoBulkWriteException).
  userMapper.bulkWrite(operationsWithConflict)
      .subscribe(r -> {}, err -> System.err.println("Bulk write failed: " + err));   // onError(MongoBulkWriteException)
  ```
- **Signature:** `public Mono<BulkWriteResult> bulkWrite(final List<? extends WriteModel<? extends Document>> requests, final BulkWriteOptions options) throws IllegalArgumentException, UnsupportedOperationException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException`
- **Summary:** Executes bulk write operations with custom options.
- **Contract:**
  - Usage Examples: After subscription, the returned publisher signals a `MongoException` if the MongoDB write command fails.
- **Parameters:**
  - `requests` (`List<? extends WriteModel<? extends Document>>`) — list of write operations to execute
  - `options` (`BulkWriteOptions`) — configuration for the bulk write behavior (may be null to use defaults)
- **Returns:** a Mono emitting BulkWriteResult with operation statistics
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `requests` is null or empty, or if it contains a null element
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if `requests` contains a WriteModel subtype that the MongoDB driver does not support
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or the document type has no usable BSON codec while the driver constructs the operation
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  BulkWriteOptions options = new BulkWriteOptions()
      .ordered(true)
      .bypassDocumentValidation(false);
  userMapper.bulkWrite(operations, options).subscribe(result ->
      System.out.println("Bulk write completed: " + result));
  ```
##### findOneAndUpdate(...) -> Mono<T>
- **Signature:** `public Mono<T> findOneAndUpdate(final Bson filter, final T update) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException`
- **Summary:** Atomically finds and updates a single document, returning it as the mapper's entity type.
- **Contract:**
  - present semantics: on subscription, the returned `Mono` emits the matched document decoded as `T` and then completes, or completes empty when no document matches the filter (no update is performed in that case).
  - Usage Examples: After subscription, the returned publisher signals a `MongoException` if the MongoDB write command fails.
- **Parameters:**
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — the query filter to identify the document to update
  - `update` (`T`) — the entity containing update values
- **Returns:** a `Mono` that emits the matched document (before update) decoded as `T`, or completes empty when no document matches
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null, or if `update` is null, or if an update document has a null field name, mixes operator and ordinary field names, or has no updatable fields after removing `_id`, or if an update value cannot be converted from a Map, bean, or array of String name/value pairs
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if a bean accessor, BSON implementation, or codec throws while preparing the request before the publisher is returned
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or the document type has no usable BSON codec while the driver constructs the operation
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Typical: match -> emits the PRE-update document (default returnDocument is BEFORE).
  User updatedUser = new User();
  updatedUser.setStatus("active");
  userMapper.findOneAndUpdate(Filters.eq("_id", userId), updatedUser)
      .subscribe(user -> System.out.println("Old status was: " + user.getStatus()));   // emits doc before update

  // Edge: no match -> Mono completes EMPTY and NO update is performed.
  userMapper.findOneAndUpdate(Filters.eq("_id", "missing"), updatedUser)
      .hasElement().subscribe(present -> System.out.println("updated? " + present));   // emits false

  // Edge: cold publisher — building it performs no update until subscribed.
  Mono<User> pending = userMapper.findOneAndUpdate(Filters.eq("_id", userId), updatedUser);   // nothing written yet

  // Negative: a null filter throws IllegalArgumentException synchronously (at the call site,
  // before any Mono is returned), because filter is validated eagerly.
  userMapper.findOneAndUpdate((Bson) null, updatedUser);   // throws IllegalArgumentException
  ```
- **See also:** `MongoCollectionExecutor#findOneAndUpdate(Bson, Object, Class)`
- **Signature:** `public Mono<T> findOneAndUpdate(final Bson filter, final T update, final FindOneAndUpdateOptions options) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException`
- **Summary:** Atomically finds and updates a document with custom options.
- **Contract:**
  - Usage Examples: After subscription, the returned publisher signals a `MongoException` if the MongoDB write command fails.
- **Parameters:**
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — the query filter to identify the document
  - `update` (`T`) — the entity containing update values
  - `options` (`FindOneAndUpdateOptions`) — configuration for the find-and-update operation (can be null to use defaults)
- **Returns:** a `Mono` that emits the matched document decoded as `T` — the pre- or post-write version per `options` — or completes empty when no document matches (an upsert with `ReturnDocument.AFTER` instead emits the newly inserted document)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null, or if `update` is null, or if an update document has a null field name, mixes operator and ordinary field names, or has no updatable fields after removing `_id`, or if an update value cannot be converted from a Map, bean, or array of String name/value pairs
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if a bean accessor, BSON implementation, or codec throws while preparing the request before the publisher is returned
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or the document type has no usable BSON codec while the driver constructs the operation
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  FindOneAndUpdateOptions options = new FindOneAndUpdateOptions()
      .returnDocument(ReturnDocument.AFTER)
      .upsert(true);
  userMapper.findOneAndUpdate(filter, update, options)
      .subscribe(user -> System.out.println("User after update: " + user));
  ```
- **Signature:** `public Mono<T> findOneAndUpdate(final Bson filter, final Collection<? extends T> objList) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException`
- **Summary:** Atomically finds and updates using multiple update objects.
- **Contract:**
  - This is useful when updates come from multiple sources or need to be aggregated from various entities.
  - When `T` is itself a `Bson` type such as `Document`, an element's values are not wrapped and are evaluated as aggregation expressions.
  - Usage Examples: After subscription, the returned publisher signals a `MongoException` if the MongoDB write command fails.
- **Parameters:**
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — the query filter to identify the document
  - `objList` (`Collection<? extends T>`) — collection of objects containing update values
- **Returns:** a `Mono` that emits the matched document (before update) decoded as `T`, or completes empty when no document matches
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null, or if `objList` is null or empty or contains a null element, or if an update document has a null field name, mixes operator and ordinary field names, or has no updatable fields after removing `_id`, or if an update value cannot be converted from a Map, bean, or array of String name/value pairs
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if a bean accessor, BSON implementation, or codec throws while preparing the request before the publisher is returned
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or the document type has no usable BSON codec while the driver constructs the operation
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<User> updates = Arrays.asList(statusUpdate, profileUpdate);
  userMapper.findOneAndUpdate(Filters.eq("_id", userId), updates)
      .subscribe(user -> System.out.println("Updated from multiple sources"));
  ```
- **Signature:** `public Mono<T> findOneAndUpdate(final Bson filter, final Collection<? extends T> objList, final FindOneAndUpdateOptions options) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException`
- **Summary:** Atomically finds and updates using multiple objects with options.
- **Contract:**
  - Usage Examples: After subscription, the returned publisher signals a `MongoException` if the MongoDB write command fails.
- **Parameters:**
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — the query filter to identify the document
  - `objList` (`Collection<? extends T>`) — collection of objects containing update values
  - `options` (`FindOneAndUpdateOptions`) — configuration for the operation (can be null to use defaults)
- **Returns:** a `Mono` that emits the matched document decoded as `T` — the pre- or post-write version per `options` — or completes empty when no document matches (an upsert with `ReturnDocument.AFTER` instead emits the newly inserted document)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null, or if `objList` is null or empty or contains a null element, or if an update document has a null field name, mixes operator and ordinary field names, or has no updatable fields after removing `_id`, or if an update value cannot be converted from a Map, bean, or array of String name/value pairs
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if a bean accessor, BSON implementation, or codec throws while preparing the request before the publisher is returned
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or the document type has no usable BSON codec while the driver constructs the operation
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  FindOneAndUpdateOptions options = new FindOneAndUpdateOptions().upsert(true);
  userMapper.findOneAndUpdate(filter, updatesList, options)
      .subscribe(user -> System.out.println("Merged updates applied"));
  ```
##### findOneAndReplace(...) -> Mono<T>
- **Signature:** `public Mono<T> findOneAndReplace(final Bson filter, final T replacement) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException`
- **Summary:** Atomically finds and replaces a single document, returning it as the mapper's entity type.
- **Contract:**
  - MongoDB retains the matched document's `_id` when the replacement omits it; a supplied value must equal the existing `_id`.
  - present semantics: on subscription, the returned `Mono` emits the matched document (before replacement) decoded as `T` and then completes, or completes empty when no document matches the filter and the operation is not configured to upsert.
  - Usage Examples: After subscription, the returned publisher signals a `MongoException` if the MongoDB write command fails.
- **Parameters:**
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — the query filter to identify the document to replace
  - `replacement` (`T`) — the complete replacement document
- **Returns:** a `Mono` that emits the matched document (before replacement) decoded as `T`, or completes empty when no document matches the filter
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null, or if `replacement` is null, or if a document value cannot be converted from a Map, bean, or array of String name/value pairs
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if a bean accessor, BSON implementation, or codec throws while preparing the request before the publisher is returned
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or the document type has no usable BSON codec while the driver constructs the operation
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Typical: match -> emits the PRE-replacement document (default returnDocument is BEFORE).
  User newUser = new User("John", "john@example.com", "active");
  userMapper.findOneAndReplace(Filters.eq("_id", userId), newUser)
      .subscribe(oldUser -> System.out.println("Replaced: " + oldUser.getName()));   // emits doc before replace

  // Edge: no match -> Mono completes EMPTY and nothing is replaced (without upsert).
  userMapper.findOneAndReplace(Filters.eq("_id", "missing"), newUser)
      .hasElement().subscribe(present -> System.out.println("replaced? " + present));   // emits false

  // Edge: cold publisher — building it performs no replace until subscribed.
  Mono<User> pending = userMapper.findOneAndReplace(Filters.eq("_id", userId), newUser);   // nothing written yet

  // Negative: a null filter throws IllegalArgumentException synchronously (at the call site,
  // before any Mono is returned), because filter is validated eagerly.
  userMapper.findOneAndReplace((Bson) null, newUser);   // throws IllegalArgumentException
  ```
- **See also:** `MongoCollectionExecutor#findOneAndReplace(Bson, Object, Class)`
- **Signature:** `public Mono<T> findOneAndReplace(final Bson filter, final T replacement, final FindOneAndReplaceOptions options) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException`
- **Summary:** Atomically finds and replaces a document with custom options.
- **Contract:**
  - Usage Examples: After subscription, the returned publisher signals a `MongoException` if the MongoDB write command fails.
- **Parameters:**
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — the query filter to identify the document
  - `replacement` (`T`) — the complete replacement document
  - `options` (`FindOneAndReplaceOptions`) — configuration for the replace operation (can be null to use defaults)
- **Returns:** a `Mono` that emits the matched document decoded as `T` — the pre- or post-write version per `options` — or completes empty when no document matches (an upsert with `ReturnDocument.AFTER` instead emits the newly inserted document)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null, or if `replacement` is null, or if a document value cannot be converted from a Map, bean, or array of String name/value pairs
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if a bean accessor, BSON implementation, or codec throws while preparing the request before the publisher is returned
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or the document type has no usable BSON codec while the driver constructs the operation
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  FindOneAndReplaceOptions options = new FindOneAndReplaceOptions()
      .returnDocument(ReturnDocument.AFTER)
      .upsert(true);
  userMapper.findOneAndReplace(filter, replacement, options)
      .subscribe(user -> System.out.println("New document: " + user));
  ```
##### findOneAndDelete(...) -> Mono<T>
- **Signature:** `public Mono<T> findOneAndDelete(final Bson filter) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException`
- **Summary:** Atomically finds and deletes a single document, returning it as the mapper's entity type.
- **Contract:**
  - present semantics: on subscription, the returned `Mono` emits the just-deleted document decoded as `T` and then completes, or completes empty when no document matches the filter (nothing is deleted in that case).
  - Usage Examples: After subscription, the returned publisher signals a `MongoException` if the MongoDB write command fails.
- **Parameters:**
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — the query filter to identify the document to delete
- **Returns:** a `Mono` that emits the deleted document decoded as `T`, or completes empty when no document matches the filter
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or the document type has no usable BSON codec while the driver constructs the operation
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Typical: match -> emits the just-deleted document, then completes.
  userMapper.findOneAndDelete(Filters.eq("status", "deleted"))
      .subscribe(deletedUser -> System.out.println("Removed user: " + deletedUser.getName()));   // emits deleted doc

  // Edge: no match -> Mono completes EMPTY and nothing is deleted.
  userMapper.findOneAndDelete(Filters.eq("status", "no-such-status"))
      .hasElement().subscribe(present -> System.out.println("deleted? " + present));   // emits false

  // Edge: cold publisher — building it deletes nothing until subscribed.
  Mono<User> pending = userMapper.findOneAndDelete(Filters.eq("status", "deleted"));   // nothing deleted yet

  // Negative: a null filter is rejected with IllegalArgumentException, thrown synchronously
  // at the call site (before any Mono is built).
  userMapper.findOneAndDelete((Bson) null);   // throws IllegalArgumentException
  ```
- **See also:** `MongoCollectionExecutor#findOneAndDelete(Bson, Class)`
- **Signature:** `public Mono<T> findOneAndDelete(final Bson filter, final FindOneAndDeleteOptions options) throws IllegalArgumentException, CodecConfigurationException, IllegalStateException`
- **Summary:** Atomically finds and deletes a document with custom options.
- **Contract:**
  - Performs an atomic find-and-delete operation with additional control over the operation behavior, such as sort order for selecting which document to delete when multiple matches exist, and projection of returned fields.
  - Usage Examples: After subscription, the returned publisher signals a `MongoException` if the MongoDB write command fails.
- **Parameters:**
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — the query filter to identify the document
  - `options` (`FindOneAndDeleteOptions`) — configuration for the delete operation (can be null to use defaults)
- **Returns:** a `Mono` that emits the deleted document decoded as `T`, or completes empty when no document matches the filter
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is null
  - `org.bson.codecs.configuration.CodecConfigurationException` — if a request value or the document type has no usable BSON codec while the driver constructs the operation
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the `MongoClient` that owns the underlying collection has been closed
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  FindOneAndDeleteOptions options = new FindOneAndDeleteOptions()
      .sort(Sorts.ascending("createdAt"));
  userMapper.findOneAndDelete(filter, options)
      .subscribe(user -> System.out.println("Deleted oldest: " + user));
  ```
##### distinct(...) -> Flux<T>
- **Signature:** `public Flux<T> distinct(final String fieldName) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns distinct values of the specified field across the whole collection, each surfaced on an entity of the mapper's row type `T`.
- **Contract:**
  - Each distinct value is surfaced under `fieldName` on an entity of the mapped type, and is only readable if the entity declares a matching property.
  - Internally this runs a `$group`/`$project` aggregation pipeline (the same approach as `#groupBy(String)`), so scalar field values decode cleanly into `T` — unlike the driver's native `distinct(field, T.class)`, which throws `BsonInvalidOperationException` when `T` is a POJO and the field is scalar.
  - When `T` itself is a single-value type (such as `String`, or a BSON value class such as `Binary` or `Code`), the `$project` stage is omitted and each distinct value is emitted directly, converted to `T`; for such a `T` the `null` value shared by documents that lack the field is not emitted, because Reactive Streams forbids `null` elements.
  - Usage Examples: After subscription, the returned publisher signals a `MongoException` if the MongoDB aggregate command fails.
- **Parameters:**
  - `fieldName` (`String`) — the name of the field to get distinct values for
- **Returns:** a cold `Flux` that, on subscription, emits each distinct value of the field surfaced on an entity of type `T`, then completes; completes empty when the collection has no documents (documents that lack the field produce a single entity whose field value is `null`, except for a single-value `T`, which skips that `null` value)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `fieldName` is null, empty, or contains an empty path segment (such as `"a..b"`)
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Distinct "country" values across the whole collection, each surfaced on a T:
  userMapper.distinct("country")
      .collectList()
      .subscribe(countries -> System.out.println("Countries: " + countries));

  // For raw scalar values, use the executor directly with an explicit value class:
  userMapper.collectionExecutor().distinct("country", String.class)
      .collectList()
      .subscribe(countries -> System.out.println("Countries: " + countries));

  // Edge: an empty collection (no documents) -> Flux completes with ZERO emissions.
  userMapper.distinct("country").count().subscribe(n -> System.out.println("distinct: " + n));   // emits 0 if empty

  // Edge: cold publisher — building it issues no query until subscribed.
  Flux<User> notRunYet = userMapper.distinct("country");   // nothing executed yet

  // Negative: a null fieldName is rejected with IllegalArgumentException.
  userMapper.distinct((String) null);   // throws IllegalArgumentException
  ```
- **See also:** `#distinct(String, Bson)`, `#groupBy(String)`, `MongoCollectionExecutor#distinct(String, Class)`
- **Signature:** `public Flux<T> distinct(final String fieldName, final Bson filter) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns distinct values of the specified field among documents matching the filter, each surfaced on an entity of the mapper's row type `T`.
- **Contract:**
  - Usage Examples: After subscription, the returned publisher signals a `MongoException` if the MongoDB aggregate command fails.
- **Parameters:**
  - `fieldName` (`String`) — the name of the field to get distinct values for
  - `filter` (`Bson`) — the query filter to apply before extracting distinct values (must not be null)
- **Returns:** a cold `Flux` that, on subscription, emits each distinct value of the field (among matching documents) surfaced on an entity of type `T`, then completes; completes empty when no distinct values are found
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `fieldName` is null, empty, or contains an empty path segment (such as `"a..b"`), or if `filter` is null
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Bson filter = Filters.eq("status", "active");
  // Distinct "department" values among active users, each surfaced on a T:
  userMapper.distinct("department", filter)
      .collectList()
      .subscribe(depts -> System.out.println("Active departments: " + depts));

  // For raw scalar values, use the executor directly with an explicit value class:
  userMapper.collectionExecutor().distinct("department", filter, String.class)
      .collectList()
      .subscribe(depts -> System.out.println("Active departments: " + depts));
  ```
- **See also:** `#distinct(String)`, `MongoCollectionExecutor#distinct(String, Bson, Class)`
##### aggregate(...) -> Flux<T>
- **Signature:** `public Flux<T> aggregate(final List<? extends Bson> pipeline) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Executes an aggregation pipeline on the collection, decoding each output document as the mapper's row type `T`.
- **Contract:**
  - Usage Examples: After subscription, the returned publisher signals a `MongoException` if the MongoDB aggregate command fails.
- **Parameters:**
  - `pipeline` (`List<? extends Bson>`) — list of aggregation stages to execute in order; the pipeline itself may be empty (which returns every document)
- **Returns:** a cold `Flux` that, on subscription, emits each output document decoded as `T` (one per emission, honouring downstream demand), then completes; completes empty if the pipeline produces no documents
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `pipeline` is null
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Typical: match then group; each output document is decoded as T.
  List<Bson> pipeline = Arrays.asList(
      Aggregates.match(Filters.gte("age", 18)),
      Aggregates.group("$country", Accumulators.sum("count", 1)));
  userMapper.aggregate(pipeline)
      .subscribe(result -> System.out.println("Aggregation result: " + result));   // one emission per group

  // Edge: an empty pipeline returns every document (no transformation).
  Flux<User> all = userMapper.aggregate(Collections.emptyList());   // emits each document as a User

  // Edge: a pipeline that matches nothing -> Flux completes with ZERO emissions.
  userMapper.aggregate(Arrays.asList(Aggregates.match(Filters.gte("age", 1000))))
      .count().subscribe(n -> System.out.println("groups: " + n));   // emits 0

  // Negative: the pipeline is validated eagerly, so a null pipeline throws
  // IllegalArgumentException synchronously at the call site (before any Flux is returned).
  userMapper.aggregate((List<Bson>) null);   // throws IllegalArgumentException
  ```
##### groupBy(...) -> Flux<T>
- **Signature:** `@Beta public Flux<T> groupBy(final String fieldName) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Annotations:** @Beta
- **Summary:** Groups documents by a single field (Beta feature).
- **Contract:**
  - This omission also applies when the mapper was created with a primitive class token such as `int.class`; the null-key group does not produce a primitive default.
  - Usage Examples: After subscription, the returned publisher signals a `MongoException` if the MongoDB aggregate command fails.
- **Parameters:**
  - `fieldName` (`String`) — the field name to group documents by; a dotted path such as `"a.b"` groups by the nested field, and each segment must be nonempty
- **Returns:** a cold `Flux` that, on subscription, emits each group result decoded as `T` (one per emission, honouring downstream demand), then completes
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `fieldName` is null, empty, or contains an empty path segment (such as `"a..b"`)
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Typical: one emission per distinct department value.
  userMapper.groupBy("department")
      .collectList()
      .subscribe(groups -> System.out.println("Grouped by department: " + groups));   // one group per department

  // Edge: an empty collection -> Flux completes with ZERO emissions.
  userMapper.groupBy("department").count().subscribe(n -> System.out.println("groups: " + n));   // emits 0 if empty

  // Edge: cold publisher — building it issues no aggregation until subscribed.
  Flux<User> notRunYet = userMapper.groupBy("department");   // nothing executed yet

  // Negative: a database/pipeline failure is delivered through onError, never thrown to the subscriber.
  userMapper.groupBy("department")
      .onErrorResume(err -> { System.err.println("group failed: " + err); return Flux.empty(); })
      .subscribe(g -> handleGroup(g));   // errors routed to onErrorResume
  ```
- **Signature:** `@Beta public Flux<T> groupBy(final Collection<String> fieldNames) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Annotations:** @Beta
- **Summary:** Groups documents by multiple fields (Beta feature).
- **Contract:**
  - In the result that field is present with the value `null` — inside `_id` when `T` is `Document`, otherwise as a field or property of the row — and a dotted path such as `"a.b"` appears as the nested document `{a: {b: <value>}}`.
  - If `fieldNames` contains only one distinct field and the mapper has a single-value row type, each group key is converted to that type.
  - Usage Examples: After subscription, the returned publisher signals a `MongoException` if the MongoDB aggregate command fails.
- **Parameters:**
  - `fieldNames` (`Collection<String>`) — collection of field names to compose the group key. Dotted paths produce nested key fields; paths must have nonempty segments, and no path may be an ancestor of another.
- **Returns:** a cold `Flux` that, on subscription, emits each group result decoded as `T` (one per emission, honouring downstream demand), then completes
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `fieldNames` is null or empty, contains a null path, an empty path segment or overlapping paths
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Typical: one emission per unique (country, department) combination.
  List<String> fields = Arrays.asList("country", "department");
  userMapper.groupBy(fields)
      .collectList()
      .subscribe(groups -> System.out.println("Multi-field groups: " + groups));   // one group per combo

  // Edge: an empty collection -> Flux completes with ZERO emissions.
  userMapper.groupBy(fields).count().subscribe(n -> System.out.println("groups: " + n));   // emits 0 if empty

  // Edge: cold publisher — building it issues no aggregation until subscribed.
  Flux<User> notRunYet = userMapper.groupBy(fields);   // nothing executed yet

  // Negative: a null or empty fieldNames collection -> IllegalArgumentException.
  userMapper.groupBy(Collections.emptyList());   // throws IllegalArgumentException
  ```
##### groupByAndCount(...) -> Flux<T>
- **Signature:** `@Beta public Flux<T> groupByAndCount(final String fieldName) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Annotations:** @Beta
- **Summary:** Groups documents by a field and counts frequency (Beta feature).
- **Contract:**
  - Equivalent to `#groupBy(String)` with a `$sum: 1` accumulator: each emitted document represents one group and carries the count of documents that fell into it under a `count` field (readable only if `T` declares a matching property).
  - Usage Examples: After subscription, the returned publisher signals a `MongoException` if the MongoDB aggregate command fails.
- **Parameters:**
  - `fieldName` (`String`) — the field name to group and count by; a dotted path such as `"a.b"` groups by the nested field, and each segment must be nonempty
- **Returns:** a cold `Flux` that, on subscription, emits each group-with-count result decoded as `T` (one per emission, honouring downstream demand), then completes
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `fieldName` is null, empty, or contains an empty path segment (such as `"a..b"`), or if `fieldName` is `"count"` or starts with `"count."`, and `T` is not `Document` (the group key conflicts with the count column)
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Typical: one emission per status, each carrying its document count.
  userMapper.groupByAndCount("status")
      .collectList()
      .subscribe(counts -> System.out.println("Status counts: " + counts));   // one entry per status

  // Edge: an empty collection -> Flux completes with ZERO emissions.
  userMapper.groupByAndCount("status").count().subscribe(n -> System.out.println("groups: " + n));   // emits 0

  // Edge: cold publisher — building it issues no aggregation until subscribed.
  Flux<User> notRunYet = userMapper.groupByAndCount("status");   // nothing executed yet

  // Edge: a database/pipeline failure is delivered through onError, never thrown synchronously.
  userMapper.groupByAndCount("status")
      .onErrorResume(err -> Flux.empty())
      .subscribe(g -> handleCount(g));   // errors routed to onErrorResume
  ```
- **Signature:** `@Beta public Flux<T> groupByAndCount(final Collection<String> fieldNames) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Annotations:** @Beta
- **Summary:** Groups documents by multiple fields with counts (Beta feature).
- **Contract:**
  - In the result that field is present with the value `null` — inside `_id` when `T` is `Document`, otherwise as a field or property of the row — and a dotted path such as `"a.b"` appears as the nested document `{a: {b: <value>}}`.
  - Usage Examples: After subscription, the returned publisher signals a `MongoException` if the MongoDB aggregate command fails.
- **Parameters:**
  - `fieldNames` (`Collection<String>`) — collection of field names to compose the group key. Dotted paths produce nested key fields; paths must have nonempty segments, and no path may be an ancestor of another.
- **Returns:** a cold `Flux` that, on subscription, emits each group-with-count result decoded as `T` (one per emission, honouring downstream demand), then completes
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `fieldNames` is null or empty, contains a null path, an empty path segment or overlapping paths, or if `fieldNames` contains `"count"` or a path starting with `"count."`, and `T` is not `Document` (the group key conflicts with the count column)
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Typical: one emission per unique (country, status) combination, each with its count.
  List<String> fields = Arrays.asList("country", "status");
  userMapper.groupByAndCount(fields)
      .collectList()
      .subscribe(counts -> System.out.println("Distribution: " + counts));   // one entry per combo

  // Edge: an empty collection -> Flux completes with ZERO emissions.
  userMapper.groupByAndCount(fields).count().subscribe(n -> System.out.println("groups: " + n));   // emits 0

  // Edge: cold publisher — building it issues no aggregation until subscribed.
  Flux<User> notRunYet = userMapper.groupByAndCount(fields);   // nothing executed yet

  // Negative: a null or empty fieldNames collection -> IllegalArgumentException.
  userMapper.groupByAndCount(Collections.emptyList());   // throws IllegalArgumentException
  ```
##### mapReduce(...) -> Flux<T>
- **Signature:** `@Deprecated public Flux<T> mapReduce(final String mapFunction, final String reduceFunction) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Executes a map-reduce operation on the collection, decoding each emitted result document as the mapper's row type `T`.
- **Deprecated:** yes — Map-reduce is deprecated in MongoDB 5.0+. Use `#aggregate(List)` with an aggregation pipeline instead.
- **Contract:**
  - Usage Examples: After subscription, the returned publisher signals a `MongoException` if the MongoDB map-reduce command fails.
- **Parameters:**
  - `mapFunction` (`String`) — the JavaScript map function; must not be null or empty
  - `reduceFunction` (`String`) — the JavaScript reduce function; must not be null or empty
- **Returns:** a `Flux` that, on subscription, emits each map-reduce output document decoded as `T`, then completes; completes empty when the operation produces no output
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `mapFunction` is null or empty, or if `reduceFunction` is null or empty
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Typical: classic count-by-category map-reduce; each output document decoded as T.
  String mapFunction = "function() { emit(this.category, 1); }";
  String reduceFunction = "function(key, values) { return Array.sum(values); }";
  userMapper.mapReduce(mapFunction, reduceFunction)
      .subscribe(result -> System.out.println("Map-reduce result: " + result));   // one emission per key

  // Edge: an empty collection -> Flux completes with ZERO emissions.
  userMapper.mapReduce(mapFunction, reduceFunction)
      .count().subscribe(n -> System.out.println("keys: " + n));   // emits 0 if empty

  // Edge: cold publisher — building it issues no map-reduce until subscribed.
  Flux<User> notRunYet = userMapper.mapReduce(mapFunction, reduceFunction);   // nothing executed yet

  // Negative: a null map function is rejected with IllegalArgumentException.
  userMapper.mapReduce((String) null, reduceFunction);   // throws IllegalArgumentException
  ```

### Class MongoDB (com.landawn.abacus.da.mongodb.reactivestreams.MongoDB)
Reactive MongoDB database executor providing reactive streams support for non-blocking database operations.

**Thread-safety:** thread-safe
**Nullability:** unspecified
**Extends:** `MongoDBBase`

#### Public Constructors
- `public MongoDB(final MongoDatabase mongoDB) throws IllegalArgumentException` — Constructs a reactive MongoDB executor with the specified reactive database instance.
  - **Throws:**
    - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `mongoDB` is `null`
  ```java
  MongoClient reactiveClient = MongoClients.create("mongodb://localhost:27017");
  com.mongodb.reactivestreams.client.MongoDatabase reactiveDb =
      reactiveClient.getDatabase("myapp");

  MongoDB reactiveMongoDB = new MongoDB(reactiveDb);          // non-null wrapper; wraps reactiveDb with the framework codec registry

  // Edge case - null database is rejected eagerly:
  new MongoDB(null);                                         // throws IllegalArgumentException: 'mongoDB' cannot be null
  ```

#### Public Static Methods
- (none)

#### Public Instance Methods
##### db(...) -> MongoDatabase
- **Signature:** `public MongoDatabase db()`
- **Summary:** Returns the underlying reactive MongoDB database instance for advanced operations.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the reactive MongoDB database instance
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  MongoDB reactiveMongoDB = new MongoDB(reactiveDatabase);

  MongoDatabase db = reactiveMongoDB.db();                   // returns the codec-configured reactive MongoDatabase (never null)

  // Use reactive driver features directly (results are Reactive Streams Publishers, not abacus Stream):
  Publisher<String> collectionNames = db.listCollectionNames();  // a cold Publisher; no I/O until subscribed

  // Repeated calls return the same wrapped instance:
  boolean same = (db == reactiveMongoDB.db());              // returns true
  ```
- **See also:** `com.mongodb.reactivestreams.client.MongoDatabase`
##### collection(...) -> varies by overload
- **Signature:** `public MongoCollection<Document> collection(final String collectionName) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns a reactive MongoDB collection for `Document` values.
- **Parameters:**
  - `collectionName` (`String`) — the name of the MongoDB collection to retrieve
- **Returns:** a reactive MongoCollection configured for Document operations
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if collectionName is null or empty
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  MongoDB reactiveMongoDB = new MongoDB(reactiveDatabase);

  MongoCollection<Document> userCollection = reactiveMongoDB.collection("users");  // returns a reactive MongoCollection<Document> (never null)
  Publisher<Document> findPublisher = userCollection.find();                       // a cold Publisher; no query runs until subscribed

  // Process with reactive streams (a Reactive Streams Publisher, not abacus Stream):
  Flux.from(findPublisher)
      .subscribe(doc -> System.out.println(doc.toJson()));

  // The name need not pre-exist: MongoDB creates the collection lazily on first write.
  MongoCollection<Document> brandNew = reactiveMongoDB.collection("not_yet_created");  // returns a handle; no server round-trip here

  // The collection name is validated up front, consistent with collectionExecutor(String):
  reactiveMongoDB.collection((String) null);                                       // throws IllegalArgumentException ("collectionName")
  ```
- **See also:** `Document`, `com.mongodb.reactivestreams.client.MongoCollection`
- **Signature:** `public <T> MongoCollection<T> collection(final String collectionName, final Class<T> rowType) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns a reactive MongoDB collection configured for a specific Java type with automatic POJO mapping.
- **Parameters:**
  - `collectionName` (`String`) — the name of the MongoDB collection to retrieve
  - `rowType` (`Class<T>`) — the Class object representing the document type
- **Returns:** a reactive MongoCollection configured for the specified type
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if collectionName is null or empty, or rowType is null
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  MongoDB reactiveMongoDB = new MongoDB(reactiveDatabase);

  MongoCollection<User> userCollection = reactiveMongoDB.collection("users", User.class);  // returns a reactive MongoCollection<User> (never null)
  Publisher<User> userPublisher = userCollection.find();                                   // a cold Publisher; decoding uses the codec registry on subscription

  // Type-safe reactive processing (a Reactive Streams Publisher, not abacus Stream):
  Flux.from(userPublisher)
      .filter(User::isActive)
      .map(User::getName)
      .subscribe(System.out::println);

  // Document.class is also valid and yields the same untyped view as collection(name):
  MongoCollection<Document> raw = reactiveMongoDB.collection("users", Document.class);     // returns a Document-typed reactive collection

  // Both arguments are validated up front, consistent with collectionMapper(String, Class):
  reactiveMongoDB.collection(null, User.class);                                           // throws IllegalArgumentException ("collectionName")
  reactiveMongoDB.collection("users", (Class<User>) null);                                // throws IllegalArgumentException ("rowType")
  ```
- **See also:** `com.mongodb.reactivestreams.client.MongoCollection`
##### collectionExecutor(...) -> MongoCollectionExecutor
- **Signature:** `public MongoCollectionExecutor collectionExecutor(final String collectionName) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates a reactive MongoCollectionExecutor for performing Publisher-based operations on the specified collection.
- **Parameters:**
  - `collectionName` (`String`) — the name of the MongoDB collection
- **Returns:** a reactive MongoCollectionExecutor for the specified collection
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if collectionName is null or empty
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  MongoDB reactiveMongoDB = new MongoDB(reactiveDatabase);

  MongoCollectionExecutor executor = reactiveMongoDB.collectionExecutor("users");  // returns a new executor wrapping the "users" collection (never null)

  // Reactive operations return Reactive Streams Publishers (Flux/Mono), not abacus Stream:
  Flux<Document> findPublisher = Flux.from(executor.list(Filters.eq("status", "active")));    // cold Flux; query runs on subscription
  Mono<InsertOneResult> insertPublisher = Mono.from(executor.insertOne(newUser));             // cold Mono; insert runs on subscription

  // Chain reactive operations:
  executor.list(Filters.eq("priority", "high"))
      .take(10)
      .subscribe(doc -> processHighPriorityItem(doc));

  // Each call returns a distinct executor instance (no pooling):
  boolean shared = (executor == reactiveMongoDB.collectionExecutor("users"));      // returns false

  // Edge case - null name is rejected eagerly:
  reactiveMongoDB.collectionExecutor((String) null);                               // throws IllegalArgumentException: 'collectionName' cannot be null or empty
  ```
- **See also:** `MongoCollectionExecutor`, `org.reactivestreams.Publisher`
- **Signature:** `public MongoCollectionExecutor collectionExecutor(final MongoCollection<Document> collection) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates a reactive MongoCollectionExecutor for performing Publisher-based operations on the provided collection instance.
- **Contract:**
  - This overload allows you to pass a pre-configured reactive MongoCollection instance, which is useful when you need specific collection-level configurations like read preferences, write concerns, or custom codec registries while maintaining reactive capabilities.
  - The driver encodes such a value only when the write runs, so the exception is signalled through the write's publisher on subscription, not thrown when the publisher is built.
- **Parameters:**
  - `collection` (`MongoCollection<Document>`) — the reactive MongoDB collection instance to wrap
- **Returns:** a reactive MongoCollectionExecutor for the provided collection
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if collection is null
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  MongoDB reactiveMongoDB = new MongoDB(reactiveDatabase);
  MongoCollection<Document> customCollection = reactiveMongoDB.db()   // keeps the framework codec registry
      .getCollection("users")
      .withReadPreference(ReadPreference.secondaryPreferred());

  MongoCollectionExecutor executor = reactiveMongoDB.collectionExecutor(customCollection);  // returns a new executor wrapping the supplied collection (never null)

  // The provided collection is wrapped as-is, so its custom settings are preserved:
  boolean same = (executor.coll() == customCollection);                                    // returns true

  // All operations will use the custom collection settings; results are Reactive Streams Publishers:
  Publisher<Long> countPublisher = executor.count();                                       // a cold Publisher; counts on subscription

  // Edge case - null collection is rejected eagerly:
  reactiveMongoDB.collectionExecutor((MongoCollection<Document>) null);                    // throws IllegalArgumentException: 'collection' cannot be null
  ```
- **See also:** `MongoCollectionExecutor`, `com.mongodb.reactivestreams.client.MongoCollection`
##### collectionMapper(...) -> MongoCollectionMapper<T>
- **Signature:** `public <T> MongoCollectionMapper<T> collectionMapper(final Class<T> rowType) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates a reactive MongoCollectionMapper for object-document mapping with automatic collection naming.
- **Parameters:**
  - `rowType` (`Class<T>`) — the Class object representing the entity type
- **Returns:** a reactive MongoCollectionMapper for the specified entity type
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if rowType is null, or if rowType has an empty simple name (for example, an anonymous class), because the derived collection name must not be empty
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  MongoDB reactiveMongoDB = new MongoDB(reactiveDatabase);

  MongoCollectionMapper<User> userMapper = reactiveMongoDB.collectionMapper(User.class);  // returns a mapper bound to the "User" collection (simple class name)

  // Reactive operations return a Reactive Streams Publisher (Flux/Mono), not abacus Stream:
  Flux<User> userFlux = Flux.from(userMapper.list(Filters.eq("active", true)));            // cold Flux; query runs on subscription
  userFlux
      .doOnNext(user -> System.out.println("Active user: " + user.getName()))
      .subscribe();

  // The collection name is derived from the SIMPLE class name, not the fully-qualified name:
  MongoCollectionMapper<Order> orderMapper = reactiveMongoDB.collectionMapper(Order.class);  // uses "Order", not "com.example.Order"

  // Edge case - null rowType is rejected eagerly, consistent with collectionMapper(String, Class):
  reactiveMongoDB.collectionMapper((Class<User>) null);                                  // throws IllegalArgumentException ("rowType")
  ```
- **See also:** `MongoCollectionMapper`, `org.reactivestreams.Publisher`
- **Signature:** `@SuppressWarnings("rawtypes") public <T> MongoCollectionMapper<T> collectionMapper(final String collectionName, final Class<T> rowType) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates a reactive MongoCollectionMapper for the specified collection and entity type.
- **Parameters:**
  - `collectionName` (`String`) — the name of the MongoDB collection to map
  - `rowType` (`Class<T>`) — the Class representing the entity type
- **Returns:** a reactive MongoCollectionMapper configured for the specified type and collection
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if collectionName is null or empty, or rowType is null
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  MongoDB reactiveMongoDB = new MongoDB(reactiveDatabase);

  MongoCollectionMapper<User> userMapper = reactiveMongoDB.collectionMapper("users", User.class);  // returns a mapper bound to the "users" collection (never null)

  // Reactive type-safe operations return Reactive Streams Publishers (Flux/Mono), not abacus Stream:
  Flux<User> activeUsers = Flux.from(userMapper.list(Filters.eq("status", "active")));  // cold Flux; query runs on subscription
  Mono<InsertOneResult> insertResult = Mono.from(userMapper.insertOne(newUser));        // cold Mono; insert runs on subscription

  // Process with backpressure:
  activeUsers
      .buffer(100)  // Process in batches
      .subscribe(batch -> processBatch(batch));

  // Edge case - null collection name is rejected eagerly:
  reactiveMongoDB.collectionMapper((String) null, User.class);                        // throws IllegalArgumentException: 'collectionName' cannot be null or empty

  // Edge case - null rowType is rejected eagerly:
  reactiveMongoDB.collectionMapper("users", (Class<User>) null);                      // throws IllegalArgumentException: 'rowType' cannot be null
  ```
- **See also:** `MongoCollectionMapper`, `org.reactivestreams.Publisher`, `#collectionMapper(Class)`
- **Signature:** `@SuppressWarnings("rawtypes") public <T> MongoCollectionMapper<T> collectionMapper(final MongoCollection<Document> collection, final Class<T> rowType) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates a reactive MongoCollectionMapper for an existing reactive MongoCollection with custom configuration.
- **Contract:**
  - This method allows creation of a reactive mapper using a pre-configured reactive MongoCollection instance, which is useful when you need specific collection-level settings like custom read preferences, write concerns, or codec registries while maintaining reactive object-document mapping capabilities.
  - The driver encodes such a value only when the write runs, so the exception is signalled through the write's publisher on subscription, not thrown when the publisher is built.
- **Parameters:**
  - `collection` (`MongoCollection<Document>`) — the pre-configured reactive MongoDB collection instance
  - `rowType` (`Class<T>`) — the Class representing the entity type for mapping
- **Returns:** a reactive MongoCollectionMapper for the provided collection and type
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if collection or rowType is null
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  MongoDB reactiveMongoDB = new MongoDB(reactiveDatabase);
  MongoCollection<Document> customCollection = reactiveMongoDB.db()   // keeps the framework codec registry
      .getCollection("users")
      .withWriteConcern(WriteConcern.MAJORITY)
      .withReadPreference(ReadPreference.primaryPreferred());

  MongoCollectionMapper<User> mapper = reactiveMongoDB.collectionMapper(customCollection, User.class);  // returns a mapper wrapping the supplied collection (never null)

  // The provided collection is wrapped as-is, so its custom settings are preserved:
  boolean same = (mapper.collectionExecutor().coll() == customCollection);                            // returns true

  // All operations use custom collection settings; results are Reactive Streams Publishers, not abacus Stream:
  Flux<User> users = Flux.from(mapper.list(Filters.eq("department", "Engineering")));                  // cold Flux; query runs on subscription

  // Edge case - null collection is rejected eagerly:
  reactiveMongoDB.collectionMapper((MongoCollection<Document>) null, User.class);                    // throws IllegalArgumentException: 'collection' cannot be null

  // Edge case - null rowType is rejected eagerly:
  reactiveMongoDB.collectionMapper(customCollection, (Class<User>) null);                            // throws IllegalArgumentException: 'rowType' cannot be null
  ```
- **See also:** `MongoCollectionMapper`, `com.mongodb.reactivestreams.client.MongoCollection`

## com.landawn.abacus.da.neo4j
### Class Neo4jExecutor (com.landawn.abacus.da.neo4j.Neo4jExecutor)
A thin executor that wraps the Neo4j OGM `Session` API, adding lightweight session pooling and `Stream`-based result handling on top of it.

**Thread-safety:** not thread-safe
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Public Constructors
- `public Neo4jExecutor(final SessionFactory sessionFactory) throws IllegalArgumentException` — Constructs a `Neo4jExecutor` that borrows sessions from the supplied `SessionFactory`.
  - **Throws:**
    - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `sessionFactory` is `null`
  ```java
  Configuration configuration = new Configuration.Builder()
          .uri("bolt://localhost")
          .credentials("neo4j", "password")
          .build();
  SessionFactory factory = new SessionFactory(configuration, "com.example.model");
  Neo4jExecutor executor = new Neo4jExecutor(factory);   // ready to use; no session opened yet
  assert executor.sessionFactory() == factory;           // factory is retained

  // A pre-built factory can be shared by many executors
  Neo4jExecutor reader = new Neo4jExecutor(factory);

  // Passing null is rejected immediately
  Neo4jExecutor bad = new Neo4jExecutor(null);           // throws IllegalArgumentException
  ```

#### Public Static Methods
- (none)

#### Public Instance Methods
##### sessionFactory(...) -> SessionFactory
- **Signature:** `public SessionFactory sessionFactory()`
- **Summary:** Returns the `SessionFactory` this executor was constructed with.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the `SessionFactory` supplied at construction time; never `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Configuration configuration = new Configuration.Builder()
          .uri("bolt://localhost")
          .credentials("neo4j", "password")
          .build();
  SessionFactory factory = new SessionFactory(configuration, "com.example.model");
  Neo4jExecutor executor = new Neo4jExecutor(factory);

  SessionFactory same = executor.sessionFactory();   // returns the exact instance passed in
  assert same == factory;                            // true

  // Open an unpooled session straight from the factory for OGM-only features
  Session adHoc = executor.sessionFactory().openSession();   // never null
  ```
- **See also:** `org.neo4j.ogm.session.SessionFactory`
##### openSession(...) -> Session
- **Signature:** `public Session openSession()`
- **Summary:** Opens a new `Session` directly via the underlying `SessionFactory`.
- **Contract:**
  - The OGM `Session` does not expose a `close()` method; `Session#clear()` releases the session's mapping context (the accumulated identity map of loaded entities) when the session is kept, except Neo4j-OGM's cache of graph IDs by primary-index value, so prefer short-lived sessions.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** a fresh, unpooled OGM `Session`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Open a session for manual management
  Session session = executor.openSession();
  try {
      Person person = session.load(Person.class, 123L);
      person.setName("Updated Name");
      session.save(person);
  } finally {
      // Release the session's mapping context (no close() to call)
      session.clear();
  }

  // Prefer using run() or call() for automatic session management
  executor.run(session -> {
      Person person = session.load(Person.class, 123L);
      person.setName("Updated Name");
      session.save(person);
  });
  ```
- **See also:** `org.neo4j.ogm.session.Session`, `#run(Consumer)`, `#call(Function)`
##### run(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `@Beta public void run(final Consumer<? super Session> action) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Annotations:** @Beta
- **Summary:** Borrows a pooled `Session`, hands it to `action`, and returns it to the pool when `action` completes (whether normally or exceptionally).
- **Contract:**
  - Use this for multi-statement work that needs to share a single session (for example, when opening an explicit transaction via `Session#beginTransaction()` so that several saves commit atomically).
  - The server sees no lock cycle (the blocked caller is the holder's own thread), so its deadlock detection does not end the wait: it lasts until a configured lock-acquisition or transaction timeout ends it, and indefinitely when none is configured (Neo4j's default).
- **Parameters:**
  - `action` (`Consumer<? super Session>`) — the callback invoked with the pooled session; must not be `null`
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `action` is `null`
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if `action` throws while using the borrowed session
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Execute operations without return value
  executor.run(session -> {
      Person person = session.load(Person.class, 123L);
      person.setName("John Doe");
      session.save(person);
  });

  // Multi-statement transaction
  Person personA = new Person("Alice", 30);
  Person personB = new Person("Bob", 32);
  executor.run(session -> {
      try (org.neo4j.ogm.transaction.Transaction tx = session.beginTransaction()) {
          session.save(personA);
          session.save(personB);
          tx.commit();
      }
  });
  ```
- **See also:** `#call(Function)`
##### call(...) -> T
- **Signature:** `@Beta public <T> T call(final Function<? super Session, ? extends T> action) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Annotations:** @Beta
- **Summary:** Borrows a pooled `Session`, applies `action` to it, returns the result, and releases the session back to the pool when `action` completes (whether normally or exceptionally).
- **Contract:**
  - Important: `action` must not return or otherwise retain the `Session` itself because it is cleared (see `Session#clear()`) and returned to the pool when this method completes.
  - Entity objects may be returned, but they are detached from that cleared session and subsequent persistence work must use another executor operation or session.
- **Parameters:**
  - `action` (`Function<? super Session, ? extends T>`) — the function invoked with the pooled session; must not be `null`
- **Returns:** the value produced by `action`
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `action` is `null`
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if `action` throws while using the borrowed session
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Execute and return a result
  Person person = executor.call(session -> session.load(Person.class, 123L));

  // Load and transform data inside the callback so nothing escapes the session
  List<String> names = executor.call(session ->
      session.loadAll(Person.class).stream()
          .map(Person::getName)
          .toList());
  ```
- **See also:** `#run(Consumer)`
##### load(...) -> T
- **Signature:** `public <T> T load(final Class<T> targetClass, final Serializable id) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Loads a single mapped entity by its OGM identifier using the default load depth.
- **Parameters:**
  - `targetClass` (`Class<T>`) — the OGM-mapped class to load
  - `id` (`Serializable`) — the configured primary-index value, or a native graph ID for an entity class without a primary index
- **Returns:** the loaded entity, or `null` if no node with that ID exists
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetClass` or `id` is `null`; also thrown by Neo4j-OGM if `targetClass` is not a managed entity class, or if the type of `id` does not match the class's primary index (or is not a `Long` native graph ID for a class without a primary index)
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if OGM cannot map the requested entities or identifiers, the database cannot be reached, or Neo4j rejects the load query
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Person person = executor.load(Person.class, 123L);
  if (person != null) {
      System.out.println("Person: " + person.getName());
  }
  ```
- **See also:** `#load(Class, Serializable, int)`, `#loadAll(Class, Collection)`
- **Signature:** `public <T> T load(final Class<T> targetClass, final Serializable id, final int depth) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Loads a single mapped entity by its OGM identifier, populating related entities to the given depth.
- **Contract:**
  - `depth == 0` loads only the node's scalar properties; `depth == 1` loads it together with immediate relationships; larger depths recurse further; `-1` loads the entire connected sub-graph reachable from this node and should be used with care on large graphs.
- **Parameters:**
  - `targetClass` (`Class<T>`) — the OGM-mapped class to load
  - `id` (`Serializable`) — the configured primary-index value, or a native graph ID for an entity class without a primary index
  - `depth` (`int`) — the depth of relationships to traverse: `0` for the node only, a positive integer for that many hops, or `-1` for unlimited (node-entity classes only)
- **Returns:** the loaded entity, or `null` if no node with that ID exists
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetClass` or `id` is `null`; also thrown by Neo4j-OGM if `targetClass` is not a managed entity class, if the type of `id` does not match the class's primary index (or is not a `Long` native graph ID for a class without a primary index), or if `depth` is negative for a relationship-entity class
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if OGM cannot map the requested entities or identifiers, the database cannot be reached, or Neo4j rejects the load query
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Person personOnly = executor.load(Person.class, 123L, 0);   // properties only
  Person withCompany = executor.load(Person.class, 123L, 1);  // immediate relationships
  Person fullGraph = executor.load(Person.class, 123L, -1);   // full reachable sub-graph
  ```
- **See also:** `#load(Class, Serializable)`, `#loadAll(Class, Collection, int)`
##### loadAll(...) -> Collection<T>
- **Signature:** `public <T> Collection<T> loadAll(final Class<T> targetClass, final Collection<? extends Serializable> ids) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Loads multiple mapped entities from Neo4j by their identifiers.
- **Parameters:**
  - `targetClass` (`Class<T>`) — the class representing the node type
  - `ids` (`Collection<? extends Serializable>`) — primary-index values, or native graph IDs for a class without a primary index, each of the ID field's Java type: an ID of another type (such as an `Integer` for a `Long` ID) never matches, so its entity is silently missing from the result (`#load(Class, Serializable)` rejects such an ID instead)
- **Returns:** collection of loaded node entities, or an empty collection if no nodes are found
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetClass` is `null`
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if OGM cannot map the requested entities or identifiers, the database cannot be reached, or Neo4j rejects the load query
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Collection<Person> people = executor.loadAll(Person.class, Arrays.asList(1L, 2L, 3L));
  // returns the matching Person nodes; IDs with no node are simply absent from the result

  for (Person p : executor.loadAll(Person.class, List.of(42L))) {
      System.out.println(p.getName());   // single-ID convenience
  }

  // Empty id collection -> empty result
  Collection<Person> none = executor.loadAll(Person.class, Collections.emptyList()); // returns empty collection

  // An unregistered/unmapped type yields an (immutable) empty collection rather than throwing
  Collection<Object> unmapped = executor.loadAll(Object.class, List.of(1L));          // returns empty collection
  ```
- **See also:** `#loadAll(Class, Collection, int)`, `#load(Class, Serializable)`
- **Signature:** `public <T> Collection<T> loadAll(final Class<T> targetClass, final Collection<? extends Serializable> ids, final int depth) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Loads multiple mapped entities from Neo4j by their identifiers with a specified relationship depth.
- **Parameters:**
  - `targetClass` (`Class<T>`) — the class representing the node type
  - `ids` (`Collection<? extends Serializable>`) — primary-index values, or native graph IDs for a class without a primary index, each of the ID field's Java type: an ID of another type (such as an `Integer` for a `Long` ID) never matches, so its entity is silently missing from the result (`#load(Class, Serializable)` rejects such an ID instead)
  - `depth` (`int`) — the depth of relationships to load (0 = node only, -1 = infinite for node-entity classes only)
- **Returns:** collection of loaded node entities with relationships, may be empty if no nodes found
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetClass` is `null`; also thrown by Neo4j-OGM if `depth` is negative for a relationship-entity class
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if OGM cannot map the requested entities or identifiers, the database cannot be reached, or Neo4j rejects the load query
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Collection<Long> ids = Arrays.asList(1L, 2L);
  Collection<Person> flat = executor.loadAll(Person.class, ids, 0);     // properties only, no relationships
  Collection<Person> withRels = executor.loadAll(Person.class, ids, 1); // each node plus immediate relationships

  // depth -1 pulls the entire reachable sub-graph for each node (use with care on large graphs)
  Collection<Person> deep = executor.loadAll(Person.class, ids, -1);

  // No matches -> empty collection
  Collection<Person> none = executor.loadAll(Person.class, Collections.emptyList(), 1); // returns empty collection
  ```
- **See also:** `#loadAll(Class, Collection)`, `#load(Class, Serializable, int)`
- **Signature:** `public <T> Collection<T> loadAll(final Class<T> targetClass, final Collection<? extends Serializable> ids, final SortOrder sortOrder) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Loads multiple mapped entities from Neo4j by their identifiers with a specified sort order.
- **Parameters:**
  - `targetClass` (`Class<T>`) — the class representing the node type
  - `ids` (`Collection<? extends Serializable>`) — primary-index values, or native graph IDs for a class without a primary index, each of the ID field's Java type: an ID of another type (such as an `Integer` for a `Long` ID) never matches, so its entity is silently missing from the result (`#load(Class, Serializable)` rejects such an ID instead)
  - `sortOrder` (`SortOrder`) — the sort order specification for results; must not be `null`
- **Returns:** collection of loaded node entities sorted as specified, may be empty if no nodes found
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetClass` is `null`
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if OGM cannot map the requested entities or identifiers, the database cannot be reached, or Neo4j rejects the load query
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Collection<Long> ids = Arrays.asList(1L, 2L, 3L);
  SortOrder byName = new SortOrder().add("name");
  Collection<Person> sorted = executor.loadAll(Person.class, ids, byName); // ordered by name ascending

  SortOrder byAgeDesc = new SortOrder(SortOrder.Direction.DESC, "age");
  Collection<Person> oldestFirst = executor.loadAll(Person.class, ids, byAgeDesc);

  // An empty SortOrder returns the matches in the iteration order of ids
  Collection<Person> inIdsOrder = executor.loadAll(Person.class, ids, new SortOrder());

  // No matching ids -> empty collection
  Collection<Person> none = executor.loadAll(Person.class, Collections.emptyList(), byName); // returns empty collection
  ```

  - `sortOrder` (`SortOrder`) — the sort order specification for results; must not be `null`
  - `depth` (`int`) — the depth of relationships to load (0 = node only, -1 = infinite for node-entity classes only)
- **Returns:** collection of loaded node entities with relationships, sorted as specified
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetClass` is `null`; also thrown by Neo4j-OGM if `depth` is negative for a relationship-entity class
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if OGM cannot map the requested entities or identifiers, the database cannot be reached, or Neo4j rejects the load query

  ```java
  SortOrder byName = new SortOrder().add("name");
  ```

- **Summary:** Loads multiple mapped entities from Neo4j by their identifiers with pagination.
- **Parameters:**
  - `targetClass` (`Class<T>`) — the class representing the node type
  - `ids` (`Collection<? extends Serializable>`) — primary-index values, or native graph IDs for a class without a primary index, each of the ID field's Java type: an ID of another type (such as an `Integer` for a `Long` ID) never matches, so its entity is silently missing from the result (`#load(Class, Serializable)` rejects such an ID instead)
  - `pagination` (`Pagination`) — pagination settings (page number and size, or an explicit offset); may be `null` for no pagination
- **Returns:** collection of loaded node entities for the specified page, may be empty
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetClass` is `null`
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if OGM cannot map the requested entities or identifiers, the database cannot be reached, or Neo4j rejects the load query
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Collection<Long> ids = Arrays.asList(1L, 2L, 3L, 4L, 5L);
  Pagination firstPage = new Pagination(0, 2);                               // page index 0, size 2

  Pagination secondPage = new Pagination(1, 2);    // page index 1, size 2
  ```

- **Signature:** `public <T> Collection<T> loadAll(final Collection<T> objects) throws RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Reloads a collection of existing node entities from Neo4j.
- **Contract:**
  - The entities must already have identifiers: an entity whose primary-index value (or native graph ID, for a class without a primary index) is `null` is skipped and is absent from the result.
- **Parameters:**
  - `objects` (`Collection<T>`) — collection of node entities to reload; may be `null` or empty, in which case it is returned unchanged without a database round-trip
- **Returns:** collection of reloaded node entities with current database state
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if OGM cannot map the requested entities or identifiers, the database cannot be reached, or Neo4j rejects the load query
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Collection<Person> stale = executor.loadAll(Person.class, Arrays.asList(1L, 2L));
  Collection<Person> fresh = executor.loadAll(stale);   // newly loaded results; stale is unchanged

  // A null collection is passed straight through and returned as-is
  Collection<Person> nil = executor.loadAll((Collection<Person>) null); // returns null

  // An empty collection is returned unchanged (the same empty instance, no DB round-trip)
  Collection<Person> empty = executor.loadAll(Collections.<Person> emptyList()); // returns empty collection
  ```
- **See also:** `#loadAll(Collection, int)`
- **Signature:** `public <T> Collection<T> loadAll(final Collection<T> objects, final int depth) throws RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Reloads a collection of existing node entities from Neo4j with specified relationship depth.
- **Parameters:**
  - `objects` (`Collection<T>`) — collection of node entities to reload; may be `null` or empty, in which case it is returned unchanged without a database round-trip
  - `depth` (`int`) — the depth of relationships to load (0 = node only, -1 = infinite for node-entity classes only)
- **Returns:** collection of reloaded node entities with relationships and current database state
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if OGM cannot map the requested entities or identifiers, the database cannot be reached, or Neo4j rejects the load query
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — thrown by Neo4j-OGM if `depth` is negative and `objects` is a non-empty collection of relationship entities
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Collection<Person> people = executor.loadAll(Person.class, Arrays.asList(1L, 2L));
  Collection<Person> withRels = executor.loadAll(people, 1);  // refreshed, with immediate relationships
  Collection<Person> deep = executor.loadAll(people, -1);     // refreshed, whole reachable sub-graph

  // null in, null out
  Collection<Person> nil = executor.loadAll((Collection<Person>) null, 1); // returns null

  // Empty in, same empty collection out
  Collection<Person> empty = executor.loadAll(Collections.<Person> emptyList(), 1); // returns empty collection
  ```

  - `pagination` (`Pagination`) — pagination settings (page number and size, or an explicit offset); may be `null` for no pagination
