- **Returns:** paginated collection of reloaded node entities with relationships
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if OGM cannot map the requested entities or identifiers, the database cannot be reached, or Neo4j rejects the load query
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — thrown by Neo4j-OGM if `depth` is negative and `objects` is a non-empty collection of relationship entities
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Collection<Person> people = executor.loadAll(Person.class, Arrays.asList(1L, 2L, 3L, 4L));

  Collection<Person> flat = executor.loadAll(people, page, 0);     // <=2 refreshed entities, properties only

  Collection<Person> nil = executor.loadAll((Collection<Person>) null, page, 1); // returns null

  Collection<Person> empty = executor.loadAll(Collections.<Person> emptyList(), page, 1); // returns empty collection
  ```

- **Signature:** `public <T> Collection<T> loadAll(final Class<T> targetClass) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Loads all nodes of the specified type from Neo4j.
- **Parameters:**
  - `targetClass` (`Class<T>`) — the class representing the node type to load
- **Returns:** collection of all nodes of the specified type, may be empty
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetClass` is `null`
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if OGM cannot map the requested entities or identifiers, the database cannot be reached, or Neo4j rejects the load query
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Collection<Person> everyone = executor.loadAll(Person.class);
  System.out.println("Total persons: " + everyone.size());

  for (Person p : executor.loadAll(Person.class)) {
      System.out.println(p.getName());
  }

  // A type with no stored nodes -> empty collection
  Collection<Company> noneYet = executor.loadAll(Company.class); // returns empty collection when none exist

  // An unregistered/unmapped type returns an (immutable) empty collection rather than throwing
  Collection<Object> unmapped = executor.loadAll(Object.class);  // returns empty collection
  ```
- **See also:** `#loadAll(Class, int)`, `#loadAll(Class, Pagination)`
- **Signature:** `public <T> Collection<T> loadAll(final Class<T> targetClass, final int depth) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Loads all nodes of the specified type from Neo4j with relationship depth.
- **Parameters:**
  - `targetClass` (`Class<T>`) — the class representing the node type to load
  - `depth` (`int`) — the depth of relationships to load (0 = node only, -1 = infinite for node-entity classes only)
- **Returns:** collection of all nodes of the specified type with relationships, may be empty
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetClass` is `null`; also thrown by Neo4j-OGM if `depth` is negative for a relationship-entity class
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if OGM cannot map the requested entities or identifiers, the database cannot be reached, or Neo4j rejects the load query
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Collection<Person> flat = executor.loadAll(Person.class, 0);     // every Person, properties only
  Collection<Person> withRels = executor.loadAll(Person.class, 1); // every Person plus immediate relationships
  Collection<Person> deep = executor.loadAll(Person.class, -1);    // entire reachable graph (use with care)

  // Unmapped type -> empty collection (no exception)
  Collection<Object> unmapped = executor.loadAll(Object.class, 1); // returns empty collection
  ```
- **See also:** `#loadAll(Class)`, `#loadAll(Class, Pagination, int)`

- **Signature:** `public <T> Collection<T> loadAll(final Class<T> targetClass, final Filter filter) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Loads nodes of the specified type from Neo4j that match the given filter criteria.
- **Parameters:**
  - `targetClass` (`Class<T>`) — the class representing the node type to load
  - `filter` (`Filter`) — the filter criteria to apply when loading nodes; must not be `null`. A copy of it is sent, so it is not modified, unless it cannot be copied faithfully (see "Filter Arguments" in the class documentation)
- **Returns:** collection of nodes matching the filter criteria, may be empty
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetClass` or `filter` is `null`
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if OGM cannot map the requested entities or identifiers, the database cannot be reached, or Neo4j rejects the load query
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Filter nameIsJohn = new Filter("name", ComparisonOperator.EQUALS, "John");
  Collection<Person> johns = executor.loadAll(Person.class, nameIsJohn); // every Person named "John"

  Filter adult = new Filter("age", ComparisonOperator.GREATER_THAN, 18);
  Collection<Person> adults = executor.loadAll(Person.class, adult);

  // A filter that matches nothing -> empty collection
  Filter impossible = new Filter("name", ComparisonOperator.EQUALS, " no-such-name");
  Collection<Person> none = executor.loadAll(Person.class, impossible); // returns empty collection
  ```
- **See also:** `#loadAll(Class, Filter, int)`, `org.neo4j.ogm.cypher.Filter`

- **Signature:** `public <T> Collection<T> loadAll(final Class<T> targetClass, final Filter filter, final SortOrder sortOrder, final Pagination pagination) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`

##### save(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `public void save(final Object object) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Persists an OGM-mapped entity, entity array, or entity `Iterable` to Neo4j using the session's default save depth.
- **Contract:**
  - Each call runs on a pooled session whose mapping context has been cleared, so OGM does not know the relationships an entity had when it was loaded by an earlier call: a relationship removed from such an entity (e.g.
- **Parameters:**
  - `object` (`Object`) — a mapped entity, an array of mapped entities, or an `Iterable` of mapped entities; must not be `null`. An element of an array or `Iterable` whose class is not mapped is not saved: it is skipped silently, or rejected with an `IllegalArgumentException` when event listeners are registered with the `SessionFactory`. A `null` element fails with a `NullPointerException`
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `object` is `null`; also thrown by Neo4j-OGM if `object` is neither an array nor an `Iterable` and is not an instance of a mapped entity class
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if OGM cannot map the supplied object, the database cannot be reached, or Neo4j rejects a write or constraint
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Create and save a new node
  Person person = new Person("John Doe", 30);
  executor.save(person);   // post-state: node persisted; person.getId() is now populated
  System.out.println("Saved with ID: " + person.getId());

  // Update an existing node together with its (potentially deep) relationships
  Person existing = executor.load(Person.class, 123L, 1);
  existing.setAge(31);
  executor.save(existing); // post-state: the matching node is updated in place
  ```
- **See also:** `#save(Object, int)`
- **Signature:** `public void save(final Object object, final int depth) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Persists an OGM-mapped entity, entity array, or entity `Iterable` to Neo4j, traversing related entities to the given depth.
- **Parameters:**
  - `object` (`Object`) — a mapped entity, an array of mapped entities, or an `Iterable` of mapped entities; must not be `null`. An element of an array or `Iterable` whose class is not mapped is not saved: it is skipped silently, or rejected with an `IllegalArgumentException` when event listeners are registered with the `SessionFactory`. A `null` element fails with a `NullPointerException`
  - `depth` (`int`) — the depth of related entities to traverse and persist: `0` for the node only, a positive integer for that many hops, or `-1` for unlimited
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `object` is `null`; also thrown by Neo4j-OGM if `object` is neither an array nor an `Iterable` and is not an instance of a mapped entity class
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if OGM cannot map the supplied object, the database cannot be reached, or Neo4j rejects a write or constraint
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Person person = new Person("John Doe");
  executor.save(person, 0);   // node only - no relationships written

  Person alice = new Person("Alice");
  Company company = new Company("Tech Corp");
  alice.worksFor(company);
  executor.save(alice, 1);    // alice and the WORKS_FOR -> company edge

  executor.save(alice, -1);    // entire reachable sub-graph (use with care)
  ```
- **See also:** `#save(Object)`
##### delete(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `public void delete(final Object object) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Deletes one or more OGM-managed entities from Neo4j.
- **Contract:**
  - The entity must carry a populated graph ID (i.e.
  - When the cleared pooled session cannot resolve the graph ID — for every entity of a class without a native graph-ID field (primary index only), and for an entity whose native graph-ID field is `null` but whose class also has a primary index — OGM first reloads the entity by its primary-index value (and logs a warning) before deleting it.
  - The deletes of an array or `Iterable` are not atomic: Neo4j-OGM deletes each entity in a transaction of its own, so when one of them fails, the entities before it stay deleted and those after it are not attempted.
  - Deleting an entity of a class without a native graph-ID field and then saving a new entity with the same primary-index value works across executor calls, but not inside one such session: Neo4j-OGM keeps the deleted node's graph ID for that value, so the session sends the save as an update of the deleted node, which writes nothing (or, if Neo4j has meanwhile reused that graph ID for another node, overwrites that node).
- **Parameters:**
  - `object` (`Object`) — a mapped entity, an array of mapped entities, or an `Iterable` of mapped entities to delete; must not be `null`. A `null` element of an array or `Iterable` fails with a `NullPointerException` before anything is deleted
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `object` is `null`; also thrown by Neo4j-OGM, before anything is deleted, if `object` (or one of its elements) is not an instance of a mapped entity class
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if OGM cannot resolve the objects to delete, the database cannot be reached, or Neo4j rejects the delete query
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Person person = executor.load(Person.class, 123L);
  if (person != null) {
      executor.delete(person);   // post-state: the node and its relationships are removed
  }

  Collection<Person> inactive = executor.loadAll(Person.class,
      new Filter("status", ComparisonOperator.EQUALS, "inactive"));
  executor.delete(inactive);   // every inactive Person node is removed (OGM sends one DELETE statement per entity)
  ```
- **See also:** `#deleteAll(Class)`
##### deleteAll(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `public void deleteAll(final Class<?> targetClass) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Deletes every entity of the supplied OGM-mapped class.
- **Contract:**
  - If `targetClass` is not a mapped entity class (or no label can be determined for it), Neo4j-OGM logs a warning and deletes nothing; no exception is thrown.
- **Parameters:**
  - `targetClass` (`Class<?>`) — the OGM-mapped entity class to delete
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetClass` is `null`
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if OGM cannot resolve the objects to delete, the database cannot be reached, or Neo4j rejects the delete query
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Remove every Person node (and its relationships) from the graph
  executor.deleteAll(Person.class);
  assert executor.count(Person.class) == 0; // post-state: no Person nodes remain

  // Typical teardown after a test run
  executor.deleteAll(Company.class);
  executor.deleteAll(Person.class);

  // Re-running on an already-empty type is harmless (still no-op deletes)
  executor.deleteAll(Person.class); // nothing left to delete
  ```
- **See also:** `#delete(Object)`
##### findOnly(...) -> Optional<T>
- **Signature:** `public <T> Optional<T> findOnly(final Class<T> targetClass, final String cypher, final Map<String, ?> parameters) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Executes a Cypher query and returns its single result mapped to `targetClass`, wrapped in an `Optional`.
- **Contract:**
  - The query must produce zero or one result; if it produces more, the underlying OGM session raises a `RuntimeException`.
  - Add a `LIMIT 1` clause or a uniqueness constraint to the Cypher when the query could otherwise produce several results.
- **Parameters:**
  - `targetClass` (`Class<T>`) — the target class — either a mapped OGM entity class or a basic value type (e.g. `Long.class` for an aggregate result); pass the wrapper class, not a primitive class such as `long.class`, with which every non-`null` result fails (and, for a numeric primitive class, a `null` value too, because it is read as zero)
  - `cypher` (`String`) — the Cypher query string with `$name` parameter placeholders; must not be `null` or empty
  - `parameters` (`Map<String, ?>`) — named parameters bound by the OGM session; may be empty but must not be `null`
- **Returns:** an `Optional` describing the single mapped result, or an empty `Optional` if there is no result (no rows or, for an entity class, no entity of that class in the result) or the single value is `null` (for example `RETURN null`)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetClass`, `cypher`, or `parameters` is `null`
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if `cypher` is empty or `targetClass` is a void type (Neo4j-OGM rejects these with a plain `RuntimeException`); if the database cannot be reached or Neo4j rejects the query; if the query produces more than one result (counted as described above); or if the result cannot be mapped to `targetClass` (Neo4j-OGM throws a `MappingException`, also for a result of a primitive `targetClass` as described above, because the value it maps is boxed)
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Query for a single person by name
  Map<String, Object> params = Map.of("name", "John Doe");
  Optional<Person> person = executor.findOnly(Person.class,
      "MATCH (p:Person {name: $name}) RETURN p", params);

  // Query for single aggregation result
  Optional<Long> count = executor.findOnly(Long.class,
      "MATCH (p:Person) WHERE p.age > $minAge RETURN count(p) as count",
      Map.of("minAge", 25));

  // Query with LIMIT 1 to guarantee a single row
  Optional<Person> oldest = executor.findOnly(Person.class,
      "MATCH (p:Person) RETURN p ORDER BY p.age DESC LIMIT 1",
      Collections.emptyMap());
  ```
- **See also:** `#stream(Class, String, Map)`, `#stream(String, Map)`
##### stream(...) -> varies by overload
- **Signature:** `public Stream<Map<String, Object>> stream(final String cypher, final Map<String, ?> parameters) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Executes a Cypher query and returns each result row as a `Map<String, Object>` keyed by the column alias declared in the `RETURN` clause.
- **Parameters:**
  - `cypher` (`String`) — the Cypher query string with `$name` parameter placeholders; must not be `null` or empty
  - `parameters` (`Map<String, ?>`) — named parameters bound by the OGM session; may be empty but must not be `null`
- **Returns:** a `Stream` over the already-fetched result rows, each row a `Map` keyed by the `RETURN`-clause aliases; it does not retain the borrowed session
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `cypher` or `parameters` is `null`
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if `cypher` is empty (Neo4j-OGM rejects it with a plain `RuntimeException`); if the database cannot be reached or Neo4j rejects the query; or if the result rows cannot be mapped
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  String cypher = "MATCH (p:Person)-[:WORKS_FOR]->(c:Company) " +
                  "WHERE c.name = $companyName " +
                  "RETURN p.name as personName, c.name as companyName";
  Map<String, Object> params = Map.of("companyName", "Tech Corp");

  try (Stream<Map<String, Object>> rows = executor.stream(cypher, params)) {
      rows.forEach(row -> System.out.println(
              row.get("personName") + " works at " + row.get("companyName")));
  }
  ```
- **See also:** `#stream(Class, String, Map)`, `#stream(String, Map, boolean)`, `#findOnly(Class, String, Map)`
- **Signature:** `public Stream<Map<String, Object>> stream(final String cypher, final Map<String, ?> parameters, final boolean readOnly) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Executes a Cypher query with an explicit read-only hint and returns each row as a `Map<String, Object>`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `cypher` (`String`) — the Cypher query string with `$name` parameter placeholders; must not be `null` or empty
  - `parameters` (`Map<String, ?>`) — named parameters bound by the OGM session; may be empty but must not be `null`
  - `readOnly` (`boolean`) — `true` to mark the query as read-only (eligible for read-replica routing); must be `false` for queries that write to the graph
- **Returns:** a `Stream` over the already-fetched result rows; it does not retain the borrowed session
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `cypher` or `parameters` is `null`
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if `cypher` is empty (Neo4j-OGM rejects it with a plain `RuntimeException`); if the database cannot be reached or Neo4j rejects the query (depending on the deployment, this includes a write query submitted with `readOnly == true`); or if the result rows cannot be mapped
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Read-only query: eligible for read-replica routing in a cluster
  Map<String, Object> params = Map.of("minAge", 25);
  try (Stream<Map<String, Object>> rows =
          executor.stream("MATCH (p:Person) WHERE p.age > $minAge RETURN p.name AS name", params, true)) {
      rows.forEach(row -> System.out.println(row.get("name")));
  }

  // Mutating query MUST pass readOnly = false
  try (Stream<Map<String, Object>> created =
          executor.stream("CREATE (p:Person {name: $name}) RETURN id(p) AS id",
                  Map.of("name", "John"), false)) {
      created.forEach(row -> System.out.println("new id: " + row.get("id")));
  }

  // The session has already been released; try-with-resources is still safe and conventional.
  ```
- **See also:** `#stream(String, Map)`, `#stream(Class, String, Map)`
- **Signature:** `public <T> Stream<T> stream(final Class<T> targetClass, final String cypher, final Map<String, ?> parameters) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Executes a Cypher query and maps its result to instances of `targetClass`.
- **Contract:**
  - `targetClass` is typically an OGM-mapped entity class for queries that return whole nodes, but may also be a basic value type when the `RETURN` clause produces a single scalar per row.
  - The two are mapped differently: For a basic value type, every row must have exactly one column, and the stream holds one converted value per row.
- **Parameters:**
  - `targetClass` (`Class<T>`) — the target class — an OGM-mapped entity class or a basic value type; a numeric primitive class such as `long.class` turns a `null` value into zero, a wrapper class keeps it `null`
  - `cypher` (`String`) — the Cypher query string with `$name` parameter placeholders; must not be `null` or empty
  - `parameters` (`Map<String, ?>`) — named parameters bound by the OGM session; may be empty but must not be `null`
- **Returns:** a `Stream` over the already-fetched results mapped to `targetClass` as described above; it does not retain the borrowed session
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetClass`, `cypher`, or `parameters` is `null`
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if `cypher` is empty or `targetClass` is a void type (Neo4j-OGM rejects these with a plain `RuntimeException`); if the database cannot be reached or Neo4j rejects the query; or if a result row cannot be mapped to `targetClass` (for example, a scalar query returns more than one column)
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  String cypher = "MATCH (p:Person) WHERE p.age > $minAge RETURN p";
  Map<String, Object> params = Map.of("minAge", 25);

  try (Stream<Person> adults = executor.stream(Person.class, cypher, params)) {
      adults.filter(p -> p.getName().startsWith("A"))
            .forEach(p -> System.out.println(p.getName()));
  }
  ```
- **See also:** `#findOnly(Class, String, Map)`, `#stream(String, Map)`
##### count(...) -> long
- **Signature:** `public long count(final Class<?> targetClass, final Iterable<Filter> filters) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Counts the number of mapped entities of the specified type that match the given filter expression.
- **Contract:**
  - Original filter objects are passed on when an iterable contains a `null` element (Neo4j-OGM then throws a `NullPointerException`), an instance of a `Filter` subclass, or a filter whose nested path holds an instance of a `Filter.NestedPathSegment` subclass: Neo4j-OGM then resolves its filters in place, and two filters of a plain list on the same property share one parameter, the last value wins and the count is silently wrong.
  - All filter objects are passed on without copying (with a warning logged once) if the Neo4j-OGM `Filter` and `Filter.NestedPathSegment` classes on the classpath do not declare exactly the fields of Neo4j-OGM 5.0.7 through 5.0.11, or if the filter's private comparison function, which the copy reads reflectively, cannot be accessed (see "Filter Arguments" in the class documentation).
  - An iterable other than a `Collection` or `Filters` is consumed once into a list before copying: if a filter cannot be copied, that list preserves every original filter, including those already inspected.
- **Parameters:**
  - `targetClass` (`Class<?>`) — the OGM-mapped class whose entities are counted
  - `filters` (`Iterable<Filter>`) — OGM `Filter`s whose `org.neo4j.ogm.cypher.BooleanOperator`s define how each filter is joined to the preceding one; pass an empty iterable to count all entities of `targetClass`. The filters of a `Filters` object or of any other iterable are copied as described above. Unlike the `Filters` overloads of `loadAll`, a `null` iterable is not accepted here
- **Returns:** the number of entities of `targetClass` that satisfy the supplied filter expression
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetClass` or `filters` is `null`
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if `targetClass` is not a mapped entity class (Neo4j-OGM rejects it with a plain `RuntimeException`, whereas `#count(Class)` returns `0` for it), if a filter after the first has no `org.neo4j.ogm.cypher.BooleanOperator`, if OGM cannot map the filters, the database cannot be reached, or Neo4j rejects the count query
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Count with single filter
  Filter statusFilter = new Filter("status", ComparisonOperator.EQUALS, "active");
  long activeCount = executor.count(Person.class, Arrays.asList(statusFilter));
  System.out.println("Active persons: " + activeCount);

  // Count with multiple filters
  Filters filters = new Filters();
  filters.add(new Filter("status", ComparisonOperator.EQUALS, "active"));
  filters.and(new Filter("age", ComparisonOperator.GREATER_THAN, 25));
  long count = executor.count(Person.class, filters);

  // Filters on the same property in a plain list: each copy is sent with a parameter of its own
  Filter minAge = new Filter("age", ComparisonOperator.GREATER_THAN, 18);
  Filter maxAge = new Filter("age", ComparisonOperator.LESS_THAN, 65);
  maxAge.setBooleanOperator(BooleanOperator.AND);
  long workingAge = executor.count(Person.class, Arrays.asList(minAge, maxAge));   // age_0 = 18, age_1 = 65

  // Count for pagination
  Filter departmentFilter = new Filter("department", ComparisonOperator.EQUALS, "IT");
  long totalItems = executor.count(Person.class, Arrays.asList(departmentFilter));
  int pageSize = 10;
  int totalPages = (int) Math.ceil((double) totalItems / pageSize);
  ```
- **See also:** `#count(Class)`, `org.neo4j.ogm.cypher.Filter`
- **Signature:** `public long count(final Class<?> targetClass) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Counts all node or relationship entities mapped by the specified type.
- **Parameters:**
  - `targetClass` (`Class<?>`) — the OGM-mapped class whose entities are counted
- **Returns:** the total number of entities mapped by `targetClass`, or `0` if the class is not mapped
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetClass` is `null`
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if OGM cannot map the target class, the database cannot be reached, or Neo4j rejects the count query
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Count all persons in the database
  long totalPersons = executor.count(Person.class);
  System.out.println("Total persons: " + totalPersons);

  // Count all companies
  long totalCompanies = executor.count(Company.class);

  // Use for database statistics
  Map<String, Long> stats = new HashMap<>();
  stats.put("persons", executor.count(Person.class));
  stats.put("companies", executor.count(Company.class));
  stats.put("projects", executor.count(Project.class));

  // Initialize a type when it has no data
  if (executor.count(Person.class) == 0) {
      executor.save(new Person("First user", 30));
  }
  ```
- **See also:** `#count(Class, Iterable)`
##### getGraphId(...) -> Long
- **Signature:** `public Long getGraphId(final Object possibleEntity) throws RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Returns the native Neo4j graph ID for `possibleEntity`, if it is an OGM-managed entity.
- **Contract:**
  - Because the executor uses a cleared pooled session for the call, this only returns a non-null ID when the entity carries an ID field that OGM has already populated (either because it was loaded from the database or because a previous `save` assigned it).
- **Parameters:**
  - `possibleEntity` (`Object`) — an object that may or may not be an OGM-mapped entity; may be `null`, in which case `null` is returned
- **Returns:** the native Neo4j graph ID for the entity, or `null` if `possibleEntity` is not a mapped/managed entity with an assigned ID, or its class has no native graph-ID field
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if OGM cannot read or convert the mapped graph identifier of `possibleEntity`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Person person = executor.load(Person.class, 123L);
  Long graphId = executor.getGraphId(person); // native graph ID; may differ from a primary-index lookup value

  Person newPerson = new Person("John Doe");
  executor.getGraphId(newPerson);                // null - not yet saved (newPerson.getId() is now a negative placeholder)
  executor.save(newPerson);                      // post-state: newPerson now has a generated id
  Long savedId = executor.getGraphId(newPerson); // assigned by Neo4j
  ```
- **See also:** `#load(Class, Serializable)`
